https://jonnyutah4congress.com/?utm_source=Jonny+Larsen+for+Congress&utm_campaign=ad618295d6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2026_09_06_07_12_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_50a203dec4-bcdbe79a1e-746037882&mc_cid=ad618295d6&mc_eid=UNIQID

** Jonny’s Team Needs YOU 🫵
------------------------------------------------------------

Hi Friend,

Can you believe it? Today is Election Day! Make sure you remind your friends, family, neighbors, and coworkers to vote. If they haven’t yet, remind them NOT to put their ballots in the mail at this point, but to place them in a secure dropbox or vote in person today until 8 pm. All details, including dropbox locations and polling sites can be found at vote.utah.gov (https://vote.utah.gov/?utm_source=Jonny+Larsen+for+Congress&utm_campaign=ad618295d6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2026_09_06_07_12_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_50a203dec4-bcdbe79a1e-746037882&mc_cid=ad618295d6&mc_eid=UNIQID) using the easy address lookup feature.

🌟 We just finished our new US Immigration video series (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LYiQJJ_rmu8&list=PLY_ZzLLurqoU&utm_source=Jonny+Larsen+for+Congress&utm_campaign=ad618295d6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2026_09_06_07_12_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_50a203dec4-bcdbe79a1e-746037882&mc_cid=ad618295d6&mc_eid=UNIQID) , a 10,000-foot view of the United States immigration system. How much does it cost to immigrate to the US? What kinds of visas are available to foreigners? How long does it take to become a citizen? Watch Jonny’s interview with UVU student and paralegal Eliza Williams to learn a little more about our system. 🌟
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LYiQJJ_rmu8&list=PLY_ZzLLurqoU&utm_source=Jonny+Larsen+for+Congress&utm_campaign=ad618295d6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2026_09_06_07_12_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_50a203dec4-bcdbe79a1e-746037882&mc_cid=ad618295d6&mc_eid=UNIQID

Plus. check out our new video series about Jonny, the campaign, and building excitement to Election Day? We’ve had fabulous feedback. Here’s the first video (https://www.instagram.com/p/De7aiyPiLBE/?utm_source=Jonny+Larsen+for+Congress&utm_campaign=ad618295d6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2026_09_06_07_12_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_50a203dec4-bcdbe79a1e-746037882&mc_cid=ad618295d6&mc_eid=UNIQID) in the My Story series.

You can find all My Story videos on Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, TikTok by searching for @jonnyutah4congress.

Please take a few moments to share all of these videos using the social buttons, text them to your friends, and email them out to everyone. Let’s get this Marine elected!
https://www.instagram.com/p/De7aiyPiLBE/?utm_source=Jonny+Larsen+for+Congress&utm_campaign=ad618295d6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2026_09_06_07_12_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_50a203dec4-bcdbe79a1e-746037882&mc_cid=ad618295d6&mc_eid=UNIQID

How many days until...
https://jonnylarsen.com?utm_source=Jonny+Larsen+for+Congress&utm_campaign=ad618295d6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2026_09_06_07_12_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_50a203dec4-bcdbe79a1e-746037882&mc_cid=ad618295d6&mc_eid=UNIQID

** Last chance! Dog year donations 🐶
------------------------------------------------------------

We’re in the final stretch! Help us meet our end-of-campaign goals. You know Jonny’s lifelong love of Great Danes, including Duke, his nearly 11-year-old buddy of today. Show some support in dog years! We’re so grateful for every donation to make this campaign possible.

** Honk if you’re hopeful! 🌊
------------------------------------------------------------

Honk n’ Wave - We’ve had a great time with volunteers and other CD-04 candidates from all races at Honk n’ Waves around the district! If you see one of our teams out today, give them a wave, and honk if you’re hopeful for big changes today!

Want a little peek? This was one of our volunteer teams out this morning (https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfSZtASjPCi/?rpxt=ZDQyYmMwMGsyZ3dw&utm_source=Jonny+Larsen+for+Congress&utm_campaign=ad618295d6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2026_09_06_07_12_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_50a203dec4-bcdbe79a1e-746037882&mc_cid=ad618295d6&mc_eid=UNIQID) !

** Do your civic duty!
------------------------------------------------------------

Ballots are out and folks arehttps://jonnylarsen.com doing their civic duty. Get out and talk to your undecided friends, family, and neighbors about voting for Jonny. It can make all the difference in the world. Some fun ways to spread the word:
* Take a photo of your ballot with your vote for Jonny. Post it on your social media and tag @jonnyutah4congress (https://us.list-manage.com/FS_FZs7POKq?e=7d3a298e66&c2id=2b1c336aa2eea8702cda8e8093a863b4&m=9bqamnzP-m6gbIFlYDF2FkFwZU_AP7lb0fjm6pIe05CJmBcqnN0mRNcjnQ8W&utm_source=Jonny+Larsen+for+Congress&utm_campaign=ad618295d6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2026_09_06_07_12_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_50a203dec4-bcdbe79a1e-746037882&mc_cid=ad618295d6&mc_eid=UNIQID) on IG or Facebook (https://us.list-manage.com/84woeLdozGF?e=7d3a298e66&c2id=2b1c336aa2eea8702cda8e8093a863b4&m=mVas_r6g_6EDqo8rAqfO_PW16oxVGfhFtFM9_HXL-3Pbj7jGtP9pdLkRm_mv&utm_source=Jonny+Larsen+for+Congress&utm_campaign=ad618295d6-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2026_09_06_07_12_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_50a203dec4-bcdbe79a1e-746037882&mc_cid=ad618295d6&mc_eid=UNIQID) .
* Record a video about why you’re voting for Jonny in 15-30 seconds and tag.
* More visible social interactions: Like, share, and comment on voting posts and news articles where good discussions are happening to show your support. Something like, “I’m voting for Jonny Larsen for Congress” is great. Always keep comments positive and hopeful, and don’t forget to tag the campaign.

Friend,
The battle to defend the America First agenda has _**never been more critical.**_
Every single day, Chuck Schumer, the mainstream media, and radical Left dark-money groups attack President Trump’s administration and the proven leaders he selected to turn our nation around.
One of their prime targets: _Secretary of State Marco Rubio._
From dismantling globalist policies and standing up to Communist China to securing our borders and projecting unapologetic American strength across the globe, Secretary Rubio is working hand-in-hand with President Trump to deliver **real results.**

name: Tim Moore
subject: Can I count on you today?

body:
Peter, today's the day, and before anything else, I want to say _THANK YOU._ Every door you knocked, every call you made, every dollar you gave got us here. Serving the people of this district has been the honor of my life, and I don't take a single vote for granted.So I'm humbly asking: **if you haven 't voted yet, will you go today?** [](https://timmoore.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fhddddk-hkhielhuy-r/) **Polls are open until 7:30 PM tonight. Find your polling place at[https://vt.ncsbe.gov/PPLkup/](https://timmoore.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fhddddk-hkhielhuy-y/) and bring your photo ID. And if you're in line at 7:30, stay in line!** Still have a mail ballot? Drop it off at your county board of elections by 7:30 PM. Polling places can't accept it. [FIND MY POLLING PLACE ->](https://timmoore.cmail19.com/t/y-l-fhddddk-hkhielhuy-j/) Democrats came into today outvoting us, and the stakes couldn't be higher. My opponent is facing a FELONY charge and refuses to denounce socialism. _Our taxes, our border, and our families ' future all hang on keeping the House._This election is too important to sit out. But I believe with all my heart that America's best days are still ahead of her, and today we get to prove it.**Please vote, and bring someone with you.** Thank you, Congressman Tim Moore

name: Mark Warner
subject: Thank you, Derek
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Mark Warner
body:
|
---

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142852706/658277610/-1927560734?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_NF_ElectionNight_261103_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YTg4MWExZS1lOWQ3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VQxHylBfp6YKLvLT1mios6eGphJ_icBTq6lxC1SYbf0=) Derek,

**The _Associated Press_ just called this race. I’m proud to say that thanks to the hard work, energy, and support from this grassroots team, we won.**

It’s been the honor of my lifetime to serve Virginia, first as Governor and now as Senator. But I’ll be honest: the past two years have been incredibly challenging.

During this campaign, I talked to voters about the choices being made in Washington:
* The choice to go to war with Iran, to put troops into harm's way without a clear strategy or plan, and with shifting objectives. And in the process, raising fuel prices on all of us.
* The choice to rip health care away from millions to pay for tax cuts for the very wealthy.
* The choice to let grifting, self-dealing, and corruption run rampant among this administration – with no accountability from the party in power.
* And then there were the choices not being made at all – to let Artificial Intelligence develop at a rapid pace without any guardrails whatsoever.

**But today, Virginia made a choice, too.**

We chose to reject the chaos and corruption from the party in control of Washington, and we chose to follow a forward-looking vision for our commonwealth and our country. So, now we know what choices need to be made next:

_**Congress needs to act NOW to lower costs for all Virginians –**_ like pushing this administration to end Trump’s war-of-choice overseas and unnecessary trade wars with our allies that are driving up costs. We also need to continue the effort to lower Virginians’ utility bills, expand access to affordable housing, and strengthen our child care workforce so care becomes more affordable for young families.

_**It’s time to move toward a system of universal health care coverage in this country.**_ Because we cannot keep patching a broken system. We need to ensure that all Americans can receive a basic standard of care, no matter their income – and we need to make sure that care is accessible no matter where you live. That means protecting our rural hospitals and clinics.

_**We must pass a set of guardrails to protect our national security, our communities, and our workforce in the face of the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence –**_ while ensuring the United States continues to lead on innovation. I’ve been raising the alarm bells for years about the major disruptions and risks AI presents, and I have a comprehensive legislative package that Congress should act on immediately.

_**And finally, we’ve got to put an end to this self-dealing in Washington.**_ I will continue to lead the fight to hold those abusing their power accountable, stop these vanity projects that are wasting taxpayer dollars, and pass stricter laws, so that public office is about public service – not grifting and taxpayer-funded payouts.

**These were the commitments I made to voters on the campaign trail and the commitments I make to you tonight as we begin the process of charting a better path forward – for Virginia and for our country.**

I know how easy it would have been to tune out the noise from Washington, but you didn’t.

You stayed engaged, kept showing up, and that’s why we won. Thank you for everything you’ve done to make tonight possible.

The fight continues,

Mark Warner

I wanted to reach out one last time before polls close tonight.
Today is the day we’ve been working toward since the day we launched this campaign. As we head into these final hours, I want you to know how grateful I am for every door you knocked, every call you made, and every dollar you chipped in to get us here.

Bowdoin College Professor Chris Potholm -- former college roommate to Maine Senator and Defense Secretary Bill Cohen, former campaign adviser to the same Cohen and then Gov. Angus King -- once told a story during his Maine politics course about an autistic sex offender he hired (off the books, of course) for a campaign because they guy was a savant with numbers. By Potholm's telling, the guy was able to get the numbers via telephone for three or four Maine communities with combined populations of less than 1,000 people and instantly call the major political races with the same degree of accuracy as the major newspapers.
Some of that may be apocryphal (except for the sex predator part, that's definitely part of the story), but the important part is that just a handful of Maine towns have an uncanny knack for serving as bellwethers for the rest of the state. Whereas Potholm had an autistic sex offender at his disposal, we have terabytes of data and a Hermes harness hooked into multiple frontier AI models.
The magic of the bellwethers is that for at least a few precious hours, you can appear to be oddly prescient, and maybe throw a few bucks on Kalshi. For example if Susan Collins carries Kennebec County by three points tonight, that's a dark omen for Republicans. Whereas if Paul LePage carries Skowhegan by three, Matt Dunlap is probably toast. The reason for this lies in the totally non-scientific but nonetheless uncanny knack for certain counties and towns in Maine to align at an unusually high rate with congressional and statewide races.
So without further ado, here's the subscribers only insight into what cities and towns might point up the winners of the big races long before the Associated Press or DDHQ starts calling races tonight...

If you haven't returned yours yet, there's still time to drop it off at an official ballot drop box. Every vote counts, and there's still time for yours to be one of them. Thank you in advance for casting your ballot! \---------- Forwarded message ---------- Peter, It’s 8 p.m., and the drop boxes and mailboxes have officially received all your ballots! So this is a really good time to say thank you. I am so grateful for the incredible support and dedication this team has shown over the past year. You’re amazing. Despite the countless attacks Christine Drazan and her Republican allies in D.C. have thrown our way, Oregonians have stood strong and stayed committed to making Oregon a place where everyone has the opportunity to thrive. You showed up. You didn’t take anything for granted. You knocked on doors, you made phone calls, you pitched in a few dollars when you could. And because of you, we’ve had the resources to build a strong grassroots campaign where people came together with a shared vision of a future dedicated to justice and opportunity for all — for an Oregon where we fight for each other, no matter where you live, where you come from, or who you are. So no matter what happens in this election, I couldn’t be more thankful for the work we’ve done together. Thank you for being on my team. — Tina | Email is a key way for us to stay in touch and make sure you get the latest updates from our campaign. name: Roy Cooper
subject: The campaign ends and the work begins
body:
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1678&source=&t=1&akid=5334%2E124072%2EaJZPcS) | | | |
---
North Carolinians made their voices heard, and they were loud!
To everyone reading this, to the volunteers and supporters of our campaign: Thank you for everything you did to take this Senate seat back for the people of North Carolina!
Tonight, the campaign ends. But tomorrow the work of governing begins.
We have to work to make health care, housing and groceries more affordable. To end this war and stop the pain at the pump. To protect Medicaid expansion that is providing affordable health care to hundreds of thousands of people. To stop the corruption and take on the special interests that get rich while people struggle to get by.
It won’t be easy. It won’t be simple. But I know that together, we can get it done.
There will be much more to say and do in the coming days, weeks, and months, but for now, I’ll leave you with this: I am still a prisoner of hope, and I believe that our best days are ahead if we work for it.
May God bless you, our country and the great state of North Carolina.
Thank you!
Roy
P.S.: The campaign may be over, but our work is not. We have wonderful staff across North Carolina that powered this win. [**_If you’re able, a contribution would go a long way to making sure we have the resources we need to keep paying them and for their health care through the end of the year._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1678&amount=5&t=3&akid=5334%2E124072%2EaJZPcS)

name: Jamie Ager
subject: We did it
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ager for Congress
body:
Thank you. This is my promise as your next Congressman for District 11.| | | |
---
Peter,
---
I wanted you to hear it from me tonight: polls are closed, the numbers are coming in, and the folks at the Associated Press have declared that they’ve seen enough to call this race for us.**We did it.** I never expected to run for Congress, but in my heart I believe this is a time in our country where we good folks need to step up and be good leaders. I love Western North Carolina. I’m proud to be from here and I couldn’t imagine living anywhere else. The people here are good, honest people, who care about their neighbors, and just want a fair chance to make a decent life for themselves and their family. So here’s my promise to you tonight, as your next member of Congress for the 11th District: I’m going to go up to Washington, DC, and fight like hell to make sure each and every one of us has that fair chance.I’ll fight for better wages and lower costs on basic needs like utilities, child care, and groceries. I’ll fight to expand affordable health care access, keep our rural hospitals open, and hold corporations like HCA accountable.I’ll fight to protect social services like Medicare, Medicaid, SNAP, Social Security, and veteran’s benefits. I’ll fight for transparency, accountability, and good governance practices. I’ll never sell out any community or sell off our shared public lands. This is the best land in the country, with the best people, and I will spend every day fighting to make sure no one is left behind, no matter who they are, what they believe, or whether I agree with them. Tonight, we get to celebrate. Tomorrow, we get the chance to start building a government founded in honesty, community, and hard work. Thank you again for believing in me — we’ll chat more soon about next steps and how you can help, because believe it or not, this next part is actually the hard part. But tonight, I hope you’ll just take a moment to sit back and be proud of all you did to help us get this result.I couldn’t have done it without you.
---
---
**Jamie Ager**
_Democrat for US Congress_

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: A Democrat FLIPS to GOP days before the election
body:
Plus: How to help San Juan County before the next storm hits | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/9fqcVxyQCv1?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | |
Two days before the election, a Democratic congresswoman in Michigan stood next to the Republican running for Senate and told voters she’s with him. Her party chair says she’s no longer a Democrat. [We tell you why we think it matters beyond Michigan.](https://us.list-manage.com/YDSQNWXjxr0?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
Then we go to San Juan County, where 1,500 homes took on water and more rain is on the way. Sheriff Ken Christesen and volunteer Jamie Decker join us from Farmington to tell you what they need. Everything you need to give is at the bottom of this email.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/18bDkiZSSKd?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |
**🔥 HALEY STEVENS WALKED AWAY FROM HER OWN PARTY’S NOMINEE**
Haley Stevens lost the Michigan Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed by one point. On Sunday morning, after church in Detroit, she stood next to Mike Rogers and said, “We can’t stand with hate.”
She didn’t do this out of nowhere. There’s an ad, a streamer named Hasan Piker, and a message from El-Sayed’s campaign telling her to stay away. We walk through all of it, and we explain what she may know about this race that the polls don’t.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/xWSV79enToX?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
**🌊 1,500 HOMES, A RIVER ABOVE ITS 1909 RECORD, AND MORE RAIN COMING**
Sheriff Christesen says the flooding runs from Pagosa Springs to Bluff, Utah, and that without Navajo Dam it would have been thousands more homes. What’s in the river now is the part people don’t understand, and he lays it out.
Jamie Decker hadn’t left her house since the rain started. Her neighborhood in Harper Valley didn’t wait for anyone to show up. She tells us how they did it, and what she needs most this week.

**🗳️ 434,818 NEW MEXICANS HAVE VOTED. REPUBLICANS ARE BEHIND 2022.**
We pulled the Secretary of State numbers and compared them to four years ago. One number is nearly identical to 2022. Another one isn’t, and it’s the one Republicans need to see before Tuesday.
We also go through who showed up on Election Day last time, and why the gap you’re hearing about doesn’t have to be erased for Republicans to win statewide.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/aeaOOuna0sv?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
**PLUS:** Our final Senate predictions, state by state, on the record. We agree on Iowa, Alaska, Maine, Michigan and Texas and split on Ohio and Kansas. One of us has it 53-47 and the other 51-49, and we’re both going against Jay McCleskey on Texas. Also: three bobcats on the trail cam, and wild turkeys on a car in Fort Collins that Mark’s brother-in-law did not bring home for Thanksgiving.

**🤝 HOW TO HELP SAN JUAN COUNTY**
If you’re far away, money moves fastest. [San Juan United Way is coordinating supplies and cash for Farmington and Bloomfield](https://us.list-manage.com/jY2RVWAEbUX?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e).
Drop-off for supplies: San Juan United Way, 903 W. Apache St., Farmington. Call ahead to confirm hours and current needs.

| Release Date: November 4, 2026
---
| Anthony Forlini Concedes
# Michigan Secretary of State Race
---
| Forlini congratulates Lt. Governor Garlin Gilchrist and thanks Michigan voters for the opportunity to share his vision for public service
---
| HARRISON TOWNSHIP, Mich. - Anthony Forlini, Republican candidate for Michigan Secretary of State, issued the following statement after the results of Tuesday's election became clear:
"Tonight, the people of Michigan made their decision. While this is not the outcome we hoped for, I respect the voters' choice and congratulate Garlin Gilchrist on his victory as Michigan's next Secretary of State. As the Clerk of Michigan's third largest county, I look forward to working with Secretary-elect Gilchrist in any way I can to better serve Michigan's clerks and citizens.
"Running for Secretary of State has been an incredible journey. I am deeply grateful to the people across Michigan who welcomed me into their communities, shared their concerns, and placed their trust in our campaign. Our message was simple: the government should serve the people. Experience matters. Reliability matters. Transparency matters. And public service should always rise above partisan politics.
"I want to thank my family, our campaign team, our volunteers, our donors and every person who displayed a sign, made a phone call, sent a text message or spoke to a neighbor on our behalf. Your commitment, friendship and encouragement have meant more to me than I can adequately express.
"I am encouraged by the Republicans, Independents, and Democrats who came together to support me. We demonstrated that people do not have to agree on every issue - or belong to the same political party - to recognize the value of experience, integrity and common-sense leadership.
"I wish Garlin Gilchrist and his family well. The Secretary of State's responsibilities are significant, and his success in serving Michigan will ultimately be our state's success.
"I will continue fulfilling my responsibilities as Macomb County Clerk with the same seriousness and dedication I have always brought to public office. The citizens who elected me deserve nothing less."

I am deeply grateful to the people across Michigan who welcomed me into their communities, shared their concerns, and placed their trust in our campaign. Our message was simple: the government should serve the people. Experience matters. Reliability matters. Transparency matters. And public service should always rise above partisan politics. "I want to thank my family, our campaign team, our volunteers, our donors and every person who displayed a sign, made a phone call, sent a text message or spoke to a neighbor on our behalf. Your commitment, friendship and encouragement have meant more to me than I can adequately express. "I am encouraged by the Republicans, Independents, and Democrats who came together to support me. We demonstrated that people do not have to agree on every issue - or belong to the same political party - to recognize the value of experience, integrity and common-sense leadership. "I wish Garlin Gilchrist and his family well. The Secretary of State's responsibilities are significant, and his success in serving Michigan will ultimately be our state's success. "I will continue fulfilling my responsibilities as Macomb County Clerk with the same seriousness and dedication I have always brought to public office. The citizens who elected me deserve nothing less." | ### | | == | | | | Paid for by CTE Anthony G. Forlini | 39285 N. Blom | Harrison Township, MI 48045 US | | | | | | |

We launched a campaign that many did not believe could win. _But all those naysayers didn't know what we could do together!_ Tonight, you chose new, bold leadership grounded in hope and a belief that we can build a better future together. You chose a willingness to fight for what is right — _even if it means taking on powerful companies, or a lawless and bullying president._ And you chose to build this grassroots movement together, so that we could start delivering on day one. Because it's time to come together and meet the challenges we face: It's time for housing and health care Coloradans can actually afford. It's time to build a stronger economy, and a brighter future for the next generation. It's time to protect our freedoms, the safety of our communities, and our land, air, and water. It's time to ensure that our government is working for us. _And it's about time to get corporate money out of our politics._ To every Coloradan, whether you voted for me or not: I want you to know that I will always show up, listen to your concerns, and work with you to deliver on the promise of building a better state for all. _Because I truly believe that all of us need all of us._ I am profoundly grateful to my family, my wife, and our two kids; to our entire campaign team; and to the thousands of volunteers who powered this campaign. None of us would be here today without you: This victory belongs to you. It is my honor to lead with hope and a belief that, in Colorado, when we work together, we can and we will build a better future. Let's get to work! With gratitude, Phil

clean_body: This victory belongs to you. = Folks, it's Phil. I am deeply grateful to have been elected to serve as Colorado's next governor. Nearly two years ago, we set out to listen to every neighbor in every corner of Colorado. We launched a campaign that many did not believe could win. But all those naysayers didn't know what we could do together! Tonight, you chose new, bold leadership grounded in hope and a belief that we can build a better future together. You chose a willingness to fight for what is right — even if it means taking on powerful companies, or a lawless and bullying president. And you chose to build this grassroots movement together, so that we could start delivering on day one. Because it's time to come together and meet the challenges we face: It's time for housing and health care Coloradans can actually afford. It's time to build a stronger economy, and a brighter future for the next generation. It's time to protect our freedoms, the safety of our communities, and our land, air, and water. It's time to ensure that our government is working for us. And it's about time to get corporate money out of our politics. To every Coloradan, whether you voted for me or not: I want you to know that I will always show up, listen to your concerns, and work with you to deliver on the promise of building a better state for all. Because I truly believe that all of us need all of us. I am profoundly grateful to my family, my wife, and our two kids; to our entire campaign team; and to the thousands of volunteers who powered this campaign. None of us would be here today without you: This victory belongs to you. It is my honor to lead with hope and a belief that, in Colorado, when we work together, we can and we will build a better future. Let's get to work! ---
| Thank You By the Grace of God, We Won Re-election VA 05!
---
|
---
First,
I want to thank God for this victory. To my wife Tracy: I could not have done this without you. Thank you for being my unwavering partner through every step of this journey. To my brother Rusty McGuire, thank you for your constant advice and support. Our dad, John McGuire Jr, passed away last week, which is tough, but I know he is smiling down on us for this win.
To my Political Director Ramona Christian, our campaign team, our dedicated volunteers, and every supporter who knocked on doors, made calls, and believed in our mission, this victory belongs to you.
Despite $4.5 million in negative and false attacks on me poured onto the airwaves by my opponent, the truth prevailed. The people of Virginia's Fifth District know who stands with them. Once again, you have placed your trust in me, and I am deeply honored and humbled by that responsibility. I will continue fighting for our shared conservative values and delivering real results for the communities we call home.
Over the past 22 Months, we put the Fifth District first. Together, we:
• Secured more than $20 billion in investments and 7,000 jobs to strengthen our economic future
• Expanded a Navy and Marine Corps educational program at Liberty University, a goal since 1971.
• Advanced critical infrastructure, including major progress on a vital emergency exit route for Wintergreen
• Returned over $10 million to constituents by helping them cut through federal red tape.
This was a tough race, but by the grace of God we won!
I love this district and whether you voted for me or not, I will keep working hard every day to earn the trust of those who did not support me this time, and to continue delivering for those who did.
Serving as your Congressman is an honor, a serious responsibility, and a profound privilege. The Fifth District is our home. Let's keep getting things done together.

clean_body: | | | | == | Thank You By the Grace of God, We Won Re-election VA 05! | First, I want to thank God for this victory. To my wife Tracy: I could not have done this without you. Thank you for being my unwavering partner through every step of this journey. To my brother Rusty McGuire, thank you for your constant advice and support. Our dad, John McGuire Jr, passed away last week, which is tough, but I know he is smiling down on us for this win. To my Political Director Ramona Christian, our campaign team, our dedicated volunteers, and every supporter who knocked on doors, made calls, and believed in our mission, this victory belongs to you. Despite $4.5 million in negative and false attacks on me poured onto the airwaves by my opponent, the truth prevailed. The people of Virginia's Fifth District know who stands with them. Once again, you have placed your trust in me, and I am deeply honored and humbled by that responsibility. I will continue fighting for our shared conservative values and delivering real results for the communities we call home. Over the past 22 Months, we put the Fifth District first. Together, we: • Secured more than $20 billion in investments and 7,000 jobs to strengthen our economic future • Expanded a Navy and Marine Corps educational program at Liberty University, a goal since 1971. • Advanced critical infrastructure, including major progress on a vital emergency exit route for Wintergreen • Returned over $10 million to constituents by helping them cut through federal red tape. This was a tough race, but by the grace of God we won! I love this district and whether you voted for me or not, I will keep working hard every day to earn the trust of those who did not support me this time, and to continue delivering for those who did. Serving as your Congressman is an honor, a serious responsibility, and a profound privilege. The Fifth District is our home. Peter, It’s official: Democrats have won back the House. The Trump plot to steal enough seats to keep control of Congress — the will of the people be damned — was systematically dismantled. And given the opportunity, voters instead chose to elect a new Democratic majority. Once again, American democracy has been defended. Let this be a lesson: never capitulate, never acquiesce to those who would use power for improper purposes. Fight. Always remember that a committed and focused American people can overcome any obstacle put in their way. Remain optimistic. Congratulations to soon-to-be Speaker of the House Hakeem Jeffries, soon-to-be House Majority Leader Katherine Clarke, soon-to-be House Majority Whip Pete Aguilar, DCCC Chair Suzan DelBene, and to everyone who stepped up to be part of this fight. The MAGA gerrymandering scheme didn't just fail all on its own — we destroyed it together. This is just the start. There are more results still to come. For now, thank you for all you’ve done to make this victory possible. In solidarity, Eric H. Holder, Jr.
82nd Attorney General of the United States

Maria

Hey everybody, it just became official.
Ohioans voted for change.
This victory belongs to every single person who gave your time, your attention, your trust, and your hard-earned money.
**Thank you.**
[](https://substack.com/redirect/58462313-03a5-491d-bdb2-5e00028b6eb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
> _We came together to put workers before billionaires._
> _We stood up against corruption, against scandal, against war._
> _We fought back against hundreds of millions of dollars in dark-money attacks._
> _We took on Big Tech, the insurance companies, the drug companies, and Wall Street._
> _We said no to a senator who screwed over working people every chance he got._
> _We told Jon Husted -- we told all of Washington -- we're not putting up with it anymore._
> _We showed up, we voted, and we won._
> _Thank you, Ohio!_

This midterm election was a proxy war between two competing visions for America... and tonight, America First lost.

America First lost *not* because it doesn't resonate with the people. It lost because of the soy-boy consultants and "influencers" who suck at telling our story and who actively alienated those who actually connect with voters.

Republicans have two years to fire these soy-boys and elevate people who actually connect with voters.

"The pendulum will swing back" is a clock. It's not a strategy. Or, not. Blessings.

body:
You have my gratitude.

| [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142854318/658304092/1546157161?refcode=em_JJR_OTH_Loss_110326&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDkxMjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZWU1ZWRmZTYtMDhkOC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=T_jTCJAoUCQuApWWAeXVIGvPNImK91Aod9BOVYiax6w=&emci=d4da60dd-05d8-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=ee5edfe6-08d8-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=32374386)
---
Peter, The voters have spoken. While I am disappointed to share the news with you that we did not get the result we hoped for, I want you to know how grateful I am for your support and for what we did together. We launched this campaign 519 days ago. With it, we have raised Floridians’ expectations of the Attorney General’s Office. Floridians expect and deserve public safety and real plans to keep our kids safe; not cruel and wasteful gimmicks. Floridians expect and deserve an Attorney General who will take on the corporations making life expensive; not one that takes their donations and walks away. We expect and deserve an AG who will enforce rights, not try to take them away — and one who will clean up corruption, not perpetrate it and try to cover it up. You supported this campaign, and I asked a lot of you. You knocked on doors, made phone calls, hosted events from the Panhandle to the Keys, and donated what you could. Thank you, from the bottom of my heart. We did not get the result we hoped for, but we do not give up. I never have and never will — and hope you won’t either. We keep working. We keep fighting. Florida’s future generations deserve nothing less from us. With gratitude, Jose Javier Rodriguez

_Republishing old content is very hackish and I don 't intend to do a lot of it, but in light of the massacre Maine Republicans endured last night, this review of the 2022 elections is worth publishing again. In the coming days, I'll have more to say about how the elections turned out, but so much of this piece written four years ago remains true as ever. _
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..PwFE0Vd4QOn9E2upBSNb4Fdsgu0UMYyyWPnWJnibf6Y?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=223426541)
It's difficult to overstate just how horrible last night went for Maine Republicans. Truly, the 2022 Maine elections will go down in history as one of the most humiliating defeats ever suffered by the Maine Republicans. For the next two years, Republicans in Augusta will be mere spectators to one-party rule. A few days ago, they were plotting which of them would ascend to Speaker of the House, but now the few GOPers who remain are an endangered species, operating an insurgency from remote outposts in the Great North Woods and Aroostook County. At times like these, it's traditional and altogether fitting for the routed party to conduct an autopsy of sorts and search out the root causes. Were Maine Republicans capable of such introspection, they might not find themselves in this predicament in this first place. So let us join the crowd of Monday Morning Quarterbacks to hazard a few guesses as to what went wrong last night with a view to charting a path for the future.
## THE GOVERNOR'S RACE
First, on the gubernatorial race: Gov. Janet Mills soundly defeated former Gov. Paul LePage by 14 points. Could be more when all is said and done. As results continue to come it, it appears that LePage underperformed both his 2014 vote total and Republican Shawn Moody's in 2018. At the same time, Mills added 30,000 voters from her last election. That's mandate territory. Just disastrous for Republicans. Clearly something went terribly, terribly wrong with the LePage campaign, and because most Republicans hitched their wagons in some form or fashion to LePage, the down ballot consequences were ruinous.
It's easy to second guess a campaign from the cheap seats, but the most basic and fair criticism is the LePage campaign never developed a strong central message. Yes, LePage was a fantastic conservative governor whose policies made life better for everyone in the state, except for the parasitic political class. And this time around, the governor had strong policies on energy, on taxes, on the drug epidemic, and on stopping the insane progressive projects emanating from Augusta. But his campaign never crystallized around a simple, memorable message. Ask yourself now, what was his campaign's message in a nutshell? Beats me.
The chief takeaway from his campaign seemed to be: here's the new and improved LePage 2.0, kinder, nicer, and totally averse to the unearned media that made him a sensation in 2010. Whereas the LePage of 2010 and 2014 achieved stardom by hurling rhetorical Molotov cocktails at progressives, LePage 2.0 seemed overly controlled--timid in the face of an incumbent whose chief accomplishment was an authoritarian, unscientific lockdown of the state.
Mills ruined lives and livelihoods by shutting down Maine's economy, and she pilfered taxpayer funds to buy off every constituency in the state. LePage had more right to be angry with her than he did with Libby Mitchell or Mike Michaud. But we saw no righteous indignation this cycle. When the old LePage did come out in the debates, he awkwardly accused Mills of lying, often without an explanation. The campaign website, JanetMillsLied.com, felt like an unnatural act of desperation, which is saying something coming from the guy who wrote half the articles to which the site links.
Even good policies can be poorly messaged. LePage told us about the threat that Maine farmland would soon be colonized with solar panels. We heard that Maine's pension fund reversing the decision to divest from oil and natural gas companies - less than a drop in the bucket of global finance - would somehow fight inflation. Sure, solar subsidies create malinvestment and ESG pension funds drive up energy costs, but these are not issues that resonate with voters. LePage's campaign never landed on a simple rationale for supporting him, or, perhaps more importantly, for rejecting Mills. Would a brasher LePage have changed the outcome? Who knows. But a muzzled LePage never put a dent in Mills.
Compare that with the Mills' campaign, whose central message sang through in every campaign ad: competent, effective, bipartisan leadership. Who cares whether it's true? Voters bought into the idea that everyone in Maine would have died of COVID-19 if Mills hadn't unilaterally seized emergency power, shutdown the state, and crushed her critics with the power of the state. The LePage campaign ceded that argument and allowed Mills' message of Pandemic Era competence to broadcast unresisted. The only explanation for this is some pollster told a consultant Mills' pandemic policies had broad support in Maine. Even if that's true, it's a sign a campaign needs to attack and change public opinion rather than avoid the subject. Why, for example, did LePage not have a massive press conference with the [health care workers](https://substack.com/redirect/b40972de-655f-4d3c-bfc5-019e978b31b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) who lost their jobs because of Mills' unscientific, authoritarian, anti-Christian health care worker vaccine mandate? Why not bring Rick Savage, whose business Mills destroyed over COVID-19, out on the campaign trail every weekend? Everyone in Maine suffered because of Mills' bumbling, authoritarian approach to managing the pandemic - she was the anti-thesis of [Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis](https://substack.com/redirect/ae35ae60-2f8a-4d51-b07f-b167cfc669ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - but LePage left that point unmade.
The LePage campaign also failed to effectively leverage help from outside allies. In the closing weeks of the race, Maine Families First PAC spent more than $800,000 on ads that were harming his opponent and motivating his base. The ads drew attention to radical left-wing material the Maine Dept. of Education was recommending for Maine elementary classrooms, including at least one book that featured cartoons of children having sex. Maine Wire columnist Sam Patten [says](https://substack.com/redirect/df002051-dacb-4dae-a094-d4b9e2fe8cf9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this issue was a distraction; I respectfully disagree. Against the backdrop of miserably low student test scores, thanks to illiberal lockdowns commanded by his opponent, LePage could have capitalized on the idea that a cabal of education bureaucrats and unionized teachers has been [brainwashing](https://substack.com/redirect/9444f96b-fd04-4498-9bdb-0b246be93e1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) children with left-wing hypersexualized poppycock rather than teaching reading, writing, and arithmetic.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..KUWBHtwssBxJtXekFH5lKWLWB8I-hJ2vaZO1OSbEzYM?)
The playbook Virginia Gov. Glen Youngkin used to win office in 2021 was served up on a silver platter. He should have asked Mills during a debate whether she recommended "[Gender Queer](https://substack.com/redirect/43116750-5ada-4568-9299-7ed10ac6e34a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" for Maine schools after finding a few copies on Eliot Cutler's bookshelf... Let the chattering classes chew on that for a few cycles rather than dissecting the twelfth iteration of his abortion stance. Ok, perhaps he shouldn't have gone that blue, but you get the point. 2010 LePage would have found a provocative way to channel the angst and furor of conservative and moderate parents over what's happening in schools. Alas, LePage 2.0 dared not go there. He called the book with the cartoons of children having sex "fine."
LePage also struggled to articulate a coherent position on abortion. Which is stunning considering this was the first election following the Supreme Court overturning Roe v. Wade. Dobbs effectively sent all abortion policies back to the states, so this was naturally going to be a predictable topic. LePage's public position, arrived at painfully through four debates, was as follows: I'm personally pro-life, but I'm not going to manifest that in any policies, including by blocking taxpayer funding for abortions through MaineCare, although I oppose taxpayer funding for abortions. This came off as consultant speak for: "I don't want to alienate pro-abortion women." The opposite became true, with many pro-life conservatives wondering what being pro-life means if you're not going to oppose taking money from pro-life people's paychecks to fund abortions. Whether a more robust pro-life position would have helped LePage is unknowable, but his actual position did nothing to stem the tide of post-Dobbs voters in Maine's blue strongholds, and the wishy-washy politician speak depressed his Christian supporters.
With that being said, every conservative in the state of Maine owes an enormous debt of gratitude to Paul LePage. Twelve years ago, the Maine Republican Party's operation was in shambles. On the strength of LePage's gritty charisma, and under the competent leadership of Maine GOP Executive Director Jason Savage, that organization was professionalized and rebuilt. Yesterday's vote shows yet another infusion of new blood and energy is needed to make the Maine GOP effective at recruiting candidates and turning out votes. But consider where we'd be if LePage decided he'd rather not enter the fray in 2010 and stayed at Mardens. If the Friendly Compromise Republicans (which at the time included this writer) had had their way in that primary, we'd have had four or eight years of Charlie Baker-style Big Government Republicanism under Les Otten or Peter Mills. The Leviathan cannot be managed but must be dismantled, and LePage understood that. During his first term in office, nearly a quarter million Mainers were on Food Stamps; today, less than 170,000 are. LePage also managed to shrink the size of the state government workforce in Maine - a heroic accomplishment. None of that happens without a tenacious governor who will fight, and Maine continues to benefit from those victories.
The lesson seems obvious: unapologetic conservative fighters win elections and policy victories, while limp wristed Republican squishes lose, and lose badly. Which brings us to the Republican legislators.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..PwFE0Vd4QOn9E2upBSNb4Fdsgu0UMYyyWPnWJnibf6Y?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=223426541)
## STATE LEGISLATURE
Republican State lawmakers in recent weeks were already jockeying for Speaker of the House. Talk about counting your eggs. Instead of refining the invite list for a lobbyist happy hour in Augusta, they're now relegated to utter irrelevance. Sure, they might have added a few seats in the House, but their overall position is weaker because Mills no longer faces the prospect of re-election. Moreover, the threat of Republican gains two years from now is laughable. Why should Democrats fear a Republican operation that failed to defend Lewisont-Auburn or send [Troy Jackson](https://substack.com/redirect/41213f2a-a1e6-43ad-a3fc-15f1b0f9c7c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to early retirement? Mills could reverse course on her campaign promises, hike the income tax to 10 percent, encircle Swan's Island with offshore windmills, legalize fourth trimester abortion, and put a Planned Parenthood in every county, and I'm not sure Republicans in Augusta would be able to win majorities two years from now.
The dwindling few Republicans who will inhabit the State House this next legislative session need a clean slate. Otherwise, they might as well spare taxpayers the per diem and stay at home. Anyone remotely connected to the old leadership must step back and allow a new generation of conservatives to lead the party. This includes staffers in the House and Senate GOP offices, if any are left once the new class of Democrats gets done cutting minority staff positions. I know the talent pool for Republican operatives is shallow in Maine, but we're at rock bottom here. Hire away a couple of Denny's workers and some College Republicans - anyone who hasn't been infected with that beaten-dog loser mentality so characteristic of Republicans in Augusta.
As for new leadership, placing young, media savvy, strategically minded conservatives in charge is the only possible path to becoming relevant again. The only bargaining chip Republican lawmakers will have this session is the potential to allow Mills and Democratic leadership to tout some awful piece of legislation as "bipartisan." It's not much, but it's all they have. And that chip should be jealously guarded by a unified minority. You're not going to get a unified minority with 60-year-old Bush Republicans who like to dine with Pharma lobbyists at the Senator Inn. The time of the Baby Boomer Republican is over; we're reaping the fruit of their happy-go-lucky incompetence now. It's time for them to step aside. Young conservatives and libertarians ought to demand it.
## CONGRESSIONAL RACES
Former Rep. Bruce Poliquin is a victim of his own success. Unlike most Members of Congress, including Rep. Chellie Pingree, Poliquin never used his office to enrich himself. Quite the contrary. The man has spent oodles of his own money trying to put himself in a place where his boundless energy might serve the public good. He's had an extraordinary career, and I truly believe his heart, like LePage's, is in the right place. But he wasn't the right fit for the Second Congressional District this time around. The Poliquin campaign understood that, perhaps, and tried to bind him publicly with LePage, but that strategy sank for reasons already mentioned.
For all his flaws, Rep. Jared Golden fits the blue-collar identity of the district much better. And Golden has smartly avoided - or been allowed to avoid - casting votes in favor of unpopular Democratic policies. Also, I don't know if you heard, but he has tattoos. Two years from now, Maine Republicans ought to find a non-political candidate with private sector experience within in the district. A blue-collar conservative with solid roots in a northern Maine community would present a formidable challenge to a back-bench Michaud clone whose only accomplishment is sprinting away for his own president's policies.
In the First Congressional District, there's really nothing to say. Ed Thelander made a solid effort against a crusty multi-millionaire incumbent with deep ties to progressive donor network. Compounding Thelander's disadvantages is a Portland-based media that is so hopelessly incapable of disinterested neutrality that no reporter ever mentioned Pingree still happens to be receiving up to a million dollars a year from Paloma Partners, her billionaire ex-husband S. Donald Sussman's hedge fund. You think a Republican with that on his [financial disclosure](https://substack.com/redirect/41213f2a-a1e6-43ad-a3fc-15f1b0f9c7c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) would have skated? Only if, as I suspect, there aren't any reporters in Maine capable of finding financial disclosures.
The first district is no place for a conservative. Indeed, Thelander would probably have fared better in greater Portland if he were a former performer at those "family friendly" drag shows rather than a former Navy Seal. A serious country would have welcomed a man of his stature and seriousness, but alas we are not living in one. Next time around, perhaps Mrs. Thelander should take a run and see whether a charismatic conservative Venezuelan immigrant can strike a chord in Northern Massachusetts.
## WHERE TO NOW?
Any Republican - and especially a conservative Republican - enters Maine politics at a serious disadvantage because of a political philosophy that effectively prevents him from leveraging the Nanny State to buy off voters. Not so for Mills and Democratic lawmakers. Mills sprinkled taxpayer money on every favored constituency like she was Whitey Bulger buying groceries for housewives in South Boston. She paid off electricity bills for small businesses and non-profits. She doled out 850 bucks to every Mainer. She funneled cash by the truckload into the sprawling web of non-profits that mostly exists to keep term-limited Democrats employed. She gave some cash to the Lobsterman's Association, to childcare providers, to college kids, to the poor and the not poor. Everyone got money from Janet Mills this year. Of course, it wasn't her money, not even money she'd accumulated by careful stewardship of the state. It was all debt-financed imaginary money handed out by a delusional federal government. The bill for all of that will come due - and soon. But none of that matters when you're trying to win an election.
The point is, all of that vote buying didn't happen overnight. It was planned months, even years ago, built into the legislative plans of Augusta Democrats and coordinated to arrive right around Election Day. An example: The Democrats planned all along to send out those inflation payments with a campaign-style letter from Mills. Republicans feared this might happen, but rather than make a fuss and demand faster electronic payments, they accepted a pinky promise from some hack commissioner in the Mills Administration that they wouldn't do exactly what they did. Republicans got snowed, plain and simple. And that wasn't the only example of Republican lawmakers obliviously allowing Democrats to build policy easter eggs that materialized come election season.
You can call the Democrats whatever you want, but you can't call them stupid - at least not when it comes to using other peoples' money to entrench their political power. Thanks to Republican weakness in the State Legislature, conservatives can do next to nothing to stop Democrats from creating the next round of constituency payoffs. The only thing they can do is adopt an aggressive public relations strategy aimed at explaining in simple terms to the Maine people precisely what is happening, as it's happening. Every Republican lawmaker must now become an investigative reporter and a social media expert. All twelve or thirteen of them should adopt AOC-style approaches to naming and shaming their colleagues when they push progressive proposals will make us poorer and less free. It's asking for a lot of aggression and ingenuity from a typically frightened bunch, I know. But Maine Republicans will not win a vote in the next two years. All they can hope to do is win in the court of public opinion.
Another structural disadvantage Maine Republicans have is turnout operation. It's too early to say exactly what went wrong in a practical sense, but LePage seriously underperformed his 2014 re-election bid. In deeply conservative areas of the State, areas LePage won with 10 percent or more of the vote in 2014, he only won yesterday by 8 percent. Mills, in contrast, grew her strongholds. In towns she won by 10 percent or more in 2018, she won by more than 30 points! And while Mills more than doubled LePage's vote count in the top largest 15 towns by population, LePage barely squeaked out an advantage in Maine's smallest rural towns.
The Maine Democrats were very effective at securing turn out in their few rural strongholds, but devastatingly so in the major cities. Part of that is the student vote. At Bowdoin College, and I'm sure at the other less prestigious colleges in Maine, college busses ran all day long dragging radicalized young liberals from out of state to the polls. Maine Republicans can do little to compete with the college student vote. And turning out geographically distributed rural voters is much harder than organizing in cities. But something must be done. A good start would be nuking the unwise Republican resistance to early voting and mail-in voting.
Republicans have always favored day-of voting, but President Donald Trump's attack on mail-in voting in 2020 really solidified an unhelpful decision to eschew early voting. If a Republican donor wanted to make a substantial difference in future state elections, he should consider making a large donation only on the condition that it be used to construct an elite early voting and mail-in voting apparatus.
Voting in modern elections now takes place over several weeks. Conservatives may not like it, it may open the door for fraud and bureaucratic shenanigans, but it's a reality. These are the rules and this is the playing field. If Republicans want to win, they must show up early, not just on game day.

## HAPPY NOTES
Ethan Strimling's band of socialists lost in Portland. Quite convincingly, too. The socialist ballot initiatives to hike the minimum wage to $18 per hour and effectively ban most low-margin businesses from the city failed. Two proposals to reduce short-term rentals and impose harsh regulations on them failed. The one socialist victory came on "tenant protections" a.k.a. rent controls. In the name of making Portland a more livable city, the socialists have effectively guaranteed that landlords will refrain from making investments in upkeep, thereby transforming middle- and lower-income neighborhoods into shabby slums. The results aren't great for Portland, but conservatives can take solace in knowing that at least one right-of-center campaign - "Enough is Enough" - managed to put up competent resistance to harmful policies. The socialists will return next year - what _else_ do they have to do? But the lesson Portland's "Enough is Enough" campaign teaches is that businesses can crush these asinine ideas if they bind together, make investments in effective campaigns, and refuse to compromise with ideological children.

At the same time, Mills added 30,000 voters from her last election. That's mandate territory. Just disastrous for Republicans. Yes, LePage was a fantastic conservative governor whose policies made life better for everyone in the state, except for the parasitic political class. Mills ruined lives and livelihoods by shutting down Maine's economy, and she pilfered taxpayer funds to buy off every constituency in the state. LePage had more right to be angry with her than he did with Libby Mitchell or Mike Michaud. But we saw no righteous indignation this cycle. When the old LePage did come out in the debates, he awkwardly accused Mills of lying, often without an explanation. The campaign website, JanetMillsLied.com, felt like an unnatural act of desperation, which is saying something coming from the guy who wrote half the articles to which the site links. Even good policies can be poorly messaged. LePage told us about the threat that Maine farmland would soon be colonized with solar panels. We heard that Maine's pension fund reversing the decision to divest from oil and natural gas companies - less than a drop in the bucket of global finance - would somehow fight inflation. Sure, solar subsidies create malinvestment and ESG pension funds drive up energy costs, but these are not issues that resonate with voters. The only explanation for this is some pollster told a consultant Mills' pandemic policies had broad support in Maine. Everyone in Maine suffered because of Mills' bumbling, authoritarian approach to managing the pandemic - she was the anti-thesis of - but LePage left that point unmade. The playbook Virginia Gov. Glen Youngkin used to win office in 2021 was served up on a silver platter. Let the chattering classes chew on that for a few cycles rather than dissecting the twelfth iteration of his abortion stance. name: Sarah McBride
subject: Thank you
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
The race has been called, and thanks to you, I’m heading back to Congress to keep fighting for Delaware! 💛
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=4115%2E21716%2EQeHeco)
Hi — it's Sarah McBride!
**The race has been called, and thanks to you, I’m heading back to Congress to keep fighting for Delaware! 💛**
Two years ago, Delawareans entrusted me with the awesome responsibility of representing our state in the United States House of Representatives. Serving you in Congress has been the privilege of a lifetime.
And tonight, despite the forces of destruction and division that too often plague our politics, Delawareans have once again chosen hope over hate, grace over greed, and faith over fear.
The last two years have certainly been long. Together, we’ve defended health care for sick patients and food for hungry families. We’ve fought back against the corruption of the powerful and the coldness of those who would unleash unrestrained technologies that leave the rich richer and everyone else behind. We’ve defended our neighbors from attacks on their rights and the lawlessness of a masked force. And together, we’ve faced down the pettiness of politicians who seek to use their constituents — and their colleagues — as political pawns in an attempt to get attention.
All of us have had a front row seat to it when we open our social media or turn on our TVs. But one of the great privileges of this office is that I also have another vantage point. Yes, I hear the loud few who fill our feeds with toxicity and cruelty, but I also get to see, that while real disagreements exist, we are not as divided as the algorithms make it seem. That people are good and decent and kind.
That is the Delaware I know. That is the Delaware I love. And thanks to your votes and your values, that is the state that I will continue to serve in the United States House of Representatives.
Today, we celebrate our wins here in Delaware. And while the night is still young, it looks like we will be able to celebrate wins across this country, including a Democratic majority in the United States Congress.
**And as we celebrate tonight, we know that the hard work of a new beginning starts tomorrow.**
Throughout this campaign, I spoke of the fundamental choice that our country has had to make at every inflection point between destroyers and builders.
And through an outstretched hand within a voting booth and with open arms toward your fellow citizens — joining together with a chorus of millions across this country — you have chosen to build a more perfect union. You have chosen to summon the better angels of our nation and to build a better future for our country.
While that work won’t be completed in a single Congress, those of us entrusted with the responsibility of leadership in this moment must meet it with urgency and boldness — to build a politics of trust and hope, of accountability and aspiration. To build a health care system where every patient can get the care they need. To build a cradle-through-career support structure with paid leave, universal child care, and strong public schools so that it’s actually affordable to start a family again. To build an economy of the future that guarantees that the new prosperity unleashed by new technologies is shared by the many and not just the few. To build a government that sees and respects all of us.
**And to build a tomorrow that is different — and better — than today.**
Thank you, God Bless You, and God Bless the Great State of Delaware.
Sarah McBride

We’ve fought back against the corruption of the powerful and the coldness of those who would unleash unrestrained technologies that leave the rich richer and everyone else behind. We’ve defended our neighbors from attacks on their rights and the lawlessness of a masked force. And together, we’ve faced down the pettiness of politicians who seek to use their constituents — and their colleagues — as political pawns in an attempt to get attention. All of us have had a front row seat to it when we open our social media or turn on our TVs. But one of the great privileges of this office is that I also have another vantage point. Yes, I hear the loud few who fill our feeds with toxicity and cruelty, but I also get to see, that while real disagreements exist, we are not as divided as the algorithms make it seem. That people are good and decent and kind. That is the Delaware I know. That is the Delaware I love. And thanks to your votes and your values, that is the state that I will continue to serve in the United States House of Representatives. Today, we celebrate our wins here in Delaware. And while the night is still young, it looks like we will be able to celebrate wins across this country, including a Democratic majority in the United States Congress. And as we celebrate tonight, we know that the hard work of a new beginning starts tomorrow. Throughout this campaign, I spoke of the fundamental choice that our country has had to make at every inflection point between destroyers and builders. And through an outstretched hand within a voting booth and with open arms toward your fellow citizens — joining together with a chorus of millions across this country — you have chosen to build a more perfect union. You have chosen to summon the better angels of our nation and to build a better future for our country. While that work won’t be completed in a single Congress, those of us entrusted with the responsibility of leadership in this moment must meet it with urgency and boldness — to build a politics of trust and hope, of accountability and aspiration. To build a health care system where every patient can get the care they need. To build a cradle-through-career support structure with paid leave, universal child care, and strong public schools so that it’s actually affordable to start a family again. To build an economy of the future that guarantees that the new prosperity unleashed by new technologies is shared by the many and not just the few. To build a government that sees and respects all of us. And to build a tomorrow that is different — and better — than today. Thank you, God Bless You, and God Bless the Great State of Delaware. Sarah McBride

| | | Friends, We did it. And I couldn't be more thankful to have had you by my side in this fight. As you're reading this, I'm taking the stage in Vancouver to deliver my victory speech. But before I celebrate with the people gathered here in Southwest Washington tonight, I wanted to take a moment to thank you personally. This has been a long, grueling race. Donald Trump, Mike Johnson, and the national Republican establishment poured millions upon millions of dollars into Southwest Washington to defeat us. With your help, we overcame the largest spending gap of any House race in the country. They wanted this seat back badly, because when a Democrat who lives on a dirt road, runs an auto repair shop, and refuses to take her marching orders from either party can win in a district Donald Trump carried three times, it threatens the Republican monopoly on rural America. They flooded our airwaves with attack ads, convinced that if they spent enough money, they could replace an independent voice with someone who would fall in line. But they fundamentally misunderstood the people of Southwest Washington. They thought this seat was theirs to buy. You showed them it wasn't. You knocked on doors in the rain, made phone calls, talked to your neighbors, chipped in what you could, and put your name alongside mine. That is something I will never take lightly. This victory belongs to all of us. When I first ran for Congress, I was a mom and an auto shop owner who was tired of seeing working people and rural communities treated like an afterthought. I believed then, as I do now, that ordinary people deserve a voice in Congress: that people who work with their hands, raise families, and struggle to make ends meet deserve a seat at the table where decisions about our lives are made. I never imagined just how many of you would stand beside me to make that possible. And now, you've given me another chance to carry those voices to Washington. Every time I walk into the Capitol, I remember where I come from and who sent me there. My loyalty has always been to this place and the people who call it home, and that's what will continue to guide my work. There's a long road ahead of us. But tonight, I am profoundly grateful for what we've built together, for the faith you've placed in me, and for the opportunity to keep fighting alongside you.

Sincerely, profoundly, thank you. Marie

In these historic midterm elections, Californians have made their voices heard in record numbers.
---
**It’s been the honor of a lifetime to serve as your Attorney General, and tonight I am humbled to have earned your trust for a second term! ** Thank you, from the bottom of my heart, for the opportunity to continue working for you and for the millions of Californians who call this great state home, taking on the bullies and holding the powerful accountable. I believe in this state and all of its promises. California represents so much of what makes America great, and that is exactly why Donald Trump has made us his primary target. In 21 months, we’ve taken Trump to court more than 100 times. A hundred times we stood up and told the bully: NO. All the while, he has escalated his attacks on our elections, our democracy, and our communities, all to protect his interests, enrich himself, and hand more power and influence to corporations and billionaires. _If Trump wants to stop losing in court, he should stop breaking the law._ We’ve defended birthright citizenship, blocked attacks on voters’ rights, and challenged his sweeping tariffs until the Supreme Court ruled them illegal. We delivered victory after victory for California’s families, workers, small businesses, and immigrant communities. This president has tried to silence us because he is afraid of what might happen if we use the tools of our democracy to take our power back. Tonight, California, you used it. My parents knew what that vote was worth. When I was just two months old, a dictator rose to power in the Philippines, so my parents brought our family to Los Angeles to raise their kids in a country with civil rights, voting rights, and democracy. It’s not lost on me that five decades later, it’s my job to protect and defend California and all those who call the Golden State home. The next few years will surely bring new challenges and tough fights. There’s no doubt in my mind that we’ll continue to face relentless attacks from the Trump administration, escalating corporate greed, and rising costs. But I’m committed to doing whatever it takes to defend our rights, our freedoms, and our values. I’ll keep fighting to stop the unlawful power grabs from the federal government, defend our immigrant communities, protect reproductive freedom, safeguard our environment, hold greedy corporations accountable, keep our communities safe from gun violence and drug trafficking, and stand up to abuse of power wherever it appears. And I’m heartened that we’ll face it together. We are at our strongest against the rising tides of tyranny when we stand united, each of us clear-eyed and committed to the roles we must play. When we fight together, we win together — and together, we secure the California dream for the next generation. Thank you for everything. —Rob

| | I am honored that my friends and neighbors in Northwest Washington have sent me back to D.C. to fight for them. Thank you for participating in our safe and secure election. **My message is simple: Affordability for you. Accountability for the President and his cronies.** I will also continue to bring investments home to Northwest Washington, combat fentanyl in our communities, protect reproductive freedom, and support our veterans. **The House Democrats have secured a majority.** Within the majority, my job will be to ensure Democrats are laser-focused on lowering costs for working families across America, which includes reversing the cost-raising tariffs, ending the war in Iran, and reining in the Trump administration. **Families in Northwest Washington need relief, and I will work within the majority to deliver results.** **Thank you to those who joined my campaign and knocked 31,000+ doors, called 100,000+ voters, and cast a ballot to support my grassroots campaign**. My campaign has reached tens of thousands of voters all across Northwest Washington, and my win would not be possible without their support. Thank you to my spouse, Tiia, for her constant support. My work for our community would not be possible without her. Thank you to my dedicated and hardworking staff and interns who worked day in and day out to reach voters and kept my campaign on track every day. **Thank you to everyone who made tonight's results possible.** It is an honor to represent the 2nd District, and I will fight to lower your costs and hold the Trump administration accountable for its corruption. Tonight, Frontline Member and Democratic nominee Derek Tran declared victory in California’s 45th Congressional District

| | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**

Tuesday, November 3, 2026Contact: [Christian Figueroa](mailto:christian@derektranforcongress.com)
---
| |
**Derek Tran Wins Historic Reelection Campaign in California’s 45th Congressional District**
---
| |
**Garden Grove, CA –** Tonight, Frontline Member and Democratic nominee Derek Tran declared victory in California’s 45th Congressional District. Tran released the following statement:
**“I am humbled that our community has placed their trust in me again to represent them. This win belongs to all of us: to those who knocked on a door, made a call, and believed in what we could accomplish together, and to the families who believed that the promise of the American Dream should be a reality for all.**
**“Fifty-one years ago, my parents fled Vietnam as democracy crumbled. They immigrated to the U.S. and found themselves here, in Southern California. Today, their son represents the largest Vietnamese diaspora in Congress. That is the legacy I carry with me. And tonight, our community has given me the honor of carrying it forward.**
**“I do not take this responsibility lightly. Congress must be focused on lowering costs, protecting affordable healthcare, and rooting out corruption from this Administration. There’s more to do, and now, we’re going to build on what we’ve done. Let’s get back to work.”**
CA-45 is one of the most competitive House seats in the country, critical to securing a Democratic House majority.
---
| | ###
_The son of refugees who worked hard and sacrificed for the American Dream, Congressman Derek Tran joined the Army at 18 to give back to the country that has given him so much. Wanting to continue his career in public service, he ran in California's 45th district to put people ahead of politics and protect democracy, and won. Now, he's running again to ensure everyone no matter what neighborhood they come from has the opportunity to succeed without fear of their freedoms being taken away._
_California’s 45th Congressional District remains one of the most contested battleground races in the country. Last cycle, Derek Tran flipped the seat by just over 600 votes (a 0.2% margin) in the second-closest and most expensive House race ($46 million spent) in the country. A majority-minority district, the District has the third largest AAPI population (41%) of any Congressional District, is 28% Latino, and is home to the largest Vietnamese community in the country. Following Proposition 50, this district brings in over 15,000 new Hispanic voters and over 7,000 new Vietnamese voters, and has a DPI of 52.8%._ _It includes all or part of the cities of Garden Grove, Westminster, Fountain Valley, Cerritos, Buena Park, Placentia, Hawaiian Gardens, Cypress, Artesia, Los Alamitos, La Palma, Norwalk, Stanton, Lakewood, Santa Ana, Seal Beach, and Fullerton, as well as the unincorporated community of Midway City._

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: I am humbled to be your next Governor of Texas
body:
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
I am grateful and in awe of the incredible grace and power of God and of Texas.
**Texas, I am humbled to be your next Governor.**
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261103_6_results.fj0YWE&refcode=em20261104-2645&amount=5&t=1&akid=2645%2E299639%2Eb674zZ)
When we started this campaign a little over a year ago, I asked a simple question:
Does Texas belong to the people of Texas: who live here, who work here, who raise their families here? Or is this the billionaires' world and the rest of us just live here?
Does Texas belong to parents and their children, or the billionaires trying to dismantle our schools?
Does Texas belong to the farmers and ranchers who have worked this land for generations, or the corporations buying it up?
Does Texas belong to the working families who pay their taxes, and do everything right, or the wealthy and well-connected who play by different rules?
Does Texas belong to the people who rise before the sun, who work two jobs, and who put everything they have into small businesses and big dreams? Or does it belong to the people who write the biggest checks to politicians?
**Tonight, Texas answered. And we didn't whisper.** We answered loud enough for every billionaire, every lobbyist, and every corrupt politician in Austin to hear.
_Texas belongs to us._
We answered in McAllen and Corpus Christi. Dallas and in Temple. In San Antonio and Lubbock. From the neighborhoods of Austin to the wide-open skies of West Texas, all the way out to Big Bend.
We answered in our big cities, where they tried to silence your voice with gerrymandered maps and closed polling sites only to see turnout like never before, and you answered in small towns, where people had been told their vote was already spoken for.
We answered in communities that politicians visit every four years to ask for your vote, only to forget about you the minute they get to Austin.
We answered in places that have been overlooked, underestimated, and left behind for far too long. And we answered across party lines.

body:
You are why I’m in this work, and you’re why we can succeed.| | | |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142855042/658306580/-642992695?refcode=261103em_sjj_victory&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1YWUzNTBkMS0xNmQ4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FiRvtDlq3EfDoKdCHnxID6P2gy1eYkqgyRtcHnFoh10=)
