Hi friends, **I’m incredibly honored to have been re-elected to Congress for a fourth term, and so grateful for the trust you’ve placed in me!** From longtime neighbors in La Mesa, Lemon Grove, and El Cajon to new constituents in Julian and Rancho San Diego, I am so proud to represent all of the communities that make up California’s 51st District. And whether you voted for me, voted for someone else, or didn't vote at all, I will work every day to make sure your voice is heard in Congress. While I am _so_ excited to continue serving my community, this win is really not about me — it’s about the hundreds of thousands of people in San Diego and the millions more around the country who stood up and demanded better from their government. To say the past two years have been challenging would be an understatement in the extreme. We've seen obscene, unprecedented corruption from Donald Trump and his inner circle. We've watched in horror as federal immigration officers occupy our streets and terrorize our neighbors. We've seen bombs dropped abroad in our name, costs at home skyrocketing — and congressional Republicans more concerned with pleasing their audience of one than working for their constituents. **With record-high turnout and amazing victories rolling in across the country, Americans delivered a clear message today: We’re ready for change.** We broke the dangerous GOP trifecta. We defeated extremists who sought to divide our country and turn neighbors against each other. And we secured a Democratic majority in the House (AND in the Senate)! We elected leaders with real plans to build a stronger, brighter future that Americans can actually afford. There will be plenty more hard fights and tough days ahead, but Democrats have spent the past two years getting ready for this moment, and we are diving in head first to get our country back on track. We have some big, daunting challenges: making it easier to find and afford child care, housing, and health care. Dismantling and overhauling ICE and centering humanity in our immigration system. Putting guardrails on AI, protecting our fundamental rights and freedoms, and pursuing a foreign policy that upholds our values and looks to the future, not the past. But solving big, daunting challenges is exactly what we were elected to do — I’m ready, and eager to get to work. It's also incredibly important to me that we rebuild trust with the people who feel government has let them down or left them behind._If you're sick and tired of our broken politics and don't have faith in either party to fight for you, I hear you._ I will do everything in my power to prove that government can still deliver real solutions to the problems you're facing. I promise to keep showing up, listening, and being honest with you, even when we disagree. And I'll work every day to earn and live up to the trust you've placed in me. Thank you again for everything you’ve done for me and for Democrats this year. Onward! —Sara

I would like to first thank you.
You believed in this campaign, this people-powered movement.
Even though we started months late against an incumbent with near-limitless cash to spend against us, you _invested_ in the idea that working-class Mainers, not billionaires or corporations, deserved a seat at the table.
**This campaign was never about me. It was about the worker who can 't afford diesel for his truck, the family choosing between groceries and prescriptions, the kid who wants to build a life here without leaving the state to do it.**
That's who I'm going to Washington to fight for, and I won't forget it for a second.
There's a lot of work ahead. But tonight, I want to say thank you. From the bottom of my heart.
Solidarity forever,
Troy Jackson
**P.S. This fight is just beginning, and when I get to D.C., the corporate interests that spent millions trying to stop us aren 't going away. They'll be lobbying from day one, and they'll be trying to stunt this movement.**
I want to walk into the Senate with the same thing that got me here: a grassroots movement that answers to working people, not big donors.

clean_body: I am beyond grateful, and ready to get to work. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more I am beyond grateful, and ready to get to work. | | | Nov 4 | | | | | | | | | | Folks, it is the honor and privilege of a lifetime to be your Senator-Elect to serve the great state of Maine. | | ---|---|--- I would like to first thank you. You believed in this campaign, this people-powered movement. Even though we started months late against an incumbent with near-limitless cash to spend against us, you invested in the idea that working-class Mainers, not billionaires or corporations, deserved a seat at the table. This campaign was never about me. It was about the worker who can 't afford diesel for his truck, the family choosing between groceries and prescriptions, the kid who wants to build a life here without leaving the state to do it. That's who I'm going to Washington to fight for, and I won't forget it for a second. There's a lot of work ahead. But tonight, I want to say thank you. From the bottom of my heart. Solidarity forever, Troy Jackson P.S. This fight is just beginning, and when I get to D.C., the corporate interests that spent millions trying to stop us aren 't going away. They'll be lobbying from day one, and they'll be trying to stunt this movement. I want to walk into the Senate with the same thing that got me here: a grassroots movement that answers to working people, not big donors. | | | | | (C) 2026 Troy Jackson 548 Market Street PMB 72296, San Francisco, CA 94104 ? ?

body:
| | | Pundits will spend all week trying to name what’s happening tonight. We’ll save them the trouble:**** this isn’t just a wave, Peter. _It’s a tectonic shift._ **Democrats have taken control of both the House and the Senate, and so far, dozens of our Working Families Slate champions are heading to the Congress.** Some of our biggest races are still too early to call, including the Senate race for **Abdul El-Sayed** in Michigan, but the night has already delivered a stinging rebuke of Trump and the Republican agenda, and the corporate politics that have failed working families for decades. Elon Musk and Donald Trump threw more than $800 million at this election to hold onto far-right control of Congress. **It wasn’t enough.** They had the money, the power, and the most powerful people in the U.S. on their side. We had volunteers knocking doors through winter snow and summer heat, and we outworked _every_ dollar they spent. Tonight, working people sent a new class of champions to Congress, and the billionaires couldn’t stop us. Come January, our champions will be fighting for lower costs, affordable healthcare, and an economy that works for all of us. **Let’s make sure they have a movement behind them.** [**Celebrate every Working Families Party champion headed to Congress by becoming a dues-paying WFP member with a recurring monthly donation of $10 or more.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9nokhzqiraQg6eXCFVZPjSL73_35wldRVl2wDZQ5X8tbF9vFwIZfyozqqH8UeY58_7mEf4y_qGzzr_Ba1naj30Q_DY_8HgrEUhTJQOSIJMi7Lk3JcpikEblJeqzx8jJZrDzlCqKghvyUmAn8EdUKXej2cX4GV_XvKYWusWRT94UUSC8yEq4nopPu1hPfG6A3M8L-isjeexwXTwAv9FofafgFJ_C2jv_4yPUKSwh_CGt3diuVHxzV28V6HjxcTxj-zQ192BuVxfuLbmrHf0zULGehr42mmEByOIyvvsJ6hNpAwEGLSn4MNSf37uI5hKniw45skmOK7lNMgoy55SIE-zg/4vg/SP8veKDlR4SfsqBI51WMZQ/h0/h001.1t2vHAahdhGIMqjAcTBQQkaKaATNJXa_YW4yWrOy_VE) **[Become a WFP member »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9nokhzqiraQg6eXCFVZPjSL73_35wldRVl2wDZQ5X8tbF9vFwIZfyozqqH8UeY58_7mEf4y_qGzzr_Ba1naj30ZPY1CItPkUp-Mx3FAR4SUCf55GAvTkR1NB8O-KdbWleXGI_30FS_M4e94eIzMHjDfDQszYqk5FSKpBAznibkAV9NiNAbAlaKs8IATcAE8h23DS_Oz434sS0HQ6SWRv-hWE9eusv3NLblxxveW66tUo1QSnr0ZEww2paMYMzEUwF0EeohWagX5aXdM5W_gqglz0ob_Qc_agP15s3W5Gv_JCX6p8A_upj12NY49xxrtAR2N5-T64daWBSBh9Davz8fA/4vg/SP8veKDlR4SfsqBI51WMZQ/h1/h001.xB_8mW676Twv4IOqwwRy-L1EeOynr_E_F8PKToqp0sU)** Results are still rolling in, and every update brings more good news. One of the biggest came out of Maine, where logger and union member **Troy Jackson** just defeated Republican Senator Susan Collins, ending her nearly 30-year run in the Senate and winning a seat Democrats haven’t held since 1988. And as House races are called across the country, some of the boldest WFP champions are making history:
* One of our first wins of the night came from one of our own: former New Jersey WFP state director **Analilia Mejia** (NJ-11). After winning an April special election for the House seat Mikie Sherrill left to become governor, she powered through a second hard-fought race and won a _full_ term in Congress tonight.
* In **Pennsylvania** , firefighter **Bob Brooks** (PA-07) just knocked off Republican Congressman Ryan Mackenzie, even with Trump pouring money into the race to save him. And in Philadelphia, **Chris Rabb** (PA-03), who took down the Democratic machine in his primary this spring, is officially headed to Congress.
* In **Ohio** , union ironworker **Brian Poindexter** (OH-07) is sending Max Miller, a former Trump aide and real estate heir, packing.
* **Michigan** isn’t finished, either. In Detroit, union organizer **Donavan McKinney** (MI-13), who toppled a multimillionaire incumbent in August, just sealed his win and is headed to Washington.
* In **Colorado** , **Melat Kiros** (CO-01), who made national headlines this year when she defeated a 30-year incumbent in her primary, is Denver’s next member of Congress.
* In **California** , teacher and longtime WFP member and leader **Randy Villegas** (CA-22) defeated David Valadao, who voted to gut Medicaid and to give ICE $38 million with no additional oversight.
* **New York** is sending a whole new class of fighters to Washington. Longtime WFP champion **Brad Lander** (NY-10), who was arrested by ICE last year while defending immigrant New Yorkers’ right to due process, is headed to Congress. Union organizer **Claire Valdez** (NY-07) will succeed Nydia Velazquez, while community organizer **Darializa Avila Chevalier** (NY-13), who unseated a five-term incumbent this summer, will represent Upper Manhattan.

These wins are just the beginning, and more races are still being counted across the country, including**Will Lawrence**(MI-07) in Michigan and four more WFP challengers in California:**Mai Vang**(CA-07),**Aisha Wahab**(CA-14),**Connie Chan**(CA-11), and**Angela Gonzales-Torres**(CA-34). [**For now, celebrate the biggest election night working people have had in years: become a dues-paying WFP member with a recurring monthly donation of $10 or more, and help us take this fight all the way to the White House in 2028.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9nokhzqiraQg6eXCFVZPjSL73_35wldRVl2wDZQ5X8tbF9vFwIZfyozqqH8UeY58_7mEf4y_qGzzr_Ba1naj30bY9ij5g0WBqPteYYVPkN62_wsD1i_Sq9j24LosRZQPHSQtVlj1IGMakjRZrEUeiRS8wFDNvqkqbVCXpxLZmO-xvjRASmlp4RQBz2gNFKoMfALZU10XzH7rCeKxew-uFuxozh5P_jnVkP9Er47WqODx-51NErQ3w6eTaYEutJSKT-DAdRL8Vvc_cO2oJgee0Yy6JgnQqofmUEDGjQMKvsQx7BTf1FfaSH8gAt6uOw3Fk5lGC2xMuCLItBgbcqOjFjg/4vg/SP8veKDlR4SfsqBI51WMZQ/h2/h001.Lv3cBIIkWaFWm8rk6DH8B4EPK22MGBPrheBBROcbqt4) **[Become a WFP member](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9nokhzqiraQg6eXCFVZPjSL73_35wldRVl2wDZQ5X8tbF9vFwIZfyozqqH8UeY58_7mEf4y_qGzzr_Ba1naj30VS4kFL-M88vPhBYbWVZ9y5BEzMVjL8dYB9IOFy7vMAyM3PH4Y2FDN_QoT00mxi56-sqawq-8ImodQ8UTtYQKy82DCsH-uc0vMA8o1269XuCJFMp2JGR16qk_nb-uREX2R5a1Q5ojwzOd4OrNcHxb75L02kNvtDWm5QqUWdHAScWT5nNUhmunQZOP_Y3yaRa1gm67fKtAEnqT065A-1M0nfiNCbH1KriqXYNd7cm19ogYOiLF9tMovsjufUkdt5uhA/4vg/SP8veKDlR4SfsqBI51WMZQ/h3/h001.tjbZbBsNGTmzGPeMtJDxHS1fKRa2rie0yEMvizIaxgk)** **This night was years in the making, Peter.** Trump promised to lower the cost of living. Instead he delivered _chaos_ , _war_ , and _rising costs_ , while his billionaire backers collected tax breaks and friendly regulators. Tonight, those broken promises came due, and voters sent Trump a clear message: you don’t get to _lie_ to working families and keep your majority. **He wasn’t the only one who got a message, though.** All cycle long, the corporate wing of the Democratic Party said candidates like ours couldn’t win. They said the only path to victory ran through _milquetoast_ moderates who promise _nothing_ and stand for even less. Then they spent millions in our primaries to make sure voters never got a real choice. It didn’t work. Voters chose every one of our priority congressional champions anyway. **And tonight, they did it again.** Trump and Musk poured more than $800 million into these midterms, much of it in the final months, and our candidates still won in exactly the places the corporate wing said they’d lose. So to every Democrat already eyeing a future run: **the path in 2028 runs through the Working Families Guarantee — a home you can afford, health care you can rely on, a good job to support your family, and childcare when and where you need it.** _That’s_ the agenda that won tonight. **And it won because of you, Peter.** Every one of the more than **30 million** calls, texts, and door knocks since January came from people who believed working families deserve better, and who gave their evenings, their weekends, and whatever they could spare to prove it. **That’s what our movement runs on. It’s what got us here tonight, and it’s what will carry us into 2027 and 2028.** [**Become a dues-paying WFP member with a recurring monthly donation of $10 or more to keep this movement growing, and make the Working Families Guarantee the agenda that wins in 2028.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9nokhzqiraQg6eXCFVZPjSL73_35wldRVl2wDZQ5X8tbF9vFwIZfyozqqH8UeY58_7mEf4y_qGzzr_Ba1naj30UYaoJg4ayDLRMNSdlI_WKFxO6zNyy8TZWuRkeZd2r_HaxYz1TxiKcTrahTsFFTL8RecrE_i7pUh8kI083tXJ6DcCih9Z0COhmf8qAjtb2RIRRC6Ulm3VDep3VfsRBZJaA6C6iAlpCjUWzLvEG5VAJjsWfOtWxD1KTaKiVtMGEOjGStCpU2KHJUpA_-OavUgxCA-5Z_nsZFSVw6tpxza4SP496VM-iqbfpdzreC3Ye0oZ0A2Nu0DUAilFhgJikNJAQ/4vg/SP8veKDlR4SfsqBI51WMZQ/h4/h001.8OR3qpIjVfhvy9cub7unnW5gwyUZcmoAChF6iUPDR-o) Thank you for everything you did to make tonight possible, Peter. clean_body: | | | Pundits will spend all week trying to name what’s happening tonight. We’ll save them the trouble:** this isn’t just a wave, Peter. It’s a tectonic shift. Democrats have taken control of both the House and the Senate, and so far, dozens of our Working Families Slate champions are heading to the Congress. Some of our biggest races are still too early to call, including the Senate race for Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, but the night has already delivered a stinging rebuke of Trump and the Republican agenda, and the corporate politics that have failed working families for decades. Elon Musk and Donald Trump threw more than $800 million at this election to hold onto far-right control of Congress. It wasn’t enough. They had the money, the power, and the most powerful people in the U.S. on their side. We had volunteers knocking doors through winter snow and summer heat, and we outworked every dollar they spent. Tonight, working people sent a new class of champions to Congress, and the billionaires couldn’t stop us. Come January, our champions will be fighting for lower costs, affordable healthcare, and an economy that works for all of us. Let’s make sure they have a movement behind them. Results are still rolling in, and every update brings more good news. One of the biggest came out of Maine, where logger and union member Troy Jackson just defeated Republican Senator Susan Collins, ending her nearly 30-year run in the Senate and winning a seat Democrats haven’t held since 1988. And as House races are called across the country, some of the boldest WFP champions are making history: One of our first wins of the night came from one of our own: former New Jersey WFP state director Analilia Mejia (NJ-11). After winning an April special election for the House seat Mikie Sherrill left to become governor, she powered through a second hard-fought race and won a full term in Congress tonight. In Pennsylvania , firefighter Bob Brooks (PA-07) just knocked off Republican Congressman Ryan Mackenzie, even with Trump pouring money into the race to save him. And in Philadelphia, Chris Rabb (PA-03), who took down the Democratic machine in his primary this spring, is officially headed to Congress. In Ohio , union ironworker Brian Poindexter (OH-07) is sending Max Miller, a former Trump aide and real estate heir, packing. Michigan isn’t finished, either. In Detroit, union organizer Donavan McKinney (MI-13), who toppled a multimillionaire incumbent in August, just sealed his win and is headed to Washington. In Colorado , Melat Kiros (CO-01), who made national headlines this year when she defeated a 30-year incumbent in her primary, is Denver’s next member of Congress. In California , teacher and longtime WFP member and leader Randy Villegas (CA-22) defeated David Valadao, who voted to gut Medicaid and to give ICE $38 million with no additional oversight. New York is sending a whole new class of fighters to Washington. Longtime WFP champion Brad Lander (NY-10), who was arrested by ICE last year while defending immigrant New Yorkers’ right to due process, is headed to Congress. Union organizer Claire Valdez (NY-07) will succeed Nydia Velazquez, while community organizer Darializa Avila Chevalier (NY-13), who unseated a five-term incumbent this summer, will represent Upper Manhattan. These wins are just the beginning, and more races are still being counted across the country, includingWill Lawrence(MI-07) in Michigan and four more WFP challengers in California:Mai Vang(CA-07),Aisha Wahab(CA-14),Connie Chan(CA-11), andAngela Gonzales-Torres(CA-34). This night was years in the making, Peter. Trump promised to lower the cost of living. Instead he delivered chaos , war , and rising costs , while his billionaire backers collected tax breaks and friendly regulators. Tonight, those broken promises came due, and voters sent Trump a clear message: you don’t get to lie to working families and keep your majority. He wasn’t the only one who got a message, though. All cycle long, the corporate wing of the Democratic Party said candidates like ours couldn’t win. They said the only path to victory ran through milquetoast moderates who promise nothing and stand for even less. Then they spent millions in our primaries to make sure voters never got a real choice. It didn’t work. Voters chose every one of our priority congressional champions anyway. And tonight, they did it again. Trump and Musk poured more than $800 million into these midterms, much of it in the final months, and our candidates still won in exactly the places the corporate wing said they’d lose. So to every Democrat already eyeing a future run: the path in 2028 runs through the Working Families Guarantee — a home you can afford, health care you can rely on, a good job to support your family, and childcare when and where you need it. That’s the agenda that won tonight. And it won because of you, Peter. Every one of the more than 30 million calls, texts, and door knocks since January came from people who believed working families deserve better, and who gave their evenings, their weekends, and whatever they could spare to prove it. That’s what our movement runs on. It’s what got us here tonight, and it’s what will carry us into 2027 and 2028. Thank you for everything you did to make tonight possible, Peter. In solidarity, All of us at WFP P.S. We can’t let tonight end without celebrating Angie Nixon , who came just two points shy of a historic upset. After winning her primary despite being outraised nearly 16-to-1, Angie never wavered in her fight for working families, even as the Democratic establishment failed to rally behind her in the general election. We’re so grateful for the heart and courage she poured into this campaign, and so proud to have stood beside her every step of the way. Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. Do you remember the trucks?

I do. Refrigerated trailers backed up to the loading docks of hospitals in New York City, because the morgues inside were full. More than a year later, about 750 bodies were still being kept in freezer trucks on the Brooklyn waterfront.

Do you remember Hart Island? A drone filmed men in white suits lowering plain pine boxes into a long trench, one beside the other. Americans watched that on the evening news and understood that it was really happening here.

Do you remember the hospital wards? Rows of strangers on ventilators, sedated and alone, with a machine breathing for them. New York was so short of those machines that the Governor ordered the National Guard to go take them from other hospitals.

And do you remember what you felt when the number climbed again that night?

You were afraid for your mother. You were afraid for your spouse. You did the math on your own age and your own lungs, and you were afraid for yourself.

For more than a million American families, that fear turned out to be justified.
https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTAsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA-wu1Djg1WbeLZRikb1rbocRup3QuibNXwBndN2TO52dQV8edDjbhf614lMsRHvy0exqlQl7yjDgClvBL__qcRVwhFN8gdMY9H7j93sl
I am going to make the man responsible answer for it, under oath.

Maybe your family is one of them.

Maybe they would not let you into the room, and a nurse in a plastic gown held a phone up to the pillow so you could say goodbye through a screen. Maybe you said “I love you” into that phone and never found out whether it was heard. Then you buried that person in front of ten people, standing six feet apart in the open air, with no singing allowed.

That is the part I cannot forgive. Not the virus — we have always had disease. The cruelty was in the rules they built around it, and in the men who wrote those rules and then refused to explain themselves.

So let me tell you what the man at the center of all of it did on July 29 of this year, when the United States Senate finally put him under subpoena.

Anthony Fauci raised his right hand and took the Fifth Amendment. Not once, and not twice. He took it 111 times.

He would not answer for the gain-of-function research his agency paid for at the Wuhan lab in Communist China. He would not answer for the years of concealment, deception and fraud that followed. He would not answer for a catastrophe that killed over a million Americans and more than 15 million people worldwide.

And in all of those 111 refusals, he never once said their names.

Innocent men do not take the Fifth 111 times.

So let me say plainly what not one politician in Washington has the spine to say.

Anthony Fauci is a criminal.

His agency paid for the creation of a weapon in a Communist Chinese laboratory, and then he lied to your face about it for years. Over a million of our countrymen are dead. In my judgment that is not incompetence and it is not bad luck — it is MASS MURDER, and I intend to prove it in a court of law.

name: Jocelyn Benson
subject: This victory is for all of us.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOCELYN BENSON FOR GOVERNOR]
body:
[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Thank you.

I am honored and humbled to be the next governor of the great state of
Michigan.

This is a victory for all of us. Yesterday, Michigan citizens spoke and
made history — electing the first all-woman ticket in Michigan history,
and the first back-to-back Democratic governors in generations.

I didn’t get here alone. This movement was carried by so many people — by
my fantastic running mate, Winnie Brinks, by my predecessor Governor
Whitmer, by my family, by my campaign staff, by volunteers all across our
great state, and most importantly, by people like you.

This
victory belongs to all of us.

For 22 months, we've traveled this state, listening to people in their
homes, at small businesses, on the job, and around kitchen tables.

And yesterday, Michiganders made their voices heard: They want lower
costs, more money in their pockets, good-paying jobs in their
neighborhoods, and more opportunity for their families.

That’s exactly why I ran for governor — and it’s how I’ll serve you.

I know the challenges ahead are serious. I know there will be
disagreements, difficult decisions, and days when the work feels harder
than we imagined.

But I also know what Michiganders can accomplish when we come together for
a common purpose. Michigan is a state that builds things, and now it’s our
turn to build the next chapter.

Michigan, you gave us this responsibility. We will meet it with everything
we have.

Thank you!

Jocelyn Benson

subject: The honor of a lifetime

body:
I could not have reached this moment without you

| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=13740%2E400544%2EUhHvtp)
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/17895?refcode=jtk1718-fr-nd&t=2&akid=13740%2E400544%2EUhHvtp)
Friend, Last night, New Mexicans sent a message loud and clear: They chose a future rooted in opportunity, not extremism. They chose leadership that puts New Mexico first, brings people together, and focuses relentlessly on what matters most to our families and communities. They chose a governor who will always put New Mexicans — not a President, not a political party — first.
**_And last night, those choices made history.
_**
I’m a daughter of Pueblo women, a New Mexican, a single mother, a former small business owner, a former Congresswoman, and the first Native American Cabinet Secretary in U.S. history. Now, I’m the 33rd Governor of New Mexico — and the first Native American woman elected Governor in our nation’s history.
I could not have reached this moment without you. Every door knocked, every conversation had, every phone call made, every person who chipped in, and every person who believed in this campaign helped make this victory possible.

**_We won this race because of you._**
This is bigger than one campaign or one election. It is a moment generations of Pueblo women, Native communities, and New Mexicans have helped make possible. And I carry that history with me as I step into this responsibility.

**It is the honor of my lifetime to lead our beautiful state.** I will never take for granted the trust New Mexicans have placed in me, and I will spend every day working to make sure that trust is well placed.
Our campaign may be over, but our work is just beginning. I cannot wait to get to work building a New Mexico that works for ALL New Mexicans.

Thank you for believing in me, believing in this vision, and helping us make history together.
Our brightest days are ahead.
Be Fierce,

Deb Haaland
Governor-Elect, New Mexico

Friends, I wanted to take a moment to thank you for your unwavering support. Our victory last night is a testament to the work we have done and the results we’ve delivered for Staten Island and Brooklyn.
---
---
I’m proud of my record of securing hundreds of millions of dollars for transportation, infrastructure, local hospitals, our NYPD, and FDNY. We’ve also successfully resolved over 25,000 constituent cases, delivered the largest middle-class tax cuts in history, secured our borders, and ensured our 9/11 heroes get the healthcare they need. Our work is far from over. In fact, the disappointing results in New York and across the United States prove it will only get tougher. But I’m committed, as I have always been, to fighting for our community and our country. I will return to Washington knowing you have my back, and that means more to me than I can express.
---
With much appreciation Nicole

A handful of votes.

Right now that is all that separates me and Cindy Hyde-Smith in
Mississippi. This race is not over.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261104_1.u-o0qx&refcode=em20261104-1&t=1001&akid=9978%2E582294%2Es9lx8e ]HuffPost: Mississippi Senate Race too close to call with most votes counted

Scott Colom

We did it, Peter!

Thanks to the unstoppable energy of this grassroots movement, Alexandria,
Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida are heading back to Congress to keep fighting
for working families.

We knew a movement like ours could win, but this cycle was anything but
easy.

Because the Squad refused to back down from fighting injustice and holding
the Trump administration accountable, the MAGA machine and outside forces
threw everything they had trying to unseat our champions.

Their goal? Silence the voices standing up for a government that serves
the people instead of just the wealthy and well-connected.

When attacks grew the loudest,
supporters like you
stepped up,
Peter. That’s the power of our
movement: the Squad has our backs in the halls of Congress because they
know we have theirs.

We didn’t win with corporate PAC checks or favors from special interests —
we won because everyday people chipped in, organized, and refused to be
intimidated into silence.

Now, Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida return to Washington to stand
firm for working families, immigrants’ rights, accessible healthcare,
racial and economic justice, and for every community this broken system
has tried to push aside.

The road ahead will demand everything we’ve got, and the Squad is ready to
keep delivering.

Thank you,
Peter, for standing with us and
proving that when we come together, people power wins.

In solidarity,

The Squad Victory Fund

name: Josh Shapiro
subject: Thank you, from the bottom of my heart
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY SHAPIRO FOR PENNSYLVANIA]
body:
[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23180?t=1001&akid=937%2E245147%2EwUxGKq ]Photo of Gov. Josh Shapiro taking the stage at 2026 victory party

Derek, thank you.

I could not be more humbled and grateful for the opportunity to keep
serving our Commonwealth as your Governor. From the bottom of my heart,
thank you for the trust you’ve placed in me and our great Lieutenant
Governor, Austin Davis, once again.

Last night, the good people of Pennsylvania spoke with resounding force:

Pennsylvania declared that we could not be more ready for the end of this
era of ruthless chaos and cruelty, this rampant corruption that raises our
costs and rattles our conscience.

And not only did we win this election, keeping the most important
Governor’s office in the country out of Donald Trump’s hands.

We came together to flip four U.S. House seats across our Commonwealth,
sending a historic Democratic majority to the House to put a check on the
chaos and corruption in Washington.

And for the first time in over three decades, Democrats won control of the
Pennsylvania State Senate, delivering a Democratic trifecta that’s ready
to raise the minimum wage, codify reproductive freedom, invest in mass
transit, and so much more.

Two hundred and fifty years since we declared our independence from a
king, our nation has been through ups, downs, and everything in between.

These past two years in particular have tested our will in previously
unimaginable ways.

You had every reason to throw up your hands. To tune out. To walk away.

But that’s not what you did.

You kept the faith. You used your power. You did your part to help change
the trajectory of this country.

I’m clear-eyed that the hard work didn’t end last night. It’s just begun,
and today, I’ll be back behind my desk continuing to work for the good
people of Pennsylvania.

This victory belongs to you,
Derek. Because of the support and
generosity of thousands of folks like you, we knocked on over 1.4 million
doors and made half a million phone calls throughout the course of this
campaign.

Every single one of those conversations made a difference last night — and
they happened because of you.

Thank you, from the bottom of my heart, for your trust, your hard work,
and your faith in me,
Derek. Let’s get back to work.

With gratitude,

Josh Shapiro

## Blackburn Wins as Green Concedes
Republican Marsha Blackburn [won Tennessee's race for governor](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOgzAQRL8GOpBtbBMKF9fQ5dor0dreBCsLjuxNUP7-xP3CdU8aaTTzfq7LFRKl_f4NGzrm27LjUQmZsSxbioxlQ8LAKe8F64u4Yg2LEsp2UnZCLxA4vXHR0EbnlZxAhxadHKdhnIRRql1dGG4XqbywUxyMicabi_JBRWsRvDZTm9xZKKXQUoqLFr2R3odRWzTKismKRguMiXPpeUXGfcdaEW_0yW8sfchbS25lftZm-GrU3Kj5OI7-A2vOZ9qo-bzVqPmZKXEKJ0LhFAhP9ATh4V9l7xgeWDuEQp-OEGJXIGAnpBRyMFr3K2_UFhefRyJK1Y6NFvcNEv2N4H8afDv1GwAA__8Y6IYv), becoming the first woman elected to the office in state history after Democrat Jerri Green conceded just after 10:30 p.m. last night. At 74, Blackburn, who campaigned with an endorsement from President Trump, will also be the oldest person ever elected governor of Tennessee. The race was tighter than pre-election polls showed, with Blackburn leading Green about 46% to 43% late Tuesday and independent David Hatley drawing roughly 9%. Blackburn [declared victory](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ8GOtDa2OancPE3dLn2SmTsJazO2JG9Ccrbn8grXPdJI43mm-_bcnMUKd2_3IGWeVsSnjUiM5bloMBYDozomXIqWJ-RK1a_SJCmE6IDtTjP9MJFuTbYVYrJKd-iFeM0jBNoKdvdbohymBSiMD5sQeI4hFGYQQ8KtN5cS_YqFAKUEPBPQa_FuvpRGdTSwGSgUYCBOJeed2RMCWtF3OI7v7D0Ph9ttDvzozbD_0bOjZzP8-zfbs_5Shs5X1qNnB85EpO_0BUmH_HCiqk7XKm769bo_M_6LKn7aGPoNiqVO1DagIbJ9DsfsS02PE6KkaoZGwX3w1H87OA_nviy8jcAAP__FxGHzA) onstage in Nashville before the AP or NBC News had called the race. In August 2026 the national debt passed $40 trillion.1 It was not
voted on. There was no ceremony. Most Americans found out from a
headline, if they found out at all.

Somebody has to absorb it

A debt that size does not simply sit there. It gets serviced,
refinanced, and eventually dealt with — and there are only three
ways to deal with it: raise taxes, cut spending, or reduce the real
value of what is owed by letting the currency weaken. The first two
require Congress to do something unpopular on the record. The third
requires nobody to do anything at all.

That is why the figure matters to a retirement account rather than
just to a budget committee. Every dollar in your IRA is a claim
denominated in the same currency the debt is denominated in.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.
If the obligation is managed down in real terms, that happens through
your savings, not around them.

The evidence is already behind us. It takes roughly $1.95 today to
buy what a dollar bought in 2000.2 Nothing was confiscated. The unit
was simply worth less each year, and savers holding it carried the
cost quietly.

Gold is the one asset in this conversation with no issuer. No
treasury can print it, no company can dilute it, no counterparty can
default on it. Central banks themselves have been buying more than a
thousand tons a year.3 They are not doing it for the yield.

You are allowed to hold physical gold inside an IRA. Most savers
have never been told that, because the firms holding their money do
not sell it. The free 2026 Gold IRA Guide walks through exactly how a
rollover from an IRA, 401(k) or TSP works, which metals the IRS
allows, how insured depository storage works, and the mistakes that
cost retirees the most. It is free and it takes about thirty seconds
to request.

body:
Your gift of just $28 helps provide one life-saving ultrasound and shares the hope of the gospel with a mother considering abortion.

| | | | [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckc-K3DAMh5_GuWWw7PwZH3JYGnLqlnYp7TEospyYdZzgOLP07cuUGeh5j_okfSD9fr-Or-iDj_M3XLlL2Y3pGIkDTwkz54UnxjP_2Vzkj-BHJVVTApSyGpGyv_FYYWE7SxaBCu6gNbo1cFWyWDoHyjZVWxviGkxrr5pqZyVachUYB4Xv7j4AWQFoCfVlks7U0uG1bifJVS0qiYFTviTezyl4wpjxeHdbIr7QthahW3LeD6FfhBqEGmZ_83G-7ImnLcX7iFDDoxJqoIXpfTuzUANSSRg4WkzlKvRwCN1_efkKUjXf34RqCNcd_RyF7mttjAGhmjOv43_8uf_orGz9uQrd84o-POCxnYlY6H5P27EzZR_np2mLmWMWuv-lxh9t-fZzKJ__KFJn9w8fgj-aVlRyviv_XZw_GdKtU38DAAD__45vog4)
---
Dear Advocate for Life, Imagine a young woman who has just discovered she's pregnant. She's frightened, overwhelmed, and unsure of what to do next. Maybe she hasn't told anyone. Maybe someone in her life is pressuring her to have an abortion. But what if, before making that decision, she had the opportunity to see her baby for the very first time? **That's the life-changing opportunity your gift to PreBorn! can help provide.** Through our PreBorn! Network Clinics across America, mothers facing unexpected pregnancies receive free ultrasounds, compassionate care, and the opportunity to hear the gospel of Jesus Christ. ## Democrats Win House, Senate
Democrats [won control](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDHO4yAUhE8DnSMeEBsXFNu4y7ZbWgQegSyYCN4myu1XyRX-bqQZfdJ8fy77xeWSj9tvV9FSbPuBr1GQCPsesA5yf9G349ZxjEdx7xZjd7sUcp4AJqF35yk_cQcebESUqDhaWFa1rGBWyZP1qxQzuDWeMSxL0Ffjw1n7II3T2s9Xnu0HByA0gAIlTt54BUZclQMzuxiZFhgytX66t3xQwlje7Yn95FvlxSaix2DqF5MbkxslTLmUT8fkllrFz6Nv_DeQyW0Go82ip4C1-e5oTL7kw6fpO5iqu7ee6c3kxrsNj1cuJY95YVrcqstfMKefqXpa-T8AAP__kpp-mw) of the U.S. House and Senate last night, flipping both chambers and setting up divided government for the final two years of President Trump's term. In the House, the party needed a net gain of just three seats. Projections put it far above the 218 needed for a majority, in what could be the party's [biggest House majority](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDkO2zAURE9DdRS4KFoKFmnUOW1K4Yv8tBhzEchvC759YBe5QOoZDN6837ftBiGGfP8FCQ35smW8WkQirJvD1AgeaEu-V2ztjPAu3lfYlFAjl5KLYQNL4YWb7JzxiAp1h0ZOi54WOS-qO4wGIQfY9YIel1mo3dnd4Q85wYIWYO-C-cxJKQYptdSit7PVcha7BjmP4D0bBLpApfZ_Ssh0oI_v8sLa25K6aA6iszH9k6mVqfW6rj7v9nPjkzO1niUGCrYxtX65MaKlUDJTq8NUbAVq_CjPhtyWTLVEnoIjrOlflV8hN071mU5uD7QPXm2GUWi9TF017rxCjKGNExvEPUGIXzT6P6Evo_4GAAD__9kijeM) in nearly two decades. The size of the [new Senate majority](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO6yAQRb8GOkcMODYuKF7jLq_d0hqbIWYXTASjRPn7lXc_Yeuje6R7Pm7LDWOKx_0_ZnIcynLQqyViprp4yo3xi7Zy3Cu19kj4LiFUXLTSQwfQqX7BjeOTFpDeBSJNRpKDcTLjBHbScndmBat0GHrSI6CfCMkTgl5xhXUdg4zu1AGoHsCAUZfNbgasWg2CHTAE0SvykUu9fJZ48E4hvcuT6mUrWSa3Mz-aMP-EnoWeeac9pnQyoee9ZDofCT03OpBJ6HkAezX22nnKZavIrXvFo_vFXY6eqeZzIKvzj1dMKbZhFL26Z4w_Xsl_K_V0-jsAAP__ead-mA) was still awaiting final results at _The Flyover_ 's deadline. Democrats flipped Republican-held seats in North Carolina, South Carolina, Texas, and Ohio, among others. [Full results here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAQhZ_GdEEeG2EoXNyGLrfdEjlmnMyuf5A9AuXtV-QVtj1H-nTO93Vf744i5ed_l9ByKGvGs0VkxrpumBq7H_QlPyu2tkf3LiFUtyqpxhvATQ6r80wHrtBtNiAq1B1aMLM2M0yz6l4WdJhh1jPKSeHkR2VwG40LwRhnwMuO7IUDkAOABi17P3kNk3xoB9PoQhCDxI241P67UOYXhvguB9bel9RF-2Lem9D_hFqEWs7z7PPDXzeuXqhlL5GYfBNq-ezGiJ6p5CtItDHW1Lpqt_2kGKmNRgzymRzFD5__ZuWw6jcAAP__P6d3Ig). The majority hands Democrats committee gavels and subpoena power over the administration. Hakeem Jeffries is in line to become the first Black speaker when the new Congress convenes Jan. 3.
## Upsets Topple GOP in Red Strongholds
Democrats took key victories in GOP strongholds last night, most prominently in Texas, where state Rep. James Talarico [defeated Ken Paxton](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1u7CAQxfGnwZ1XDFgYFxS3cbe3TWnNwmCTYGPBZD_ePtq8Quoj_aTz_7guV0w5Het_3MlxLMtBj5aJmeoSaG-MX-TLsVZq7cz4KjFWXJRUpgfo5bCg53SnBbrgIpEi3ZGDcdLjBHZS3ea0n8wQbmQiBWlGC4PR0QdrLXp7G6BL7s0ByAFAg5YXb70GK28awRqMUQySQuJSL58lHbxRzK9yp3rxZe-y25jPJvQ_oWahZt5oSzm_N6Hmrez0fiTU7HE_Ma2HULOB0YBWPWPGmnzpA0VCbv2JTy5Hz_TEo_8-G7FQc1ddOB8p59TMKAa57ph-_Y7_Vuzu1E8AAAD___gigQQ) for Senate, becoming the first Democrat to win statewide there since 1994. Also on the Texas ballot, Gina Hinojosa [unseated Gov. Greg Abbott](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1ugzAUhZ8GNiP_ECCDhy5s6doRXexr49TYkX0bmrevyCt0u9LV-XS-83VbbhBiSP4TdtTk8pLwqBGJsCwW90rwjSYnX7DWR4RXdq7AIrkcmBCM9wsYCk9cRGu1Q5SoWtRivKrxKqarbDd9gd5aFP0FFbcrB7NahSMfRgkKbY9t0CdOCN4LoYTinZmMEhNfFYhpAOeanqMNlEt3zyHRhi6-8hNLZ_LeRr0RPWqjPho5N3I-jqMzaz01zn8j5_Ns5Ez4C5X5M5hyYRjRUMiJvV18Qc9gXTMR8yEB20LK91yBFaw_kU5AW7R9HCHGUIex6bnfIcR3B_rfck8t_wIAAP__J6WFbQ), who was seeking a fourth term, and will be the state's first Latina governor. In Kansas, Democrat Adam Hamilton, a Methodist megachurch pastor and first-time candidate, [unseated Sen. Roger Marshall](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLuO5CAQRb8GZ7Qo8PgREGzibDbd0KqBwmaHhwWlHvXfr9y_sPGVztU5fz73T4wpluM3ZrIc6l7opydiprZ7yp3xm1wtR6Per4SvGkLDXSs9SQCpxh0dxyftMHgbiDSZgSzMq5lXWFY9nNZ_gDdfjggBgkPC1a_aKK0MrsHQxxDtjQNQI4ABox5ucQYW9WUQlglDEKMiH7m2x98aC58U0qs-qT1czUOyJ_PVhfkl9Cb0xiedMaV7E3o7a6bbSOjNYb4wHkXobYJFzxNIT7m6hizRY5Yn5pi4FhlSvLr8xtKxy04FmWQnZPnWztEztXwjh2b99RNTin2axaiOjPH9PPD_tXxa_S8AAP__40eKTA), becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the state since 1932. In Ohio, Democrat Sherrod Brown [reclaimed his Senate seat](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uxCAQhU-DO1vMgPxTUKRxt2lTWhgPaxJsVjBZtLePvFdI96QnvZ_v67bcbIjhvH_agwz7tJxUSyRmystGR2H7Qy6d90ylPKJ9Je-zXVBi3wK0Ui_WcXjSAs1mPBGSasjAMKlhgnHCZjcAEgYa5aRpRO1B61Wp3rltWEEDYRPMFQcgNYACJTs3OgWjXJWFsbfeCy1pC5xy953CyTv5-EpPyp1LRxPNzvwoQn0InAXOtdbOreW6cfkC50sKnNMeUvseXui0TO3-W5i2ds2pngLnJpvtUUOMofSD0PJ-2BDfFfw_ME-DfwEAAP__-_V3PQ) from appointed GOP Sen. ## Ukraine Peace Negotiations Set
The United States will [mediate peace negotiations](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OwyAQRk-DOyIYHP8UFNu4y7ZbWhMY7NlgsAxJlNuvkits_el7T3o_l_mCHDkt37iRrSHPiZ4lUq10zJ62UvFGLqfloFL2iK8cwoEzKOik1lK1M7rKD5p1420gAjINWd2Pph_1MEKzWn_2iMY7IBhaCEYRoBnPzoE-B_B9w_aN01q1Whtt1MkNzuhBXQ3qocMQRKvIc83H6TdzqiuF-MoPOk4ub020a617EeZLwCRgqiutHON7EzDtObJ7CZg4VToSVs4Jo4Cp06MaeyOfXG85BIkp5XtyVCRe79KveGW5EzqSiZZc-fMsAqbmsH5_coxcul60atmQP7am_q_fw8JfAAAA__-KBYab) between Ukraine and Russia next week on Nov. 10 and 11 in Abu Dhabi, according to U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff. In preparation, American negotiators meet first [this week in Brussels](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unTAQhJ8GOiOvTfgpXKQ53U2bEi32GjYYjGxzyHn7iLzCbWek0Xzf76_pCznwsfzCnUzxcTrozoFKoTQ52nPBjWw8lkQ5nwE_0fuEk5KqEwBCthPawm-aoHbGEynSNRnoR92PMIyqXo32dpDoOnDt3CnXw9jNSsHo-x-dpRlrNs8cgGwBNGjZ2MFqGOSsEYYOva9aSY5LTM2fyEdZyYdPfFNqbNzrYNZSzlzpn5V6Vep133fj498H4-mfJKbgKvW6stjJMRYS12njzsciri0hHyTSlTOjKBi2LHC-hFtxZnFz2aL3IuMn18m48-YQOHd91cplRw7_L5TviXsb9S8AAP__sWqF0Q), Belgium, with France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the EU, and NATO to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine. Closer to home, First Lady Melania Trump [will host officials](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1urDAQhZ8GOpDH9vJTuLgN3d42JZrY42WyBiPbu4S3j8grpPukIx2d833c5zty4O3xH1cyxcd5oyMHKoXS7GjNBZ9k4_ZIlPMe8IzeJ5ylkF0D0Ag9oy38phlqZzyRJFWTgX5U_QjDKOvFaO-wI5Be907fQI1CAQ5CeCdw8Lar2Vx1AEIDKFCitYNVMIhPhTB06H2lBTkuMbVfkbeykA9nfFNqbVzrYJZS9lypf5WcKjkdx9GeuMR4pZWcrj-VnPYYuLC9EFNhG-jClQJujM0Sc2lez4S8UZNeOTM29F0SxuR4w3Q2oG-90rdOtEtZQ52M2w8OgXPXV1o8VuTwO6f8TeLbyJ8AAAD__wN8iDI) from both countries at the White House on Thursday, the White House said, calling it an “extraordinary moment in American history.” She brokered last month’s local ceasefire that moved hundreds of civilians out of Russian-occupied Oleshky. President Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping could also [meet about the war](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1urDAQxfGnMZ2Rx-byUbi4Dd2mTYkGM16cNRjZw5J9-2jzCqmP9NPR__M23TDEsN8_cCPLPk07XSUSM-Vpoa0wPsil_Z6plCPiK3mfcdJKtxJAqmZCx-FJE1SL9USaTEUWusF0A_SDrlarjJuXHlw79157dEqDG7zX6h921JCvgn1zAKoBMGBU7XpnoFezQehb9F40ipbAKddfKey8ko-v9KRcu7RV0a7MRxHmv9Cj0ON1XbXbZ_cehR7ftNAjgNCjMkKP-SwloDwfGcNO8iB0JBnjo0icT7msOAfJ-dwOeZwcdvkd6pW3WGW7HFeIMZS2E426bxji7wP-W7en1T8BAAD__7MngqY) in the coming weeks. The Kremlin said yesterday that it hopes to finalize plans for a three-way meeting, which Moscow has proposed to hold at an economic summit in Shenzhen, China, on Nov. 18-19.

name: Gabby Giffords
subject: A personal note from me
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
Together, we have built a gun safety coalition. We do more than just talk about gun violence — we take action to stop it.
#

Friend, hi. This is Gabby Giffords.
I wanted to send you a personal message today, after a busy night and a busy few months.
Over the last year, I have been on the road for 174 days. I have made 70 trips to 40 cities to support our allies and fight for gun safety. GIFFORDS endorsed 443 candidates this cycle. We donated $500,000 directly to candidates and their campaigns. We invested $5.7 million in House races alone, and $10 million total across key races.
So far, candidates endorsed by GIFFORDS PAC went head-to-head against candidates backed by the NRA in 39 races. Our candidates won 38 of those 39 races. What a day.
**But the real reason I’m reaching out today is to thank you.**
Together, we have built a gun safety coalition. We do more than just talk about gun violence — we take action to stop it.
When I founded this organization, this is exactly what I hoped to build. But back then, this issue looked a lot different than it does today. Thanks to you, we’ve changed that.
We’ve made gun safety a kitchen table issue for Americans. We’ve elected leaders who are willing to fight the tough battles to protect their constituents. We’ve passed more than 820 gun safety laws in states across the country.
And we’ve saved countless lives from gun violence.**That is why we do this work.**
I know it’s been a long election cycle. I’m exhausted, just like you. But I’m also incredibly grateful to stand shoulder to shoulder with you in this fight. Days like today are worth what it takes to get them.
Tomorrow, there will be more work to do. There always is.
But today, take care. Celebrate. You’ve earned it.
All the best,
Gabby

Wait! Please, don’t click away just yet.
**GIFFORDS PAC put more than $10 million behind our candidates in the 2026 election.** We raised those resources through emails like this one, with help from supporters like you. We are incredibly grateful for that.
But here is the truth: 97% of our supporters do not donate. Everything we accomplish is funded by just 3% of our members.**Imagine what we could do if we increased that number to 10%, or even 5%.**
We can’t wait to prepare for the next election, because our opponents have already started. **[Will you make a contribution to GIFFORDS so we can keep the fight going in the months and years ahead?](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261104-1-B&t=1&akid=12002%2E3935704%2E52VicQ)**

Dear Patriot, This letter couldn't wait. That's why Kirk Cameron personally asked me to write you on the post-production budget shortfall for "Iggy and Mr. Kirk." He wanted to make sure you heard about this urgent situation as soon as possible. **And after you hear what's going on, I hope you'll support BRAVE FOR GOOD.** **[We are facing a serious budget shortfall of $48,523.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTAsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA-2nqdW9AmlBjA5v5z0dvlRtLE6hwTqQQQdfKtnzTTQ7icGpU6gD2Gm9bCgQG7lDOGjBntMMucVSvLDx4vzp7CMdNuLG29O2R2HfCAO7GA)** But before I go into more detail, let me tell you a little about our mission to help parents instill wholesome and Godly values in America's children. Kirk just wrapped up this year's "See You at the Library Day," where we countered the Left and brought conservative values straight to America's children. Kirk is busy spearheading the "Bible Revival" movement that gets Biblical values -- that America was founded upon -- back into schools. Not to mention the thousands of 'Queer Kid' videos on platforms like YouTube Kids. The days of The Andy Griffith Show and Father Knows Best are gone. The Left has purposely used TV to create a generation of zombie children who are glued to their screens. "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" is the antidote to that Leftist TV brainwashing. It uses low-stimulation production and teaches children how to respond to the deceitful culture with Biblical values and steadfast faith. Like when Mr. Kirk teaches Iggy:
---
* to love how God created him as an iguana, even when the villainous Culture the Vulture says Iggy must become a human to fit in.
* to rely on the wisdom of parents -- one mom and one dad -- to solve life's problems.
* to be BRAVE by speaking truth in the face of the Left's lies.

Fellow Patriot, please help. Because this is so urgent, I wanted to reach out to Americans who share our concern for the next generation. On behalf of myself, Kirk, and our entire team, thank you for considering supporting BRAVE FOR GOOD. Together, we will rebuild a culture that honors God and His will for our lives.

Sincerely, Dr. Trent TalbotFounder, BRAVE for Good

## Hinojosa Makes History
Democratic state Rep. Gina Hinojosa [defeated Gov. Greg Abbott](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO8yAQBeDT4M4WDGBCQfE37vK3W1rYTGwkAhbMxtnbr5wrbDka6Xt67-s-331MMW___RMdvR9lzni2hERYZ0y4Uiy5YvtO1MqB1V93mIHD2AvRczX7leILZ9EFt_BgRYdOGCuNleNNdbtbhLGj5SjXcXlIAK3DDUatuASjl5vvors0IbgSwAWoQRqlAYzVRkPgMjDFMUQqdaAdCd--PdJPeWEd1vLsktuJjsbkPwYTg-k8z2Hda8nXl8F09WEw-UpxTchg-gj9dgG51N4vSyHqt5h9D6CsUdYMx3501YXjjCnFNhqm-Pb0MX0S6Y9DvRz8BgAA__9vIXx7) on Tuesday, becoming Texas' first Latina governor and ending Republican control of the office that began in 1995. She led 57% to 42% when Abbott conceded. Abbott called Hinojosa to concede, then [told supporters](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O6yAQBeCnwR0RjPEPBcVt3OW2W1oYBhstMRFMnOTtV17tPsGWo5HO0Xc-rvPVxhT39b-9oaFXyPOOz5qQCMuMCR3FvBesj0Q137HY8_YzCOi5lFyo2TqKB86y8WYRXssGjRx0O-i2H1WzGb_0XdBLGP1oRetdF7SyoJ3SoxhDr5tozjQphZIgJKhLO6gOYNDd0IEXrWdKoI-Uy4U2JHzZGtI7H1guLt-aZDaie2XtPwYTg-kz5Bcd54vBdGIYTCk7mxhMaz74WnDldlkyEafMn5bcxn-l3Ns3_-HyuHP7qBT3phh_f8aUYu0HpsR6szF9l9MfNzsMfAUAAP__qm2DJA) in Austin, "_There are still votes to be counted, but mathematically, we're not going to be able to win this election_." He pledged to help her team with the transition. "_Everything is bigger in Texas, including the shock of this win_ ," Hinojosa [told a cheering crowd](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2SnTAQhE8DmSj9IhQocEK2Th1SAg0wtkCUNPt4e3sXe4UNp6a6v-7-8zF9BEx4br_DAZ7ea55OuGsCIigTJFgI81mgfiaq-YISnjtOksueCcG4nsJC-IJJtNHPPDrRghfWKetUP-h294ObQSizSusGbRflpDHGrWsYoDdSqBb94yYE10JyIXWnrDZSWmeskZGr2GgOESmXjnYgeIe6pq_8gtIt-WiT34mu2qhfjRwbOd733a35_dR4_o0cr5yQcKmNHCMceSmB2IZnYDue-W-ugVX6PCsL85yJ2BH-QWU7Vsrli61YKrEU6BF8w9n2sM9c2uLjdWNKWHvbaL4dAdN3JvrhlC8v_wcAAP__tHGMRg) in Austin. The Rio Grande Valley native added that no one imagined "a little girl from the RGV would stand before you here as the next governor." "_It never bothered me that they doubted me, it bothered me that they doubted us_ ," Hinojosa [said in her speech](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAMhp8mbEGJCQSGDF3YrmtHlEvMETWXIOKD69tXnK5P0MmybH32_31dposNMaTbp72joeecp4RHiUiE24QRHYWcNiyPSCWvuNmz9xMI6LiUXKjJOgo7TrLy5ir8ICs0Ug-NHpquV9ViBtH3re362dtW69mr-doJDQ7sMLi-U1UwJ01KoSQICaputGoB9NDqFrxoPFMCfaC81bQg4dOWOf7kHbfa5XsVzUK0FtZ8MBgZjMdx1C4G9w1LfhTK6dxiMHp0oYSc-HmNwfguUjIYRcNgfJFfU_4XnKdwW4jHsCN_S-A2ef5YvSUsDMZqM349QoyhdJopcbvbEF9_0T917gZ-AwAA__8bpIhV). She is the first Democrat elected governor since Ann Richards in 1990.
## Talarico Flips U.S. Senate Seat
Democrat James Talarico [defeated Republican Ken Paxton](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOgzAQRL_GdI68xsC5cHENXa69Ejn2EiwtGNkbkvz9ifzClaMnjebN73W6-kRpu__4FR2_5jxt-KyEzFgmJAyc8lawPohr3rH4M8dJK91LAKnM5AOnAydoorupaKFBB4NtB9v2X6ZZHIDq0M69gh5UnGdlZ7RqgBZiZ2zomuTONgBlQCvQ5tIOptN6sN3Q6ajaKIzCmDiXCy_I-PJ1pnc-sFxCXhtyC_NeRfst9Cj0GG7VPyqn7aRCj6eP0CPl4Enocfcvzps8qmRPvqSQJS8oQ1535HSqyJAr01tW3DyjLD58MFbJWXoZKFdsiov7MxGl2g_CqPvqE33m8D9fPJz-CwAA__9iCIk5) on Tuesday, becoming the first Democrat Texans have elected to the U.S. Senate since 1988. With about two-thirds of the vote counted, he led roughly 59% to 39%. Paxton [conceded in a short speech](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHO4yAQhJ8Gd0SwxnYoKK5xl2uvtPbMOkYCg2Dj5N7-5F_6n-AvRyPNzDd_HssDQwzH8zcmcvzZ8nLQu0ViprpQpJVDPiq1V-SWC1W8tF9AwSi1lsosuHI4adGdd3-Vt7ojpyfbT7Yf76bbnYHRqk2BIZy2O26WQOG4rdYOeCflu-CuNK2V0aA0mFs_mQFgssM0gFe9F0aRD5zrjXdi-mDb4r98Ur2tOXXR7cylif6XgFnAzDvtIcbLEzDvOdFFJGBeMRUMz0PAPGqrrNEyhpPkq3hkapLrKxWZgmeqSX6zN3mtEzBjKgLmrjpf3iHG0MZJGPVMGL66Ov7hfaeD_wEAAP__FaiEgA) Tuesday night. "_Well, let me start off by congratulating James Talarico_ ," he said, adding that he "_will be praying for him that he will do good for Texas and this nation_." Sen. John Cornyn, who lost the GOP nomination to Paxton in May, will hand his seat to Talarico on Jan. 3. "_The voters have spoken_ ," Cornyn [wrote on X](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uwyAUxfGnwVsi7gWMPTBUlTxUSteOFoHrGImYCG6-3r5yX6HjOcNv-P-c5pNPOW2Xb38lx6-lzBs9WyZmqjNlCpzKVqndM7dyo-r3HWeU2B8ADlLPPnB60AxddGcZR-jIgR2VHVU_6G51i8IlhN72i_HQn89-kFGHAYMdYVDSdMntGoDUgBJQH5XVBtGOxhqMUkWhJcXEpR55JaaXb0t-lwfVYyjXLruV-daE-hA4CZxe-ytw-irr9lnq9t4ETo0935vACQHsgGpQYMAYqe2ouuri7ZlyTq23QsvL1af8R_M_izwc_gYAAP__J4ZyYg), offering to help with the transition. Talarico, a 37-year-old Austin state representative, will be the Senate's youngest member. He will be the first Democrat to represent Texas in the Senate since Robert Krueger, who was [appointed in 1993](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO8yAQBOCnwZ0tWIixC4q_cZe_vdLawDpGIgbBXpx7-1PyCleORvpGmq_resWY4nH_jw9y_NryetDZEjFTXSmR55iPSu07ccuFKr5zWEHC2CvVS7Oi5_ikVXXB3WSYVUdO2VnbWY-T6XYXtDbjDQEUkbEbTX5Uk7kp3GiUI8guuremlDQKpAIzaGsuAHa-2AsEqYMwkkLkXAfeiemFbUs_-Ul18PnRJbczlyb0PwGLgOU8z8HvNR_vVsBScoocfROwYOXoEwlYGBPW6HNf8MX56D9q3-hApr6ipx7ATHaSeih76aoL5YwpxTZaYeT9gTF9xvmPnz0d_AYAAP__1maBcQ) to fill Lloyd Bentsen's vacancy.
## Democrats Lead Down-Ballot Races
Democrats also led all six of Texas' other statewide executive races on Tuesday, [according to returns](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0Luu4yAQBuCnwd1EMMbmuHCxjbuz7ZYWl3GCRCCCSZy8_Yqttj_dXKRP-v8_3_u3jSnm6297p5XfR9kznS0RM9WdEnmOJVdqz8StPKjavocdJc6gFEi9W8_xRbsawupkWNRAqzLLaJZx_tLDbQ1fYTLTjBqdm-RoSKOa3EzO0TLOzgxx7ZpSUiuUCvVlNHpCNMtkJgxyDEJLCpFLvfCNmN62HelTXlQvvtyHtN6YH02MvwRuArfzPC_Z-XCc_S1w64EEbo-SIkffx1QyQWNb4b9jh3MDLhDIx0BQMljIdIJlLjXTB66UqdoENgc4yrNC4RvVLjEBvck_exVQjiN6ah3I5QWjwE3LBZWcBW5DXcPjjCnFNhuh5fVuY_oXhH_Y_2vFvwEAAP__fBCciw) available at our deadline. Democratic state Rep. Vikki Goodwin led Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick 51.9% to 45.6%, as Patrick sought a fourth term. In the open race to succeed Ken Paxton as attorney general, Democratic state Sen. Nathan Johnson led Republican state Sen. Mayes Middleton 52% to 46%. For comptroller, Democratic state Sen. Sarah Eckhardt led acting Comptroller Don Huffines 51% to 46%. Democrat Benjamin Flores led incumbent Land Commissioner Dawn Buckingham 51.5% to 47%. For agriculture commissioner, Democrat Clayton Tucker led Republican Nate Sheets 51.4% to 46.8%. Sheets had ousted longtime Commissioner Sid Miller in the March primary. In the Railroad Commission race, Democrat Jon Rosenthal led Republican Bo French 52.6% to 45.6%.

According to a menopause specialist, when estrogen drops after 50, the relative balance of [a hormone called DHT rises](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkEGK4zAURE8j72KkL9myFloMBBNmcJhFQzfZCNn6TgSKHazvOLl9475CL4tXVBX12bnOxxSn69nf0dJrnN2EW05IhIvDhAPFeVowr4ny_MDF7zo44FAfhDhw5fxA8YlOFMH2PBhRoBXaSG1k3ajiZuumUmCGsR-MFL4y3NfjKBvfDBCwN6GIdk8TgisBXIAqpVYVgDaVriBwGZjiGCLNS0k3JHz5PKb3_MSlHOZ7keyN6JGZ_MOgZdBu21aO6_U97ZRB-_H_X1f_PZ8YtF9dezl1x8tulO0aA5NHxbViUOe1F0we8e5jcvsWl8kTFosNjy2mFHOtmeLXnf_U0i_felr4DgAA__8vNnvy). And DHT is known for one thing: shrinking hair follicles. That's why so many women who never had hair trouble in their 30s and 40s suddenly see it later. It's also why thickening shampoos and biotin gummies often disappoint. [They don't address what's happening at the follicle](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkEGK4zAURE8j72KkL9myFloMBBNmcJhFQzfZCNn6TgSKHazvOLl9475CL4tXVBX12bnOxxSn69nf0dJrnN2EW05IhIvDhAPFeVowr4ny_MDF7zo44FAfhDhw5fxA8YlOFMH2PBhRoBXaSG1k3ajiZuumUmCGsR-MFL4y3NfjKBvfDBCwN6GIdk8TgisBXIAqpVYVgDaVriBwGZjiGCLNS0k3JHz5PKb3_MSlHOZ7keyN6JGZ_MOgZdBu21aO6_U97ZRB-_H_X1f_PZ8YtF9dezl1x8tulO0aA5NHxbViUOe1F0we8e5jcvsWl8kTFosNjy2mFHOtmeLXnf_U0i_felr4DgAA__8vNnvy). The good news? She says many of those follicles aren't gone, just dormant. Her approach skips the serums and foams entirely. It's two capsules a day, built around a mineral pairing many women over 50 run low on. On this day in 1835 , delegates to the Texas Consultation finally at San Felipe de Austin and chose Branch T. Archer to preside. Nine days later, they formed a provisional government and named Sam Houston army commander. Have you heard you're not supposed to drink coffee on an empty stomach? The warning is all over social media, and it claims that the first cup before breakfast is doing damage you can't feel. Gastroenterologists just weighed in, and their answer isn't what the internet says. Researchers performed endoscopies on more than 8,000 people to test the claim. A separate experiment found one common morning combo that backfires, sending blood sugar climbing when you'd least want it. So is your pre-breakfast cup safe or not? Gina Hinojosa on Tuesday, becoming Texas' first Latina governor and ending Republican control of the office that began in 1995. She led 57% to 42% when Abbott conceded. Abbott called Hinojosa to concede, then in Austin, "There are still votes to be counted, but mathematically, we're not going to be able to win this election." He pledged to help her team with the transition. "Everything is bigger in Texas, including the shock of this win ," Hinojosa in Austin. The Rio Grande Valley native added that no one imagined "a little girl from the RGV would stand before you here as the next governor." "It never bothered me that they doubted me, it bothered me that they doubted us ," Hinojosa . She is the first Democrat elected governor since Ann Richards in 1990. Talarico Flips U.S. Senate Seat Democrat James Talarico on Tuesday, becoming the first Democrat Texans have elected to the U.S. Senate since 1988. With about two-thirds of the vote counted, he led roughly 59% to 39%. Paxton Tuesday night. This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College

| | Dear Fellow American, How are you today? Here on campus, it’s not unusual to see students wandering back and forth outside a classroom, practicing before a big test. It reminds me of the story of someone else who wandered around, searching for something he lost... **The Headless Horseman.** According to the legend, this Hessian soldier was decapitated by a cannonball during the Revolutionary War. Gruesome, right? Well, each night, his ghost rides through Sleepy Hollow, searching for his missing head. It’s the unforgettable image at the heart of Washington Irving’s “The Legend of Sleepy Hollow.” But Irving’s story isn’t just a ghost story we tell around Halloween. **It’s a tale about what happens when people lose touch with their past.** The past is old stories, myths, landmarks, and traditions that connect the people of Sleepy Hollow to those who came before them. Irving understood something we desperately need to remember today: **A people who forget the stories that made them will lose the inheritance those stories built.** As in the town of Sleepy Hollow, too many Americans today are losing touch with the past — reframing or abandoning the founding stories and myths that built America. But those stories are too important to surrender, especially because no inheritance passes itself on. Someone must preserve it. Someone must teach it. And someone must make sure the next generation understands why it matters. That’s why Hillsdale College continues to teach great American works like “The Legend of Sleepy Hollow _._ ” The story is featured in our new **American Folktales** , an online course taught by Hillsdale College Professor Kevin Slack, who teaches about American politics, history, and culture here on campus. Professor Slack brings greater context and insight to familiar stories—revealing what memorable characters like Ichabod Crane and the Headless Horseman can teach us about human nature, early America, and the stories that shaped it. **The full short study is available now,** but to help you get even more from the course, **we’ve created a special American Folktales Study Guide that is available as a FREE download here:** **[https://info.hillsdale.edu/american-folk-tales](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0c2O1DAMB_CnSW-t8tVpe-hhxTCCwyyCOXCMguO0FvkoTbqIt0dFOy_AzbL_8k-yv9_N3VKgtLzaiDOVYlx2ZsVS0O6wUlp83kuOWM96NZLLSytEy7WxUOkNjbaNm3spRj82OIthUsM0qEk169z3UvfTJAC4l15bQIABRz15P-IAoqH53CcE10JxJWTnBNcj9B5-aHe5-IlpfmzOVuwoFXJYIOdty4EqQenyvjRhXmvdClMvTN6YvFHyuVsphOJswA7dweTNRtwJbGp9Dj_bagMWpm4Fl4ipfsgOmbpyJXVvOfcQcXHZIf5i8nLUaEo-djgj257LhlApLe-jiI6OyNQVo6Xw3gQbN0tLYur6hM0J_3NNqYf7sxzk8BnPqWKqTF0_ffn2-Hh_eTVfh_bz49E-j9Pss9t-UwhULgPTfDmxDnJs6v--7G2WfwMAAP__JuarBw)** Inside this special resource, you’ll find background on the stories, key themes and characters, discussion questions, and insights you may not have considered. Luka now alleges that the medical professionals who treated her failed to provide the proper standard of care and failed to obtain informed consent. **Her case is headed toward a jury trial currently scheduled for June, 2027.** **But the legal battle is already raging. **Right now, the defendants are challenging expert testimony Luka intends to present regarding the standard of care. **These kinds of fights mean more motions, more legal work, more time, and more expense. **

clean_body: Powerful institutions can drag out a lawsuit. Your support helps us keep fighting. | | | | Peter, | | | Her name is Luka Hein. She was 16 years old when doctors removed her breasts. Now she wants a jury to hear what happened to her. But getting Luka into that courtroom has become a battle of its own. I'm Mark Trammell, CEO of theCenter for American Liberty , a nonprofit public interest law firm that takes on cases many organizations won't touch. And I'm asking you to help us fight for Luka. As we described in her lawsuit, Luka was a deeply troubled teenager. Her parents had divorced. She struggled with anxiety, isolation, school, panic attacks, self-harm, and thoughts of suicide. Then she encountered transgender influencers online. At 15, Luka began receiving gender-related care. At 16, doctors removed her breasts. Testosterone came months later. Luka now alleges that the medical professionals who treated her failed to provide the proper standard of care and failed to obtain informed consent. Her case is headed toward a jury trial currently scheduled for June, 2027. But the legal battle is already raging. Right now, the defendants are challenging expert testimony Luka intends to present regarding the standard of care. These kinds of fights mean more motions, more legal work, more time, and more expense. And that can become a strategy all its own -- make litigation so long and expensive that the other side runs out of resources. We refuse to let that happen. We've been here before. The Center for American Liberty represents detransitioner Chloe Cole in her lawsuit against the medical providers she alleged harmed her. The hospital defendants aggressively filed motions delaying Chloe's trial by years. We fought back and now Chloe's trial is scheduled for April. We are prepared to fight just as hard for Luka. But unlike the powerful institutions we face, the Center for American Liberty is a nonprofit. We depend on Americans like you. This is why our organization exists. There are Americans all across this country who have been silenced, pushed out, or left to fight powerful institutions alone. We stand beside them. And we fight. I came to the Center for American Liberty because I wanted to get my hands dirty and be in the courtroom fighting these cases because somebody has to do it. As I often ask: Who 's going to represent these people if we don't? Luka had the courage to put her name on this lawsuit. She is prepared to tell a jury what happened. 714,000 people saw that post. The campaigns saw it too. Then Detroit came out, and a man who swore he could spot one of us from across the room learned that he had been talking to one of my journalists all along.

Then Detroit came out, and a man who swore he could spot one of us from across the room learned that he had been talking to one of my journalists all along. So what's on the other tapes? Thank you Wake County!
Last night, you elected me as your next District Attorney. I'm humbled by your support, and ready to get to work on January 1st.
I'm going to be focused on justice and accountability. That means keeping families safe, going after violent criminals, and standing up for victims. And it means everyone gets treated the same under the law, no matter who they are or who they know.
It was a huge night for Democrats, too. Roy Cooper is headed to the U.S. Senate. Democrats flipped the U.S. House and the Senate in a major way. When I was in Congress, I voted for Hakeem Jeffries 19 times for Speaker. I'm very glad my friend is about to get that gavel.
So many of you knocked doors, made calls and showed up to make this happen. You earned it. The American people sent a clear message that they're tired of corruption and they want elected officials who will solve real problems.
Now I'd love to be able to take a victory lap and just celebrate these amazing wins for a minute. But I need to be straight with you. There are immediate fights coming very soon, and they won't wait. One is about who gets to prosecute corruption in North Carolina. The other is about whether this office has the people it needs to keep you safe.
### **The corruption fight**
Because the state capital is in Wake County, the Wake DA's office handles public corruption cases involving state government. When state money gets misspent or someone in power breaks the law, this is the office that decides whether or not to investigate and prosecute those cases.
Political corruption was the issue I heard about most on the campaign trail. People are fed up, and they should be.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4e1e3c20-1b4d-42f1-8526-fb0911494820?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now, [The News & Observer reports](https://substack.com/redirect/4e1e3c20-1b4d-42f1-8526-fb0911494820?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Republican lawmakers are considering returning to Raleigh in just a few days and using the post-election lame duck session to strip the Wake DA's office of that authority.
We've seen this before. In 2016, after Roy Cooper won the governor's race, legislators held a lame duck session, stripped the incoming governor's power to appoint university trustees, and made his cabinet picks subject to Senate confirmation. They also tried to cut his political appointees from 1,500 to 425 and tried to take away his control of the State Board of Elections. Courts struck down those last two.
In 2024, after Josh Stein won the governor's race, lawmakers did it again. They used a Helene relief bill to move State Board of Elections appointments from the incoming governor to the Republican state auditor.
And we know what happens when politicians take corruption cases away from the capital. Texas did it in 2015. The Texas legislature passed a law that took corruption cases against state lawmakers out of Austin and handed them to a DA in each lawmaker's home county. So a legislator accused of corruption now gets charged or not charged by a prosecutor who runs for office in the same county, often from the same party. That's generally letting politicians pick their own friendly prosecutor. According to a 2021 Texas Observer investigation cited by the N&O, corruption prosecutions dropped significantly afterward. That's not accountability.
Here's my view. Any law that changes who prosecutes politicians, written by politicians, should get a lot of scrutiny. If a nurse or a truck driver breaks the law, they answer for it. The same has to be true for the most powerful people in state government.
I don't care if you're a Democrat or a Republican. If you break the law in Wake County, you'll be held accountable.
### **The funding fight**
I'm inheriting the worst funded District Attorney's office in North Carolina.
Mecklenburg County has 95 prosecutors. Wake has just 45. That's less than 65% of what the courts' own workload formula says we need.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/11f4f7a2-1971-4211-a3ef-0d3f5eaa3874?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This year, it looked like help was coming. [The Senate budget included 10 new prosecutors for Wake](https://substack.com/redirect/c0693dec-0b69-4220-9282-e629b11e110e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). By the time the final budget passed, every one of them was gone. The budget funded 18 new prosecutors across the state. Wake got zero.
Here's what that means for public safety. The average caseload for a Wake County prosecutor is over 2,500 cases a year. That's more than double the average caseload in Mecklenburg and Durham where its an average of just over 1,000 cases a year. When there aren't enough prosecutors, victims have to wait years rather than months for justice, and repeat offenders stay out on the streets much longer. We're all less safe as a result.
### **What 's next**
I'll keep pushing the General Assembly and the Wake County Board of Commissioners to fund this office. If a Wake DA bill drops in the General Assembly during the lame duck session you'll hear about it here first.
But those fights don't change how excited I am to do this job. There are some truly amazing public servants in the DAs office, and I can't wait to work alongside them.
### **Save the date**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9b06593f-bf9d-4c02-ae3f-edb3df4df3d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I'm getting sworn in on Tuesday, January 5th, at 1 p.m. at the Wake County Justice Center. It's a public ceremony and everyone's invited.
You got us here, and I'll never forget it. I'm going to work every day to build a District Attorney's office worthy of the trust you've placed in me.
Wiley

body:
|
Cinde Warmington is running for Governor because she believes that everyone in New Hampshire deserves leaders who are going to help them and their families get ahead. If you’d like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3-gP0Xd1LL-Lub7Gk22PHy9ShbPgxu4DFRkJPyKXJZ7SucX1CdKgpVQPvMXIjKiagYZNJ54LFIKIpOtkR29qnwmAZLX-_-ehVjRTq0El2tz5BqDkdPWgrWX8JbAX4BDIKxuB3r1S_V4XRo85W4-EUOmeRS5iXhmiFeFXRuKoCh8i6wF0cTnxZ2BlGWJbgqgnENlW5HozYWKIyTm_qH3Esna2CQB-1dPuQlATtrXItuQFSyrF5mEEDT_hCUa-fxTjfaxAwY9k-S-9OWfK1KWqJH8qz6snHKHGvXLr1_1BR_U8K0L0M-bCIFIq37KZtt5bYVLo7Tsu1l8YQiBP72jjBIPnSlMxMbDKG5Wo2zq3W7ciSPh0gV3FTNuHyMBzTACbfamUWRwMGG8tQmdhDukjZCK/4vg/bC5vnnQfS2y5GjtxBui6bw/h0/h001.fq4HppnlhPLrawhuPo_LmVc2G83kLswnTdmvscgBOgo)

Thank you.
From the very beginning, this campaign was about putting the needs of working families first and fighting for a future where they can actually get ahead. It’s the very same fight I brought to the Executive Council, where I fought for Granite Staters who have been left behind for far too long.
While this isn’t the outcome we were hoping for, I am so proud of the race we ran and the support we earned across the state. I was honored to lead our party at the top of the ticket, and I’m heartened that this was such a close race even though we were outspent by more than 6 to 1.
I’m proud that we fought for public education, housing, and health care, and that we stood up against the corruption and self-dealing that has made its way to Concord from Washington. Most of all, I’m proud that we fought for a more affordable New Hampshire without ever compromising our values.
And I’m pleased that the fight for those values will continue with strong majorities on the Executive Council and in the Senate and House.
I called Kelly Ayotte to congratulate her on her victory. I wish her the best in her second term, and I hope she will work collaboratively with the newly elected Democratic majorities, because we have real challenges ahead. It will take all of us, working together, to tackle them.
I want to thank my husband Bill, my mom, my two kids, my four beautiful grandkids, and my entire family for their love and support every step of the way. I want to recognize my campaign team for their hard work and late nights. And thank you to every single volunteer, donor, and supporter who gave this campaign their all and fought hard for a better tomorrow.
Even if you’re disappointed, please don’t ever stop fighting. This work remains unfinished, and we need you.
Thank you, New Hampshire.

clean_body: | Cinde Warmington is running for Governor because she believes that everyone in New Hampshire deserves leaders who are going to help them and their families get ahead. If you’d like to unsubscribe, | Thank you. From the very beginning, this campaign was about putting the needs of working families first and fighting for a future where they can actually get ahead. It’s the very same fight I brought to the Executive Council, where I fought for Granite Staters who have been left behind for far too long. While this isn’t the outcome we were hoping for, I am so proud of the race we ran and the support we earned across the state. I was honored to lead our party at the top of the ticket, and I’m heartened that this was such a close race even though we were outspent by more than 6 to 1. I’m proud that we fought for public education, housing, and health care, and that we stood up against the corruption and self-dealing that has made its way to Concord from Washington. Most of all, I’m proud that we fought for a more affordable New Hampshire without ever compromising our values. And I’m pleased that the fight for those values will continue with strong majorities on the Executive Council and in the Senate and House. I called Kelly Ayotte to congratulate her on her victory. I wish her the best in her second term, and I hope she will work collaboratively with the newly elected Democratic majorities, because we have real challenges ahead. It will take all of us, working together, to tackle them. I want to thank my husband Bill, my mom, my two kids, my four beautiful grandkids, and my entire family for their love and support every step of the way. I want to recognize my campaign team for their hard work and late nights. And thank you to every single volunteer, donor, and supporter who gave this campaign their all and fought hard for a better tomorrow. Even if you’re disappointed, please don’t ever stop fighting. This work remains unfinished, and we need you. Thank you, New Hampshire. Cinde Warmington * Follow us on social! | Friends,
Elections don't always end the way we hope. Please know how much I appreciate everything you did to make this campaign possible.
---
| To everyone who knocked on doors, made phone calls, put up signs, attended events, and volunteered countless hours, I offer my heartfelt thanks. To those who contributed financially, your generosity made this campaign possible and kept our message moving across Michigan. Every hour given, every dollar contributed, and every word of encouragement helped bring this campaign to life. I am proud of what we accomplished together and deeply grateful for your belief in me.
Thank you also to everyone who sent well wishes, offered encouragement, and stood beside me. One of the greatest rewards of this journey was meeting wonderful people and making new friends across our state. Those friendships mean a great deal to me.
The Democratic Party did a tremendous job keeping its candidates focused on one central theme: opposition to the President. That became the defining message of the election, often overshadowing the responsibilities, experience, and qualifications of the offices we were seeking. We chose to focus on experience, service, accountability, and Michigan's future. I am proud of that.
A special thank you to Amy Hawkins and Scott Greenlee, who worked tirelessly behind the scenes. Their advice, guidance, encouragement, and friendship were invaluable. Much of their work happened outside the spotlight, but it made a real difference.
We may not have won, but your efforts were never wasted. I am grateful for your belief in me and for the opportunity to have shared this journey with you.
---
|
---
Anthony Forlini Macomb County Clerk

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: We won, Peter
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
None of these wins would be possible without our people-powered progressive movement.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20261104-6932-footer&t=1&akid=6932%2E420207%2EqEz-UG)
We won, Peter!
**It’s such an honor to be re-elected to represent Washington’s 7th District.** None of this would be possible without the organizers, volunteers, and voters who stuck beside me and kept this movement running. Thank you, thank you, thank you from the bottom of my heart.
And it wasn’t just me — the blue wave is here! 🌊 The people took back their power from greedy corporations and outrageous Republican dark money spending across the country:
**Abdul El-Sayed** is Michigan’s next U.S. Senator. He was up against millions of dollars in outside spending, but Michigan voters made it clear their state and their votes are not for sale. He ran on Medicare For All, refused a single cent of corporate PAC money, and stayed laser-focused on working families from day one. I’m proud to have stood with him, and I can’t wait to work with him in Washington!
**Peggy Flanagan** is Minnesota’s next U.S. Senator. Peggy is a dear friend and fellow organizer who has spent her life advocating for working families and communities that too often get overlooked. In Congress, she’s going to continue fighting for them and stand up to the Trump administration. Go Peggy!
**Sam Forstag** flipped Montana’s House seat blue! As a union leader and smokejumper (a firefighter who parachutes out of planes to battle wildfires), Sam knows what it’s like to barely scrape by even after working thousands of hours of overtime. He understands that Americans simply can’t afford for Congress to stay on the path of profit before people, and I know he’ll fight hard for working people across this country.
**Matt Little** won his seat in MN-02. I saw firsthand during the weekends I spent in Minnesota with Matt — he showed up in every community and connected with as many voters as possible. He proved that a bold agenda for working people can win _anywhere_.
**Randy Villegas** flipped CA-22! This seat was absolutely critical to taking back the House. Randy grew his campaign from the ground up, door by door and conversation by conversation. He never took a dime from anyone trying to buy his vote — he answers to working families, and no one else. He’s going to be an incredible member of our progressive movement.
**Will Lawrence** flipped MI-07! Will is an organizer at heart, and ran a true grassroots campaign across mid-Michigan. He’s going to help us pass Medicare For All and build an economy that works for working people.
A massive congratulations to every single incredible progressive fighter I’ve had the honor of rallying alongside this cycle. **Last night proved what I have always believed: when we organize, we win.**
Now the real work begins. Let’s get to it!
With so much gratitude,
Pramila Jayapal
