Hey, my fellow angry Democrats. This morning, we're waking up to a landslide.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b9edac83-7674-48ac-a158-786410b88c31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The polls were wrong, but they were wrong because they did not capture the sheer slaughter of Republicans across the country. Republicans held on to plenty of seats, but Democrats broke through in places that were supposed to be out of reach.
Democrats have won control of the House and Senate. With races still being counted, we're waiting to see just how large those majorities will become.
Yesterday, I wrote that this election would be a litmus test. Would character matter? Would broken promises matter? Would people cross party lines when they had finally had enough?
**This morning, we have an answer.**
* * *
## Ohio Showed Up
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4397e5c2-def4-4e79-8522-4680f8cfcfd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ohio Democrats flipped the 7th and 15th Congressional Districts, with a third flip projected 10th.
**Brian Poindexter defeated Max Miller.** Don Leonard defeated Mike Carey. Kristina Knickerbocker declared victory over Mike Turner, with the Associated Press call still outstanding in the early-morning reporting.
Three Republican-held districts, with two flips called by AP and another projected by Decision Desk HQ. Think about that.
**Marcy Kaptur** also held on to her seat, despite Republicans redrawing her district to make it even harder for her to win. They made the district more Republican, and she survived anyway.
Amy Acton won the governor's race. Sherrod Brown is heading back to the Senate. Democrats made gains down the ballot and into the Statehouse.
For everyone who has spent years being told that Ohio is hopeless, that these districts cannot be won, and that running in them is a waste of time, take a moment this morning.
Look at what happened. I definitely have more to say about this.
* * *
## The Local Races Count, Too
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fb8d328f-d097-4f01-abc0-a532c6e27486?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Rep Elect Megan Coy
The gains reached into our local races.
Megan Coy defeated Mike Dovilla, flipping Ohio House District 17. That is a Statehouse seat going from Republican to Democrat.
Courtney Scheff's defeated Michael Gallagher the last Republican on the Cuyahoga County Council.
These races deserve attention alongside the congressional and statewide victories. Candidates, organizers, volunteers, and local parties put in the work in districts where winning was never guaranteed.
Congratulations to everyone who ran one of those hard races. You gave voters a choice, built an organization, and made Republicans defend seats they expected to keep.
* * *
## This Was a Rejection of Trump
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8772c2b9-3626-4e26-9f7f-0397b02ff05a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
My read is straightforward: This was a mandate against Trump and his administration's betrayal of the American people.
Lower costs were promised. No more forever wars were promised. Instead, people got higher fuel costs, another prolonged war, and an administration surrounded by corruption and the use of public office for personal gain.
Voters had the opportunity to respond. They did.
The rejection reached beyond one candidate or one state. Republicans lost seats in places where Trump had won comfortably just two years ago.
I'll be writing more about what drove these results, what the polling missed, and what Democrats need to do with the power voters have handed them. There is plenty to examine.
But this morning, congratulations come first.
* * *
## Congratulations, Brian
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/49bd60af-72fa-4898-a714-0e6766c40067?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Finally, I want to say congratulations to Brian Poindexter for flipping Ohio's Seventh District and kicking Max Miller out of Congress.
Brian was the right person, with the right team, at the right time.
His hard work, organization, and coalition building delivered. He put together the campaign that could win this district, and he won it.
Having run against Max twice myself, I know what goes into taking on that race. I know the work, the fundraising, and the challenge of convincing people that a district like this is worth fighting for.
Brian and his team got it done. They deserve this moment.
To everyone who won, everyone who volunteered, everyone who knocked doors, made calls, donated, and voted: Congratulations.
What a morning.

Maybe someone in her life is pressuring her to have an abortion. But what if, before making that decision, she had the opportunity to see her baby for the very first time? **That's the life-changing opportunity your gift to PreBorn! can help provide.** Through our PreBorn! name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: We did it
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=3880%2E251025%2EzGATDi ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=3880%2E251025%2EzGATDi ]Abdul for US Senate

We did it, Michigan.

My name is Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed, and I am proud and honored to be
the Senator-elect from the great state of Michigan.

Up until this moment, you might have noticed that I always say
‘insha’Allah” or God Willing whenever the outcome of this race is
mentioned.

Today, we turn that insha’Allah into Alhamdulillah — praise be to God.

This is ALL yours. Michigan, I can’t wait to serve you with the same
big-heartedness, open-mindedness, grit, and earnestness you’ve shown me.

You welcomed me to your homes, your churches, your synagogues, your VFW,
and union halls. You shared your moments of frustration and sadness and
vulnerability with me.

You gave me grace and strength in my lowest moments, and the hope and
inspiration that powered my best.

I hope to bring it all with me to Washington in your service. Thank you
for your trust, your belief, and your kindness. I will take it all with me
to Washington — and I hope to bring back the kind of leadership that more
than earns it.

The last month has brought the stakes of this election into sharp relief.
Ours is a movement built over the past year and a half campaigning across
Michigan’s biggest cities and smallest towns. We spoke of a brighter,
bigger, more hopeful Michigan. Theirs? An astroturfed corporate-funded
advertising campaign to deceive and distract. They preached hate and fear.

Day by day, Trump’s insults became uglier and coarser. But I got to spend
those days with you — learning about your struggles, your hopes, and the
things that inspire you. A mom of two kids with a genetic lung disease in
East Jordan, fighting the system to make sure her kids don’t lose the meds
they rely on to stay alive. Her hope? That they don’t have to struggle
with health insurance like she has.

A grandma on the East Side fighting to make sure the violence that took
her son doesn’t take her grandson, too. Her hope? An America where boys
get to grow up.

I met Josh, the UAW autoworker fighting the corporate bosses who hadn’t
raised their wages in two decades — despite billions in profit. They won
that fight. His hope? An America where every single worker gets the right
to a union.

I met a small business owner fighting to make sure that another heart
attack doesn’t take food off the table for his 30 employees or their
families. His hope? That his workers don’t have to worry about how they’ll
feed their families.

I didn’t get into this to defend myself. No. I got into this because their
fights are my fight — and their hopes are all of ours.

We don’t do this work for ourselves. We do this work for each other. To
defend us all from another generation’s youth, treasure, and opportunity
squandered at the altar of endless war. To defend us all from corporate
oligarchs who’ve bought and sold our government to rig the system against
us. To defend us all from a healthcare system more interested in
monetizing our illness than healing our bodies and minds. To defend us all
from air too putrid to breathe and water too putrid to drink. To defend us
all from losing our voting or reproductive or human rights.

I ran to defend us all from politicians who want to divide us rather than
movements that work to dignify us. Across our primary and general election
campaigns, they spent over 350 million dollars trying to beat us. That’s a
record here in Michigan. 70 million alone in the primary, funded by all
the same cats who funded the general election — that’s a record anywhere
in this country!

But we built something bigger than a bank account. We built a movement.
Government of the people, by the people, and for the people.

We showed that in a battle between the money and the many — that the many
can win.

Mike, enjoy your retirement in Florida. You chose hate. Michigan chose
hope. May we never have to see the likes of you in our state again.

JD, there’s a delicious irony in the fact that you’re constitutionally
obligated to swear me in in January. Wolverine 1 - Buckeye 0.

Donald, I know you’ve struggled with my name. After JD swears me in in
January, you can just call me “Senator.”

To the Super PACs and special interests that tried to beat us, we’re
coming for your system of politics. To AIPAC, who spent $42 million
dollars against us, thank you for giving me the opportunity to beat you
twice. They try to call you hateful if you believe that Palestinian kids
should get to grow up in the land of their forefathers without being
murdered by our tax dollars. If you believe in equal rights to peace,
dignity, and self-determination. That’s not hate. It’s love.

We showed that a movement of the people, by the people, and for the people
will ultimately win — Michigan understands solidarity. It’s the people who
decide who we send to Washington and what Washington will do. We decide —
not the big money or their stooges. The people of Michigan will be heard.

We showed that we can defeat a record 70 million dollars of outside
spending and an 11-1 money disadvantage in a primary election. That we can
defeat a quarter of a billion dollars in a general election. We can defeat
the cynicism of a politics that preys on our earnestness, undersells our
intelligence, and exploits our disagreements.

Michigan, we beat a machine. And we proved once again how big America
really is. Because where else but in America can a doctor named
Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed, a child of immigrants raised by his father
and his daughter of the American revolution stepmother, get elected
senator from America’s greatest state?

To all of us: this fight is not yet over. The day I jumped into this race,
I promised you that I’d put in the work, fight the fights on your behalf.
I asked for your time, your energy, your support over the last 19 months.
Now, I’m asking for the next 6 years.

This work is bigger than one senator; it’s about changing our politics. So
please, don’t send me to DC all by myself. Come with me. Winning a single
US Senate seat was never the goal. The goal is to use that seat to
transform our politics.

The beauty and soul of America is that we, the people, are what America is
all about. We deserve an America for all of her kids.

Thank you,

Abdul

[1]Abdul El-Sayed

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Emails like this help us stay connected with grassroots supporters like you, so thank you for taking the time to read this message. To contribute via check, please address it to Abdul for U.S. Senate, PO Box 126, St. Clair Shores, MI 48080.

And, surprise surprise, the American midterm elections increasingly dominated the news. | | **OCTOBER 4, 2026**

Interest rates are on an upward march. The 10-year Treasury just hit 5.33%; the 30-year hit 5.69%. Those are 24-year highs. But this is not just an American phenomenon. The UK 30-year punched through 6% for the first time since 1998. France’s 10-year hit its highest since 2002. The bond market is telegraphing distress.

What is going on? The answer comes down to three forces. And they’re all connected.
**1\. Inflation: Stimulus & War**The inflation story started with COVID. Governments flooded their economies with trillions in stimulus, central banks monetized it, and demand came roaring back before supply chains could. That was the first wave. The second wave came from two wars. Russia’s invasion of Ukraine rapidly and massively disrupted the energy and grain markets, beginning in 2022 but continuing to the present. The Iran war compounded an already problematic situation: Goldman Sachs called the Iran War the largest oil...

| | **OCTOBER 11, 2026**
The frozen pizza business is booming...and that’s concerning. That probably sounds strange. But not if you understand what frozen pizza actually _is,_ economically speaking. Frozen pizza isn’t a product. It’s a _signal_. And right now, the signal is flashing red.
You see, frozen pizza thrives when the economy doesn’t. In 2009, at the depths of the Great Recession, frozen pizza sales surged while restaurants sat empty. When COVID hit in 2020, [sales jumped roughly a billion dollars in a single year](https://us.list-manage.com/8sV_Rwivw56?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586), from $5.6 billion to $6.6 billion. The pattern is proving so reliable, it’s almost mechanical: when families start trading down from dining out to eating in, that journey includes regular stops in the frozen food aisle.
And right now? The frozen aisle is as busy as ever.

| | **OCTOBER 18, 2026**

In March, [QatarEnergy declared _force majeure_](https://us.list-manage.com/ls29ctAlwNA?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586) on its natural gas exports. One announcement, one simple sentence. And just like that, twenty percent of the world’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply went offline. Seven months later, it’s still dark. [In the first six months of the war](https://us.list-manage.com/LnSMBTxXO5H?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586), Qatar shipped 18 LNG cargoes. In the same period the year before, it shipped 509. The lost sales are valued at around $24 billion. As of this writing, there’s still no firm date for resumption.
Natural gas supplies [about a quarter of the world’s energy](https://us.list-manage.com/j6gooJvl_gV?e=93b2c2b824&c2id=8d3705edc40ffd26940a732b7f12f586), and LNG (gas chilled to negative 162 degrees Celsius until it liquefies and shrinks to one six-hundredth of its volume) is how it crosses oceans to countries that need it most. If you’re unfamiliar with how this actually happens...

| | **OCTOBER 25, 2026**

In 1972, a journalist asked Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai about the impact of the French Revolution. His answer, the story goes, was, “It’s too early to say.” The line has become a staple of geopolitical commentary. It’s a great reminder that revolutions unfold on very long timelines (and that the Chinese generally think about dynamics over the long-term compared vs. the short attention spans of the West). Interestingly, some thought Enlai was being asked about the then-more-recent 1968 student protests that had rocked the country, but whether he was referring to 1789 or 1968, the quote is worth keeping in mind, because, as this weekend’s activity showed, the next revolution seems to be underway.
It started with a high school in Créteil. On September 21, the day after their teachers went on strike, students at the Lycée Antoine-de-Saint-Exupéry in the Paris suburbs walked out over unfilled teaching posts, classroom sizes of 35, and rooms without enough tables. By the end of the month, more than a thousand lycées were disrupted. On one day in particular, French police had arrested nearly 2,000 people (mostly minors). Within a month, the unrest had grown from just students to include teachers, parents, unions, farmers and Yellow Vest veterans. Hundreds of thousands of people were in the streets and the historic town hall in Limoges, a building that survived two world wars, was burning...

Dear Patriot,

My name is James O'Keefe. For twenty years I have sent undercover
reporters into places powerful people would rather you never see, and
I have published exactly what those cameras recorded.

THAT WORK MAKES ENEMIES, AND A NUMBER OF THEM RESPOND BY FILING
LAWSUITS.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom._ZA/sbq55c266c5
[Donation Page]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom._ZA/sbq55c266c5

In 2016 we placed a reporter inside Democracy Partners, a Democratic
consulting firm founded by longtime operative Robert Creamer, whose
organizations worked with the Democratic National Committee during
that election. She accepted an unpaid role, answered phones, and
recorded what people around her said. We published it.

They sued me in June 2017, and a jury eventually found against us,
entering a $130,000 judgment on the books.

We appealed, and then we waited for years while continuing to pay
attorneys.

► WATCH JAMES O'KEEFE'S REACTION AND CHIP IN $35 ◄
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom._ZA/sbq55c266c5
On AUGUST 21, 2026, the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled in our
favor TWO TO ONE, and the entire judgment was erased.

Here is why that decision matters far beyond me.

The verdict had rested on the idea that our undercover reporter owed a
FIDUCIARY DUTY to the organization she was investigating. Read that
again, because it would mean a journalist who takes an internship to
document wrongdoing is legally required to protect the interests of
the people committing it. That theory WOULD EFFECTIVELY END UNDERCOVER
REPORTING IN THIS COUNTRY.

The appeals court threw it out, holding that she was NEVER A FIDUCIARY
because she performed clerical tasks and had no power to act for the
firm. With the fiduciary theory gone, the wiretapping claims fell with
it. The judges also held that a plaintiff cannot collect damages when
protected speech, rather than unlawful conduct, caused the harm, and
they found that the "VAST SHARE" of our published material had been
lawfully obtained.

Nine years of my life, and the result is federal appellate case law
that protects the next reporter who does what we did.

► STAND WITH JAMES O'KEEFE. DONATE TO THE O'KEEFE DEFENSE FUND
HOSTED BY LIBERTY GUARD. ◄
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom._ZA/sbq55c266c5
I want you to understand the game being played here, because winning
was never really the objective.

People who cannot beat our reporting take us to court to drain us
instead. Depositions replace investigations, filing deadlines replace
field work, and legal invoices arrive every single month for nine
years running. If they can keep me busy and broke, they never have to
answer a single question our cameras raised.

That is why the O'KEEFE DEFENSE FUND exists. It pays the attorneys, it
keeps my reporters working, and it converts each attack into precedent
that protects the journalist who comes after us.

► CHIP IN $35 AND HELP US FIGHT THE NEXT ONE ◄
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom._ZA/sbq55c266c5
The fund is NEARLY EMPTY after this appeal, and other cases are still
open.

If you believe a reporter with a camera should be able to walk into a
room and show you the truth, then I am asking you to send whatever you
can today. Any amount helps, and all of it goes to the fight.

THEY HAD NINE YEARS TO BREAK ME. I AM UNDEFEATED.

For Liberty,[James O'Keefe]
James O'Keefe
Founder and CEO
O'Keefe Media Group

P.S. The court's ruling did not simply clear a debt, it established a
rule that every undercover journalist in America can now stand on.

| | Yesterday, Democrats won big, electing new generations of leadership across the country. **Thank you all for giving us this experience of waking up today with hope. You took democracy into your own hands and stepped up to speak out against Trump's lawlessness and corruption.** And the voters were clear about why. 90% of voters say government corruption was a factor in their congressional vote. Voters stepped up for a new vision of politics where public servants work for the people to secure the future their families deserve. This is about building a future where every child, every senior, and every family can get the healthcare they need. Where our tax dollars go towards healthcare and housing, not wars and corruption. And where the American people can trust that Washington is working for them, not the billionaires or special interests. **I've always said election day is the starting line, not the finish line. body:
[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261104-61968&t=1001&akid=61968%2E1407376%2EEyM8xO ]Demand Justice PAC[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261104-61968&t=1002&akid=61968%2E1407376%2EEyM8xO ]Demand Justice PAC

Last night
was a huge win in the fight for Supreme Court reform.

Voters in four key Senate races elected candidates who aren’t afraid to
say it: the Court needs reform.

* Abdul El-Sayed (Michigan): “I believe in Supreme Court reform. There
is nothing in the Constitution that says there have to be nine
judges.”
* Troy Jackson (Maine): “I’m not against putting more people on the
Court, because this Court is obviously not working. It’s working at
the behest of Donald Trump and the billionaire class.”
* Peggy Flanagan (Minnesota): “I think it’s absolutely time to overhaul
the Supreme Court and expand it.”
* James Talarico (Texas): “I am open to a discussion about expanding the
number of justices.”

For years, Washington insiders said court reform was too risky to say out
loud. Voters just proved them wrong.

This is exactly what Demand Justice has been fighting for.

From day one, our mission has been clear: root out corruption in our
courts and make sure they work for the people, not for Trump, his
billionaire backers, and corporations.

We’ve exposed the Roberts majority that has shredded precedent, gutted
rights, and treated its own ethics like optional suggestions. And we’ve
refused to accept that a captured Court is just the way things have to be.

Last night, voters showed they’re with us. Court reform isn’t a fringe
idea anymore. It’s a winning position.

And this is only the beginning. Every new voice for reform makes the next
one easier. Every win brings us closer to a Supreme Court that answers to
the Constitution and the people, not to the powerful few who’ve spent
years trying to buy it.

Our movement to fix the Court is growing, and we’re not slowing down.
Thank you for standing with us this cycle. You helped get us here. Now
let’s keep building on this victory.

In solidarity,

Demand Justice PAC

Supreme Court reform just became impossible to ignore. Now we have to keep
the momentum going.

name: Jane Fonda
subject: We flipped the flippin’ U.S. House and Senate!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee
body:
# [](https://act.janepac.com/go/30?t=1&akid=17%2E6803%2EOgbz03)
What a night.
**YOU, yes you, helped flip the flippin’ U.S. House and Senate! We’re changing who our government serves because of your support._Just take a look for yourself:_**
✅**In my home state of California, Randy Villegas unseated David Valadao!** He overcame over $14 million in spending against him to flip this seat. Randy ran on a fierce, unapologetic platform for working families, and he’s ready to take on polluters and the Washington establishment in D.C.
✅ **In Michigan, tens of millions in outside spending couldn’t stop Will Lawrence from flipping the 7th Congressional District. It was a close one,** but Will never compromised on his call for a national moratorium on runaway data centers. His victory proved that voters will not let AI tech monopolies treat our communities like their personal playground.
✅ **In Texas, Gina Hinojosa unseated one of the most powerful incumbents in the heart of oil and gas country!** She faced at least $281 million in spending from Greg Abbott _and_ millions from Elon Musk. But money couldn't stop her from making history as Texas's first Democratic governor in over three decades!
✅ **In Minnesota, Peggy Flanagan overcame millions in outside spending in the primary and a MAGA opponent in the general election.** She’s now the first Native American woman elected to the U.S. Senate! JanePAC backed Peggy from the start, and we can’t wait to see fierce spirit in Washington.
A new day is here. I can feel it in my bones.
A few years ago, who could have imagined we'd elect climate champions in places where Big Oil once seemed untouchable?
Together, we’re restoring hope in what politics can be. Government _can_ work for the many, not just the privileged few. Every one of these climate champions is proof of that.
**I cannot tell you how honored I am to be part of this movement with you.**
Wherever you call home, these victories are _your_ victories. Volunteers knocked on doors, organizers brought communities together, and grassroots donors gave whatever they could.
THIS is what I’ve spent my life fighting for. The belief that every single one of us has the power to change things. That hope isn't sitting back and waiting for a better world to come along.
Hope is putting our values into action.
And last night, we did what we do best: **we showed up in numbers they couldn’t ignore.**
The many proved more powerful than the money. This new dawn belongs to all of us.
From the bottom of my heart, thank you.
xx Jane

IDCCA is proud of everything we did to assist the statewide coordinated campaign in getting out the vote, as well as all of our persuasion and communication efforts including our statewide TV ad, our billboards, and our mail campaign.

If you made a contribution over the last 2 years, you helped make these victories possible. If you attend the County Chairs’ Brunch, attend our 10th Annual Boot Camp training, bought our merch, interacted on social media, or opened an email from us – _**thank you.**_

We proved a point to Trump, to MAGA, and their Illinois GOP enablers yesterday. We made it clear that we won’t stand for their blatant corruption and greed.

Last night was incredible, and we are so grateful to you.

– IDCCA

name: Molly Gray
subject: We won. Thank you.
body:
I am still taking it all in. And before anything else, I wanted to say thank you. Dear Peter, Good morning! I am still taking it all in. And before anything else, **I wanted to say thank you. ** To the people who believed in this campaign from the very beginning, taking a chance on me wasn't necessarily the easiest decision: thank you. To our small but mighty campaign team, our interns, and the countless volunteers who knocked doors, made more than 50,000 calls, and sent over 125,000 text messages, _this victory belongs to you, too._ Over the last ten months, we traveled across Vermont, listened to our neighbors, and brought people into a conversation about a different future for our state. More than 1,600 Vermonters from all 14 counties helped fund this campaign. We did it without accepting a dime of corporate or corporate PAC money. And we won by focusing on the issues that matter: making health care more accessible, addressing our housing crisis, lowering costs for working families, and standing up for our neighbors and our shared values. We did it the Vermont way: by keeping it positive and focusing on solutions. We also showed that politics in Vermont can look different. That we can lift people up rather than tear them down. That we can bring people together across communities, backgrounds, and beliefs. And that we don't have to accept the status quo simply because that’s the way things have always been done. While I didn’t agree with his style of campaigning, I want to recognize John Rodgers and thank him for his 18 years of service and his advocacy for rural Vermont. I also want to thank Ryan McLaren and Esther Charlestin for their hard-fought campaigns in the primary, and every candidate across Vermont who stepped forward to serve their communities. There were some incredible wins in the legislature last evening. That being said, this election was not a mandate. It was an opportunity. An opportunity to urgently deliver meaningful results for Vermonters. I don’t take the support or the vote of a single Vermonter for granted. I know both the joy and optimism of a victory, and the very public pain of a loss. But here’s what I have learned: When you love Vermont, when you love her people, and when you believe in what her future can be, **there is no giving up. ** **Not when the outcome isn't what you hoped for. Not when times are difficult. Not ever. ** I understand the responsibility that comes with this office, and I promise to bring urgency, experience, and a willingness to work with anyone. I will fight for working families. I will work alongside our Legislature and statewide elected leaders to advance practical solutions that make life more affordable. And when Vermont’s rights and freedoms are threatened, I will stand shoulder to shoulder with our leaders to protect every Vermonter. From the very beginning, we said we weren’t just building a coalition to win an election. We were building a coalition to do some important work. Yesterday, we proved what is possible. Today, we get some rest and prepare for the work ahead. Thank you for believing in me and this campaign! With so much gratitude, _Molly Gray_ | | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142879597/658355798/679520187?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZDA1MWNhYy01ZWQ4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-sc48h4FwQJb0R14tKrvYz2OZDv7E2av0w9ugmFz1W0=)

| | | Peter, What a night. We’ve only got good news, because there is so much of it. **Here in Massachusetts,** we re-elected our incredible Constitutional officers, sending Governor Maura Healey and Lieutenant Governor Kim Driscoll back to the corner office to keep moving Massachusetts forward for every person in our great Commonwealth. In the State Legislature, we expanded our blue majority, and our fantastic Senator, Ed Markey, is heading back to the U.S. Senate to continue fighting for working-class people across Massachusetts and our nation. **And across the country,** Democrats have won back the House _and_ the Senate. We flipped governorships in Texas, Georgia, Iowa, Ohio, and Nevada, victories in states that so many had long written off. Voters rejected division and hate and instead chose leaders who will fight for them. But the scoreboard is only the beginning of the story. Here is what last night really means. It means people showed up. They looked at the cost of living, at their health care, at who is actually looking out for them, and they turned out in force to ask for something better. It means no place is out of reach. A Democrat is headed to the Senate from Texas for the first time in decades. Georgia has elected the first Black woman governor in American history. Maine sent Republican Senator Susan Collins packing, 100 days after engaging in an unprecedented process to nominate Troy Jackson. Democrats won races in states that even the most tuned-in of national pundits never bothered to get briefed on. So the next time someone tells you the map is set in stone, remember last night and smile. It means our values are not fragile. Right here in Massachusetts, voters upheld our gun safety law, passed Election Day registration, said no to big money in our primary elections, gave public defenders the right to unionize, and said no to repealing legal cannabis. That is our Commonwealth, speaking loudly and proudly. And it means that no race, in any state, is untouchable. So when someone tells you the best days are behind us, remember who you are and where you live. Progress was never handed down. It was built, argued over, and often paid for by people who never lived to see the result. Last night, you added your chapter to the story, one door knocked, one call made, one neighbor convinced at a time. There's work ahead: lowering costs, improving schools, building housing people can afford, creating government people can trust. We'll get to it, together, and we'll be in touch very soon about how you can support these efforts. But not today. Today, you celebrate. Call a friend. Raise a glass. Dance in the kitchen. Because Democrats, **we f*cking did it.** Sincerely,

**Wednesday, November 4, 2026**
My brother and I were going over the list yesterday.
Turkey. Arroz con gandules. Candied sweet potatoes. Bread stuffing. Salad. Alcapurrias. Flan cheesecake.
"Oh, and I want to make that dip I told you about," he said. "But let's not go overboard. Remember last time? After you left, I kept finding more food. Where it came from, I don't know."
"What are you talking about? We can eat it the next day. It's a little like Sukkot. Thanksgiving is all about having food in abundance."
"What are we having for appetizers?" he asked.
I started thinking back to what we had last year.
There is always room for more.
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper. **
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

Thank you.
I'm honored beyond words to be elected as New Hampshire's next U.S. Senator.
Voters said, in a resounding voice, that America needs a course correction. Washington needs a new generation at the table to fix things. And New Hampshire needs independent leadership to stand up and get things done.
Voters in New Hampshire and all across the country have simply had enough and are demanding a change in direction. **And I 'm ready to fight with everything I've got to deliver the change we need.**
New Hampshire, we must be clear-eyed about the scale of the challenges we face and the work it'll take to move forward.
Whether it's building the housing Granite Staters need, expanding access to health care and child care, saving Social Security, protecting our planet, restoring reproductive freedom, rooting out corruption, or holding the administration accountable, we don't have a moment to waste.
There will be moments ahead that test our resolve, and there will be times when we hit roadblocks and get frustrated with the pace of progress.
But we can never give up, and we must be committed to renewing the purpose of American democracy and working with persistence and urgency every day.
I'll be honored to stand shoulder to shoulder with you, to work with anyone willing to deliver for the people of New Hampshire, and to stand up to anyone who tries to set us back.
**Across the state Granite Staters are showing the fighting spirit, resilience, and determination we 're known for.**
That's how we do things in New Hampshire. We step up, we roll up our sleeves, and we make it happen. And that's the spirit I'll bring to my work in the Senate.
_This was a hard-won victory._
Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and the corporate special interests threw money, attack ads, and outright lies at us for months. _$67 million worth of it._ But we beat them anyway.
Whether you chipped in, made phone calls, knocked on doors, talked to your friends and neighbors about what's at stake, or simply kept up with our campaign by reading emails like this one. _Thank you._ I wouldn't be here without you.
So as we celebrate, let's think about the brighter future that we will build together. Let's remember what's possible when we join with a common purpose to fight for a freer, fairer New Hampshire.
Let's keep going.
Thank you,
Chris Pappas

name: Ken Martin
subject: About last night:
body:
The strength of our grassroots movement was on full display last night. [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/98055?t=1&akid=10234%2E22930333%2EsqDRYn)
---
Derek, The American people sent a powerful message to Donald Trump and his MAGA cronies in Congress last night. **Democrats across the country swept races up and down the ballot in a historic blue wave. They campaigned on bringing down costs and ending Trump’s rampant corruption. They put in the hard work on the ground, and won. Make no mistake: The strength of our grassroots movement was on _full display_ last night.** We went up against MAGA billionaires hellbent on dismantling our democracy and buying political power for themselves. They thought they could drown out the voice of the people with their chaos, division, and dark money, _but they were wrong_. **Together, we proved them wrong. Together, we proved that, when we stand united, no amount of money can stop the power of the people.** **We all have a lot to be proud of, Derek._Take a moment to feel that pride, that joy, and that relief._** [**But after you take that moment, we need to shift our focus and momentum to our next goal: Keeping control of Congress and taking back the White House in 2028. This fight is far from over, and the work to win in 2028 starts right now. If you're ready to keep building our Democratic movement, please chip in $7 to help us lay the groundwork for electing the next Democratic president and Democrats up and down the ballot in two years.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.gb4rMu&refcode=em_20261104_10234_fr&amount=7&t=6&akid=10234%2E22930333%2EsqDRYn) Our wins this year didn't happen by chance — they were built block by block, neighborhood by neighborhood. Democrats won up and down the ballot across the country, because supporters like you chipped in $5 or $7 at a time to help us. Here’s what their donations funded: Over the past two years, the DNC built a relentless, year-round organizing operation to ensure we’re connecting with voters and communities every single day.
* **Our State Partnership Program** delivered historic funding directly to state Democratic parties, establishing deep, year-round infrastructure nationwide.
* **We built organizing and training programs** that expanded grassroots Democratic power by equipping **_tens of thousands_** of staff, volunteers, and candidates through our national organizing programs. These volunteers made 3.3 million calls and sent 19.2 million texts to get out the vote for our Democratic candidates up and down the ballot in this election.
* **And we focused on Voter Protection & Legal Actions,** taking the Trump administration to court when they tried to undermine voting rights, defending free and fair elections nationwide, and deploying thousands of election observers all across the country to ensure every American could make their voice heard.

**Last night proved that when Democrats invest early, organize tirelessly, and stand up for our values, we win. And, while we’re excited about these victories, we know that our ability to protect our democracy and permanently stop the MAGA agenda in 2028 depends on what we build today.** Instead of resting on our laurels, instead of assuming we have 2028 in the bag, instead of letting victory make us complacent, we’re doubling down on our election-winning programs. And I’m asking you to stay with us in this fight. [**If you can, I hope you’ll consider investing $7 or more in our work to elect Democrats up and down the ballot next election cycle and send a Democrat back to the White House. Your contribution will be put to work immediately.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.gb4rMu&refcode=em_20261104_10234_fr&amount=7&t=7&akid=10234%2E22930333%2EsqDRYn) _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._ | | | **[Donate $7](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89866?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.9s4leO&amount=7&refcode=em_20261104_10234_fr&t=8&akid=10234%2E22930333%2EsqDRYn)**

Thank you, Ohio! Thank you so much!
The voters of our great state have spoken, and they have chosen a future rooted in fairness, accessibility, and transparency.
I am so deeply honored and profoundly humbled to be your next Ohio Secretary of State.
This victory does not belong to me alone -- it belongs to thousands of grassroots volunteers, community organizers, supporters, and voters across all 88 counties who worked tirelessly to make this evening possible.
When we launched this campaign back in August 2025, we traveled across Ohio -- from Cincinnati to Cleveland, from Sidney to Cadiz, from Defiance to Ironton, and everywhere in between. We spoke with everyday citizens who simply want to know that their voice matters, that their vote counts, and that the rules of our democracy apply equally to everyone. We listened to small business owners who wanted streamlined services to help their enterprises thrive.
For my entire career, I've always believed that good policy relies on trust, accountability, and putting people before politics. The office of the Secretary of State touches the core of our daily lives -- it's the guardian of our democracy, and it's the gateway for starting a business.
Ohioans have sent a clear message: you want an elections system that is secure, efficient, accessible, and transparent for every eligible voter, no matter where they live or how they vote.
As your next Secretary of State, my mission is also clear:

* We will be working every day to Protect and Expand voter access. That means ensuring robust voter education, removing unnecessary barriers, and making sure every eligible Ohioan knows how, when, and where to vote.

* We will be laser-focused on strengthening Trust in our elections and this office: That means ensuring the highest standards of election integrity and protecting our systems so that every citizen can have complete confidence in the results of every election, the information they see in the voting booth, and their right to privacy. It also means that we will unapologetically push back on dis and mis-information, no matter who it comes from.

* We will make it easier to Start and Grow small businesses in Ohio: That means modernizing our business services to be a true resource, not just a starting point, for those Ohioans who want to own businesses and innovate in our great state.

Listen: Democracy is not a spectator sport -- it requires constant stewardship. My commitment to you is that I will manage this office with fairness, integrity, and an unyielding commitment to the rule of law.
Whether you voted for me, supported another candidate, or are just beginning to engage in our political process, please know this: I am here to serve ALL Ohioans.
The work of building a stronger, more inclusive state does not end today. We can celebrate today, BUT this is not the finish line. The real work begins tomorrow. It will take ALL OF US, working together across communities and party lines, to live up to what the voters of Ohio have entrusted us to do and to keep moving Ohio forward.
Thank you again, Ohio, for your trust, your hard work, and your faith in our shared future. I have the best damn team in Ohio, and there's no better and more loyal group of people to share this win with!
God bless you, and God bless the great state of Ohio!
-- Allison Russo

Years ago, I met the people who rescue children from trafficking.

When I heard what is done to these children, I asked myself one question:

What if it were my child?

That question changed my life. And it is why I am writing to you today.

I want to tell you about a little girl. For her safety, we call her “Lola.”

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTAsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA-8pfRY1nrP-NAOxJyZHcllJOdEn6yYkJhZ0LF-WrXxwENCKAu3EYHCdz9maukX-X55_U2F5SDffUx9S_sJyfPKa-8WObRWAwBzSX_yc

Lola’s mother was a hardworking single mom, doing everything she could for her little girl.

Then she met a man online.

He promised her the moon and the stars.

He traveled a long way to get them. He said his parents had a beautiful home in California and they would all be cared for.

It was a lie.

Soon, Lola and her mother were missing.

One of our house parents moved fast. Investigators believed the family had reached southern Mexico.

So she sounded the alarm.

She worked with authorities to get an AMBER Alert out with Lola’s picture and pushed her case into the public eye.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTAsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA-8pfRY2HTF1xFifd4J6fRjqJF6OiMC808vBEyTF3JV1vIW5hDigDmDdNGRf5-waKVXhv7Xc7UMqZAoiX2-gwMCOAn6BCymz0F1a3MHq
Sound the Alarm Now. Give Today

And that very same day Lola was dropped off and left in front of child protective services.

Alone. Frightened.

But alive.

Lola said her mother had died on the journey while she was crossing water. She could not swim.

We may never know what truly happened. But everything pointed to one terrible fear — that this man groomed her mother to get to her daughter. And that he planned to take Lola into the United States to be trafficked.

But he did not get to keep her.

We stopped him.

Today, Lola is safe. She was reunited with her grandparents and adopted by her loving aunt.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTAsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA-8pfRY3ZpfF25SwyXxQ9vRK0-9dO8tLuiTAf3GX_fkkGWAOQt6TOmpneq9cUspxECld2bRIBBuObc6BnmI01U5nmr-TlmP_lnlYTLc5

Friend, this is not a movie.

About two million children are exploited in the sex trade around the world, according to the U.S. State Department.

Two million. Each one made in the image of God.

Our nation was built on the belief that every life has worth because God gave it.

That truth does not let us look away.

Jesus said, “Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.” (Matthew 19:14 NIV)

That is why Sound of Freedom Foundation exists — to stop the sale of God’s children.

And Lola’s story shows the most important truth of all: children are found when people pay attention.

Here is how you can join the fight today:

1. Stay alert. Traffickers often start online with kindness and big promises.

2. If you see something, say something. Read every AMBER Alert. Share it. If something feels wrong, call 911 or report a trafficking tip through Sound of Freedom Foundation's partner, Rescue America, at 1-833-599-3733.

3. Make your first gift. Help Sound of Freedom Foundation and our partners keep sounding the alarm.

Will you give $25, $50, $75, $100, or whatever you can right now to help sound the alarm for the next child like Lola?

When good people keep quiet, they become part of the problem.

But when good people speak up, God’s children come home.

Tonight, a child is waiting to be found. You can be the one who steps in right now.

---
Dear Friend, Yesterday, Rhode Islanders put their trust in me to serve as our next Attorney General. I am incredibly grateful, humbled, and excited for the opportunity to serve the state I love.
---
|
---
First, I want to say thank you. Whether you knocked on doors, made phone calls, donated to our campaign, put up a yard sign, or simply talked to your friends and neighbors about this campaign, you helped make this victory possible. I couldn't have done it without you. Over the past year, I have traveled across Rhode Island and met so many people who care deeply about our state's future. I've heard from parents worried about keeping their kids safe, working families struggling to make ends meet, and Rhode Islanders who want to know that their rights will be protected. Those conversations have shaped this campaign, and they'll guide me every day as Attorney General.
---
|
---
Yesterday was a historic day for our state. For the first time, a majority of Rhode Island's general officers will be women. I'm proud to be a part of this historic moment, and also proud to be the first Democratic woman, the first mom, and the first openly gay person elected Attorney General in our state. I know what these milestones mean, especially to young people who have not always seen themselves represented in positions of leadership. But I also know that what matters most isn't making history. It's what we do with the opportunity we've been given.
---
|
---
I ran for Attorney General because I believe everyone deserves to feel safe in their community, to know their fundamental rights are protected, and to trust that their elected leaders are working every day to make their lives a little easier. That's the work ahead of us. And I promise to bring the same determination, compassion, and commitment to public service that guided this campaign to the Attorney General's Office. My parents taught me that public service is about showing up, listening, and doing the work. That's exactly what I will do as AG. Thank you again for believing in me and for being part of this campaign. Now, let's get to work! Sincerely, Kim
---

clean_body: | | ~ Dear Friend, Yesterday, Rhode Islanders put their trust in me to serve as our next Attorney General. I am incredibly grateful, humbled, and excited for the opportunity to serve the state I love. | First, I want to say thank you. Whether you knocked on doors, made phone calls, donated to our campaign, put up a yard sign, or simply talked to your friends and neighbors about this campaign, you helped make this victory possible. I couldn't have done it without you. Over the past year, I have traveled across Rhode Island and met so many people who care deeply about our state's future. I've heard from parents worried about keeping their kids safe, working families struggling to make ends meet, and Rhode Islanders who want to know that their rights will be protected. Those conversations have shaped this campaign, and they'll guide me every day as Attorney General. | Yesterday was a historic day for our state. For the first time, a majority of Rhode Island's general officers will be women. I'm proud to be a part of this historic moment, and also proud to be the first Democratic woman, the first mom, and the first openly gay person elected Attorney General in our state. I know what these milestones mean, especially to young people who have not always seen themselves represented in positions of leadership. But I also know that what matters most isn't making history. It's what we do with the opportunity we've been given. | I ran for Attorney General because I believe everyone deserves to feel safe in their community, to know their fundamental rights are protected, and to trust that their elected leaders are working every day to make their lives a little easier. That's the work ahead of us. And I promise to bring the same determination, compassion, and commitment to public service that guided this campaign to the Attorney General's Office. My parents taught me that public service is about showing up, listening, and doing the work. That's exactly what I will do as AG. Thank you again for believing in me and for being part of this campaign. Now, let's get to work! Peter, we won!!!

I have wanted to write those words for a long time. After three campaigns, we finally did it. I knew this would take a lot of people coming together, but seeing it happen is something else entirely.

They say the third time's the charm. Maybe so. But I think there is something more to this victory than luck or timing. I think it is what happens when people decide that their voices matter and that the future is worth fighting for.

I hope you know that when I walk into Congress, I will remember the people who inspired me to do this. I will remember the families who are working hard and still struggling to get by. The farmers who carry the weight of uncertainty every season. The small-business owners who have poured everything they have into building something of their own. The young people wondering whether they can afford to build a future here. The seniors who deserve dignity and security. The veterans who have given so much to this country and deserve a government that keeps its promises.

I also want to thank Representative Miller-Meeks for her service to IA-01. We may not have seen eye to eye on many things, but I believe she loves our country, and I appreciate the sacrifice of all those who serve in our government.

I have a lot more to say, and I promise I will. But right now, I mostly just want to say THANK YOU. I am so grateful for your support, so proud of what we accomplished together, and so privileged to go to Congress and represent the place I call home.

— Christina

Peter,

Thank you to my family, friends, campaign staff, and the countless supporters who stood with us during this campaign. We could not have won this race without every person who knocked on doors, worked the polls, hosted events, and pitched in to help the cause. I am truly grateful to all of you. This victory belongs to the people of Texas’ 21st District. I’m not going to Washington for myself, but rather to be a strong, responsive voice for every family in this district.

Together, we can build a better future for our families, our neighbors, and every community across Texas 21. I’m excited to get to work. I will be praying for all of you and for the future of this great nation.

God bless Texas, and God bless America.

**— Mark “Tex” Teixeira**

It is with great honor and gratitude that I share that **I have been re-elected to represent Ohio’s 11th Congressional District.**

**In my next term, I vow to continue the fight for the future of our nation.** In Congress, we have delivered on big bills, including passing the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which is bringing millions of dollars to repair roads and bridges, capping the price of insulin at $35 a month for seniors, and limiting the cost of prescription drugs to $2,000 a year for seniors. With you by my side, I am ready to get back to work for the American people and preserve our democracy for generations to come.

**With your support, we not only secured my re-election, but Democrats also took back the U.S. House and won big across Ohio!** This includes Amy Acton being elected our next governor and Sherrod Brown flipping Ohio’s Senate seat, and incredible wins in the House – protecting all of our incumbents and flipping major seats for Democrats.

With Trump and his Republican cronies wreaking havoc in Washington, these wins will help restore checks and balances to this out-of-control administration at both the state and federal levels. Finally, our voices will be heard as we fight back against their efforts to dismantle our elections, make healthcare woefully out of reach for millions, slash food security, and more. I vow to take full advantage of this moment to get to work for the people.

**Thank you again for your unwavering support. We could not have done this without you. Now, the real work begins.**

Onward,

Shontel | Shontel Brown is proud to be elected as the Congresswoman for Ohio’s 11th District. She has spent the last decade serving the people of Ohio and building coalitions. As she enters her second full term in Congress, she will use that experience to continue the fight for affordable quality health care, jobs that pay fair wages, a strong public education system, and to preserve and protect our democracy for generations to come. Will you join her and be the change we need?

Thank you for every minute you spent telling a neighbor why this seat was worth defending. **Thank you for helping me WIN.** Polls are closed, and the 7th district stays ours. Not because of a commercial. Because of people like you, who treated this race like it was their own. I will not forget what it took. The early mornings. The forwarded emails. The friend you dragged to the polls at 7 AM because you were not willing to leave it to chance. That is how a seat gets held. From my family to yours, thank you.******This WIN is yours as much as it is mine.** Thank you for your support,

* * *

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

name: Rick Bennett
subject: Thank you
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Bennett for Governor · P
body:
Thank you to every single one of you who voted, showed up, and supported this campaign.

| | |
---
---
---
---
Hi Peter, Thank you. Thank you to every single one of you who voted, showed up, and supported this campaign.

I think about the people of this campaign more than you know. On the long days, it was the folks I've met who kept me going; the parent working two jobs and still showing up, the young Mainer wondering if they can afford to build a life in the state they love, the retired couple who told me they'd never given to a campaign before but believed in this one.

Your stories stay with me. Honestly, they're the reason I ran.

You did something most people never do. You didn't wait for someone else to fix things. You stepped up. You gave what you could, at times more than you could, you knocked on doors, you made calls after a long day of work, and you talked to your neighbors about what's possible. That takes courage, and it means more to me than I can put into words.

I promise you this: I will not let you down. I carry what you've told me with me every single day, and I always will.

Maine is worth fighting for. So are you.

With all my heart, thank you.

Rick Bennett
Independent for a Better Maine
---

body:
And what lies ahead

| |
---
Peter, Last night, voters across Pennsylvania made their voices heard loud and clear, re-electing Governor Josh Shapiro and Lt. Governor Austin Davis, while also sending a Democratic trifecta to Harrisburg for the first time since 1992 to get to work for the folks of the commonwealth. Austin has been at the forefront of these victories raising over $1.5 million to help elect Democrats up and down the ballot. Including: \- $1.2 million for Governor Shapiro’s campaign
\- $102,000 for the PA Coordinated campaign
\- $100,000 to frontline Senate candidates
\- $75,000 to the PA House Democratic Campaign Committee
\- $50,000 to the PA Senate Democratic Campaign Committee He also traveled to every corner of Pennsylvania focused on building the next generation of Democratic leaders, strengthening county and local party organizations, and expanding reach to voters in the commonwealth through digital media. After these historic results, Austin will preside over a Democratic State Senate and continue his nonstop work to fight for the wonderful people of the Keystone State. Austin has set a new standard for what a Lieutenant Governor contributes to a statewide election effort and the results speak for themselves. Thank you for all your hard work to make these victories possible. We couldn’t have done it without you. Now, it’s time to get to work! — Team Davis

subject: Charlie showed up every single day. Will you?
body:
| | | |

| | | Peter,

Thank you. **I am so proud to be reelected to serve the great state of Colorado in the U.S. Senate.** The message we heard last night is the same one we’ve heard day after day on the road: our fight doesn’t end with Trump. It’s where our fight begins again. Millions of Coloradans made a clear choice: to defend this seat from MAGA's hands and send a real fighter for Colorado back to Washington. My commitment has been and always will be to bring people together and solve problems. Now we’re ready to bring that same focus into this next term. That’s how we’ll tackle this cost-of-living emergency, end this reckless war in Iran, and hold the president accountable for his corruption. But let’s be clear: we have NO interest in just restringing the safety nets Trump chopped down. We want to build a strong floor, finally get universal health coverage, and unrig our economy so the American dream can once again be within reach. There’s a lot of work ahead of us, and we’re so grateful to have you on our side. But it isn’t lost on us that we’ll still face a Trump White House. No doubt they’ll spread lies and try to cheat their way out of losing. No question they’ll try to block and veto our bills. But we’re ready for them. We’re ready to take them on and stop them — just like we did when they tried to sell our public lands and just like we did today. All the hard work that volunteers and campaigns across the country put in is not just about taking back Congress this year. It’s about building the groundwork for kicking Trump and MAGA out of the White House — once and for all — in 2028. We’ll close with this: Thank you, truly. We could not have won this race without you. Thank you to everyone who volunteered, who endorsed this campaign, put up a sign, talked to a friend, chipped in a few bucks, made phone calls, sent texts, or cast a vote. And thank you to the people of Colorado for your continued confidence and trust. I’m honored to represent you in Washington. Now let’s get back to work. With gratitude,
John Hickenlooper

name: True the Vote
subject: 2028 starts today.
body:
We have a country to preserve. And no time to waste.
| | | November 04, 2026 | [**Read Online**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/n4uz4vr7xohvhgw6r99f6h66wrlp7ulhqvn23/x0hph6hem65vdzc5hl/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2Ivdjh1M2hyaDQyZWc5OWFscTIyOXE1c3Z2MGc2bmdhOWgwbHhtMg==) | |
---
|
### 2028 starts today.
Yesterday was a rout. Failed leadership. Squandered opportunities. Too many people entrusted with responsibility who could not find the courage to meet it. But if we come out of this with nothing more than a list of people to blame, we will have wasted even this. Something deeper is happening to our country. And we had better find the courage to face it. We have become careless with an extraordinary inheritance. Careless with our freedom. Careless with the truth. Careless with one another. We enjoy blessings that generations before us sacrificed everything to secure, and somewhere along the way, we began treating those blessings as guarantees. They are not guaranteed. Neither is America. A nation cannot remain free when its people forget what freedom requires. We cannot outsource courage to a candidate, responsibility to a party, or the future of our children to whoever happens to win the next election. We have to become people capable of preserving what we say we love. That requires some brutal honesty. Have we mistaken posting for participating? Have we demanded integrity from public officials while excusing dishonesty when it benefits our side? Have we spent more time condemning strangers than helping our neighbors? Have we become so consumed by what is wrong that we have forgotten to thank God for what is still good—and accept responsibility for protecting it? I am asking myself every one of those questions. There is a spiritual desert beneath all this noise. Ingratitude. Pride. Indifference. Cowardice. The dangerous belief that someone else will do the hard things while we watch. No election can do that soul-searching for us. We need humility enough to examine ourselves and courage enough to change. We need to get on our knees before God, then get on our feet and take responsibility for the work in front of us. To everyone who checked a voter record, helped a friend vote, served at the polls, documented a problem, prayed, volunteered, or gave to keep this work going: thank you. You showed up. Your work mattered. Please hear that today. And hear this, too: we are going to need each other for what comes next. At True the Vote, we will examine our own work with the same scrutiny we ask of others. We will keep pursuing answers, equipping citizens, and insisting on election processes the public can verify. We will keep showing up in the communities where trust has been broken and people have been forgotten. 2028 starts today. Let’s go. Never quit. Isaiah 6:8. Ephesians 6. Game on. Ever onward — |
---
P.S. We have to work harder than we ever have. Starting immediately. And we need your financial support to do it. [_Please make a gift to True the Vote today._](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/n4uz4vr7xohvhgw6r99f6h66wrlp7ulhqvn23/kkhmh6hnpqk023blh7/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvZG9uYXRl) Help us pursue answers, equip citizens, and stay in the fight for trustworthy elections. Every day between now and 2028 matters.

| | | Team,Yesterday, Americans turned out to choose our leaders in record numbers. **Now we must make sure every eligible vote is counted.**

The Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska and countless House races are still too close to call, along with state and local races. **Each and every vote matters,** because in America, voters pick our leaders — not the other way around.

**We cannot allow politicians to stop the process or keep eligible votes from counting.** Doing so could change who wins — allowing politicians to seize power against the will of the people. **[Send a letter to Congress: Demand that lawmakers protect every eligible vote, investigate attempts to stop the count, and ensure that federal voting rights laws are enforced>>](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142889680/658383069/849990692?source=direct_link&referrer=group-od-action&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg5MjE1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImM1NWVlOTExLTY5ZDgtZjExMS1iZjViLTAwMGQzYTU0NDQyZSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=dnOZKJjVTD9EkKYfqOnRmgoGq2haaEiaAf_OaQR_3bw=&emci=90e1df7f-65d8-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=c55ee911-69d8-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=33603084)**

**Election Night results are not final results.** Mail-in ballots, provisional ballots, and votes from military and overseas Americans can take additional time to count. **Every eligible vote matters, regardless of when it's counted.**

Politicians don't get to declare themselves the winners by throwing out votes they don't like. That's election sabotage, and it threatens to take the power to choose our leaders away from the people.

**Wednesday, November 4, 2026 -**_****_
_**U.S.:** Democrats win Senate and House in historic landslide, upending President Donald Trump's second term and GOP agenda. Trump is relatively conciliatory in late-night comments. _**Iran:** Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says Americans voted "NO TO WAR"; President Donald Trump says he would launch Iran war again despite election losses. Israeli forces displace 25 families in Tulkarm, arrest 45 Palestinians across the occupied West Bank. Israel's election committee approves results. Trump says U.S. will cut $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel._
