# U.S. News
* **Democrats win Senate and House in historic landslide, upending Trump 's second term and GOP agenda: **Democrats took control of the House of Representatives and the Senate following midterm elections on Tuesday. It is the third time in 50 years that control of both chambers has changed in a single election. Democratic candidates flipped seven seats in the Senate, giving them a 54-46 majority in the upper chamber. The Democrats are estimated to win 258 House seats, and 55 Senate seats. Democrats also won gubernatorial races in Texas, Georgia, Nevada, Ohio, and Iowa.
* **Trump is relatively conciliatory in late-night comments:** President Donald**** Trump congratulated the Democrats in a [call](https://substack.com/redirect/c2b26951-82b8-4bd7-b499-c195339cd2f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to CBS News, saying that he was "looking forward to working with [them] for the good of the country." But on Fox News, he said that he would veto anything passed by Democrats that was "insane," and on Truth Social he posted an image of a hat with "VETO" on it.
* He also [addressed](https://substack.com/redirect/c2b26951-82b8-4bd7-b499-c195339cd2f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the prospect of resuming the Iran war now that the midterms had concluded with CBS, saying the war would conclude "when I say it's over, basically. It'll end when I say it ends."
* **Here are the results from the night 's marquee races:**
* **Democratic victories in "toss-up" Senate races: **Going into the election, seven Senate races were rated "toss-ups" by Cook Political Report: Texas, Ohio, Iowa, Maine, Michigan, Alaska, and Kansas. Democrats won all of those races except for Alaska, which has not yet been called.
* **Abdul El-Sayed becomes first Muslim senator, beating back Islamophobic attacks and pro-Israel opposition:** In Michigan, **Abdul El-Sayed** , a progressive physician, defeated **Mike Rogers** by nearly 10 points to become the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. President Trump and other Republicans used Islamophobic rhetoric to rally voters against him. "To AIPAC, who spent $42 million against us, thank you for giving me the opportunity to beat you twice," he said in his victory speech.
* **James Talarico, Gina Hinojosa turn Texas blue:** Democrat **James Talarico** defeated Republican **Ken Paxton** in Texas. Talarico, a 37-year-old Democratic state legislator and seminarian, is the first Democrat elected to the U.S. Senate in Texas since 1993. **Gina Hinojosa** , another state legislator, defeated incumbent governor **Greg Abbott** , making her the first Democrat to win a Texas governor's race since 1995.
* **Annie Andrews ' surprise victory in South Carolina: **The night's biggest upset was in South Carolina, where pediatrician Annie Andrews defeated Darline Graham, the sister of recently deceased Sen. Lindsey Graham and interim Senator appointed to fill his seat in July. Andrews is the first Democrat to represent the state in the Senate since 1998, and is the first woman elected to the post in the state's history.
* **Amy Acton, Sherrod Brown take Ohio:** Democrats **Amy Acton** and **Sherrod Brown** won in Ohio, a state that has been solidly Republican since Trump won the state in 2016. Acton, a former state health official, defeated the Republican **Vivek Ramaswamy** , an entrepreneur and former head of the Department of Government Efficiency. Brown took back a seat he had lost in 2024 to **Bernie Moreno**. Brown previously served for 18 years in the Senate; he is regarded as one of the strongest pro-labor voices in the Democratic Party.
* **Adam Hamilton wins Kansas:** Democrat **Adam Hamilton** , a Methodist pastor, defeated incumbent Republican Sen. **Roger Marshall** , making him the first member of his party to win a Senate seat in Kansas in 94 years. The race attracted huge interest: Political spending topped $110 million, and Trump hosted two rallies in support of the Republican candidate. Hamilton's victory was largely [secured](https://substack.com/redirect/66860c73-68ea-419c-a72a-9cd66f626bd2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the state's moderate voters: About seven in 10 moderates backed him over Marshall, according to an AP voter poll. (Read the [Barn Raiser x Drop Site profile of Hamilton](https://substack.com/redirect/d6093a5d-09d5-4581-8c13-f14894666eed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to understand why he won.)
* **Democratic socialists advance in House:** After winning primaries in safe districts, candidates aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America secured victories in the general election. Winners include **Darializa Avila Chevalier** , **Brad Lander** , and **Claire Valdez** in New York City,**Donavan McKinney** in Michigan, **Melat Kiros** in Colorado, **Chris Rabb** in Pennsylvania, and **Analilia Mejia** in New Jersey. **Matt Little** , a progressive running to replace outgoing Rep. **Annie Craig** , won in Minnesota's second congressional district.
* **Mississippi Senate race too close to call:** The Mississippi Senate race remained deadlocked as of Wednesday morning. Democrat **Scott Colom** is in an unexpected dead heat with incumbent GOP Sen. **Cindy Hyde-Smith**. Colom is ahead by just 28 votes out of more than 1 million votes cast. If Colom wins, he would be the state's first Democratic senator since 1982, and its first Black senator since **Blanche K. Bruce** , elected in 1875.
* **Climate activist William Lawrence declares victory in Michigan: William Lawrence** , co-founder of the Sunrise Movement, [declared](https://substack.com/redirect/a00b437e-9ec5-4776-9c1e-48bc57a8d1d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) victory in his Michigan congressional race, citing an unofficial tally that had him up by several percentage points. As of Wednesday morning, he leads his Republican opponent, incumbent **Tom Barrett** , by three percentage points, 51% to 47.8%. Over 95% of votes have been received, according to AP election results.
* **Sanders-backed progressive beats Central Valley, Calif., Republican: Randy Villegas** , a community college professor and son of immigrants, [defeated](https://substack.com/redirect/7137e442-3316-426f-9e92-fe6c809387b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) incumbent Republican Rep. **David Valadao** in California's Central Valley. Villegas received an early endorsement from Sen. **Bernie Sanders** in his primary contest. Valadao, who served five terms in Congress, was one of 10 Republicans who voted to impeach Trump in 2021.
* **Socialist wins Providence, Rhode Island, mayoral race; city votes to divest from Israel:** State representative **David Morales** , a 28-year-old member of the Democratic Socialists of America, was [elected](https://substack.com/redirect/a66f8be2-14c7-4d16-8c75-c4065d2b610a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) mayor of Providence, Rhode Island, easily [defeating](https://substack.com/redirect/c5fa0492-017b-4361-952d-33d162dce488?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his Republican opponent, **Dave Talan**. Separately, Providence voters approved a referendum on divesting from "countries and companies committing genocide." The group that organized the referendum, Providence for Palestine, said that the language of the item was a reference to Israel. At least 75 percent of voters supported the measure.
* **Major Democratic gubernatorial victories:** Democrats scored several high-profile gubernatorial victories. In Iowa, State Auditor **Rob Sand** defeated moderate Republican **Zach Lahn** ; in Wisconsin, **David Crowley** defeated Trump-endorsed Rep. **Tom Tiffany** ; and in Michigan, **Jocelyn Benson** defeated Republican Rep. **John James**. Former Atlanta Mayor **Keisha Lance Bottoms** won in Georgia, becoming the first Black female governor in U.S. history. **Deb Haaland** , Secretary of the Interior under **Joe Biden** , won in New Mexico, making her the first Native American to lead a U.S. state.
* **House flips in Pennsylvania:** Democrats flipped two high-profile seats in Pennsylvania. Democrat **Paige Cognetti** , mayor of Scranton, won in Pennsylvania's eighth congressional district, unseating first-term Republican Rep. **Rob Bresnahan**. Democrat **Bob Brooks** , a firefighter, also defeated a first-term Republican incumbent, Rep. **Ryan Mackenzie**.
* **Other notable House races:** Incumbent Republican Rep. **Mario D iaz-Balart** [appeared](https://substack.com/redirect/691be541-2232-47b8-a3a3-6f8b5783e44a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) poised to win in his unexpectedly close re-election race against Democrat **Nicole Locklin**. The Miami-area representative is the longest-serving member of Florida's congressional delegation. **Lauren Boebert** lost in Colorado,**** after switching districts this cycle to one she believed was easier for a Republican to win. **Sam Forstag,** a labor leader backed by **Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez** , is leading the Republican in Montana's first congressional district, but the race has not been called. **Richard Ojeda,** a former state senator in West Virginia known for supporting the 2018 teachers' strike, won in North Carolina.

📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com
# Iran
* **Iran 's Ghalibaf says Americans voted "NO TO WAR"; Trump says he would launch Iran war again despite election losses:** American voters rejected the war with Iran in the midterm elections, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Wednesday, [writing](https://substack.com/redirect/de9f77c4-6651-423a-a02c-6d9166f97de6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X, "Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message."
* He added that if the U.S. government "betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare."
* President Trump said on Tuesday that the war with Iran contributed to Republican losses. "Part of it was Iran," Trump told Fox News. In a separate interview with the Wall Street Journal, Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/3c337aa1-8323-4d0f-b433-22e290fd3072?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he did not regret launching the war: "I did the right thing. I would have done it again."
* **Trump says U.S. "locked and loaded" for Iran strikes but has no immediate plans to attack:** Trump [downplayed](https://substack.com/redirect/016bc8d7-0367-4734-ab08-fb89304c830d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) speculation of renewed U.S. strikes on Iran following the midterm elections, telling the Financial Times that Washington had no immediate plans to attack despite indications from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that strikes could take place later this week. "I'm ready, we're ready. We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it," Trump said.
* Referring to ongoing negotiations with Tehran, he added, "We seem to be getting everything we want." Trump said the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports was damaging Tehran's economy, calling it "a brilliant situation."
* Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said that Tehran remained committed to diplomatic talks through its seven-day roadmap presented to Qatari mediators but was "ready for any scenario." Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned that any renewed U.S. attacks would result in "much broader dimensions" of war.
* **Europe approaches winter with lowest gas reserves since 2013 amid Hormuz supply disruptions:** Europe is approaching the winter season with its lowest natural gas storage levels in more than a decade, raising the risk of tight global gas supplies and higher prices through 2027, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/cde2f00f-4eb7-4af7-a0ed-68c7be0079e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the International Energy Agency. The effective halt of liquefied natural gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz has cut exports from Qatar and the UAE by more than 60 billion cubic meters between March and October, pushing Asian and European gas prices to their highest levels since the 2022-23 energy crisis.
* **Iran claims four oil tankers destroyed by mines in Hormuz, U.S. MQ-9 drone shot down:** Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) [said](https://substack.com/redirect/98436a91-34d7-47da-a894-c709e9db1855?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday that four oil tankers attempting to cross a "prohibited" corridor south of the Strait of Hormuz struck naval mines and were destroyed, with the vessels still burning. Two other vessels were stopped, according to the IRGC.
* The group also claimed its air defense forces shot down a U.S. MQ-9 drone over the strait, bringing the number of MQ-9 drones it says it has downed to 56.

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed three Palestinians--two in new attacks and one due to wounds sustained in an earlier attack--and injured 21 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,618 killed and 175,920 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,602 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,794, while 847 bodies have been recovered.
* **Palestinian journalist loses 16 kilograms amid solitary confinement in Israeli prison:** Palestinian journalist Bushra Al-Tawil, from Al-Bireh in the occupied West Bank, lost 16 kilograms since her arrest on February 5, amid severe food shortages, medical neglect, and prolonged solitary confinement, according to the Palestinian Commission of Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs.
* Al-Tawil has been held in isolation since August 17 and is currently detained at Israel's Ohalei Oz prison. Her isolation was extended for another month on November 2.
* The commission said that she is suffering from dark skin lesions caused by scabies, as well as painful tendon inflammation in her hands and feet. Israeli prison authorities have ignored repeated requests for medical treatment.
* **Israel declares 627 acres of Palestinian land near Ramallah "state property":** Israeli authorities [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/be9c735a-d38b-4d9a-a087-9679c7333537?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an order on November 3 declaring 627 acres (2,536 dunams) of Palestinian land in Beitillu, Al-Mazra'a Al-Qibliya, and Deir Ammar, northwest of Ramallah in the West Bank, as "state property," according to the Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission.
* The land surrounds the Israeli settlement of Kerem Reim, and the commission warned that the declaration would facilitate the expansion of settlements. Palestinian landowners have 45 days from the order's publication to file legal objections.
* **Israeli forces displace 25 families in Tulkarm, arrest 45 Palestinians across the West Bank:** Israeli forces carried out raids, demolitions, and arrests across the West Bank on Wednesday, WAFA reported. The Palestinian Prisoners' Society reported at least 45 arrests, including five women and two journalists.
* **Tulkarm:** Israeli forces [forcibly displaced](https://substack.com/redirect/d78cfa05-0184-4e29-babd-977de4d9ef67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 25 families from homes near Tulkarm refugee camp, converting some into military barracks. Israel's assault on the Tulkarm, Nur Shams, and Jenin refugee camps has continued for 647 days, displacing more than 32,000 Palestinians in what Human Rights Watch found amounted to war crimes and crimes against humanity.
* **Ramallah:** Israeli forces [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/6ae455d2-18fa-46f1-b2f9-0b2f642a9f54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tear gas toward a school in Al-Mughayyer, causing students to suffer from tear gas inhalation. Soldiers also detained a teacher and closed the school entrance.
* **Tubas/Northern Jordan Valley:** Israeli bulldozers [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/3f230040-df5e-4953-8c35-ea8471d9bfbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) residential and livestock structures belonging to three Palestinians in the Al-Deir area of the northern Jordan Valley.
* **Hebron:** Under military protection, armed Israeli settlers [destroyed](https://substack.com/redirect/64f19a06-ae35-40d0-a5fe-c5807a64fdb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) olive trees in Surif, northwest of Hebron.
* **Israel 's election committee approves results:** Israel's Central Elections Committee presidium [voted](https://substack.com/redirect/24df4233-480b-476d-ac01-40d6273acbee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday to certify last week's election results, despite efforts by Netanyahu's Likud party and other outgoing coalition parties to delay certification over unsubstantiated claims of election fraud.
* The committee found no irregularities indicating that the vote had been compromised, it said. The results will be submitted to President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday, after which he will consult party leaders on whom to task with forming the next government.
* **Trump says U.S. will cut $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel:** The U.S. will stop providing $4 billion in aid each year to Israel "at the end of the year," President Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/3d2eb96c-d4be-4a1a-bcb6-454d31994e23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday, but will sell arms to Tel Aviv. "We give them $4 billion of things and money, and they don't need it. And I was approached by Bibi Netanyahu, and we've been talking about it for a couple of years because it's a lot of money," Trump told Fox News as voting was underway. "Why should we suffer the slings from lunatics like an El-Sayed when they don't need it?" he said, a reference to Abdul El-Sayed, a forthright critic of Israel who was elected in Michigan to the U.S. Senate.
* Trump's announcement comes as Congress considers phasing out aid to Israel, instead expanding U.S.-Israel cooperation in the countries' military-industrial operations.
* In 2016, President Barack Obama signed an unprecedented security agreement giving Israel $38 billion to its military over 10 years, which is set to expire in 2028. Trump seemed to suggest on Tuesday that he may cancel the agreement two years early, with Israel's consent, though such a decision would probably require Congressional approval. Even if U.S. aid were suddenly cut, there are still many years of already purchased weaponry yet to be delivered, according to AP.

# Yemen
* **20+ killed in Ansarallah missile strike on Saudi-backed government camp:** More than 20 people were killed, and several others wounded, in an Ansarallah ballistic missile [strike](https://substack.com/redirect/369f4146-69f6-4e8d-97b8-5f463789aef3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) targeting a military training camp in the Maris area of Dhale governorate, Sky News Arabia reported.
* Meanwhile, Saudi-backed forces claimed that they captured the Al-Dahida heights and surrounding areas in eastern Al-Jawf governorate, backed by airstrikes targeting Ansarallah positions and supply lines.
* The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia announced that a second Indian national injured in the October 10 Ansarallah attack on Riyadh airport had died, following an attack that killed at least 12 people and wounded hundreds.
* **Hezbollah denies sending military experts to Yemen:** Lebanon's Hezbollah denied claims that its military experts are operating in Yemen and helping Ansarallah develop weapons, train fighters, and manage military operations.
* On Tuesday, the Yemeni Saudi-backed government claimed that 21 foreign military experts, including 14 from Iran's IRGC and seven from Hezbollah, were working with Ansarallah. Their roles extended beyond financing, arming, and training fighters to directly overseeing military operations and political and media activities, according to the government.
* In a statement on Wednesday, Hezbollah called the accusations "completely baseless." The group said that Yemenis can defend their country without outside intervention, and called for dialogue to preserve Yemen's unity and sovereignty.

# Lebanon
* **Again violating ceasefire, Israeli forces burn homes and shell towns in southern Lebanon:** Israeli forces [set fire](https://substack.com/redirect/1cbcb2cd-8530-4933-b9cf-538d1e3de6c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to homes in the town of Hadatha in the Bint Jbeil district, while Israeli artillery shelled Baraachit in the same district, violating the ceasefire, Lebanon's National News Agency reported on Wednesday. Israeli forces also [shelled](https://substack.com/redirect/7b7c1b99-4361-4a11-9abf-13096c009869?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Mansouri and Wadi Zibqin in the Tyre (Sour) district earlier in the morning.

Wednesday, November 4, 2026 -** U.S.: Democrats win Senate and House in historic landslide, upending President Donald Trump's second term and GOP agenda. Trump is relatively conciliatory in late-night comments. Abdul El-Sayed becomes first Muslim senator, beating back Islamophobic attacks and pro-Israel opposition. James Talarico, Gina Hinojosa turn Texas blue. Annie Andrews wins in South Carolina. Amy Acton, Sherrod Brown take Ohio. Adam Hamilton wins Kansas. Democratic socialists advance in House. Mississippi Senate race too close to call.Climate activist William Lawrence declares victory in Michigan. Sanders-backed progressive beats Central Valley, Calif., Republican. Socialist wins Providence, Rhode Island, mayoral race; city votes to divest from Israel. Major Democratic gubernatorial victories. House flips in Pennsylvania. Other notable House races. Iran: Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says Americans voted "NO TO WAR"; President Donald Trump says he would launch Iran war again despite election losses. Trump says U.S. "locked and loaded" for Iran strikes but has no immediate plans to attack. Europe approaches winter with lowest gas reserves since 2013 amid Strait of Hormuz supply disruptions. Iran claims four oil tankers destroyed by mines in Hormuz, U.S. MQ-9 drone shot down. Palestine: Palestinian journalist loses 16 kilograms amid solitary confinement in Israeli prison. Israel declares 627 acres of Palestinian land near Ramallah "state property." Israeli forces displace 25 families in Tulkarm, arrest 45 Palestinians across the occupied West Bank. Israel's election committee approves results. Trump says U.S. will cut $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel. Yemen: 20+ killed in Ansarallah missile strike on Saudi-backed government camp. Hezbollah denies sending military experts to Yemen. Lebanon: Again violating ceasefire, Israeli forces burn homes and shell towns in southern Lebanon. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday U.S. News Democrats win Senate and House in historic landslide, upending Trump 's second term and GOP agenda: Democrats took control of the House of Representatives and the Senate following midterm elections on Tuesday. It is the third time in 50 years that control of both chambers has changed in a single election. Democratic candidates flipped seven seats in the Senate, giving them a 54-46 majority in the upper chamber. The Democrats are estimated to win 258 House seats, and 55 Senate seats. Democrats also won gubernatorial races in Texas, Georgia, Nevada, Ohio, and Iowa. Trump is relatively conciliatory in late-night comments: President Donald** Trump congratulated the Democrats in a to CBS News, saying that he was "looking forward to working with [them] for the good of the country." But on Fox News, he said that he would veto anything passed by Democrats that was "insane," and on Truth Social he posted an image of a hat with "VETO" on it. He also the prospect of resuming the Iran war now that the midterms had concluded with CBS, saying the war would conclude "when I say it's over, basically. It'll end when I say it ends." Here are the results from the night 's marquee races: Democratic victories in "toss-up" Senate races: Going into the election, seven Senate races were rated "toss-ups" by Cook Political Report: Texas, Ohio, Iowa, Maine, Michigan, Alaska, and Kansas. Democrats won all of those races except for Alaska, which has not yet been called. Abdul El-Sayed becomes first Muslim senator, beating back Islamophobic attacks and pro-Israel opposition: In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed , a progressive physician, defeated Mike Rogers by nearly 10 points to become the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. President Trump and other Republicans used Islamophobic rhetoric to rally voters against him. "To AIPAC, who spent $42 million against us, thank you for giving me the opportunity to beat you twice," he said in his victory speech. James Talarico, Gina Hinojosa turn Texas blue: Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton in Texas. Talarico, a 37-year-old Democratic state legislator and seminarian, is the first Democrat elected to the U.S. Senate in Texas since 1993. Gina Hinojosa , another state legislator, defeated incumbent governor Greg Abbott , making her the first Democrat to win a Texas governor's race since 1995. Annie Andrews ' surprise victory in South Carolina: The night's biggest upset was in South Carolina, where pediatrician Annie Andrews defeated Darline Graham, the sister of recently deceased Sen. Lindsey Graham and interim Senator appointed to fill his seat in July. Andrews is the first Democrat to represent the state in the Senate since 1998, and is the first woman elected to the post in the state's history. Amy Acton, Sherrod Brown take Ohio: Democrats Amy Acton and Sherrod Brown won in Ohio, a state that has been solidly Republican since Trump won the state in 2016. Acton, a former state health official, defeated the Republican Vivek Ramaswamy , an entrepreneur and former head of the Department of Government Efficiency. Brown took back a seat he had lost in 2024 to Bernie Moreno. Brown previously served for 18 years in the Senate; he is regarded as one of the strongest pro-labor voices in the Democratic Party. Adam Hamilton wins Kansas: Democrat Adam Hamilton , a Methodist pastor, defeated incumbent Republican Sen. Roger Marshall , making him the first member of his party to win a Senate seat in Kansas in 94 years. The race attracted huge interest: Political spending topped $110 million, and Trump hosted two rallies in support of the Republican candidate. Hamilton's victory was largely by the state's moderate voters: About seven in 10 moderates backed him over Marshall, according to an AP voter poll. (Read the to understand why he won.) Democratic socialists advance in House: After winning primaries in safe districts, candidates aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America secured victories in the general election. Winners include Darializa Avila Chevalier , Brad Lander , and Claire Valdez in New York City,Donavan McKinney in Michigan, Melat Kiros in Colorado, Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania, and Analilia Mejia in New Jersey. Matt Little , a progressive running to replace outgoing Rep. Annie Craig , won in Minnesota's second congressional district. Mississippi Senate race too close to call: The Mississippi Senate race remained deadlocked as of Wednesday morning. Democrat Scott Colom is in an unexpected dead heat with incumbent GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. Colom is ahead by just 28 votes out of more than 1 million votes cast. If Colom wins, he would be the state's first Democratic senator since 1982, and its first Black senator since Blanche K. Bruce , elected in 1875. Climate activist William Lawrence declares victory in Michigan: William Lawrence , co-founder of the Sunrise Movement, victory in his Michigan congressional race, citing an unofficial tally that had him up by several percentage points. As of Wednesday morning, he leads his Republican opponent, incumbent Tom Barrett , by three percentage points, 51% to 47.8%. Over 95% of votes have been received, according to AP election results. Sanders-backed progressive beats Central Valley, Calif., Republican: Randy Villegas , a community college professor and son of immigrants, incumbent Republican Rep. David Valadao in California's Central Valley. Villegas received an early endorsement from Sen. Bernie Sanders in his primary contest. Valadao, who served five terms in Congress, was one of 10 Republicans who voted to impeach Trump in 2021. Socialist wins Providence, Rhode Island, mayoral race; city votes to divest from Israel: State representative David Morales , a 28-year-old member of the Democratic Socialists of America, was mayor of Providence, Rhode Island, easily his Republican opponent, Dave Talan. Separately, Providence voters approved a referendum on divesting from "countries and companies committing genocide." The group that organized the referendum, Providence for Palestine, said that the language of the item was a reference to Israel. At least 75 percent of voters supported the measure. Major Democratic gubernatorial victories: Democrats scored several high-profile gubernatorial victories. In Iowa, State Auditor Rob Sand defeated moderate Republican Zach Lahn ; in Wisconsin, David Crowley defeated Trump-endorsed Rep. Tom Tiffany ; and in Michigan, Jocelyn Benson defeated Republican Rep. John James. Former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms won in Georgia, becoming the first Black female governor in U.S. history. Deb Haaland , Secretary of the Interior under Joe Biden , won in New Mexico, making her the first Native American to lead a U.S. state. House flips in Pennsylvania: Democrats flipped two high-profile seats in Pennsylvania. Democrat Paige Cognetti , mayor of Scranton, won in Pennsylvania's eighth congressional district, unseating first-term Republican Rep. Rob Bresnahan. Democrat Bob Brooks , a firefighter, also defeated a first-term Republican incumbent, Rep. Ryan Mackenzie. Other notable House races: Incumbent Republican Rep. Mario D iaz-Balart poised to win in his unexpectedly close re-election race against Democrat Nicole Locklin. The Miami-area representative is the longest-serving member of Florida's congressional delegation. Lauren Boebert lost in Colorado, after switching districts this cycle to one she believed was easier for a Republican to win. Sam Forstag, a labor leader backed by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez , is leading the Republican in Montana's first congressional district, but the race has not been called. Richard Ojeda, a former state senator in West Virginia known for supporting the 2018 teachers' strike, won in North Carolina. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Iran Iran 's Ghalibaf says Americans voted "NO TO WAR"; Trump says he would launch Iran war again despite election losses: American voters rejected the war with Iran in the midterm elections, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Wednesday, on X, "Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message." He added that if the U.S. government "betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare." President Trump said on Tuesday that the war with Iran contributed to Republican losses. "Part of it was Iran," Trump told Fox News. In a separate interview with the Wall Street Journal, Trump he did not regret launching the war: "I did the right thing. I would have done it again." Trump says U.S. "locked and loaded" for Iran strikes but has no immediate plans to attack: Trump speculation of renewed U.S. strikes on Iran following the midterm elections, telling the Financial Times that Washington had no immediate plans to attack despite indications from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that strikes could take place later this week. "I'm ready, we're ready. We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it," Trump said. Referring to ongoing negotiations with Tehran, he added, "We seem to be getting everything we want." Trump said the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports was damaging Tehran's economy, calling it "a brilliant situation." Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said that Tehran remained committed to diplomatic talks through its seven-day roadmap presented to Qatari mediators but was "ready for any scenario." Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned that any renewed U.S. attacks would result in "much broader dimensions" of war. Europe approaches winter with lowest gas reserves since 2013 amid Hormuz supply disruptions: Europe is approaching the winter season with its lowest natural gas storage levels in more than a decade, raising the risk of tight global gas supplies and higher prices through 2027, to the International Energy Agency. The effective halt of liquefied natural gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz has cut exports from Qatar and the UAE by more than 60 billion cubic meters between March and October, pushing Asian and European gas prices to their highest levels since the 2022-23 energy crisis. Iran claims four oil tankers destroyed by mines in Hormuz, U.S. MQ-9 drone shot down: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Wednesday that four oil tankers attempting to cross a "prohibited" corridor south of the Strait of Hormuz struck naval mines and were destroyed, with the vessels still burning. Two other vessels were stopped, according to the IRGC. The group also claimed its air defense forces shot down a U.S. MQ-9 drone over the strait, bringing the number of MQ-9 drones it says it has downed to 56. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed three Palestinians--two in new attacks and one due to wounds sustained in an earlier attack--and injured 21 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,618 killed and 175,920 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,602 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,794, while 847 bodies have been recovered. Palestinian journalist loses 16 kilograms amid solitary confinement in Israeli prison: Palestinian journalist Bushra Al-Tawil, from Al-Bireh in the occupied West Bank, lost 16 kilograms since her arrest on February 5, amid severe food shortages, medical neglect, and prolonged solitary confinement, according to the Palestinian Commission of Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs. Al-Tawil has been held in isolation since August 17 and is currently detained at Israel's Ohalei Oz prison. Her isolation was extended for another month on November 2. The commission said that she is suffering from dark skin lesions caused by scabies, as well as painful tendon inflammation in her hands and feet. Israeli prison authorities have ignored repeated requests for medical treatment. Israel declares 627 acres of Palestinian land near Ramallah "state property": Israeli authorities an order on November 3 declaring 627 acres (2,536 dunams) of Palestinian land in Beitillu, Al-Mazra'a Al-Qibliya, and Deir Ammar, northwest of Ramallah in the West Bank, as "state property," according to the Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission. The land surrounds the Israeli settlement of Kerem Reim, and the commission warned that the declaration would facilitate the expansion of settlements. Palestinian landowners have 45 days from the order's publication to file legal objections. Israeli forces displace 25 families in Tulkarm, arrest 45 Palestinians across the West Bank: Israeli forces carried out raids, demolitions, and arrests across the West Bank on Wednesday, WAFA reported. The Palestinian Prisoners' Society reported at least 45 arrests, including five women and two journalists. Tulkarm: Israeli forces 25 families from homes near Tulkarm refugee camp, converting some into military barracks. Israel's assault on the Tulkarm, Nur Shams, and Jenin refugee camps has continued for 647 days, displacing more than 32,000 Palestinians in what Human Rights Watch found amounted to war crimes and crimes against humanity. Ramallah: Israeli forces tear gas toward a school in Al-Mughayyer, causing students to suffer from tear gas inhalation. Soldiers also detained a teacher and closed the school entrance. Tubas/Northern Jordan Valley: Israeli bulldozers residential and livestock structures belonging to three Palestinians in the Al-Deir area of the northern Jordan Valley. Hebron: Under military protection, armed Israeli settlers olive trees in Surif, northwest of Hebron. Israel 's election committee approves results: Israel's Central Elections Committee presidium Wednesday to certify last week's election results, despite efforts by Netanyahu's Likud party and other outgoing coalition parties to delay certification over unsubstantiated claims of election fraud. The committee found no irregularities indicating that the vote had been compromised, it said. The results will be submitted to President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday, after which he will consult party leaders on whom to task with forming the next government. Trump says U.S. will cut $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel: The U.S. will stop providing $4 billion in aid each year to Israel "at the end of the year," President Trump on Tuesday, but will sell arms to Tel Aviv. "We give them $4 billion of things and money, and they don't need it. And I was approached by Bibi Netanyahu, and we've been talking about it for a couple of years because it's a lot of money," Trump told Fox News as voting was underway. "Why should we suffer the slings from lunatics like an El-Sayed when they don't need it?" he said, a reference to Abdul El-Sayed, a forthright critic of Israel who was elected in Michigan to the U.S. Senate. Trump's announcement comes as Congress considers phasing out aid to Israel, instead expanding U.S.-Israel cooperation in the countries' military-industrial operations. In 2016, President Barack Obama signed an unprecedented security agreement giving Israel $38 billion to its military over 10 years, which is set to expire in 2028. Trump seemed to suggest on Tuesday that he may cancel the agreement two years early, with Israel's consent, though such a decision would probably require Congressional approval. Even if U.S. aid were suddenly cut, there are still many years of already purchased weaponry yet to be delivered, according to AP. Yemen 20+ killed in Ansarallah missile strike on Saudi-backed government camp: More than 20 people were killed, and several others wounded, in an Ansarallah ballistic missile targeting a military training camp in the Maris area of Dhale governorate, Sky News Arabia reported. Meanwhile, Saudi-backed forces claimed that they captured the Al-Dahida heights and surrounding areas in eastern Al-Jawf governorate, backed by airstrikes targeting Ansarallah positions and supply lines. The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia announced that a second Indian national injured in the October 10 Ansarallah attack on Riyadh airport had died, following an attack that killed at least 12 people and wounded hundreds. Hezbollah denies sending military experts to Yemen: Lebanon's Hezbollah denied claims that its military experts are operating in Yemen and helping Ansarallah develop weapons, train fighters, and manage military operations. On Tuesday, the Yemeni Saudi-backed government claimed that 21 foreign military experts, including 14 from Iran's IRGC and seven from Hezbollah, were working with Ansarallah. Their roles extended beyond financing, arming, and training fighters to directly overseeing military operations and political and media activities, according to the government. In a statement on Wednesday, Hezbollah called the accusations "completely baseless." The group said that Yemenis can defend their country without outside intervention, and called for dialogue to preserve Yemen's unity and sovereignty. Lebanon Again violating ceasefire, Israeli forces burn homes and shell towns in southern Lebanon: Israeli forces to homes in the town of Hadatha in the Bint Jbeil district, while Israeli artillery shelled Baraachit in the same district, violating the ceasefire, Lebanon's National News Agency reported on Wednesday. name: Andrew Bowman
subject: A New Chapter for Wildlife
body:
This historic election signals a new chapter for wildlife conservation

This historic election signals a new chapter for wildlife conservation
                  

()

Defender,

Last night, Americans voted decisively for change, delivering a historic midterm election that will reshape the political landscape in Washington and across the country. For those of us committed to protecting America's wildlife and wild places, this is a moment of renewed hope and possibility.

Over the past two years, we have faced extraordinary challenges, including relentless efforts to weaken the Endangered Species Act, roll back protections for public lands and undermine decades of conservation progress. Through it all, Defenders – and you - stood in firm support of the animals we love.

We have fought back in Congress, challenged unlawful actions in court, mobilized advocates across the country and demonstrated time and again what determination and collective action can accomplish.

Last night's election will change the landscape in which we do that work in the coming years.

A new Congress offers opportunities to defend bedrock environmental laws and advance conservation priorities that have faced significant political headwinds. It also creates new possibilities for bipartisan cooperation around something we know transcends political divisions: America's shared commitment to wildlife and our natural heritage.

But we must remain clear-eyed. The administration's efforts to dismantle wildlife protections will continue, and the months ahead will bring difficult battles. A new Congress does not eliminate those threats, nor does it guarantee progress. What it does provide is a new opportunity to meet those challenges and pursue meaningful change.

That’s why I want to take this moment to recognize you, Defender. Your committed support enables Defenders to seize the opportunities now before us. Your support sustains our mission when it matters most.

Today, we have good reason to celebrate and even more reason to look ahead with renewed energy and determination.

Sincerely,

Andrew Bowman

President and CEO

Defenders of Wildlife

P.S. I invite you to check out my latest video (https://support.defenders.org/s/6248512/38SyG9Xl) on what these election results could mean for wildlife and our work ahead.

Defenders of Wildlife 1130 17th Street NW • Washington, DC 20036 defenders.org (https://defenders.org)

subject: Tonight, you renewed that trust.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY APRIL MCCLAIN DELANEY FOR CONGRESS
body:
Thank you for making this possible.

---
| | | | Peter, I have the honor of saying something I will never take for granted: **I get to keep fighting for Maryland's 6th District in Congress.**
---
**Because of you, we won re-election.**
I am thinking about the families I met on doorsteps, the small business owners who shared their hopes for their communities, the parents worried about the future their children will inherit, and the countless Marylanders who reminded me why this work matters.
You trusted me with the opportunity to represent you once, and _**this election renewed that trust.**_
Public service has never been about a title or a position. It is about showing up when people need you, listening even when the answers aren't easy, and doing everything in your power to make life better for the people you represent.
That's the commitment I made when I first ran for Congress. And it's the commitment I will carry with me back to Washington.
There is so much more work to do. We have families counting on us to make life more affordable, communities that deserve investment, and a future worth fighting for. **I am ready to get back into fighting for a future Marylanders deserve.**
To everyone who voted, volunteered, supported this campaign, or encouraged someone else to join us: thank you for making this possible.
I am deeply honored to serve as your representative, and I promise to keep earning that trust every single day.
With Gratitude,
April McClain Delaney

Peter, **With immense gratitude, I am proud to announce that I officially won reelection! ** **** The American people just sent a resounding message: WE have the power to determine our future – not a king or a president and certainly not a trillionaire. Now is not the time to tinker around the edges. Now is not the time to send another sternly worded letter. Now is the time to think big. Over the past two years, we’ve been playing defense. But today, we go on offense. Here’s what that means to me. **We are going to impeach Pete Hegseth.** We are going to stop this war. We are going to bring our troops home. We are going to bring gas prices down. We are going to bring fertilizer costs down. We are going to bring home heating costs down. **We are going to repeal Trump’s tariffs.** We are going to make sure that the money goes back to you—to the American people—not to big corporations like Amazon and Walmart. **We are going to get ICE permanently the hell out of the Hudson Valley.** We are going to freeze their funding. And while we’re at it, we are going to make sure that there are absolutely no Flock cameras here in the Hudson Valley and no data centers here in New York or anywhere in our country. **We are going to reverse Republicans’ $1 trillion cut to health care and expand Medicare.** We are going to fight to make sure every single American has quality healthcare they can afford. **We are going to break up the corporate monopolies that have strangled our middle class and our small businesses.** From Optum to UnitedHealth, we are going to shut down exploitative corporations that employ anti-competitive practices to drive up their profits at Americans’ expense. **We’re going to build things again.** We’re going to build 10 million homes. We’re going to create a national housing corps in the spirit of FDR’s New Deal. And we’re going to make sure that young people can buy their own homes. **We’re going to give tax breaks to _you_** —to the American people, to the working class, to the middle class—not to Elon and the tech oligarchs who have screwed us over for far too long. **We are going to clean up corruption in Washington.** We are going to ban stock trading by members of Congress. We are going to ban members of Congress from becoming lobbyists. We are going to pass term limits for Congress and for the Supreme Court. This is my promise to you. I am going to work like hell over the next two years to defend the American Dream, lower your costs, and build a better future for our kids and grandkids. Yours in this fight, Pat Ryan

| | Dear Peter,
This morning, With Honor Action Co-Founder & CEO Rye Barcott spoke with Hugo Rifkind on Times Radio about last night's election results. You can view the interview [here](https://us.list-manage.com/fjDTKBjd3Ud?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720).
As the release below indicates, we expect roughly the same number of principled veterans in Congress who have committed to [our pledge](https://us.list-manage.com/1lTdNxRMBPC?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720). Our hope is that they can find common ground and pass meaningful legislation over the next two years, especially in national security and national service.
Thank you for your continued support of our mission to elect and work with principled veteran leaders on Capitol Hill.
---
|
---
| | [**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**](https://us.list-manage.com/UAYPnvvoRAG?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720)
**With Honor Congratulates Veterans Elected to Congress, Including a Record Number of Women Veterans**
_Veterans will hold at least 79 seats in the 120th Congress, with at least 11 women veterans, the most ever to serve at one time._
**WASHINGTON, Nov. 4, 2026** — At least 69 military veterans won election to Congress on Tuesday, 65 in the House and 4 in the Senate, according to With Honor Action data as of 8:30 a.m. EST. At least 13 of the winners are new to Congress. Another 9 races with a veteran candidate remain too close to call.
Including the ten veteran senators who were not up for election this year, veterans are projected to make up at least 15% of the 120th Congress, which would be a decline from 19%. The number of veterans in Congress who have taken the [With Honor pledge](https://us.list-manage.com/132o8vl9II0?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720) will likely rise slightly from the current 50 members.
Women veterans gained ground at every stage of the 2026 election. At least 95 ran for Congress, more than double the 40 who ran in 2024, and 38 of the 258 veterans on the general election ballot were women, up from 21 in 2024. At least 10 won on Tuesday: 8 Democrats and 2 Republicans. They join Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), who was not up for reelection. When the 120th Congress convenes in January, at least 11 women veterans will serve, up from nine and the most in history. Candidate and primary figures come from With Honor data previously reported by [Politico](https://us.list-manage.com/QM6ZlRMeRGl?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720) and [Stars and Stripes](https://us.list-manage.com/1Dn5RzhzbEX?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720).
The incoming class of veterans to the 120th Congress will be more evenly split between the parties. At least 46 Republican veterans and 33 Democratic veterans will serve in the 120th Congress, compared with 72 Republicans and 28 Democrats in the 119th.
As trust in institutions falls, Americans still trust veterans. [With Honor-Gallup research released in July](https://us.list-manage.com/aFiaLk0SMbl?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720) found that 70% of Americans have confidence in military veterans, and 77% trust people with military experience to perform well in elected office.
When the 120th Congress convenes, With Honor Action will work with returning and newly elected veterans in the House to grow the bipartisan [For Country Caucus](https://us.list-manage.com/2sJykB3pQoj?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720). Barcott is available for interviews through the week; contact Susan Forbes at [press@withhonor.org](https://us.list-manage.com/PQIXwq5t7IQ?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720).
"Veterans learn early that the person next to you matters more than their politics. On Tuesday, voters sent a more evenly divided class of Republican and Democratic veterans to Washington, and helped produce the most women veterans ever to serve at one time. Many of them came up through a military that didn't always make room for them. They earned it anyway,” said**Rye Barcott, With Honor Co-Founder and CEO and author of** _**Courage Can Save US**_. “We're going to work with all of them to grow the For Country Caucus, because the next two years will demand exactly what they learned in uniform: put the mission first and don't leave anyone behind.”

First of all, **congratulations, everyone.**
Amazing, amazing work.
The better angels of America are ascendant, and it is a joy to the heart to see.
Al-Sayed. Hinojosa. Brown. Talarico. Acton. And many, many others -- **thank you, and thanks to every poll worker, PCO, organizer, activist, and courageous citizen who made today possible.**
You are our hope and courage shining through.
Trump may functionally concede. I credit his narcissistic cowardice that much.
I am much more concerned, however, about the powers that support him.
There are far too-powerful interests behind him - ideological, economic, flat-out pathological - for whom concession is an existential threat.
(I'm looking at you, Project 2025 - among others.)
So, as a contribution to the steadfast courage that it **will** take to protect and defend the Constitution of the United States of America against all enemies, foreign and domestic....
....now and into the future...
...and protect the people of the United States of America, ensuring **liberty and justice for ALL -- **
I offer this:
## Declaration of Interposition
When in the course of human events, it becomes manifest that federal powers no longer hold themselves bound by law, decency, proportion, humanity, or even the Constitution itself--when they protect the corrupt and the violent while targeting the innocent for imprisonment in concentration camps, when they desecrate the social compact on which this nation rests--then those who hold office in the States, and who have sworn an oath to defend the Constitution against all enemies foreign and domestic, are not only empowered but duty-bound to interpose, to withdraw cooperation from such actors, and to claim their rightful and God-given responsibility to protect democracy and the rule of law within their own borders.
Wherefore, the Great State of Washington declares that it shall:
#### 1\. Cease Voluntary Cooperation with Abusive Federal Agencies.
• Suspend voluntary data-sharing between state agencies and federal immigration authorities, unless explicitly compelled by judicial order.
• Bar state and local law enforcement from participation in joint task forces that target Washington residents on the basis of religion, ethnicity, or immigration status.
#### 2\. Protect State Revenues and Institutions.
• Place federal tax withholdings collected within Washington into escrow pending constitutional compliance audits, ensuring Washington's wealth does not subsidize lawless persecution.
• Direct state pension funds, investments, and banking functions away from federal debt instruments, shifting instead toward state-chartered financial institutions.
#### 3\. Assert State Sovereignty over Infrastructure and Commerce.
• Deny use of state highways, ports, and airports for federal actions that contravene constitutional rights.
• Review and, where permissible, revoke contracts and leases that allow federal agencies to occupy state or municipal real estate for the purpose of unlawful detention or discriminatory enforcement.
• Condition business licenses and registrations on compliance with inalienable rights--life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness--as articulated in our founding documents.
#### 4\. Strengthen Interstate Compacts for the Public Good.
• Form binding compacts with sister states to preserve free commerce, healthcare access, climate action, and freedom of movement, thereby insulating our people from federal neglect or abuse.
• Establish joint state protections for immigrants, refugees, and targeted communities, ensuring that no one within our borders is deprived of safety or dignity.
#### 5\. Defend Human Rights at the State Level.
• Enact laws guaranteeing that immigrants and refugees in Washington are afforded due process, housing stability, healthcare access, and freedom from arbitrary detention.
• Establish independent state-level commissions to investigate and, where appropriate, prosecute federal actors who commit crimes against residents of Washington within state jurisdiction.
**For the truth remains: the sovereignty of the United States resides not in federal agencies, but in the people, and in the several States who serve them.** When the federal government departs from its own compact, the responsibility falls to us to sustain the Union by guarding the liberty of our people.
Therefore, let it be known: the State of Washington will fulfill its duty--not in defiance of the Constitution, but in its defense. And in doing so, we reaffirm the most ancient of truths: that governments derive their just powers from the consent of the governed, and that when power is abused, it is the right and obligation of free people, and of free states, to set limits, restore balance, and protect the inalienable rights endowed by the Creator upon all.

| | | Friend, _did you hear the incredible news?_ Virginians across the political spectrum showed up and decisively approved the Reproductive Freedom Amendment, sealing a historic victory for our Commonwealth. **Thanks to voters from every corner of the Commonwealth, this amendment will become part of Virginia’s Constitution on January 1, 2027, explicitly protecting the right to abortion, birth control, miscarriage management, fertility care, prenatal care, childbirth, and postpartum care. **
---
---
Virginians of all ages, regions, faiths, and political beliefs came together to fight for our right to make reproductive health decisions without political interference. In every corner of the state, VRF supporters contacted tens of thousands of voters through door-to-door canvasses, phone banks, and organizing events. Thanks to your support, Virginians for Reproductive Freedom built an impressive coalition of Virginia families, doctors, nurses, and advocacy groups. We knocked tens of thousands of doors from Bristol to Arlington, and inspired millions of people to vote yes.
---
---
**We have so much to celebrate! Virginians made history with this vote.** Virginians can feel proud that we are the first state in the south with constitutional protections for our reproductive freedoms. But the work is not over with the passage of this amendment. We must continue to work to expand access to reproductive healthcare — from abortion and birth control, to IVF and pregnancy care, to labor and post-partum care — for all Virginians and ensure politicians stay out of our personal healthcare decisions. Thank you to everyone who volunteered, donated, spoke out, and voted to support this amendment. Because of you, Virginians' rights are secured for generations to come! In community, Han Jones Campaign Manager

Team,
Thank you. Last night, you proved that we can win an election by telling the truth. That we can win by rejecting AIPAC and corporate PAC money. And that we can win by loving our neighbors and standing up for what's right.
**I'm proud of the campaign we ran, and I couldn't be more grateful to everyone who helped make this victory possible.**
Now we've got work to do. We're going to fight for accountability for the deaths of Renee Good and Alex Pretti, and for what ICE continues to do to our neighbors. We're going to fight to end arms sales to Israel and stop the genocide in Gaza. We're going to pass Medicare for All and a data center moratorium, make the ultrawealthy pay their fair share, and stand up for our Somali neighbors, our immigrant neighbors, and our trans neighbors.
**And we weren't alone last night. **
Across Minnesota and the country, voters rejected Donald Trump and the MAGA politics of fear, hate, and division. Democrats won back the House and Senate, and we're heading to Washington with a majority and a real opportunity to fight for working people.
Thank you to everyone who called, texted, knocked on doors, planted a yard sign, chipped in, or stopped to talk with me on the campaign trail, even if we disagreed. And thank you to my wife, Coco, my daughter Poppy, and my parents for being with me every step of the way. I couldn't have done this without you.
**We're just getting started. Let's roll up our sleeves and get to work!**
Thank you so much,
Matt Little

**The Rhyme**
Mark Twain almost certainly never said that history doesn't repeat itself but rhymes. He should have. Place the presidencies of John Adams and George H. W. Bush side by side and the meter is unmistakable: two one-term presidents inherit the party of a national titan -- Washington, Reagan -- serve dutifully, lose to a charismatic outsider selling a new founding, and slide down the rankings, remembered as a bridge rather than a pillar. Reagan sits in every major scholarly survey's top ten; Bush floats in the teens. Adams has never escaped Washington's shadow in two centuries of historians' balloting.
But rhymes have meaning, and this one turns on a fork in the road.
**Adams Kept the Faith**
In 1798 Adams faced the era's equivalent of an intelligence-community pressure campaign: Hamilton's unauthorized "New Army," a cabinet conspiring with its author, warmongers promising Paris by Christmas. He chose Washingtonism. Adams purged Pickering and McHenry, broke up the standing army, and in 1800 signed the Convention of Mortefontaine -- peace with Revolutionary France -- against his own party's interest and his own reelection. The Hamiltonians split the Federalists, Jefferson swept the ruins, and Adams went home to Quincy. He paid with office to keep the founder's line. (The Alien and Sedition Acts remain his stain, but on the two pillars of the Farewell Address -- peace and public credit -- he held.)
Washingtonism, it is worth recovering, meant something specific: "cherish public credit... use it as sparingly as possible"; beware "overgrown military establishments," which are "inauspicious to liberty"; "steer clear of permanent alliances"; and above all, no faction wearing the government as a uniform. A limited republic -- solvent at home, modest abroad, jealous of its own executive. Adams kept it. Bush spent it...

Election Day was the clearest message it could be - "We don't like who's in charge and we're willing to vote for his opponents up and down the ballot."
It was a Democratic blowout, with statewide victories in South Carolina, Texas, Kansas, Iowa, and Ohio as well as Michigan, Maine, New Hampshire, and North Carolina. Even Mississippi went down to the wire! The Dems will enjoy a substantial majority in both the House (around 258 Congressmembers) and the Senate (at least 54 Senators) for the next two years.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c9e80394-4539-402f-b065-442a69c80755?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Forward's slate of Independent military veteran Senate candidates each fell short, with the incumbents winning in Idaho, South Dakota and Montana. Republicans won narrow victories in Nebraska, Florida and Louisiana as well. Still, this was a blue tsunami, with the polling underestimating the strength of the anti-Trump vote.
I expected Dems to have a great night, as it's not every day you have a 2nd term President with a 32% approval rating starting an unpopular war that has elevated prices for an unhappy populace. I thought Adam Hamilton, James Talarico, and Sherrod Brown were going to win. But even I was surprised by the breadth of the rebuke, as Democrats won and competed in unlikely precincts.
Trump's reaction was par for the course, saying that if he had been on the ballot - which he kind of was - the Republicans "would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!" But he also said that Democrats did "a good job" and that he was "absolutely willing to accept" the results. He admitted he would "look forward to working with" the Democrats and "we'll probably work something out."
So now what?
I am very encouraged as there has been a dawning realization among electeds that politics-as-usual isn't going to cut it, and there need to be sweeping policy changes that improve the lives of millions of Americans economically. That could be awesome. The Republicans didn't deliver - they actually did active harm via the war and tariffs - and now the Democrats will want to take big swings. I believe even some Republicans will go along with certain measures, as they know that people are unhappy. The new Democratic Congress will start passing legislation daring Trump to veto it. That's exciting.
They will also hold hearings and proceedings on corruption and malfeasance on the part of various Trump officials. This will be less productive. Some Dem members will be jockeying for '28 positioning, as the contest for the Democratic nomination will now begin in earnest. They'll be hungry for a video clip of them giving it to some Trump crony or associate.
The biggest concern is that Trump escalates the war in Iran further or initiates other military actions, or that the Dems try to prosecute Trump and D.C. gets bogged down in partisan conflict. Anytime we've imagined Trump is done, he's managed to claw his way back.
Still, Donald Trump is now 80 years old and has dominated national politics for over 10 years. All movements come to an end. MAGA may have ended last night, with Trump now the lamest of ducks. He's made his money. His followers are disillusioned. He may accept his lot and try to go out on a relative high.
The country is trying to turn the page, and now we will see what the next chapter brings. There is hope in the air, and I'm glad for it. Here's hoping we make the most of it.

clean_body: Two platforms recently decided not to pay us. You are now the entire budget. Two platforms recently decided not to pay us. You are now the entire budget. | Dear Patriot, is exactly one reason this newsroom continues to exist, and it is not complicated. It is you. I want to explain why that sentence is not a slogan, because something happened recently that made it painfully literal. I am now banned on TikTok. I am demonetized on YouTube. On TikTok I cannot get an account under my own name. Meanwhile accounts that are not me keep reposting my footage and building audiences on it. On YouTube, the videos still play. They simply generate nothing. I do not take positions. I do not sit behind a microphone and tell you what to think. I do first-person observation journalism. I show you what actually happened, and then I get out of the way. That is the whole method, and here is the thing I have learned in fifteen years of doing it: The more factual you are, the more of a threat you are. Let me be plain about what this actually means for the work. Most media companies have a stack of revenue lines. Platform payouts, advertisers, a parent corporation, and usually a billionaire who enjoys being invited to expensive parties. We take no money from the government. We answer to no corporate owner. There is no billionaire behind me. Two of the few outside revenue lines we actually had were eliminated inside a single month. So the arithmetic is not complicated anymore. Donations are not the supplement. Donations are the budget. And this happened in the same month I put two teams undercover in two different states at the same time. Two hotels, two rental cars, two sets of plane tickets, and two teams of people whose assignments I cannot describe to you yet. I want to be careful here, because self-pity is not a strategy and I will not sell it to you. Getting throttled is not remotely the same thing as getting stopped. We were never going to be funded by the companies we investigate. That was always going to end. What matters is that the work did not end with it. In the last several weeks alone, a woman we filmed buying signatures for two dollars on Skid Row pleaded guilty to a federal felony. A federal prosecutor said on the record that our video is what opened the FBI investigation. We put noncitizens on the government's own "worst of the worst" list on camera in Michigan, and the Justice Department wrote to that state. And we demonstrated how a single Minnesotan can vouch for eight complete strangers without any identification. None of that was funded by a platform.** That system works, and it is the only one we have left. Whatever is happening in the two states my teams are sitting in right now is happening whether anyone films it or not. So here is the arrangement, and it is the same one it has always been. You fund the mission. My team takes the risk. You see the result with your own eyes. They can take the payouts, and they can take the accounts. They cannot take the camera, and Thank you for all that you do, and please . . . stay tuned. In Truth,James O'KeefeFounder, O'Keefe Media Group P.S. Banned on one platform, demonetized on another, and two teams in the field in the same month. I am not asking you to be outraged about it. |

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

We have tough news to share: Justin J. Pearson came up just 1% short in
his race against Donald Trump-backed Republican Brent Taylor in
Tennessee’s 9th Congressional District.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261104-2.CKzQa4&refcode=em20261104-38415&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=38415%2E1203867%2EPeosM5 ]TN-09 election results showing Republican Brent Taylor with 111,968
votes (49.6%) and Justin Pearson with 109,429 votes (48.5%) with 99%
expected votes in.

We may not have won this one, but the razor-thin margin speaks volumes
about the historic, grassroots campaign Justin ran, uniting Tennesseans
across 15 counties on the front lines of our modern civil rights movement.
We’re incredibly proud of him and every single person who stood with him
to make the race this close.

Remember how we got here: Justice Democrats first recruited Justin as our
third 2026 primary candidate to run in TN-09, a reliably blue district
represented by a Do-Nothing Democratic incumbent.

Then, Donald Trump directed the Republican-led state legislature to take
advantage of the newly gutted Voting Rights Act to gerrymander the only
Black-majority district in Tennessee out of existence.

The Democratic incumbent dropped out of the race — Justin could have
walked away from this uphill battle against a MAGA Republican too.
Instead, he refused to let white supremacists and billionaires take away
the voices of hundreds of thousands of voters without a fight. He kept
running in a district redrawn to shut out his community, against a
self-funding millionaire who lent his own campaign $1.5 million, and came
within a single point of winning.

Justin campaigned in every corner of the new district. He held a listening
tour across all 15 counties, showing up in overlooked Black, poor, and
rural communities that politicians usually ignore.

That’s who Justin is. He’s the lifelong Memphian who fought for textbooks
at his underfunded high school. He’s the organizer who helped defeat a
crude oil pipeline that would have poisoned Memphis’s drinking water. He’s
one of the “Tennessee Three,” expelled by the GOP for protesting gun
violence, then reinstated days later. He walked union picket lines and
stood up to Elon Musk’s xAI plant to demand accountability for the
pollution it created.

He ran on a vision of an economy that serves the working class instead of
corporations and billionaires, and on uniting voters to take back their
power.

Justice Democrats is proud to have supported Justin from day one. Together
with grassroots supporters like you, we raised his campaign over $108,000
from more than 2,700 contributions, with an average gift of just $39.

That’s what people power looks like. Justin built a movement that brought
voters together across a district drawn to keep them divided. And
Republicans can redraw a map, but they can’t erase what he built. They
rigged these maps for Justin to lose by 21 points, and the movement he
bore swung this district by 20 points.

It’s a tough loss, but the infrastructure he built has changed Tennessee
forever.

The future of growing and organizing power for the working class goes
through the South, and we're ready to help every community take back their
power from corporations, billionaire oligarchs, and the politicians they
buy.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261104-2.CKzQa4&refcode=em20261104-38415&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=38415%2E1203867%2EPeosM5 ]Can you chip in to Justice Democrats today to help us continue
organizing in the South and recruit more working-class champions who will
fight for communities this Party has left behind?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261104-2.CKzQa4&refcode=em20261104-38415&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1022&akid=38415%2E1203867%2EPeosM5 ]Contribute $5

Thank you again for the support you showed Justin this cycle.

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

Good Morning!**
****What if we told you America tried getting rid of the time change 50 years ago --and people hated the result?** We all know the twice-a-year ritual. Change the clocks, lose or gain an hour, and complain about it. **But there's a surprising reason we're still doing it!** In this week's **_Flyover Focus_** , Amy uncovers the strange history of **[Daylight Saving Time](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJysz0FugzAQQNHTwC6IsQGHhReVKnap2m6ytAZ7HKYyODKTRLl91apH6AHel_755E7IibfLG65kJWYXs7_tbqPHnkiEisOVCnuUwhRoC7xdZCHhlZxq1XAAOLTdn4I62EikSNdkwYz62I4jdPVicfDz6LEfjDboR9REYIDQGEDE-Viz_akBtB0MGnrdGOqHzkA0Uc2BPFRdS4Ell-Yr8yYLxfTMdyqNz2ud7CJy3Sv9UqmpUtMz3-TWzFSp6f38_Ojd9PqZfV1suD44Jd4HU3XtZUVOv17-Yf1u1XcAAAD__3QCcDw)** , including a bug collector, two world wars, and a 1974 experiment that didn't go quite as planned. **So what happened when America tried to stop changing the clocks? clean_body: The 1974 experiment backfired. Here's why we're still changing our clocks 50 years later. | | | Good Morning! What if we told you America tried getting rid of the time change 50 years ago --and people hated the result? We all know the twice-a-year ritual. Change the clocks, lose or gain an hour, and complain about it. But there's a surprising reason we're still doing it! In this week's Flyover Focus , Amy uncovers the strange history of , including a bug collector, two world wars, and a 1974 experiment that didn't go quite as planned. So what happened when America tried to stop changing the clocks? And why haven't we been able to fix it since? ➤ And here's a question for you: Would you rather have more daylight in the morning or keep those longer summer evenings? Reply to this email or leave a comment on YouTube and tell us which you'd choose. If you enjoy this week's Flyover Focus - there's plenty more where that came from! Catch The Flyover Podcast for the news you need, seven days a week. () Thanks for cruising with us, The Flyover✈️ (Step One) The Flyover, LLC 1910 Thomes Ave. Cheyenne, WY 82001-3527 | ---|---

name: Brian Lenney
subject: We can’t keep doing this
body:
Idaho stopped the extreme abortionists last night.

| |
---|---|---
|
# We can't keep doing this
| | | [Brian Lenney](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
| Nov 4
---
| [](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
Idaho stopped the extreme abortionists last night.

We also decided that English should be the official language of the state and embedded in our constitution.

I won my race too, by double digits as always. But that's to be expected because Canyon County doesn't elect Democrats.

Obviously, the country was set back last night, but this is the time to dig in and fight not retreat into despair.

Last night was a referendum on voting for the same people for the same positions year after year after year who get into office and ignore the people who put them there.
This chart proves it:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8c647ac5-8536-4ec3-bb2e-3e579fbc5364?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
18-29 year olds were the biggest swing.
Two years ago we were celebrating how many young people were coming to our side, and now they're sprinting full speed ahead toward the Dems.

So, what happenned?

It's a question I have too...

What happened to mass deportations? What happened to "no wars in Iran?" What happened to the cost of living and gas prices? Did they really think that simping for foreign laborers would resonate with middle class White America?

Epstein anyone?

**Republicans lost because they forgot about the people who put them there.**

We can't keep doing this.
(C) 2026 Brian Lenney

# [#]
Wow. What a turnout.

I’m honored to have won the opportunity to continue representing CA-25. And I couldn’t have done this without you.

This is our victory to celebrate. I choose to represent the folks of our district proudly, and I’m ready to get back to work.

As we wait for more votes to get tallied and polls to report their numbers across the nation, I look forward to putting the concerns of CA-25 back on the list of priorities in Washington: affordable groceries, access to healthcare, veterans’ rights, and safer communities that our children can grow up in.

Whether you’ve been with me since the beginning or are just joining the team, all I can say is: thank you. Thank you for giving me the honor to represent such an amazing district.

I’m looking forward to doing good work, and I will not let you down.

Dr. Raul Ruiz
