### **Help us take back this country! Support PolitiBrawl by becoming a paid subscriber today:**
[ Support Our Journalism](https://substack.com/redirect/f61f4831-41a3-4628-9578-a9daa0df1834?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
**By Wendy M. Yurgo**
Republicans called Texas safe right up until Texans took it away.
They replaced a sitting U.S. senator and a sitting railroad commissioner in the primaries. Donald Trump had carried Texas by double digits two years earlier. How much trouble could they possibly be in?
Enough to lose the U.S. Senate race, the governor's mansion, the lieutenant governorship, the attorney general's office, and a seat on the Railroad Commission. In unofficial returns reported early Wednesday, James Talarico led Ken Paxton by roughly 12 percentage points and Gina Hinojosa led Greg Abbott by about seven. Vikki Goodwin, Nathan Johnson, and Jon Rosenthal also won. Texans had gone more than three decades without electing a Democrat as governor or railroad commissioner. On Tuesday, they did both.
Some Republican nominees were vulnerable, and the party knew it. Ken Paxton beat John Cornyn after Republicans warned Paxton would be easier to beat in November. Bo French beat Jim Wright in the runoff and lost the seat in the general. We can argue about how Cornyn or Wright would have done. Then somebody needs to explain Greg Abbott and Dan Patrick. They had the name recognition, the organization, and years in office. Texans knew exactly whom they were voting out.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f61f4831-41a3-4628-9578-a9daa0df1834?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
South Carolina was the Republicans' race to lose. And they lost it.
Lindsey Graham made his name as a foreign-policy hawk. National security was his thing. His sister Darline was appointed to finish his term. When she was asked in a Republican primary debate about Taiwan and the South China Sea, she said, "National security is not my thing." Trump encouraged her to run, endorsed her, and campaigned for her. Republican voters chose her over Ralph Norman, a sitting congressman. That was a misplaced use of the president's influence. What did he see in her candidacy that justified asking South Carolinians to give her six years in the United States Senate?
I have no patience for treating a Senate seat like a family inheritance. About two-thirds of South Carolina Senate voters told AP that Graham lacked the right experience. Then they elected Annie Andrews, the first Democrat to win a U.S. Senate race there in 28 years. The national mood made the seat harder to hold. Republicans made it easier to lose.
Then came Kansas. The last time Kansas elected a Democrat to the United States Senate, Franklin Roosevelt was on the ballot. Ninety-four years later, a Methodist pastor named Adam Hamilton beat Republican incumbent Roger Marshall. Trump rallied in Kansas twice in October. Hamilton won roughly seven in ten moderates, according to AP's voter poll. If two visits from a Republican president can't save a Republican senator in Kansas, the people running the party should spend less time asking where Trump needs to rally and more time asking why voters in Kansas needed convincing in the first place.
Georgia was a battleground Republicans knew they had to fight for. They still lost the governor's mansion for the first time in more than two decades. Former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms defeated Republican Rick Jackson and became the first Black woman elected governor of any U.S. state. Jon Ossoff held his Senate seat by a wide margin, and Democrats picked up other statewide offices. By the time you get to Georgia, the excuse that Republicans picked the wrong candidate in a few races starts to wear thin.
Yes, the president's party usually takes a beating in the midterms. That's a reason to prepare for one. Republicans lost both chambers of Congress and the governor's offices in Texas, Georgia, Nevada, Iowa, and Ohio. Democrats flipped at least seven Republican-held U.S. Senate seats in Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina, and Texas. In Texas, Iowa, and Ohio, Republicans lost both a Senate seat and the governor's office. How much of the map did Republican leaders think they could defend on habit alone?
* * *
# We will not give up hope, and neither should you
Tuesday was a wake up call to all American patriots...
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f61f4831-41a3-4628-9578-a9daa0df1834?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The battle ahead will surely be hard and up-hill. But think of the brave Americans who stormed the beaches of Normandy, or the men who fought and bled at Shiloh and Lexington.
They had a dream for America they were willing to die for. We cannot let their sacrifice be in vain.
We must fight for our nation with every thing we have within us, even on the darkest days, as our ancestors did.
**PolitiBrawl will hold our place in line on the battleground for information and news.**
We appreciate your readership and support.
Do not give up hope. Tomorrow is a brighter day.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..wYysa46eDeELHEh4sEf8SdKbMuJ6JjJ68x89I6RjtMQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=223497985)
* * *
_**(Piece continues):**_
If you want to understand the size of the beating, start at the gas pump. People were angry about gas and groceries. They were watching a war in Iran and asking what it was costing us and how long we'd be in it. In the AP Voter Poll, roughly half of voters said the cost of living was crucial to their vote for Congress. Roughly half said the same about government corruption. Fewer said that about the war itself. Republicans had spent years telling Americans to judge the people in charge by what it cost to live. Americans took them at their word.
Nevada and Michigan are both home to me. In Nevada, Joe Lombardo was nearly 94,000 votes behind in the unofficial count in Clark County, where he used to be sheriff. Democrats swept all six statewide executive offices. In Michigan, a state Trump carried two years ago, Democrats held the governorship, the U.S. Senate seat, the attorney general's office, and the secretary of state's office. Republicans had two years to make a case to Michigan voters worried about the economy. What did they give those voters to come back for?
Abdul El-Sayed walked out to give his victory speech in a white dress shirt, open at the collar, looking like he was on his way to a nightclub. Then I heard what he had to say. "We don't want our money sent to do apartheid, or genocide, or war," he said, in remarks The Times of Israel understood as aimed at Israel. El-Sayed is the first Muslim elected to the United States Senate. I've read the Quran, and I believe its teachings are incompatible with the U.S. Constitution. Michigan has given him six years in the Senate to turn his positions into votes. This is a warning.
Arizona may be the hardest result for either party to explain away. About 57 percent backed a measure restricting school sports participation and locker room access based on sex at birth in the unofficial returns. On the same ballot, Arizona reelected Katie Hobbs, who had vetoed similar legislation three years running. I'm a mother with a daughter who plays volleyball. I care who gets to compete in girls' sports. I also understand why a mother who agrees with me wants to know what the person asking for her vote plans to do about the price of gas. She gets to ask both questions. A party asking to govern should be able to answer both.
Democrats won both chambers of Congress, and the returns were still coming in when Robert Garcia, the Democrat in line to chair House Oversight, posted "LAWYER UP." Senator Ron Wyden needed one word. "Subpoenas." Hakeem Jeffries pledged on election night to reverse Medicaid cuts. He'd left the door open to impeachment back in September. The AP Voter Poll found broad support for Congress doing more to check the president. Where the facts warrant an investigation, hold one. But if the first thing you want Americans to hear after they hand you a majority is that somebody in Washington should call a lawyer, you'd better have something to say to the people who handed it to you. They still have to fill up their cars on Friday.
James Talarico gets six years in the United States Senate. That alone would have been devastating. Look at the rest of the Texas ballot. Democrats took the governor's mansion, the lieutenant governorship, the attorney general's office, and a seat on the Railroad Commission. The consequences will be felt in Washington and in Austin long after the people who lost those races have finished explaining them away.
Republican leaders spent years talking about Texas as though the state belonged to them. Texans took it away, office by office.
**The votes belonged to Texans. The loss belongs to the Republican Party.**

| | **Spartz: Republicans Must Regroup and Fight for 2028**
---
| | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
**November 4, 2026** **WESTFIELD, IN** - Congresswoman Victoria Spartz issued the following statement on the 2026 election: “Democrats ran a ruthless, well-funded, well-organized offensive across the country, using lies and exploiting people’s frustrations. However, I believe people will wake up and realize how destructive Democrat policies are. Republicans can’t afford another cycle of disorganization, weak turnout, and soft messaging. We need to get sharper, tougher, and far more effective. We need to engage Democrats in debates over real policy solutions. We also need to clean up our own party and confront those who collude with Democrats. “As for my race, God always has a reason for everything. Now I will have more time back home in Indiana to regroup and reorganize—instead of wasting my time on Democrat circuses in D.C.

“And to my political adversaries in both parties: I am not going anywhere. I will have more time on the ground now—be careful what you wish for! I will make some announcements in the next few months.”

Team, thank you. This campaign was the run of a lifetime.
Although last night didn't deliver the results we had hoped for, we came closer than the establishment ever thought was possible.
Running a 100% people-powered campaign in deep-red Kentucky is no small undertaking. None of this would be possible without my amazing team and supporters in Kentucky and beyond.
**Regardless of this result, I couldn 't be prouder of what we've accomplished.**
Even without this Senate seat, the movement for people-first leadership is palpable, and it doesn't end here. Times are changing.
Grassroots-funded leaders all across our country just secured historic landslide wins, and I am ready to stand alongside them every step of the way. **Together, we can end the era of political corruption once and for all.**
I can't thank all of you enough for standing beside me and believing in what this movement has to offer. I know the fight is far from over, but my hope for the future is boundless.
This won't be the last time you hear from me. I'll never give up on Kentucky!
Solidarity,
Charles Booker

subject: 🧡 Our power starts with caring for each other. Meet Jennifer!
body:
Join us on November 10 for a special space to heal, connect, and care for ourselves. | | | 🧘🏽 **When was the last time you gave yourself permission to slow down, breathe, and put your well-being first?** For many of us in immigrant communities, taking care of ourselves can feel like a luxury. But **we have a right to more than survival. We have a right to peace, healing, and joy.** 🧡 That's something [**Jennifer León Salinas**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMWn3R7U15hZOprFI75oZg46iCG-85MPnsOAUDArmeSa9zO4oUJEMIaXiV9ztCm8bIf53v-AfUEG7ZMxTXKXCKYIfxRepAuZwajA1Y1UWzy0-KyOkNg5bx5OHmG25yOfT1ZAa8Rf2ODt3YizjKhVMn_V0QAxMG3VIjMjQ1EFF3EV_WaWVfvKT1xq_K6U3YQ2H9a06iufYWJIEo3lurn8x7rh6HxyPZrP25-5oF5CB2TX-foG4LTNtFWARu6k2O6KPXNM8lijSM2bc3DduGagGISa2fjRoJWnK-n9dnWsORHYJN2yk__hN1BSntjQPg6-MNdeB2VdKc16P7InBefn_jQnHWn-JOZ5Q7SreQEoFBXZ2DqVEPezcFHOs-KhiufJD5w/4vg/7IjSX8EZSa6yjPazyrvoXA/h0/h001.FWcgCCtmbkDkkRCwSOxv6oZ1yomiNFRMC-EsDnS95Lc) understands deeply. DO YOU REMEMBER THE TRUCKS?

I do. Refrigerated trailers backed up to the loading docks of
hospitals in New York City, because the morgues inside were full. More
than a year later, about 750 bodies were still being kept in freezer
trucks on the Brooklyn waterfront.

Do you remember Hart Island? A drone filmed men in white suits
lowering plain pine boxes into a long trench, one beside the other.
Americans watched that on the evening news and understood that it was
really happening here.

Do you remember the hospital wards? Rows of strangers on ventilators,
sedated and alone, with a machine breathing for them. New York was so
short of those machines that the Governor ordered the National Guard
to go take them from other hospitals.

And do you remember what you felt when the number climbed again that
night?

You were afraid for your mother. You were afraid for your spouse. You
did the math on your own age and your own lungs, and you were afraid
for yourself.

For more than a million American families, that fear turned out to be
justified. I am going to make the man responsible answer for it, under
oath.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e11235427/UaHR0cHM6Ly9mcmVlZG9td2F0Y2gucmV2di5jby9mdy1yZW1lbWJlci10aGUtdHJ1Y2tzLW1iLW9tLw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDQ/LbmNsTjdvSXlxRA/qP3V0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1tYiZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPW9tJnV0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZnctcmVtZW1iZXItdGhlLXRydWNrcyZ1dG1fdGVybT0yMzg1N193cjFd/gautpYw/s2mf92813ce

Maybe your family is one of them.

Maybe they would not let you into the room, and a nurse in a plastic
gown held a phone up to the pillow so you could say goodbye through a
screen. Maybe you said “I love you” into that phone and never
found out whether it was heard. Then you buried that person in front
of ten people, standing six feet apart in the open air, with no
singing allowed.

That is the part I cannot forgive. Not the virus — we have always
had disease. The cruelty was in the rules they built around it, and in
the men who wrote those rules and then refused to explain themselves.

So let me tell you what the man at the center of all of it did on July
29 of this year, when the United States Senate finally put him under
subpoena.

Anthony Fauci raised his right hand and took the Fifth Amendment. Not
once, and not twice. HE TOOK IT 111 TIMES.

He would not answer for the gain-of-function research his agency paid
for at the Wuhan lab in Communist China. He would not answer for the
years of concealment, deception and fraud that followed. He would not
answer for a catastrophe that killed over a million Americans and more
than 15 million people worldwide.

And in all of those 111 refusals, he never once said their names.

INNOCENT MEN DO NOT TAKE THE FIFTH 111 TIMES.

So let me say plainly what not one politician in Washington has the
spine to say.

ANTHONY FAUCI IS A CRIMINAL.

His agency paid for the creation of a weapon in a Communist Chinese
laboratory, and then he lied to your face about it for years. Over a
million of our countrymen are dead. In my judgment that is not
incompetence and it is not bad luck — IT IS MASS MURDER, and I
intend to prove it in a court of law. Help me put him under oath.

If you're reading this, you know the good news. Democrats won the U.S. House and the Senate. Democrats won Senate races in Texas, Kansas, and Ohio; they could plausibly win a Senate race in Mississippi.
That's not normal stuff. That's a thorough and unapologetic repudiation of a president whose policies are bad and who's hurting the American people.
This was the headline earlier this morning from _The New York Times_ :
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b83865c9-494c-4d55-b858-772210b9c6c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But there's so much more good news than that. There are a lot of other races flying below the collective American radar that you might've missed.
I'm sharing this just in case you wanted to feel a little more excited and a little more hopeful about where we're headed.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MjIzNDc3OTc4LCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzkzODE0OTcyLCJleHAiOjIxMDkzOTA5NzIsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.0mY1-rcDZlUSK9rtkKypsjNPEwRrCgXkSMViOmQ_Uv8?)
### Gerrymandering backfired on Republicans
Gerrymandering is an inexact science. And when you get too aggressive, in a wave election like we saw last night, you risk spreading yourself too thin.
Right now, Ohio has [10 Republicans and five Democrats](https://substack.com/redirect/bd8cc808-49d5-443d-a776-d0982fa37de5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in its Congressional delegation. Pressed by the Trump administration, Ohio redrew its Congressional map, expecting that it'd yield [12 Republicans and three Democrats](https://substack.com/redirect/e034442b-7f52-480b-9b77-015e45d2229a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
What happened? Ohio Republicans spread themselves too thin, and the state will now have [seven Republicans and eight Democrats](https://substack.com/redirect/b16b2c3c-3573-4fa7-b9fc-35489f2c1034?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Same story in North Carolina. Right now, North Carolina has [10 Republicans and four Democrats](https://substack.com/redirect/e006d0ef-8bb2-43b0-836d-6a520071b794?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).1 Pressed by the Trump administration, the North Carolina legislature redrew its Congressional map, expecting that it'd yield [11 Republicans and three Democrats](https://substack.com/redirect/b878dacb-031f-4ab2-92e0-2380ebdbf00c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
What happened? North Carolina Republican folly will lead to a delegation that will likely have [10 Democrats and four Republicans](https://substack.com/redirect/4bdb7d90-b20d-4b89-9beb-7afcf6128877?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).2
Whoops! The same thing happened in [Florida](https://substack.com/redirect/c5224353-b6bb-4085-8e2f-37e349cb94f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Texas](https://substack.com/redirect/68c8c20d-d721-46fe-b1b5-a8a565c5d134?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and elsewhere too.
And speaking of repudiating gerrymandering: Missouri [easily defeated Proposition A](https://substack.com/redirect/b4ed3842-d7da-4f82-ac23-d3c1ff2beded?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the [proposed gerrymander of the state's Congressional map](https://substack.com/redirect/d03cb9d3-229e-4d2a-b313-e318ab6901f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).3 And just for good measure, [Ann Wagner lost in Missouri-02](https://substack.com/redirect/e5834bcf-d263-4b31-9fcb-9a820c6eaeba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a seat [I ran for four years ago](https://substack.com/redirect/8c972dd9-7224-4440-ab4b-290bcb55d95e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and a seat I've long said in private wasn't really winnable. Shows what I know.
I hope this is a lesson for political operatives and a staple of future political science classes: gerrymandering isn't a guarantee. I have to think this sort of norm-breaking, mid-decade gerrymandering won't be happening again for a long time.4

### State legislatures flipped, some for the first time in decades
One of the longest-lasting consequences of the [2010 tea party movement](https://substack.com/redirect/062034e7-e77c-40d1-b529-e3495bc7476b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was Republicans [winning control of a substantial number of state legislative chambers](https://substack.com/redirect/b179a47d-d8e6-4859-ba7a-988357c470be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). We're still living in the shadow of that, in part because legislatures have been able to draw themselves favorable maps.
That wasn't undone last night. But if current projections hold, it was an extraordinary night for Democrats winning back some of that control. Based on early and unofficial results, [Democrats are poised to flip](https://substack.com/redirect/f10e7ef9-6d9b-44cd-936e-9c1f0f7fb467?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
* Arizona's Senate, for the first time since 2000
* Georgia's House, for the first time since 2004
* Minnesota's House, giving Democrats control of both chambers and the governor's office (a so-called trifecta)
* Michigan's House, giving Democrats a trifecta
* North Carolina's House
* Pennsylvania's Senate, for the first time since 1994, giving Democrats a trifecta
* Wisconsin's House and Senate, for the first time since 2010, giving Democrats a trifecta

Most surprising of all, perhaps, is that Texas' House is likely to flip to Democrats, which would be the first time that's happened since 2002. And while Missouri remains controlled by Republicans, they [don't have a supermajority in either chamber](https://substack.com/redirect/919eb2a1-05c8-409d-9cdb-d32ae6cb6f08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for the first time since 2008.5 Republicans lost their [supermajority in the Indiana House too](https://substack.com/redirect/88bd6a4b-9228-4f5d-8c7c-e32a5964ee2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Indiana is yet another state surprisingly [poised to elect](https://substack.com/redirect/7bfb967a-760a-4d86-ba31-ba6a999463bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) several statewide Democrats.
### Voters strengthened democracy
[Amendment 6 in Missouri](https://substack.com/redirect/6eeade56-df42-4511-b9b8-e3e7e2e1506a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) handily passed, again with support from around the state.6 This is a big deal--[I've complained repeatedly](https://substack.com/redirect/1a73a753-e86e-420a-a6d5-6fcd2636f079?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about the legislature messing around with the ballot measure process, and Amendment 6 enshrines meaningful protections for that process.7
Those sorts of wins happened all over America. In [North Dakota](https://substack.com/redirect/0a2901c7-6bb7-4840-b954-4f3e819ae251?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [South Dakota](https://substack.com/redirect/d41e93f0-3e7c-40c5-b22d-e3d214f990ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),8 voters rejected the legislatures' efforts to make it harder to pass constitutional amendments. [Utah](https://substack.com/redirect/fc52e88a-5fa4-46fe-842e-228c750e12a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) did something similar. In Montana, voters emphatically passed amendments that [keep judicial elections nonpartisan](https://substack.com/redirect/3685cbf3-6f29-4a12-9c6b-9306de3ff401?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [protect their ballot measure process](https://substack.com/redirect/ada31838-71c0-496c-b3cf-818647399c4a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Voters there also passed [meaningful campaign finance reform](https://substack.com/redirect/26d46164-35e6-4eaa-9acb-b2ca30d4169a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
It's too early to tell for certain, but I think Alaska will--[again](https://substack.com/redirect/8cdd265d-9599-47b5-8bad-0401a1052edf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--[defeat an effort](https://substack.com/redirect/00cc781a-6491-45c1-bc66-d90ffcf33c14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to get rid of ranked-choice voting.9
This wasn't a uniform win. Question 3 in Massachusetts, which would've created a top-two open primary, [failed](https://substack.com/redirect/d31d95db-47aa-42b5-baa1-5e998c51a8e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and that's too bad. But overall, it was a great night for democracy.
### The tide is turning on online sports gambling
Online sports gambling is dangerous and destructive. I [write](https://substack.com/redirect/09a90ec9-1240-4f0f-99be-f793ec164dd5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [about](https://substack.com/redirect/c08df8d4-cef4-4a7f-955c-e6c7254c043e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [this](https://substack.com/redirect/5dc4949b-8f43-4cca-87f9-f72c4378f2d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [a](https://substack.com/redirect/a08c3730-fe15-4618-b5e8-af0d47294fda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [lot](https://substack.com/redirect/034e65f5-9b23-4fc8-a70f-da0234dfb19b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). So I was happy and relieved to see that Nebraskans [defeated two](https://substack.com/redirect/14761e5e-e941-41db-93b6-e9f492a394fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [ballot measures](https://substack.com/redirect/eccc600e-2484-479e-a776-cab7aa9ecfbe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that would have legalized online sports gambling.
The shift in public opinion has been happening for a while now:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c08df8d4-cef4-4a7f-955c-e6c7254c043e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Public opinion is turning against sports gambling](https://substack.com/redirect/c08df8d4-cef4-4a7f-955c-e6c7254c043e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/profile/12425779-ben-samuels)| | *
---|---|---
| December 17, 2025
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/c08df8d4-cef4-4a7f-955c-e6c7254c043e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But this is a big deal because, by some measures, these sports gambling ballot measures in Nebraska were the [most expensive in the history of the state](https://substack.com/redirect/ebcd1aa4-73e7-49ef-8d9c-df714f87a0cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).10 The sports gambling industry is spending substantially, obviously on ads to recruit customers but also on political giving. Among issue-specific advocacy groups, super PACs that supported legalized sports gambling were the second-largest this cycle, behind only the pro-cryptocurrency people.11
Based on these Nebraska ballot measures, and based on polling I look at, their efforts to buy public opinion don't seem to be working.
### Some truly odious candidates lost
Republican Bo French, [so plainly bigoted](https://substack.com/redirect/071f5cd2-7391-4f52-af96-32ff2091f5aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that [Karl Rove endorsed his Democratic opponent](https://substack.com/redirect/56cc1226-f022-4324-b069-1b553c7c5228?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [lost his statewide election](https://substack.com/redirect/bf8c8121-4271-4f05-8425-2b2c49a84a9b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for Texas railroad commissioner.
[Brandon Herrera](https://substack.com/redirect/caf9b57a-2e59-4989-960b-a0f8651dc48c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), known as "the AK guy" who had to issue a clarification that [he was not, in fact, a neo-Nazi](https://substack.com/redirect/38386710-5439-4d7b-977d-4f99b313b07d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [lost his election](https://substack.com/redirect/2a4a0dd1-dc98-467a-b147-d7c616ec37e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for Texas' 23rd congressional district.
[Alex Kolodin](https://substack.com/redirect/97b75afb-bda9-4275-b84b-7da7ef817ef4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), an election denier who would've run Arizona's elections as its secretary of state, [lost](https://substack.com/redirect/8a24bc01-80a3-447d-b0c3-b35da39dd31e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Same with [Jim Marchant in Nevada](https://substack.com/redirect/8eb91ffd-52c2-4225-bf78-f6eaf3edc8e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [another election denier](https://substack.com/redirect/8620d502-c92a-4c4e-ae8d-85c885174b60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
And perhaps most wonderfully of all, Vivek Ramaswamy, a generally bad dude [who ran perhaps the most repugnant political ad](https://substack.com/redirect/294842e0-6702-4ae6-b141-ff1748bdc5ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) since [Willie Horton](https://substack.com/redirect/811ed8a4-737d-4df5-afe2-9402d6856ed8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), lost too.
Lots of lunatics won. But a lot of the worst Republican candidates lost.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=223477978&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIzNDc3OTc4LCJpYXQiOjE3OTM4MTQ5NzIsImV4cCI6MTc5NjQwNjk3MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.P8i6GW7HiAECtPVNGXIUUUvAJBi_NSODck72c5kpHk8)
### What now?
It's very 2000-and-late to quote _Hamilton_ ,12 but I've been thinking about [this quote](https://substack.com/redirect/814bff9f-33fd-474a-aee2-21533d0aa8b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this morning: "Winning is easy, young man. Governing's harder."
Democrats were elected to address affordability, to address corruption, to improve democracy, and to make our lives better.
This is an opportunity to focus on substantive policy change that I'll write about more in the coming weeks. And I'm encouraged by the fact that there will be dozens of members of the U.S. House and Senate who represent Republican areas and will need to cater to everyone, not just primary voters.
Democrats shouldn't just launch into impeachments of Trump and fall back on culture wars. They didn't work after the '18 elections, and they didn't work in '24\. Don't take the bait.
Americans just elected scores of new Democratic legislators. Let's not squander the opportunity.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MjIzNDc3OTc4LCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzkzODE0OTcyLCJleHAiOjIxMDkzOTA5NzIsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.0mY1-rcDZlUSK9rtkKypsjNPEwRrCgXkSMViOmQ_Uv8?)
_**Feel free to share this post with someone who will find this interesting.** If you're reading this email because someone sent it to you, [please consider subscribing](https://substack.com/redirect/008e2927-b765-47de-9deb-792afe547c6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)._
1
Already an absurd gerrymander, given that it's a pretty 50/50 state.
2
Some of this is attributable to having the ever-popular Roy Cooper at the top of the ticket, who [easily flipped a U.S. Senate seat](https://substack.com/redirect/65646135-8031-47f5-993a-ce25f965f752?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). But North Carolina Democrats flipped a bunch of seats without necessarily having the strongest candidates. Richard Ojeda, for instance, [flipped North Carolina-09](https://substack.com/redirect/3f2831a7-b6cd-4558-bc52-4d22334ee290?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), despite the fact that he was most recently an [elected official in West Virginia](https://substack.com/redirect/35c2fdcb-2be7-4f26-80ed-84799fc3627d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). He ran for the U.S. Senate there in 2020 and [lost in the primary](https://substack.com/redirect/70b9cfba-68f6-4e4e-b282-b720f6eed032?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
One of the races hasn't been called in North Carolina, at least not by the time I was writing this. So it's possible that there are nine Democrats and five Republicans. Even still, not what they were going for there!
3
I was surprised how decisive this was; it was defeated in counties all over the state. Take Oregon County, Missouri, for example: [Trump won 84% of the vote there in '24](https://substack.com/redirect/5f40d727-0719-4100-a27c-d540d35fe522?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and Prop A lost there. This was a bipartisan repudiation of gerrymandering in Missouri.
4
A lot of these seats will probably flip back at some point; it's hard to imagine the 2028 election will be like this. But I think people will be pointing to this as an example of the so-called [dummymander](https://substack.com/redirect/46eeb6c5-1a04-42f3-bf42-1bdec9bd4b78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for a very long time.
5
This is more than a symbolic victory. It means, for instance, that the legislature cannot unilaterally pass legislation with an [emergency clause](https://substack.com/redirect/3b3104e3-d51a-43c7-ac16-89757d348cac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which expedites legislation and exempts it in some situations from a veto referendum.
6
Other than perhaps being on the wrong side of [Amendment 8](https://substack.com/redirect/26d46164-35e6-4eaa-9acb-b2ca30d4169a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--which I called "the least consequential statewide ballot measure"--we had a good night on Missouri's ballot measures:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/782ea7f6-2cc7-4f84-94a0-fd10574ea36e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Voter guide for November 3](https://substack.com/redirect/782ea7f6-2cc7-4f84-94a0-fd10574ea36e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| [| Read full story

7
It's an abstract idea, but it matters. For instance, abortion access--which Missourians [also voted to protect last night](https://substack.com/redirect/6c24756a-6b2e-4fb1-82a6-d7b4167a7c6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--is likely here to stay because of Amendment 6. Writing trick ballot language is now plainly unconstitutional. But this is a protection that extends to all sorts of initiatives that voters want.
8
South Dakota also [defeated a ballot measure](https://substack.com/redirect/82d5ca54-1a54-4542-b435-ee5e22477626?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that would've rolled back the state's Medicaid expansion.
9
I've been a longtime supporter of ranked-choice voting:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/df432142-4c15-4322-b7a9-e064acb67817?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [The case for ranked-choice voting and open primaries](https://substack.com/redirect/df432142-4c15-4322-b7a9-e064acb67817?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/profile/12425779-ben-samuels)| | *
---|---|---
| October 22, 2024
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/df432142-4c15-4322-b7a9-e064acb67817?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Having paid attention to elections in Alaska--[the "Dan Sullivan" shenanigans](https://substack.com/redirect/47b815a9-ceb2-412c-ab45-86197c9b9761?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Democrats and [similar underhandedness by Republicans](https://substack.com/redirect/0107e76e-cda0-4203-ac08-ce2736aee576?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--I do think this system needs reform.
Ranked-choice works in the sense that Alaska has some of the most effective cross-partisan legislating of any state in America. Ranked-choice voting is doing its job. But this sort of election tinkering undermines faith in the system, and something about ballot qualification should probably change.
I honestly don't know what form that takes. But we should think about how to keep ranked-choice voting and the benefits it confers without encouraging this sort of plainly bad-faith manipulation of it.
10
It sort of depends how you count. In 2024, there were dueling ballot measures related to abortion access. In aggregate, [more was spent on those](https://substack.com/redirect/3dda862e-6678-4f1e-8fcb-23243a16a051?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than was spent supporting the sports gambling ballot measures. But those were for competing ballot measures, not complementary ones, and there was roughly equal spending on both sides of that issue in '24.
So it's a little squishy. Still, it's definitely fair to say that these sports gambling measures were _among_ the most expensive in the history of Nebraska, if not the most expensive.
11
This is also complicated because a) there are a ton of smaller super PACs, and b) sometimes the objectives of a super PAC are opaque. But here's a graph that illustrates some of the largest super PACs this cycle:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/083329bf-33ce-474f-a63d-8231d3ef6fef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It's complicated because certain advocacy groups have multiple super PACs they operate. But across the two largest sports gambling super PACs, they spent $145 million on this election, behind only the cryptocurrency super PACs that spent $182 million.
You can look up this data in more detail on the [FEC website](https://substack.com/redirect/26d938ea-a357-47f3-92d7-01cc31228d6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Note that the accounting here can be weird, because there are often transfers that go from one super PAC to another. There's likely some double-counting. But this should give you some directional sense of what's what.
By the way: I think this chart is really interesting and I might write a stand-alone article about it at some point.
12
And making a [2000-and-late](https://substack.com/redirect/c08263bf-ef90-46eb-964a-53f1f2039d5f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reference is, itself, very 2000-and-late.

| | Hi Friend, The voters have spoken, and last night we came up short. I congratulate Congressman Stauber on his victory.I want you to know how grateful I am. To the more than 1,000 volunteers who knocked on doors, made calls, and gave up evenings and weekends to this campaign. To everyone who donated, who shared our message, who talked with a neighbor or brought a friend to the polls. And to the people across this district who came to our town halls and told me what matters most to them. You made this campaign what it was. We started this race as underdogs in a district that hasn’t been competitive in years, and together, we made it a real race. That’s not nothing. It shows that people across northern and central Minnesota want a representative who shows up, listens, and fights for opportunity here at home. I am honored that 168,350 District 8 voters cast their ballots for me, and delivered Congressman Stauber’s closest reelection race to date. The issues that brought us together aren’t going away: rural hospitals that need support, jobs that should stay in Minnesota, families struggling with rising costs, and the land and water we love.I’ll keep standing up for them, and I hope you will too. I’m so proud of what we built together. Thank you for believing in this campaign, in me, and the future of this district.We’re just getting started,

clean_body: What we built together isn’t going anywhere.| | | | | Hi Friend, The voters have spoken, and last night we came up short. I congratulate Congressman Stauber on his victory.I want you to know how grateful I am. To the more than 1,000 volunteers who knocked on doors, made calls, and gave up evenings and weekends to this campaign. To everyone who donated, who shared our message, who talked with a neighbor or brought a friend to the polls. And to the people across this district who came to our town halls and told me what matters most to them. You made this campaign what it was. We started this race as underdogs in a district that hasn’t been competitive in years, and together, we made it a real race. That’s not nothing. It shows that people across northern and central Minnesota want a representative who shows up, listens, and fights for opportunity here at home. I am honored that 168,350 District 8 voters cast their ballots for me, and delivered Congressman Stauber’s closest reelection race to date. The issues that brought us together aren’t going away: rural hospitals that need support, jobs that should stay in Minnesota, families struggling with rising costs, and the land and water we love.I’ll keep standing up for them, and I hope you will too. I’m so proud of what we built together. Thank you for believing in this campaign, in me, and the future of this district.We’re just getting started, Trina Swanson | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Trina for Congress Trina for Congress PO Box 1063 Duluth, MN 55810 United States If you believe you received this message in error or wish to no longer receive email from us, please .

Dear Friends, Last night, we redefined the politics of our community and our country. We defied the odds and shattered the sense of what is possible in Virginia, transforming a district with two blue dots surrounded by deep red into a mosaic of blue, purple, pink and red. We helped to flip the City Council in Lynchburg and put three historic freedoms into the Virginia Constitution. And we are not done yet. We are in overtime and still leaving it all on the field. We are behind in the count, but the next two days will include a canvass, ballot curing, and counting more outstanding ballots than the current lead. We owe it to the voters and to our democracy to make sure that every vote is counted, and we will keep you updated – not like you have not been hitting refresh already on VPAP! – with any developments from the count. As we continue our fight to flip this seat, I hope you will take a moment to celebrate what we have already won. In every single county, we overperformed 2022 numbers. We overperformed in Goochland by 16.2 points from 2022, 17.7 points in Buckingham, and by double-digit numbers in every single jurisdiction except Charlottesville City. We turned Prince Edward County blue again.

| | | Friends, What a night for our democracy and our fundamental right to vote! It is truly hard to find the words, even as votes are still being counted, to describe how great it has been to watch Americans from coast to coast stand up and make their voices heard. Thank you for voting, thank you for your support of us, and thank you for all you did to take part in this election and help others do so. A movement this big and results this good only come from a full team effort. Before we get into the impact, I want to share this snapshot of election results from Mississippi. Every time someone says their vote doesn't matter, this should pop up:
---
---
I'll save you the math: With nearly one million votes cast and almost all of them counted, one candidate leads by 43 votes. Not 43,000, not 4,300, 43 individual votes. Regardless of the eventual winner, this election should showcase how important voting is, and how critical it is that we fight for every vote. Voter Action Project is part of a coalition launching a campaign today to make every vote count. We hope you sign on. This race in Mississippi, like so many others across the country, is not over, and we need to ensure that every eligible ballot is counted and not discarded. We'll have more news soon, but the work to defend our fundamental right to vote will go on, and our movement will continue. Most of all, we have to hold these new majorities in Congress and in the states accountable for their promises and the work we sent them there to do. Before that, however, a deep thank you goes out from our team to all of you. We are grateful for the opportunity you gave us to make a difference for voters across the country and protect our fundamental right to vote. We couldn't have done it without you, and we will never forget the trust you placed in us to get the job done.Onward,MikeMichael Kanick

clean_body: We truly appreciate your support of Voter Action Project.| | | | | | Friends, What a night for our democracy and our fundamental right to vote! It is truly hard to find the words, even as votes are still being counted, to describe how great it has been to watch Americans from coast to coast stand up and make their voices heard. Thank you for voting, thank you for your support of us, and thank you for all you did to take part in this election and help others do so. A movement this big and results this good only come from a full team effort. Before we get into the impact, I want to share this snapshot of election results from Mississippi. Every time someone says their vote doesn't matter, this should pop up: I'll save you the math: With nearly one million votes cast and almost all of them counted, one candidate leads by 43 votes. Not 43,000, not 4,300, 43 individual votes. Regardless of the eventual winner, this election should showcase how important voting is, and how critical it is that we fight for every vote. Voter Action Project is part of a coalition launching a campaign today to make every vote count. We hope you sign on. This race in Mississippi, like so many others across the country, is not over, and we need to ensure that every eligible ballot is counted and not discarded. We'll have more news soon, but the work to defend our fundamental right to vote will go on, and our movement will continue. Most of all, we have to hold these new majorities in Congress and in the states accountable for their promises and the work we sent them there to do. Before that, however, a deep thank you goes out from our team to all of you. We are grateful for the opportunity you gave us to make a difference for voters across the country and protect our fundamental right to vote. Elections change lives. [Today, millions of lives change for the better.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/142899875/658414590/2141984067?sourceid=1151715&utm_campaign=27emaus-1101aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=postelection&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMmRjM2ViZC03NWQ4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QTS_4BEoaS9AfLXqx2qnkGE01PC2lUTCdlVg3547u2E=&emci=73e9f82b-14d8-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=32dc3ebd-75d8-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=954237) And this is no fluke. Since _Roe_ fell in 2022, reproductive rights have been on the ballot 22 times. Voters chose reproductive freedom 17 times. The majority is on our side.

But a win on Election Day is only the beginning. [New protections have to be enforced, defended in court, and guarded against attack. And our rights weren’t just affirmed at the federal level: we’re seeing unexpected shifts in state houses and governors’ mansions. In three states where abortion was on the ballot, voters chose to protect their rights. | Peter, voters in Missouri, Nevada, and Virginia just protected reproductive rights in their states. Because of them, millions more people now live under stronger legal protections. Elections change lives. And this is no fluke. Since Roe fell in 2022, reproductive rights have been on the ballot 22 times. Voters chose reproductive freedom 17 times. The majority is on our side. But a win on Election Day is only the beginning. We’re prepared: Already we’re meeting with partners and allies to prepare for the very moment in January when the most pro-reproductive-freedom Congress in history takes office. subject: We made history 💙
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Amanda for Colorado
body:
| | | Hi Peter, Last night, when I looked at the screen and saw that I'd been projected the winner, I threw my arms in the air and hugged the first person I could reach. What a surreal feeling. The room was cheering, people were crying, and I felt the enormity of what we'd just accomplished. **I am so honored to be your first Latina Colorado Secretary of State!** We couldn't bring all of our supporters on stage at the celebration last night, but it was important to me to stand alongside some of the incredible Latinas who paved the way for us. The madrinas, the godmothers of Colorado, who organized their neighborhoods, fought for their families, opened doors, and made things happen in their communities long before I ever thought about running for office. Women who taught me that you don't wait for someone to give you power. **You build it together.** Standing on that stage with them, I thought about Dolores Huerta. About generations of women who fought to be heard, who were told no and then did it anyway. And I thought about **how much that same courage matters right now** , when so much has felt so heavy for so long. The anger and horror of watching families be torn apart. The fear in our communities. The exhaustion of waking up to another violent headline and wondering what on earth you can do to make any of it stop. When the people making these decisions seem so far away, it's easy to feel powerless. But last night was a reminder that **you are not powerless**. You showed up. You voted for your own future, and for people who couldn't cast a ballot themselves. For the neighbor who's afraid to go to the grocery store. The families who deserve to feel safe in their own communities. And together, we made history. **I wish I could bottle up the feeling in that room last night** and send a little bit to every single one of you. The joy, pride and overwhelming gratitude. And underneath all of it, something fierce and defiant. A feeling that says: You will not take our democracy from us. You will not decide who belongs in this country, whose voice matters, or whose future is worth fighting for. Not without us standing up. Not without us fighting back. **Last night, we showed what happens when a community refuses to surrender its power.** There will be a day when we wake up and don't dread the headlines. When families can afford their homes and get the healthcare they need. When our leaders spend their time solving problems instead of creating new ones. That's the democracy I believe in. And last night reminded me that **we have the power to build it.** I know the responsibility ahead of me is enormous, and I don't take it lightly. But today, more than anything, I feel grateful. I'm so proud of Colorado. Of the volunteers who gave up their evenings and weekends, the people who knocked on doors and had hard conversations, and everyone who **kept pulling us forward when it felt like the whole country was sliding backward**. And I'm proud of you. Today, I hope you'll let yourself celebrate. We needed this. We earned this. And we did it together.
From the bottom of my heart, thank you. Amanda Gonzalez, **Colorado Secretary of State-Elect** _Paid for by Amanda for Colorado. Registered Agent Ashton Narzisi._

Peter,
Thank you, Minnesota, for putting your trust in me once again. It has been the honor of my lifetime to be your lawyer these last eight years, and I’m looking forward to all we can accomplish together in the next four.
To everyone who cast a ballot, knocked on doors, made phone calls, contributed, or talked with a neighbor about this race: **This victory belongs to you.**
Last night was an incredible night for Minnesota and our country. Here at home, we rejected Trump’s politics of cruelty, division, and hate and stood up for one another in the face of his threats and attacks on our state.
Trump tried to break Minnesota’s spirit, our courage, and our compassion. He failed.
I have never been more proud of my state than I have been these last two years. You refused to turn on your neighbors. You kept showing up for one another. And you made clear that Minnesotans want an Attorney General who will stand up to powerful interests and fight for them.
My mission remains simple: help Minnesotans afford their lives and live with dignity, safety, and respect.
It’s easy to feel helpless when people with power and deep pockets rip you off, whether it’s a predatory corporation or the Trump administration. My job is to balance those scales, put power back in your hands, and fight for you.
Together, we’ve reduced the cost of insulin to $35, helped people struggling with medical debt, taken on landlords who rip off tenants, and held fraudsters accountable for stealing from taxpayers. We’ve also protected almost $8 billion in funding from Trump’s cuts—funding that supports our schools, childcare, public health, and so much more.
**We won, but there’s more work to do. And I’m ready to keep doing it.**
For today, I hope you take a moment to feel proud of what you helped make possible. I’m deeply grateful for your trust, your hard work, and your belief in what we can accomplish together.
I promise to match your spirit, your courage, and your compassion in my next term.
Thank you for standing with me,
Keith Ellison

#### _**[Last night wasn't won by DC consultants. It was won by regular people who organized, knocked doors, and refused to wait for Washington's permission. Endless Urgency works the same way: independent media that answers to you, demands accountability, and holds our own party to the urgency this moment demands. Your paid subscription helps our small team grow, pays the people doing this work a livable wage, and keeps us exposing the corruption others would rather ignore. This is the beginning of the end for Trump and MAGA. For just $8/month, help us finish the job.](https://substack.com/redirect/092e527a-ae6a-4efe-8771-9637d546dd0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_

* * *
Folks, what an incredible night.
Across the country, the American people stood up and said enough is enough. Enough with the miserable, corrupt MAGA candidates Donald Trump dragged out of the ether of American politics. In their place, we're electing good, hardworking, decent, empathetic people like Josh Turek and James Talarico and Annie Andrews and Keisha Lance Bottoms and Gina Hinojosa, and the list goes on and on and on.
I've been doing this for a long time now and I don't think I've ever seen a shift in American politics this big. We just won Texas. Not just the Senate seat. Every statewide seat in Texas. We control the statewide seats in a lot of other places too, and we flipped legislatures all over the country.
And before I get into anything else, I want to make something very clear: this victory belongs to _you_.
I want everybody to celebrate, and you especially, sitting at home, should celebrate. At a time when most of the party leadership didn't know what to do, it was everyday, regular Democrats who stood up. You organized the No Kings protests. You knocked on doors. You showed up to ICE rallies. Never forget that Minneapolis and Chicago were ground zero for the resistance, for refusing to roll over while these people attacked immigrant communities. You didn't wait for permission from Washington, and you didn't need it. That's the same spirit that keeps this newsletter going.
You did all of that when the future looked pretty damn bleak. When it felt like nobody in Washington was listening. When the headlines got worse every day and it would've been a hell of a lot easier to tune everything out. But you didn't. You kept showing up. You kept fighting. And look what happened.
That's what I want you to remember about last night. Not just the numbers on the map or the names of the people we elected. I want you to remember what happened when millions of ordinary Americans decided they weren't going to give up on this country. You changed the direction of American politics. Never let anybody convince you otherwise.
This is the best election cycle for Democrats since 2008, and I want to enjoy at least a day or two of that sweet taste of victory. But I'm already seeing some takes from people in my own party that are driving me absolutely nuts,, and I'd be remiss if I didn't issue two warnings about what comes next.
The first: **this is not the end of MAGA.**
I keep hearing it, "Trump is done. Trump is finished."
He's not. As of now, at least, we still have two more years of this crisis. Yes, he's rolling over on Fox News, talking about how excited he is to work with Democrats, accepting the election results, and lording his veto power over everyone.
There's blood in the water. But a wounded animal is still incredibly dangerous. And I think we're going to see more chaos, more destruction, and more theft in these final two years if Democrats aren't prepared to do what is necessary.
That's why Democrats need to get to work and force Donald Trump, his administration, and his MAGA movement to defend everything they've done over the last two years. The investigations must be sweeping, public, and merciless. Every abuse of power. Every corrupt deal. Every single way these people have hurt the American people. All of it needs to be brought into the light.
Put them in a position to perjure themselves. Pit them against each other. Donald Trump is going to pardon everybody anyway, so force him to do it now. Force his DOJ to sit on its hands so we can shine a light on the corruption of this administration. Go after Elon Musk. Go after everyone who has abused our campaign finance laws. Go after everyone in the MAGA movement acting as a foreign agent and taking money from governments like Qatar and China and Russia. Go get them. Expose them. Show the truth.
Because if we don't go after these people now, if they don't feel the full wrath of the law for the crimes they've committed, they will scatter when Trump is gone. They'll regroup, and they'll come back stronger, with a much savvier plan to loot the American government and hurt the people we love. We have to break them now.
And frame every bit of it through the lens of affordability. Democrats need to make clear how this corruption has affected the lives and livelihoods of ordinary Americans. People fundamentally understand, and that's what last night showed, that the corruption in Washington is the reason their lives have gotten so much worse over the last two years.
* * *
#### **[Winning elections doesn't mean the fight is over. It means we have an opportunity to demand something better. Endless Urgency will keep exposing corruption, demanding justice, and holding both parties accountable long after the election-night celebrations end. This work is free to read and always will be, thanks to paid subscribers. If you're able, become one today and help us keep fighting. Just $8/month makes a huge difference:](https://substack.com/redirect/092e527a-ae6a-4efe-8771-9637d546dd0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

_Already a paid subscriber? Share this rant with someone who needs to hear it. That 's how we keep growing._
* * *
Take no prisoners. I don't want any Democratic infighting. I don't want to hear anybody whining to Politico about how we're getting killed on Fox News over it. Screw it. It's time. The American people will reward us with something that has been lost: a restoration of trust and faith
Which brings me to my second warning: Democrats are not back.
But a lot of DC pundits, DC politicians, and DC consultants are going to act like they suddenly cracked the code. Like we're suddenly popular again. We're not. This is a country recoiling from something deeply destructive. This is our candidates rising above a very bad Democratic Party brand. The fresh blood and energy and youth and media savvy coming into this party is extraordinary, and I'm so excited about it. But the pendulum can swing back just as hard if Democrats don't take this seriously.
Democrats must understand what, you, the American people actually told them last night. They told us they're sick of the corruption. They're sick of the cruelty. They're sick of watching the richest people in this country get richer while everybody else struggles to get by.
But we shouldn't confuse their rejection of Donald Trump with some sweeping endorsement of everything the Democratic Party has done. A lot of people who voted for them are still deeply skeptical of it. And frankly, they've got every reason to be.
The American people have given Democrats an extraordinary opportunity. They've entrusted us with power. But that doesn't mean we've fully earned their trust. We're going to have to prove ourselves, and we're going to have to do it by actually making their lives better.
We have to show people that government can move with the same urgency we saw from Donald Trump at the start of his term last year, but in a way that actually makes their lives better. Pass single-issue, easy-to-explain bills. Make Trump pull out that veto pen. Then go out and say: we passed this, it would have improved your life in this way, Donald Trump vetoed it, and that's why we need a Democratic president, more Democratic senators, and more Democratic House members. Find the things Democrats agree on across the spectrum, and there are many. Our policies are popular.
And take on corruption in our own party too. Ban insider trading. Take on super PACs. Make Trump veto that too. And if there are Democrats standing in the way of those reforms, they should have to answer for it just like everybody else. We cannot demand accountability from Republicans and then make excuses for corruption in our own ranks.
Because here's the thing: we can win every election in the country, but if the people who put us in office are still struggling to afford groceries, still getting crushed by healthcare costs, still wondering whether they'll ever own a home, then what the hell have we actually accomplished?
Winning elections gives us the opportunity to change people's lives. That's what all of this is supposed to be about. And if we lose sight of that, we'll deserve every bit of the backlash that comes our way.
Above all, approach this victory with humility. This is happening because so many people in this country are hurting. People who are giving up on the American dream. Who can't pay their bills. Who don't think they'll ever buy a house or start a family. Who worry that their dignity is being stripped away by big tech companies, that the concentration of wealth and power is making their vote feel meaningless, that nothing will ever change, and that Democrats can't do anything even when they're right on the issues.
We can prove them wrong.
So take today, hell, take tomorrow, and celebrate. I'm going to. I'm doing a bunch of media today, and this weekend I'm watching Notre Dame play Miami with my brother and unplugging for a little while.
Then we get back to work. We've got a presidential election coming. Here in Chicago, we've got a mayoral race. We've got more senators and House members to elect.
**[The DC consultant class is going to spend the next two years taking credit for what you did. I'm going to spend it telling the truth about who actually won this thing and holding this party to the urgency the moment demands. I can only do that because I answer to you, not to them. If you want that voice in this fight, become a paid subscriber to Endless Urgency today. It's how this stays independent, and it's how you make sure somebody keeps saying the things Washington doesn't want said.](https://substack.com/redirect/092e527a-ae6a-4efe-8771-9637d546dd0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Because this isn't the end. It's the beginning of the end. In some ways it'll be better, and in some ways it'll be worse, but the work goes on, and we need you to be a part of it.
Thank you for everything you've done. Thank you for this community we've built together. I get to do what I do because of you, and I love you guys so damn much.
God bless America.
With urgency,
-Mike

Because if we don't go after these people now, if they don't feel the full wrath of the law for the crimes they've committed, they will scatter when Trump is gone. They'll regroup, and they'll come back stronger, with a much savvier plan to loot the American government and hurt the people we love. We have to break them now. And frame every bit of it through the lens of affordability. Democrats need to make clear how this corruption has affected the lives and livelihoods of ordinary Americans. People fundamentally understand, and that's what last night showed, that the corruption in Washington is the reason their lives have gotten so much worse over the last two years. Already a paid subscriber? Share this rant with someone who needs to hear it. That 's how we keep growing. Take no prisoners. I don't want any Democratic infighting. I don't want to hear anybody whining to Politico about how we're getting killed on Fox News over it. Screw it. It's time. The American people will reward us with something that has been lost: a restoration of trust and faith Which brings me to my second warning: Democrats are not back. But a lot of DC pundits, DC politicians, and DC consultants are going to act like they suddenly cracked the code. Like we're suddenly popular again. We're not. This is a country recoiling from something deeply destructive. This is our candidates rising above a very bad Democratic Party brand. The fresh blood and energy and youth and media savvy coming into this party is extraordinary, and I'm so excited about it. But the pendulum can swing back just as hard if Democrats don't take this seriously. Democrats must understand what, you, the American people actually told them last night. They told us they're sick of the corruption. They're sick of the cruelty. They're sick of watching the richest people in this country get richer while everybody else struggles to get by. But we shouldn't confuse their rejection of Donald Trump with some sweeping endorsement of everything the Democratic Party has done. A lot of people who voted for them are still deeply skeptical of it. And frankly, they've got every reason to be. The American people have given Democrats an extraordinary opportunity. They've entrusted us with power. But that doesn't mean we've fully earned their trust. We're going to have to prove ourselves, and we're going to have to do it by actually making their lives better. We have to show people that government can move with the same urgency we saw from Donald Trump at the start of his term last year, but in a way that actually makes their lives better. Pass single-issue, easy-to-explain bills. Make Trump pull out that veto pen. Then go out and say: we passed this, it would have improved your life in this way, Donald Trump vetoed it, and that's why we need a Democratic president, more Democratic senators, and more Democratic House members. Find the things Democrats agree on across the spectrum, and there are many. Our policies are popular. And take on corruption in our own party too. Ban insider trading. Take on super PACs. Make Trump veto that too. And if there are Democrats standing in the way of those reforms, they should have to answer for it just like everybody else. We cannot demand accountability from Republicans and then make excuses for corruption in our own ranks. Because here's the thing: we can win every election in the country, but if the people who put us in office are still struggling to afford groceries, still getting crushed by healthcare costs, still wondering whether they'll ever own a home, then what the hell have we actually accomplished? Winning elections gives us the opportunity to change people's lives. That's what all of this is supposed to be about. And if we lose sight of that, we'll deserve every bit of the backlash that comes our way. Above all, approach this victory with humility. This is happening because so many people in this country are hurting. People who are giving up on the American dream. Who can't pay their bills. Who don't think they'll ever buy a house or start a family. Who worry that their dignity is being stripped away by big tech companies, that the concentration of wealth and power is making their vote feel meaningless, that nothing will ever change, and that Democrats can't do anything even when they're right on the issues. We can prove them wrong. So take today, hell, take tomorrow, and celebrate. I'm going to. I'm doing a bunch of media today, and this weekend I'm watching Notre Dame play Miami with my brother and unplugging for a little while. Then we get back to work. We've got a presidential election coming. Here in Chicago, we've got a mayoral race. We've got more senators and House members to elect. ** Because this isn't the end. It's the beginning of the end. In some ways it'll be better, and in some ways it'll be worse, but the work goes on, and we need you to be a part of it. Thank you for everything you've done. Thank you for this community we've built together. I get to do what I do because of you, and I love you guys so damn much. God bless America. name: Wesley Bell (personal)
subject: This victory belongs to YOU.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
I couldn't be more grateful for the people who made this possible. _Peter, we did it._

I'm incredibly honored and humbled to have earned the opportunity to continue representing St. Louis in Congress. But before anything else, **I just want to say thank you.**

_**Thank you**_ to everyone who knocked on doors, made phone calls, talked to neighbors, volunteered their time, chipped in what they could, and believed in what we were building together. And _**thank you**_ to every voter who put their trust in me once again.

Campaigns can be exhausting and unpredictable. There are early mornings, late nights, and moments when the finish line feels impossibly far away. But through all of it, one thing has remained constant: The people who showed up for this campaign. You are truly the backbone of everything we've accomplished, and this victory belongs just as much to you as it does to me.

I'm proud of what we've built together, but I also know that winning an election isn't the finish line. It's a responsibility. There's still important work ahead to make sure St. Louis families have the opportunities, resources, and representation they deserve. And I'm ready to get back to that work. **For now, I just want you to know how deeply grateful I am for your trust, your encouragement, and your belief in this campaign. Thank you for being part of this journey.**

With gratitude,

Wesley Bell

| PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI

Friend,

Her name is Luka Hein.

She was 16 years old when doctors removed her breasts.

Now she wants a jury to hear what happened to her.

But getting Luka into that courtroom has become a battle of its own.

I’m Mark Trammell, CEO of the Center for American Liberty, a nonprofit public interest law firm that takes on cases many organizations won’t touch.

And I’m asking you to help us fight for Luka.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTAsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA--WRqUh8SkNSJooSpoYrjxAmqwxQfqZmfI2jjEqSBW5ThugesLjqy17T3T4zhjritj6xkpX6NSDKDue0Jhd_auKCNADkCp2fZrCIMAN

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTAsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA--WRqUi-c2kbI4hpUAtAUWeWD2njDVw60pbvl6vv2r1QVVsRD_YxU4CdJHWqq2y2GypjzzOgHEKV9eTyzgzfGtgYD7TOe_XKs_wnog-
Help Luka Get Her Day in Court

As we described in her lawsuit, Luka was a deeply troubled teenager.

Her parents had divorced. She struggled with anxiety, isolation, school, panic attacks, self-harm, and thoughts of suicide.

Then she encountered transgender influencers online.

At 15, Luka began receiving gender-related care.

At 16, doctors removed her breasts.

Testosterone came months later.

Luka now alleges that the medical professionals who treated her failed to provide the proper standard of care and failed to obtain informed consent.

Her case is headed toward a jury trial currently scheduled for June, 2027.

But the legal battle is already raging.

Right now, the defendants are challenging expert testimony Luka intends to present regarding the standard of care.

These kinds of fights mean more motions, more legal work, more time, and more expense.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTAsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA--WRqUjFTqsvnnojKEN1NR2B3wlDAlQG7W93RVPvacqBijTaP9IeAxOoSn6-3NixIoirGNLmtoDMg2Iak0YzLQOmv8aJXCK5yREhUGT
Help Luka Get Her Day in Court

And that can become a strategy all its own — make litigation so long and expensive that the other side runs out of resources.

We refuse to let that happen.

We’ve been here before.

The Center for American Liberty represents detransitioner Chloe Cole in her lawsuit against the medical providers she alleged harmed her.

The hospital defendants aggressively filed motions delaying Chloe’s trial by years.

We fought back and now Chloe’s trial is scheduled for April.

We are prepared to fight just as hard for Luka.

But unlike the powerful institutions we face, the Center for American Liberty is a nonprofit.

We depend on Americans like you.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTAsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA--WRqUk5TDWkdj-RYcGBjtqDajbRQhnobS7SsJbZtXt_y8zHfYIAh3pb_leecEljXeIH0BoGvZvsnUK1SUfeD6mLIpslnYabq4WtKRk
Your first gift of $25, $50, $100, $250, or whatever you can give, helps us answer these legal challenges and keep Luka’s case moving toward a jury.

https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTAsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA--WRqUlrVbzjNZzoQZu8o1i_YvgdB_Jdq6E-6qAVrvt21x4zMmLToIY15vwUGWLtaK3W7yFIT_FfkdhDZPr16ryvCQz_iYUKkbODaKn
Help Luka Get Her Day in Court

This is why our organization exists.

There are Americans all across this country who have been silenced, pushed out, or left to fight powerful institutions alone.

We stand beside them.

And we fight.

I came to the Center for American Liberty because I wanted to get my hands dirty and be in the courtroom fighting these cases because somebody has to do it.

As I often ask:

Who’s going to represent these people if we don’t?

Luka had the courage to put her name on this lawsuit.

She is prepared to tell a jury what happened. Now she needs Americans willing to stand behind her.

Please make your first gift to the Center for American Liberty today.

Help us fight every legal obstacle between Luka and her day in court.

For Liberty,

Mark Trammell

Because they believe our government should _work for the people, not just the powerful._ And we showed the powers that be something important: **We will not be ignored. Not in this election, and certainly not in the fight that comes next.** _So the work doesn't stop here._ We have to keep showing up, Tennessee. We have to keep making our voices heard. And we have to keep holding those in power accountable for the votes they cast and the choices they make. If they want to _double down on school voucher_ s, then we will _double down on knocking doors_ until the next election. If they want to _ignore rural healthcare_ , then we're going to _run for office_ in those small towns even harder. And if they want to _continue lining their own pockets_ while Tennessee families _struggle with the rising cost of living_ , then we are going to _keep showing up at their offices_ , demanding answers, until they listen. We have to wipe our tears, pick ourselves up, and get back in the fight. We fight for the people who are too often left behind. For those who are afraid to speak up. For those who feel like nobody in power is listening. _And for those who can't fight for themselves._ That's why we started this campaign. And that's why this work must continue. And we aren't done fighting.**_ Thank you, Tennessee. God bless you, and God bless this great state.
