The November 3 midterm elections changed the balance of power in Washington. Democrats won control of both the House and Senate, according to the Associated Press and Reuters. Final margins are still being counted and certified, but beginning in January, Congress will have a new majority.
The shift is significant. But the election is not the end of the story. It is the beginning of another test.
Now that voters have changed the balance of power in Congress, what happens next--and what is the public's role in making sure that power is exercised responsibly?
## DECODE
### Conflict: What changes when power changes hands?
Congress does more than pass laws. It shapes the federal budget, decides which issues receive attention, questions agency officials, investigates government operations, and oversees public spending.
With control of both chambers, Democrats will lead committees and have greater influence over the legislative agenda and congressional oversight. They can advance priorities, hold hearings, investigate decisions, and scrutinize the administration.
But a majority is not unlimited power. The president retains veto authority, and legislation still requires votes and negotiation. Winning control does not guarantee that every campaign promise becomes law. Nor does it mean every voter who supported a winning candidate endorsed every position that candidate holds.
An election gives representatives the authority to serve. It does not relieve citizens of the responsibility to pay attention.
### Impact: Where public decisions reach our lives
Decisions in Washington can touch all four pillars of daily life:
* **Family:** Health care, education, public safety, and household stability.
* **Economy:** Taxes, federal spending, jobs, prices, and the cost of doing business.
* **Environment:** Clean water, energy policy, public lands, and community infrastructure.
* **Politics and Government:** The use of public authority, transparency, investigations, and accountability.

Those decisions reach our states, counties, cities, schools, and neighborhoods. And not every consequential decision is made in Washington. County commissions, city councils, school boards, and special districts make choices about budgets, roads, utilities, development, public safety, and local services.
### Strategy: Choose a concern. Follow it.
We do not have to become political experts, follow every issue, or attend every meeting.
Start with one concern that matters to you. Maybe it is the cost of living, your child's school, water quality, a road project, public safety, or how your local government spends your tax dollars.
Pick one. Learn which office or agency makes the decisions. Read an agenda when you can. Ask a question. Contact your representative. Keep track of what happens next.
That is participation. It can fit into ordinary life, with a notebook to keep you organized.
## AUDIT
### Look beyond the announcement.
An announcement tells us what someone wants us to know. Asking questions helps us understand what is actually happening.
Start with something simple. If your local government announces a new road project, ask why it is needed. How much will it cost? Who approved it? Where is the money coming from?
One answer may lead to another question. That is how we begin to understand a decision and its consequences.
Look for the public record: meeting agendas, budgets, votes, contracts, and updates on the work itself. Did the project move forward as promised? Did the cost change? Was the intended result achieved?
You do not need to know everything before you begin. Start with a question, follow the answer, and keep going when something does not add up.
The new Congress takes office in January. We can use that same approach in Washington: look at what is promised, what is pursued, and what is actually done.
And this responsibility does not belong to one party's voters. It belongs to all of us.
## KITCHEN TABLE PERSPECTIVE
Most of us have full lives. We work, raise families, care for others, manage bills, and try to make our communities better places to live. Civic participation should not feel like one more impossible demand.
It can begin simply: stay curious about one thing that touches your life. Ask a question. Take an interest in the answer. Speak up when it matters.
The election is over. The work of citizenship continues.
Our voices do not become less important after Election Day. That is when the people we elected begin making decisions in our name.

**Ivette DECODES

name: Caitlin Rourk
subject: Thank you, Peter
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/119050/images/Rourk%20Wrapper%20Header.png]

Peter, I want to thank you.

When I decided to run for Congress fifteen months ago, I knew the odds would be stacked against us. I still put everything I had into this campaign, because I believed with every fiber of my being that Texas families deserve better. I believed we could build a grassroots movement to fight for and win the kind of leadership we deserve.

Today, I believe that more strongly than ever. The things we've accomplished inspire me and fill me with hope.

Together, we mobilized hundreds of volunteers, knocked tens of thousands of doors, and came close to flipping this seat.

For years, people told us Texas would never turn blue. Last night, Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott, James Talarico beat Ken Paxton, and Democrats broke a 32-year losing streak statewide. We helped build that wave, and I couldn’t be prouder.

This isn't the end, Peter; it's just the beginning. We'll keep planning, we'll keep organizing, and we'll keep fighting for the leadership we deserve.

I'm so proud to be in this work with you.

Onward,

Caitlin
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP62/1/119050/images/Rourk%20Headshot.jpg]

About Caitlin Rourk
Caitlin is a longtime Central Texan with experience in public policy, military service, and the private sector. Inspired by her family’s legacy of service and shaped by more than a decade in the community, she’s running for Congress to improve public schools, lower costs, and ensure veterans receive the care and benefits they’ve earned, delivering real solutions rooted in integrity, accountability, and a commitment to the people she serves.

Peter, The votes have been counted, and you’ve chosen to send your neighbor back to Congress! Thank you, Central and Northwestern Illinois, for your trust and support. It’s the honor of my life to continue working for you. And thank you to each and every one of you who’s been by our side in this re-election campaign. To the volunteers, donors, staff members, and everyone who contributed in their own way: YOU are the reason we won this race. And Peter, we’re not heading back to Washington alone. I am excited to get back to work with a number of new friends and Democratic allies across our region and throughout the country, and January can’t come soon enough. Gasoline, groceries, childcare, a roof over your head. These aren’t extravagant costs. They’re basic needs. But after two years of full Republican control, we’ve watched countless neighbors feel the pinch from tariffs, poor spending, and an unauthorized, unplanned war to boot. The American people sent a strong message last night, and our mission on day one is to roll back these bad choices and make your life affordable again. Onward, For the people. Let’s get to work! -Eric

Peter, **Oh, Vermont. My heart is so full today! ❤️** Last night, standing in a room full of friends, neighbors, volunteers, and people who believe so deeply in this little state of ours, I was reminded all over again why I love Vermont so much. And waking up this morning knowing you've put your trust in me to represent you for another two years? _Well, that's a feeling I'll never take for granted._ **Thank you. Thank you. THANK YOU!** To every person who knocked on a door, made a phone call, chipped in a few dollars, talked to a neighbor, or cast a ballot: you made this possible. And I hope you're feeling pretty darn proud of yourselves today. You should be! I also want to thank every single person who put their name on the ballot this year. It takes courage to put yourself out there, share what you believe in, and ask your neighbors to put their trust in you. And whether you won or lost, that willingness to step forward and serve your community matters. Now, because of all of you, I get to head back to Washington with a full heart, a renewed sense of purpose, and the strength of Vermont behind me. **And as you all know by now, I may be tiny, but I am mighty. And I've got a whole lot of fight in me ready to take back!** I know what's at stake. Vermont has just one voice in the U.S. House of Representatives, and I intend to make sure that voice is heard loud and clear. I know you're counting on me to show up every single day, stand up for our neighbors, fight for working families, and push back against people in power who seem to have completely lost their moral compass. **And I'm ready to get to work!** There's so much worth fighting for. So much good we can do. And so many people counting on us to be bolder, braver, louder, more compassionate, and more determined than ever to stand up for what's right. **And if there's one thing I know about Vermonters, it's that we've never been afraid to stand up for what we believe in.** _We believe in taking care of our neighbors. We believe that kindness and courage matter. And we believe that when people come together, we can make some pretty**mighty** things happen._ That's the Vermont I know and love. And that's the spirit I'm bringing back to Washington. Because we've got families struggling to afford groceries, housing, and healthcare. We've got small businesses and farmers who need someone in their corner. We've got rights and freedoms to protect, a democracy to defend, and a whole lot of people counting on us to keep showing up. **And there's so much important work ahead of us right here at home, too.** We need to come together, find common ground, and make government work for the people who count on it. That means listening to one another, staying in the hard conversations, and remembering why we were elected in the first place. **Because at the end of the day, we're all here to serve the people of Vermont. And they deserve our VERY best.** I'm heading into these next two years more determined than ever to make good on the trust you've placed in me. But before we dive into everything ahead, I hope you'll take a little time today to enjoy this moment. Call a friend. Hug somebody you love. Thank a volunteer. Eat a little leftover Halloween candy. (_I certainly won't judge!_) And remember that even when the world feels overwhelming, there are good people all around us doing good things. There is still so much worth fighting for. And there is so much we can accomplish when we do it together. **Today, I hope you'll soak up every bit of this joy and take pride in what we've accomplished together. Tomorrow, we get right back to work!** With SO much love and gratitude, — Becca

Peter, the Associated Press called the U.S. House majority for Democrats. There will be plenty of time to unpack these results — but I want to take a minute to reflect on what this moment means. **Republicans tried to rig this election to lock Democrats out of the U.S. House.** On Donald Trump’s demand, they launched a nationwide mid-decade gerrymandering blitzkrieg. They dumped millions into this effort — to try to guarantee they would win the midterm election. _They failed.. _ **...But they didn’t fail by chance!** Republicans underestimated the relentless resistance they would face from the American people, and they did not anticipate the aggressive, united, multi-pronged response from Democrats under Attorney General Holder’s leadership. It was an outstanding, awe-inspiring effort. **We just proved that when we defend democracy with all we’ve got, we can and will prevail. ** We still have a lot of work to do. The next round of this fight is bound to bring even more twists and turns. Today, I just want to say I’m so proud to be in this alongside you. More soon — thanks, Biz John Bisognano

---

---

---

---
Onward,Gabe

Claire Valdez won New York with 83%**. Four of our five Indigenous women were elected, in a historic night for Democrats powered by people like you. Exactly two years ago--the Wednesday after the 2024 general election--I was sitting in a waiting room with my wife, about to get the ultrasound results telling us if we were going to have another baby. The television on the wall was blasting out the apocalyptic news of Trump's victory, and all I could think was that it might be for the best if we did not bring a new child into this fucked up world. Then we got the results--we were, in fact, bringing a new child into this fucked up world. So we'd just have to fight our hardest to unfuck it.
By sheer coincidence, this morning I took that same child to his 18-month pediatric check-up. There was a television in the waiting room blasting out the news--that the American people had said hell no to fascism, delivering the most stunning repudiation to the authoritarian right we've yet seen. All I could think this time was that the kid sitting on my lap has a real chance.
Of course, it's still just a chance--a chance that could easily be blown. And that's the topic of a piece I have today in _[The New Republic](https://substack.com/redirect/09405f04-5d51-48bd-bad7-c2601b643b1b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ that I wanted to share with you.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/45c0eb30-dcfd-4330-85f1-829939a87af4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The midterm elections are over. Yes, some returns are still being counted, but the outcome was clear before midnight on Tuesday. Democrats across the country crushed their Republican opponents, in many cases by running on "[top vs. bottom](https://substack.com/redirect/b05ba980-1f15-4156-99b0-d00c4582c848?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" economic populism. Victorious candidates--including James Talarico in Texas, Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, Troy Jackson in Maine, and Sherrod Brown in Ohio--pledged to take on the corporate corruption that has rigged the game against regular Americans. This message worked, even in Republican-leaning districts where Democrats were badly outspent, like Michigan's 7th, which Sunrise co-founder Will Lawrence managed to flip despite over $23 million in Republican outside spending, the [most faced](https://substack.com/redirect/520ef742-d723-403c-8f70-ffa988e5d875?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by any House candidate this cycle.
With these electoral triumphs, Democrats have seized the initiative. Now, they have to decide what to do with it--and already we are seeing very different answers to this question.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=223498719&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIzNDk4NzE5LCJpYXQiOjE3OTM4MTY4NjIsImV4cCI6MTc5NjQwODg2MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.mOLDzyftgZ-r8PgeMAhGQn2EhMPub6mG5RwKdl6yn34)
On one side is Team Small Potatoes. Senator Brian Schatz of Hawaii went on CNN recently to [articulate](https://substack.com/redirect/df81ac39-e465-442a-9d08-650b98435a4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this uninspiring view. "I do not think it is time to propose things that the President of the United States is guaranteed to veto," said Schatz, [who is in line](https://substack.com/redirect/2978cb25-6252-4a76-92b6-272fda8d2b71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to be the Senate's next Democratic whip and is a favorite to eventually succeed Senator Chuck Schumer as leader. "I think that's a bit of wasted energy. If we want to be more aspirational, if we want to make more bold policy changes ... that's for 2028. Right now it's about stabilizing the country itself." Soon-to-be Speaker Hakeem Jeffries signaled a similar perspective in August when he [preemptively announced](https://substack.com/redirect/7d51fcfc-7cde-4942-bbbd-1a9f5b9a81df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his opposition to Medicare for All.
On the other side of the debate is Team Go Big, who are refusing to cede ground to the Small Potatoes crowd. Congressman Greg Casar, who is Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, went so far as to directly [respond](https://substack.com/redirect/9272c775-a42c-4ae1-9cf6-dde42658b20d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Schatz's statement, saying he "100% disagree[s]." Casar warned that Democrats "cannot be the party of nervous lawyers who just tinker around the edges" or they will "sleepwalk into President Vance 2028." On election night, Senator Bernie Sanders similarly [declared](https://substack.com/redirect/645dfa4a-e573-44a2-9e9f-6b2385f9cf74?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that holding Trump accountable is not enough: "At a time of massive income and wealth inequality, we must do more. We must aggressively fight for working families."
These arguments raise an obvious question for Small Potatoes advocates like Schatz: Why, exactly, is it "wasted energy" to propose and pass legislation that President Trump might veto? Democrats have a wide array of extremely popular economic policies at their disposal: anti-price gouging laws to bring down the cost of food and housing, an excess profits tax on Big Oil to crack down on fossil fuel profiteering, paid sick leave and family leave and vacation leave, a congressional stock trading ban, a data center moratorium and AGI kill switch--the list goes on. What is the downside to daring Trump to veto bills like these that are supported by 70-80 percent of Americans?
As Congressman Ro Khanna [posted](https://substack.com/redirect/c7e18d87-09d3-4363-8ec8-c3951c351fce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in response to Schatz's statement: "Make him veto Medicare for All. Make him veto a $25 living wage. Make him veto free childcare. Make him veto Block the Bombs to Israel." If Trump does veto these popular policies, great--that demonstrates which side is fighting to bring down prices and end corruption, and which side is standing in the way. And it provides the clearest possible pitch for why voters need to put a Democrat in the White House in 2028.
While Team Go Big's approach is all upside, Team Small Potatoes' strategy has very real costs. Though Tuesday's election results represent a major backlash to Trump's garbage fire of a second term, the Democratic Party is still [severely unpopular](https://substack.com/redirect/8730cd72-ba28-4dc3-b942-7dcd17da0dbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and many working-class voters do not trust it to fight for them. If Democrats' response to winning big majorities in both the House and Senate is to timidly spend the next two years focused just on "stabilizing the country," as Schatz suggested, they will once again be aligning themselves with the status quo.
Americans are furious with the status quo. Democrats already tried a "nothing will fundamentally change" strategy--not once but twice, in 2016 and 2024. Both of these bad bets threw the door open to the fascists. To repeat this catastrophic mistake again--after an election in which voters sent such a clear message that they want change--would be madness.
Of course, there's another reason establishment Democrats might not Go Big in tackling corporate profiteering and corruption: Many don't want to. They oppose passing these policies not because Trump will veto them, but because they're scared of having to vote on bills their corporate donors hate. The problem is that they, like Trump, are on the wrong side of supermajority issues--which doesn't matter if a bill is never brought to a vote, but becomes quite uncomfortable when you actually have to pick a side.
We need to be crystal clear about this dynamic. There is no political rationale for failing to advance incredibly popular policies. The Democrats who oppose these populist measures are not trying to improve their party's political position--they're trying to protect their own pro-corporate interests, at the expense of the Democratic Party's future prospects.
Voters don't want small potatoes. They have made abundantly clear they aren't looking for leaders who will just manage a broken system. They want leaders who will change it for the better--who will go big. That's the lesson of this week's blue tsunami, and if Democrats don't heed it, they will blow a historic opportunity that this party may not get again for decades to come.

clean_body: Will the party go big? Or will it continue to feed us small potatoes? | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more Will the party go big? Or will it continue to feed us small potatoes? | | | Nov 4 | | | | | | | | | | | | Exactly two years ago--the Wednesday after the 2024 general election--I was sitting in a waiting room with my wife, about to get the ultrasound results telling us if we were going to have another baby. The television on the wall was blasting out the apocalyptic news of Trump's victory, and all I could think was that it might be for the best if we did not bring a new child into this fucked up world. Then we got the results--we were, in fact, bringing a new child into this fucked up world. So we'd just have to fight our hardest to unfuck it. By sheer coincidence, this morning I took that same child to his 18-month pediatric check-up. There was a television in the waiting room blasting out the news--that the American people had said hell no to fascism, delivering the most stunning repudiation to the authoritarian right we've yet seen. All I could think this time was that the kid sitting on my lap has a real chance. Of course, it's still just a chance--a chance that could easily be blown. And that's the topic of a piece I have today in that I wanted to share with you. | | ---|---|--- The midterm elections are over. Yes, some returns are still being counted, but the outcome was clear before midnight on Tuesday. Democrats across the country crushed their Republican opponents, in many cases by running on "" economic populism. Victorious candidates--including James Talarico in Texas, Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, Troy Jackson in Maine, and Sherrod Brown in Ohio--pledged to take on the corporate corruption that has rigged the game against regular Americans. This message worked, even in Republican-leaning districts where Democrats were badly outspent, like Michigan's 7th, which Sunrise co-founder Will Lawrence managed to flip despite over $23 million in Republican outside spending, the by any House candidate this cycle. With these electoral triumphs, Democrats have seized the initiative. Now, they have to decide what to do with it--and already we are seeing very different answers to this question. On one side is Team Small Potatoes. Senator Brian Schatz of Hawaii went on CNN recently to this uninspiring view. "I do not think it is time to propose things that the President of the United States is guaranteed to veto," said Schatz, to be the Senate's next Democratic whip and is a favorite to eventually succeed Senator Chuck Schumer as leader. "I think that's a bit of wasted energy. If we want to be more aspirational, if we want to make more bold policy changes ... that's for 2028. Right now it's about stabilizing the country itself." Soon-to-be Speaker Hakeem Jeffries signaled a similar perspective in August when he his opposition to Medicare for All. On the other side of the debate is Team Go Big, who are refusing to cede ground to the Small Potatoes crowd. Congressman Greg Casar, who is Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, went so far as to directly to Schatz's statement, saying he "100% disagree[s]." Casar warned that Democrats "cannot be the party of nervous lawyers who just tinker around the edges" or they will "sleepwalk into President Vance 2028." On election night, Senator Bernie Sanders similarly that holding Trump accountable is not enough: "At a time of massive income and wealth inequality, we must do more. We must aggressively fight for working families." These arguments raise an obvious question for Small Potatoes advocates like Schatz: Why, exactly, is it "wasted energy" to propose and pass legislation that President Trump might veto? Democrats have a wide array of extremely popular economic policies at their disposal: anti-price gouging laws to bring down the cost of food and housing, an excess profits tax on Big Oil to crack down on fossil fuel profiteering, paid sick leave and family leave and vacation leave, a congressional stock trading ban, a data center moratorium and AGI kill switch--the list goes on. What is the downside to daring Trump to veto bills like these that are supported by 70-80 percent of Americans? As Congressman Ro Khanna in response to Schatz's statement: "Make him veto Medicare for All. Make him veto a $25 living wage. Make him veto free childcare. Make him veto Block the Bombs to Israel." If Trump does veto these popular policies, great--that demonstrates which side is fighting to bring down prices and end corruption, and which side is standing in the way. And it provides the clearest possible pitch for why voters need to put a Democrat in the White House in 2028. While Team Go Big's approach is all upside, Team Small Potatoes' strategy has very real costs. Though Tuesday's election results represent a major backlash to Trump's garbage fire of a second term, the Democratic Party is still , and many working-class voters do not trust it to fight for them. If Democrats' response to winning big majorities in both the House and Senate is to timidly spend the next two years focused just on "stabilizing the country," as Schatz suggested, they will once again be aligning themselves with the status quo. Americans are furious with the status quo. Democrats already tried a "nothing will fundamentally change" strategy--not once but twice, in 2016 and 2024. Both of these bad bets threw the door open to the fascists. To repeat this catastrophic mistake again--after an election in which voters sent such a clear message that they want change--would be madness. Of course, there's another reason establishment Democrats might not Go Big in tackling corporate profiteering and corruption: Many don't want to. They oppose passing these policies not because Trump will veto them, but because they're scared of having to vote on bills their corporate donors hate. The problem is that they, like Trump, are on the wrong side of supermajority issues--which doesn't matter if a bill is never brought to a vote, but becomes quite uncomfortable when you actually have to pick a side. We need to be crystal clear about this dynamic. There is no political rationale for failing to advance incredibly popular policies. The Democrats who oppose these populist measures are not trying to improve their party's political position--they're trying to protect their own pro-corporate interests, at the expense of the Democratic Party's future prospects. Voters don't want small potatoes. They have made abundantly clear they aren't looking for leaders who will just manage a broken system. They want leaders who will change it for the better--who will go big. That's the lesson of this week's blue tsunami, and if Democrats don't heed it, they will blow a historic opportunity that this party may not get again for decades to come. body:
73% Democratic Control. A Historic Governor's Race. And Three
Grassroots Victories.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

NOVEMBER 4, 2026

RMV ELECTION REPORT

WELL, COLORADO. WE HAVE A LOT TO TALK ABOUT.

Election Day has come and gone, and while ballots are still being
counted, one thing is clear: Colorado's political landscape has
shifted dramatically.

Some of the results are historic. Others are surprising. And a few
offer reasons to celebrate. And we'll preface this email with the fact
that this might be a little shocking, even depressing, to read, but
it's necessary for us to face the facts.

But perhaps the biggest question this morning isn't simply what
happened yesterday. _IT'S WHAT HAPPENS NEXT._ Let's break it down.

_Want the full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast
here
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
or watch on YouTube
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
or Rumble
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

--

🏛️ COLORADO'S LEGISLATURE IS NOW AS BLUE AS CALIFORNIA'S
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

This might be the most consequential story coming out of Election Day.

Democrats are currently leading in 73 of Colorado's 100 legislative
seats — 49 in the House and 24 in the Senate. That's 73% of the
legislature, putting Colorado's Democratic representation on par with
California's and _ON TRACK FOR THE LARGEST DEMOCRATIC LEGISLATIVE
MAJORITY IN COLORADO HISTORY_.

Republicans are poised to lose seven legislative seats
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
with six Republican-held House seats and one Senate seat showing
Democratic leads. Not a single Democratic-held seat has flipped the
other direction in the preliminary returns.

And here's why that matters: _DEMOCRATS ARE ON TRACK TO HOLD A
TWO-THIRDS SUPERMAJORITY
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
IN BOTH CHAMBERS._ That gives them the numbers needed to override
gubernatorial vetoes and refer constitutional amendments to voters
without Republican support, provided enough members of their caucus
vote together. These results are still unofficial, but the
implications for Colorado's legislative future are enormous.

READ: _COLORADO DEMOCRATS HIT TWO-THIRDS AS REPUBLICANS LOSE 7
LEGISLATIVE SEATS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

--

🇺🇸 A HISTORIC GUBERNATORIAL DEFEAT

Democrat Phil Weiser will be Colorado's next governor
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
defeating Republican Victor Marx by a substantial margin, with the
race called at nearly 7 p.m. just minutes after polls closed. As of
this morning, Weiser had approximately 61% of the vote to Marx's 34%,
a margin of more than _27 PERCENTAGE POINTS_.

According to historical comparisons, Marx's defeat ranks among the
four largest gubernatorial blowouts in Colorado's 150-year history.
And here's another sobering statistic: Colorado hasn't elected a
Republican governor since 2002. That's nearly a quarter-century.

Weiser now inherits a state facing significant budget challenges,
alongside an ambitious 109-page policy agenda
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
RMV's latest investigation examines what he has promised, what those
proposals might cost, and the questions that remain unanswered.

READ: _WEISER ELECTED GOVERNOR — WHAT HE PROMISED, AND WHAT HE DID
NOT PRICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

--

🗳️ FOUR REPUBLICAN CONGRESSIONAL SEATS IN PLAY
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Remember the four congressional races we warned about in Monday's
newsletter? Well, they're delivering some of the biggest surprises of
this election.

_COLORADO'S 8TH CONGRESSIONAL DISTRICT HAS FLIPPED.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
Democrat Manny Rutinel defeated Republican incumbent Gabe Evans after
just one term.

Meanwhile, three other Republican-held districts remain unresolved in
the returns we're tracking:

*
CD3: Republican Jeff Hurd has moved into the lead against Democrat
Dwayne Romero, reversing an earlier deficit as additional votes were
counted.

*
CD4: Democrat Eileen Laubacher leads Republican incumbent Lauren
Boebert.

*
CD5: Democrat Jessica Killin leads Republican incumbent Jeff Crank.
_IF KILLIN WINS, SHE WILL BE THE FIRST DEMOCRAT TO HOLD THIS SEAT. _

Perhaps the most interesting development is in CD3. Despite the
district's long Republican history and questions about Hurd's standing
with parts of the Republican base, he's currently showing the
strongest position among the three remaining Republican incumbents.

There's still counting to do, and these races shouldn't be treated as
decided until they're called. But regardless of the results, it's a
giant wake-up call to Colorado.

READ: _DEMOCRATS LEAD ACROSS COLORADO'S FEDERAL RACES AS KEY DISTRICTS
CONTINUE COUNTING
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_--_

🎉 A BRIGHT SPOT: PROTECT KIDS COLORADO'S GRASSROOTS VICTORY
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Now, for some news worth celebrating for supporters of Protect Kids
Colorado! All three ballot measures backed by the grassroots
organization led by Erin Lee are on track to pass.

The measures include:

PROPOSITION 133: Strengthening penalties for child sex trafficking.

PROPOSITION 134: Establishing biological-sex-based eligibility
requirements for school and collegiate sports.

PROPOSITION 135: Prohibiting certain sex-characteristic-altering
surgeries on minors.

The preliminary results show all three receiving majority support,
with Proposition 133 already called by the Associated Press. These
measures reached the ballot through a citizen-led signature-gathering
effort, making their apparent success particularly noteworthy amid the
broader election results.

But here's the important caveat: _WINNING AT THE BALLOT BOX ISN'T
NECESSARILY THE END OF THE LEGISLATIVE DEBATE._

Because these are statutory propositions rather than constitutional
amendments, the legislature can subsequently amend or repeal them,
subject to applicable legal requirements.

Whether lawmakers will pursue those changes remains to be seen. But
the next chapter will involve implementation, potential legislation
and continued public debate. Regardless, for the organizers,
volunteers and voters who worked on these measures, yesterday
represents a significant milestone.

READ: _COLORADO BALLOT MEASURES — 7 ON TRACK TO PASS, 7 ON TRACK TO
FAIL
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

--

⚖️ A NEW SECRETARY OF STATE, AND QUESTIONS AHEAD
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Democrat Amanda Gonzalez has also been elected Colorado's next
secretary of state, defeating Republican James Wiley. Gonzalez,
currently Jefferson County's clerk and recorder, will succeed Jena
Griswold, who won the attorney general's race.

But she'll inherit an office already facing litigation
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
and ongoing debates about election administration, transparency and
oversight. Our latest reporting examines her record, the election
reforms proposed by her opponent, and the legal questions awaiting her
administration.

READ: _GONZALEZ ELECTED SECRETARY OF STATE, INHERITS OFFICE ALREADY IN
LITIGATION
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_--_

_SO, WHERE DO WE GO FROM HERE?_

We've seen the comments flooding our social media since last night:
_“That's it. I'm moving.” “Colorado is lost.” “Time to get
out.”_

We understand the frustration. After an election like this, it's
natural to wonder what the future holds for the state we love. But
here's something worth remembering: _COLORADO IS SO MUCH MORE THAN THE
POLITICIANS WHO HAPPEN TO HOLD OFFICE._

It's our families, our neighbors, our churches, our small businesses,
our communities, and the extraordinary place we're blessed to call
home. An election changes who governs. It doesn't erase everything
that makes Colorado worth loving.

_AND OUR MISSION AT ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE REMAINS THE SAME._

We will follow the money. We will hold elected officials accountable.
We will investigate the stories others overlook. And we will make sure
Coloradans have access to the information they need to understand
what's happening in their state.

That work doesn't end when the ballots are counted. In many ways, it's
just beginning.

We're grateful to every Coloradan who participated in this election,
every candidate who stepped forward, and every volunteer who invested
their time in the issues they care about. And we're especially
grateful to you for being part of the RMV community.

_STAY SHARP. STAY BOLD. STAY IN THE FIGHT. AND DON'T LOSE YOUR JOY._

We'll be here every step of the way.

For the latest results as ballots continue to be counted, bookmark
_RMV'S LIVE COLORADO ELECTION RESULTS TRACKER
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

In truth & liberty,
Team RMV

ELECTION COVERAGE

COLORADO 2026 ELECTION RESULTS: EVERY RACE ON THE BALLOT
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[UPDATED LIVE] Colorado voters have chosen a governor, a U.S. senator
and four statewide officers, and have voted on eight congressional
seats, 21 state Senate seats, all 65 state House seats and 14
statewide ballot measures.

WEISER ELECTED GOVERNOR: WHAT HE PROMISED, AND WHAT HE DID NOT PRICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Phil Weiser will be Colorado’s next governor. The Democrat attorney
general defeated Republican Victor Marx. The Associated Press called
the race at 7 p.m., minutes after polls closed. Counting had barely
begun.
__

COLORADO DEMOCRATS HIT TWO-THIRDS AS REPUBLICANS LOSE 7 LEGISLATIVE
SEATS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Six Republican-held seats in the Colorado House have flipped to
Democrats on preliminary returns. Not one Democratic seat went the
other way. That is the shape of Tuesday night in the state
legislature, and it is enough to put Democrats at two-thirds in both
chambers for the first time.

COLORADO BALLOT MEASURES 2026: 7 ON TRACK TO PASS, 7 ON TRACK TO FAIL
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Eight of Colorado’s 14 statewide ballot measures have drawn more yes
votes than no votes. Only seven of them are on track to pass. The
count on the Secretary of State site, posted at 4:02 a.m. MST
Wednesday, has six of the seven propositions headed for passage and
every constitutional amendment but one headed for defeat.

DEMOCRATS LEAD EVERY COLORADO FEDERAL RACE: THE 8TH HAS FLIPPED, THREE
MORE ARE STILL COUNTING
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY JOHN DOWNS, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Democrats spent the fall saying they could take all eight of
Colorado’s U.S. House seats. By late Tuesday they led all eight, and
the Senate seat with them. One of the four Republican-held districts
is gone.
__

GABE EVANS UNSEATED AFTER ONE TERM AS RUTINEL TAKES COLORADO’S 8TH
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

The bill Gabe Evans said he was proudest of passed the U.S. House
417-3. Seven weeks later he lost the seat. He trails by 32,919 votes
in a count that is not finished. In the Secretary of State’s
unofficial returns, last updated at 4:02 a.m. Wednesday, Democrat
Manny Rutinel had 124,631 votes to Evans’ 91,712.

GONZALEZ ELECTED SECRETARY OF STATE, AND INHERITS AN OFFICE ALREADY IN
LITIGATION
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Amanda Gonzalez was a candidate on a ballot her own office counted. On
Tuesday she won the job of running elections statewide. The Democrat,
who sits as Jefferson County’s clerk and recorder, beat Republican
James Wiley. The Associated Press called the race at 7:52 p.m., when
Gonzalez led by 23.5 percentage points, the Colorado Sun reported.

These results are still unofficial, but the implications for Colorado's legislative future are enormous. READ: COLORADO DEMOCRATS HIT TWO-THIRDS AS REPUBLICANS LOSE 7 LEGISLATIVE SEATS [ -- 🇺🇸 A HISTORIC GUBERNATORIAL DEFEAT Democrat Phil Weiser will be Colorado's next governor [ defeating Republican Victor Marx by a substantial margin, with the race called at nearly 7 p.m. just minutes after polls closed. As of this morning, Weiser had approximately 61% of the vote to Marx's 34%, a margin of more than 27 PERCENTAGE POINTS. According to historical comparisons, Marx's defeat ranks among the four largest gubernatorial blowouts in Colorado's 150-year history. And here's another sobering statistic: Colorado hasn't elected a Republican governor since 2002. That's nearly a quarter-century. Weiser now inherits a state facing significant budget challenges, alongside an ambitious 109-page policy agenda [ RMV's latest investigation examines what he has promised, what those proposals might cost, and the questions that remain unanswered. CD4: Democrat Eileen Laubacher leads Republican incumbent Lauren Boebert. * CD5: Democrat Jessica Killin leads Republican incumbent Jeff Crank. IF KILLIN WINS, SHE WILL BE THE FIRST DEMOCRAT TO HOLD THIS SEAT. Perhaps the most interesting development is in CD3. Despite the district's long Republican history and questions about Hurd's standing with parts of the Republican base, he's currently showing the strongest position among the three remaining Republican incumbents. There's still counting to do, and these races shouldn't be treated as decided until they're called. But regardless of the results, it's a giant wake-up call to Colorado. READ: DEMOCRATS LEAD ACROSS COLORADO'S FEDERAL RACES AS KEY DISTRICTS CONTINUE COUNTING [ -- 🎉 A BRIGHT SPOT: PROTECT KIDS COLORADO'S GRASSROOTS VICTORY [ Now, for some news worth celebrating for supporters of Protect Kids Colorado! All three ballot measures backed by the grassroots organization led by Erin Lee are on track to pass. The measures include: PROPOSITION 133: Strengthening penalties for child sex trafficking. PROPOSITION 134: Establishing biological-sex-based eligibility requirements for school and collegiate sports. PROPOSITION 135: Prohibiting certain sex-characteristic-altering surgeries on minors. The preliminary results show all three receiving majority support, with Proposition 133 already called by the Associated Press. Because these are statutory propositions rather than constitutional amendments, the legislature can subsequently amend or repeal them, subject to applicable legal requirements. Whether lawmakers will pursue those changes remains to be seen. But the next chapter will involve implementation, potential legislation and continued public debate. Regardless, for the organizers, volunteers and voters who worked on these measures, yesterday represents a significant milestone. | **Governor-elect Barlow Names Transition Team and Rolls Out New**[**Website**](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M6KY2JDP0GE372CSQHJX3PFF_1) FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASENovember 4, 2026Media Contact:Jessica JaubertCommunications Director, Governor-elect Eric Barlow[comms.transition@wyo.gov](mailto:comms.transition@wyo.gov)**Cheyenne, Wyoming –** Today, Wyoming Governor-elect Eric Barlow announced key members of his transition team.Barlow announced that Eydie Trautwein, former Deputy State Auditor and Jennifer Thomson, Barlow’s campaign manager, will serve as Joint Leads for his transition team. I want to thank Governor Gordon for his leadership and commitment to ensure a seamless transition.”Also today, Governor-elect Barlow rolled out his new website for the transition, [governor-elect.wyo.gov](https://ctrk.klclick.com/l/01M6KY2JDP0GE372CSQHJX3PFF_2).Visitors to the website can submit resumes for those interested in serving in the Barlow Administration, get to know our future Governor and First Lady, and learn more about the inauguration as information becomes available.

name: Wes Moore
subject: The work continues, Maryland
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2269%2E1086043%2EFEC79r)
Peter, we did it.
Four years ago, we started this improbable journey together. You had faith in a candidate who did not come from a family that was used to making policies but came from a family that was used to suffering the consequences of them.
I got into this work feeling our politics often forgets people — or leaves them out on purpose. That’s why I ran for governor: To reject the false choices that make our politics a zero-sum game — where the same people always are left with zero.
**While some in politics say you are on your own, I believe our politics should leave no one behind.**
It’s something the Army taught me at 17 years old. It wasn’t just a mantra, it became our governing philosophy.
"Leave no one behind" means no matter where you start in life, everyone deserves a fair shot.
Now, over these past four years, we’ve celebrated together, and we’ve mourned together. We’ve seen historic drops in violent crime, yet we’ve still had to attend too many funerals. We’ve watched Marylanders start 64,000 new businesses, creating new jobs — despite having more than 31,000 of our neighbors fired by Donald Trump and JD Vance as they wreck our nation’s economy.
We’ve endured a lot, but together we’ve persevered. And tonight, I’m humbled to lead Maryland into the future.
First, I want to thank God for continuing to rain His blessings on all of us. I want to thank my wife, first lady Dawn Moore, our daughter Mia, and our son James, as well as my mom and all the other members of my family — I love you eternally.
To my partner in this work, Lt. Gov. Aruna Miller: It is a joy being on this journey with you.
To the Moore-Miller campaign, every volunteer who knocked on doors, made calls in every corner of this state, or chipped in to this campaign: **You did this.** Thank you.
And to Dan Cox — we wish you and your family the best in your future endeavors.
I was raised right by my family, I was trained right by the United States Army, and I serve a mighty God. When I was growing up, my mother would tell me: “If you never forget who you are fighting for, you will never stop fighting.”
**Tonight, Maryland made clear who we’re fighting for.**
We're fighting for Krystal Gonzalez. Three years ago, she lost her daughter, Aaliyah. I swore to her that we would do everything in our power to bring down the violent crime rate. **Now, Maryland has the lowest rate of violent crime in 40 years.**
We're fighting for Pastor Daniel Omar Fuentes Espinal from the Eastern Shore, who was abducted by ICE. And I made it clear that our immigrant community in this state will be safe — and that we will embrace the beautiful diversity that makes Maryland who we are. And we made it illegal for this Trump-Vance ICE operation to deputize our brave, well-trained local law enforcement officers.
And we’re fighting for and alongside partners like Ray Morriss, Jack Coburn, Judy Hamilton and Travis Marion — local leaders who happen to be Republican mayors, but are Marylanders first. **Because like me, they know progress is not partisan.**
And while we’re proud of what we've accomplished together, and while we’re proud of our progress in Maryland, we know the work isn’t finished.
We are going to build upon our progress and build the best public education system in America, because every child in Maryland deserves a school that believes in them.
We will continue growing our economy and make our state less dependent on an unreliable Washington. That means more jobs, higher wages and more Marylanders building wealth.
We will continue to create more affordable housing, turn more renters into homeowners and give people a chance to pass something down to their children besides debt.
We will continue the greatest public safety turnaround story in America.
And we will complete the mission that brought us to politics in the first place — Maryland will lead the most aggressive charge to end child poverty in the United States of America!
I know our goals are ambitious and audacious. But if that’s not why we’re here, then why bother?
Americans are tired of these mealy-mouthed, weak-kneed, so-called leaders who tell us running fast on a treadmill is taking us somewhere. **That’s not why I’m here.**
And if anyone thinks I’m slowing down, they have another thing coming. That’s not what Maryland voted for!
And Marylanders didn’t just vote for a Governor. They voted to protect the great gift of our democracy. While our democracy was under attack by this president, and the Voting Rights Act was gutted, we voted yes on Question 3.
In this moment, when too many Americans feel left behind by Washington, our nation needs repair. And this can be and will be a moment when Maryland helps save our country again. When our time is done, I want a Maryland where everyone has that shot to succeed no matter where their story begins, and where how much money your family has does not determine your value or how high you can climb.
Four years ago, we started this journey together. Tonight, the work continues — for our people, for our state and for our country! Let’s keep proving a different kind of politics is possible — **and let’s leave no one behind.**
God bless you, and God bless the great state of Maryland,
Wes

Subject: Tonight, working families won Pundits will spend all week trying to name what’s happening tonight. We’ll save them the trouble:**** this isn’t just a wave, Peter. _It’s a tectonic shift._ **Democrats have taken control of both the House and the Senate, and so far, dozens of our Working Families Slate champions are heading to Congress.** Some of our biggest races are still too early to call, including the Senate race for **Abdul El-Sayed** in Michigan, but the night has already delivered a stinging rebuke of Trump and the Republican agenda, and the corporate politics that have failed working families for decades. In Pennsylvania , firefighter Bob Brooks (PA-07) just knocked off Republican Congressman Ryan Mackenzie, even with Trump pouring money into the race to save him. And in Philadelphia, Chris Rabb (PA-03), who took down the Democratic machine in his primary this spring, is officially headed to Congress. In Ohio , union ironworker Brian Poindexter (OH-07) is sending Max Miller, a former Trump aide and real estate heir, packing. Michigan isn’t finished, either. In Detroit, union organizer Donavan McKinney (MI-13), who toppled a multimillionaire incumbent in August, just sealed his win and is headed to Washington. In Colorado , Melat Kiros (CO-01), who made national headlines this year when she defeated a 30-year incumbent in her primary, is Denver’s next member of Congress. In California , teacher and longtime WFP member and leader Randy Villegas (CA-22) defeated David Valadao, who voted to gut Medicaid and to give ICE $38 million with no additional oversight. New York is sending a whole new class of fighters to Washington. Longtime WFP champion Brad Lander (NY-10), who was arrested by ICE last year while defending immigrant New Yorkers’ right to due process, is headed to Congress. Union organizer Claire Valdez (NY-07) will succeed Nydia Velazquez, while community organizer Darializa Avila Chevalier (NY-13), who unseated a five-term incumbent this summer, will represent Upper Manhattan. These wins are just the beginning, and more races are still being counted across the country, includingWill Lawrence(MI-07) in Michigan and four more WFP challengers in California:Mai Vang(CA-07),Aisha Wahab(CA-14),Connie Chan(CA-11), andAngela Gonzales-Torres(CA-34). This night was years in the making, Peter. Trump promised to lower the cost of living. Instead he delivered chaos , war , and rising costs , while his billionaire backers collected tax breaks and friendly regulators. Tonight, those broken promises came due, and voters sent Trump a clear message: you don’t get to lie to working families and keep your majority. He wasn’t the only one who got a message, though. All cycle long, the corporate wing of the Democratic Party said candidates like ours couldn’t win. They said the only path to victory ran through milquetoast moderates who promise nothing and stand for even less. Then they spent millions in our primaries to make sure voters never got a real choice. It didn’t work. Voters chose every one of our priority congressional champions anyway. And tonight, they did it again. Trump and Musk poured more than $800 million into these midterms, much of it in the final months, and our candidates still won in exactly the places the corporate wing said they’d lose. So to every Democrat already eyeing a future run: the path in 2028 runs through the Working Families Guarantee — a home you can afford, health care you can rely on, a good job to support your family, and childcare when and where you need it. That’s the agenda that won tonight. And it won because of you, Peter. Every one of the more than 30 million calls, texts, and door knocks since January came from people who believed working families deserve better, and who gave their evenings, their weekends, and whatever they could spare to prove it. That’s what our movement runs on. It’s what got us here tonight, and it’s what will carry us into 2027 and 2028. Thank you for everything you did to make tonight possible, Peter. In solidarity, All of us at WFP P.S. We can’t let tonight end without celebrating Angie Nixon , who came just two points shy of a historic upset. After winning her primary despite being outraised nearly 16-to-1, Angie never wavered in her fight for working families, even as the Democratic establishment failed to rally behind her in the general election. We’re so grateful for the heart and courage she poured into this campaign, and so proud to have stood beside her every step of the way. Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. **Eric Conroy Concedes OH-01 Race, Puts Greg Landsman on Notice: “This Is the Beginning, Not the End”****CINCINNATI** — Eric Conroy, the Republican nominee in Ohio's 1st Congressional District, conceded the race to Rep. Greg Landsman tonight after a strong first-time campaign built on service to country and community:.Conroy released the following statement:“While we came up short, I am proud of the campaign that we ran. Our campaign along with an aligned super PAC raised millions of dollars for both the primary and general elections. Collectively the campaign and outside groups knocked over 350,000 doors across the district targeting voters with a ground game never before seen in OH-01. I had never run for office before. I ran because voters are looking for service, not another corrupt career politician. Across this district, that message connected with people who are tired of a Washington that works for itself. To my supporters and volunteers: thank you. You knocked on tens of thousands of doors, put up thousands of yard signs and talked to voters in every part of this district. I am humbled by everything you gave to this campaign. We could not have done this without you. To the people of this district: this is the beginning, not the end. Greg Landsman is a crook and hypocrite whose entire campaign proves he has nothing but contempt for the people of this district. But like many crooked politicians who will tell any lie to get elected, they are hard to dislodge, especially in a challenging political environment. I am a proud Cincinnatian. This is my home and the community I love, and I am not done fighting for it. We didn’t win the battle today, but we will win the war. Greg, enjoy your next two years of corruption and insider trading. See you in 2028.”Conroy is a Cincinnati native, a graduate of Elder High School and the U.S. Air Force Academy, and a former CIA case officer.**###**

name: David Hogg
subject: We did it, Peter
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
These wins are as much yours as they are ours.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261104-1&t=1&akid=4232%2E587540%2E_pEjcj)
What an incredible night, Peter!
When we first started Leaders We Deserve, so many people told us that young candidates didn’t have what it takes to win. That they needed to wait their turn.
They said state legislative races in red states weren’t worth the investment, and that we wouldn’t be able to fight back against the flood of corporate PAC money and right-wing billionaire spending.
**Last night, our endorsed candidates proved them wrong.**
Together, we have so far flipped 12 seats from red to blue, won 27 state legislative seats, breaking 2 GOP supermajorities and flipping 7 state legislative chambers blue, and won 7 congressional seats, helping flip the House and Senate. And according to The AP Voter Poll, young voters swung hard to the left. 7 in 10 voters under 30 supported House Democrats, up from 5 in 10 in 2024. _That’s our power_.
Here’s how the results shook out:
**🇺🇸 CONGRESS:**
* Randy Villegas (CA-22)
* Angela Gonzalez-Torres (CA-34)
* Donavan McKinney (MI-13)
* Abdul El-Sayed (MI-Sen)
* Matt Little (MN-02)
* Claire Valdez (NY-07)
* Kristina Knickerbocker (OH-10)
* Christian Menefee (TX-18)

**🏛️ STATE LEGISLATURES:** Our candidates broke GOP supermajorities in Florida and Missouri and flipped chambers blue in Arizona, Georgia, New Hampshire, North Carolina, Michigan, Texas, and Wisconsin.
* Jacob Martinez (AZ-LD-09)
* Armando Montero (AZ-LD-12)
* Jane Aman (FL-HD-37)
* Akbar Ali (GA-HD-109)
* Bentley Hudgins (GA-HD-90
* Jyot Singh (GA-HD-97)
* Ruwa Romman (GA-SD-07)
* Demi Palecek (IL-HD-13)
* Nabeela Syed (IL-SD-26)
* Matt Post (MD-LD-14)
* Spencer Dixon (MD-LD-32)
* Katrina Manetta (MI-HD-58)
* Abbas Alawieh (MI-SD-02)
* Cat Clayton (MO-HD-105)
* Ken McCool (NC-HD-105)
* Ella Barrett (NH-Grafton-9)
* Alice Wade (NH-Strafford-21)
* Aber Kawas (NY-SD-12)
* Tim Hayes (PA-HD-143)
* Kristian Carranza (TX-HD-118)
* Tyler Smith (TX-HD-138)
* Julio Salinas (TX-HD-41)
* Jeff Haylon (VT-Rutland)
* Nikhil Goyal (VT-SD-Chittenden-Central)
* Ismael Luna (WI-HD-08)
* Christian Phelps (WI-HD-93)
* Trevor Jung (WI-SD-21)

We’re still waiting on results for Mai Vang in California and Brad Chambers in Pennsylvania. In Vermont, Audrey Grant’s race is heading to a recount and currently only 8 votes separate her from her GOP opponent.
**Peter, these wins are as much yours as they are ours.** Because of your generous support, we were able to invest early in leaders we truly believe in and power our endorsed candidates to victory from start to finish.
And we’re not stopping now. We’re already laying the groundwork for the next cycle, and we’ll ramp up in the coming weeks. But for now, let’s celebrate these wins.
Thank you so much for believing in our work. Seriously, none of this would be possible without you.
Onward,
David Hogg
P.S. Last night proved what’s possible when we put real resources behind young leaders we truly believe in. **[If you can, please pitch in $5 to help us keep this momentum going and hit the ground running for the next cycle.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261104_1_results.suMksk&refcode=em20261104-4232&amount=5&t=2&akid=4232%2E587540%2E_pEjcj)**

# [Tesla and Space X tank as Dems sweep 2026](https://substack.com/redirect/31023a5b-ce45-4d52-8c2f-64c40995ccf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Dow futures and the index surged nearly 1,000 points Wednesday after Democrats flipped the Senate and House, sparking a relief rally even as SpaceX and Tesla fell on Texas results and AI regulatory fears.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/31023a5b-ce45-4d52-8c2f-64c40995ccf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Relief rally takes hold:** Futures turned green as the blue wave became clear; the Dow later jumped 975 points while S&P and Nasdaq also advanced.
* **Musk names lag:** SpaceX and Tesla dropped in premarket trading after all Ai moratoriums on the ballots passed; CoreWeave and other AI infrastructure names also lagged.
* **Tuesday mixed close:** The Dow fell 0.4% while the S&P rose 0.4% and Nasdaq gained 0.8% on chip strength ahead of results.
* **AI muddy:** Markets liked the gridlock potential, but AI-linked shares saw muted gains on concerns over data-center rules and spending.

# [AMD data center surge lifts AI based stocks](https://substack.com/redirect/31023a5b-ce45-4d52-8c2f-64c40995ccf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
AMD shares jumped after third-quarter results showed data-center revenue nearly doubling and a strong fourth-quarter outlook that calmed worries about an AI spending slowdown.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/31023a5b-ce45-4d52-8c2f-64c40995ccf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Data center surge:** Segment revenue rose 97% to roughly $8.5 billion as total quarterly revenue climbed 45% to about $13.4 billion.
* **Guidance strong:** Management guided fourth-quarter revenue near $17 billion; 2027 growth is expected above 80%.
* **Demand quote:** CEO Lisa Su said AI demand remains robust and the company is expanding capacity to meet it.
* **Market reaction:** Shares advanced in after-hours and premarket trading, helping lift chip names even as broader AI infrastructure lagged on election news.

# [Democratic wins put AI data center buildout at risk](https://substack.com/redirect/31023a5b-ce45-4d52-8c2f-64c40995ccf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Gina Hinojosa's victory in the Texas governor's race and local ballot measures rejecting data centers raised the risk of moratoriums and tighter rules that could slow the AI infrastructure rollout.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/31023a5b-ce45-4d52-8c2f-64c40995ccf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Texas blow:** Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott after campaigning to halt new data-center construction, ending decades of Republican control.
* **Local bans:** Voters in more than 30 communities across nine states approved limits or moratoriums on data-center projects.
* **Stocks react:** AI data-center and infrastructure names dipped premarket on fears of regulatory hurdles in Texas, Ohio, and Georgia.
* **Cost context:** One analysis put the all-in cost of a U.S. AI data center near $49 billion per gigawatt, up sharply from three years earlier.

# [Musk's $474M Texas bet fails](https://substack.com/redirect/31023a5b-ce45-4d52-8c2f-64c40995ccf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
SpaceX and Tesla shares fell early Wednesday after Elon Musk's heavy Republican donations failed to stop Democratic wins in Texas's Senate and governor races, putting his relocated empire under new scrutiny.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/31023a5b-ce45-4d52-8c2f-64c40995ccf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Stocks hit hard:** Premarket declines hit both names as results showed Democrats taking Texas; one analysis framed the moves as major hurdles for AI build-out tied to Musk.
* **Donations miss:** Musk spent heavily in Texas; the outcome left him with fewer political allies in the state where he moved operations from California.
* **Qualcomm deal:** SpaceX signed a multiyear agreement to use Qualcomm's Dragonwing hardware and software in base stations for its Starlink Mobile network, challenging the big carriers.
* **Analyst view:** Morgan Stanley's Adam Jonas now sees SpaceX generating positive free cash flow by 2031, four years earlier than previously expected, with Starship Flight 15 as a potential catalyst.

# [Super Micro revenue nearly quadruples to $20B on AI](https://substack.com/redirect/31023a5b-ce45-4d52-8c2f-64c40995ccf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Super Micro Computer shares jumped more than 7% after fiscal first-quarter results showed revenue nearly quadrupling to $20 billion on surging AI server demand, with guidance also topping estimates.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/31023a5b-ce45-4d52-8c2f-64c40995ccf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Blowout quarter:** Profit reached $1.59 billion, or $1.75 a share, as AI infrastructure orders drove the top-line surge.
* **Demand scale:** An executive said a single AI order is now large enough to exceed an entire quarter from a year earlier.
* **Stock reaction:** Shares rose over 7% after hours and premarket; analysts called the print one of the best of the season.
* **Outlook strong:** Full-year guidance came in above prior targets as the company expands capacity for hyperscaler and AI customers.

# [CVS plans 2028 split to break up pharmacy and insurance](https://substack.com/redirect/31023a5b-ce45-4d52-8c2f-64c40995ccf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
CVS Health said it will break into two publicly traded companies by the first half of 2028, separating its drugstore operations from Aetna and the PBM while raising its full-year outlook after a beat.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/93bb0b0b-d07e-4b41-a055-41fb0f94e313?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Breakup timeline:** The split unwinds the $78 billion 2018 Aetna deal; one company will hold the 9,000-plus drugstores, the other the insurance and care businesses.
* **Earnings beat:** Adjusted EPS of $2.09 topped the $1.65 expected; the company raised guidance on strength in health-care benefits and pharmacy.
* **Market focus:** Investors weighed the strategic shift against risks in a federal drug program that had created a cliffhanger on the prior call.
* **Strategic context:** The move comes as pressure mounts on vertical integration in healthcare; Reuters and others traced the empire's assembly before the planned dismantling.

# [Oil slips as Trump ties midterm loss to Iran war and prices](https://substack.com/redirect/31023a5b-ce45-4d52-8c2f-64c40995ccf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Crude prices eased Wednesday after President Trump linked Republican midterm losses to the Iran war and high pump prices, while physical markets flipped from bidding war to fire sale as Gulf barrels returned.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/31023a5b-ce45-4d52-8c2f-64c40995ccf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Trump connection:** Markets assessed the political shift; Trump explicitly tied the defeat to high gasoline prices and the Iran conflict.
* **Physical market:** Dated Brent and North Sea Forties, which had stayed parabolic above $140 earlier, saw Gulf flows via ship-to-ship transfers exceed demand.
* **Price levels:** Brent traded near $104 and WTI near $97 amid choppy trading; Dubai benchmark slipped into contango for the first time since July.
* **Supply view:** JPMorgan said rising Middle East exports and softer demand are pushing the global market back into surplus; Goldman lifted its year-end Brent call to $105.

# Palantir hits first $2B quarter as commercial surpasses gov
Palantir CEO Alex Karp signaled he wants to dominate the entire market after the company posted its first $2 billion quarter, even as shares slid on slower contract momentum and commercial bookings concerns.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c49c44f9-cd36-4dfd-9a31-8aacb6ede557?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Milestone quarter:** Revenue nearly doubled; American commercial customers generated more revenue than government clients for the first time after a 148% surge.
* **Karp stance:** The CEO used the shareholder letter to declare traditional enterprise software sales "dead" and push for broader dominance.
* **Stock reaction:** Shares fell despite the beat and raised targets from some analysts; ARK bought the dip while investors focused on contract growth.
* **Backlog signal:** Slower contract momentum and new deal structures weighed on the narrative even as AI demand accelerated.

Democratic wins put AI data center build outs at risk | | | Nov 4 | | | | | | | | | | | | Dow futures and the index surged nearly 1,000 points Wednesday after Democrats flipped the Senate and House, sparking a relief rally even as SpaceX and Tesla fell on Texas results and AI regulatory fears. | | ---|---|--- Relief rally takes hold: Futures turned green as the blue wave became clear; the Dow later jumped 975 points while S&P and Nasdaq also advanced. Musk names lag: SpaceX and Tesla dropped in premarket trading after all Ai moratoriums on the ballots passed; CoreWeave and other AI infrastructure names also lagged. Tuesday mixed close: The Dow fell 0.4% while the S&P rose 0.4% and Nasdaq gained 0.8% on chip strength ahead of results. AI muddy: Markets liked the gridlock potential, but AI-linked shares saw muted gains on concerns over data-center rules and spending. AMD shares jumped after third-quarter results showed data-center revenue nearly doubling and a strong fourth-quarter outlook that calmed worries about an AI spending slowdown. | | ---|---|--- Data center surge: Segment revenue rose 97% to roughly $8.5 billion as total quarterly revenue climbed 45% to about $13.4 billion. Guidance strong: Management guided fourth-quarter revenue near $17 billion; 2027 growth is expected above 80%. Demand quote: CEO Lisa Su said AI demand remains robust and the company is expanding capacity to meet it. Market reaction: Shares advanced in after-hours and premarket trading, helping lift chip names even as broader AI infrastructure lagged on election news. Gina Hinojosa's victory in the Texas governor's race and local ballot measures rejecting data centers raised the risk of moratoriums and tighter rules that could slow the AI infrastructure rollout. | | ---|---|--- Texas blow: Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott after campaigning to halt new data-center construction, ending decades of Republican control. Local bans: Voters in more than 30 communities across nine states approved limits or moratoriums on data-center projects. Stocks react: AI data-center and infrastructure names dipped premarket on fears of regulatory hurdles in Texas, Ohio, and Georgia. Cost context: One analysis put the all-in cost of a U.S. AI data center near $49 billion per gigawatt, up sharply from three years earlier. SpaceX and Tesla shares fell early Wednesday after Elon Musk's heavy Republican donations failed to stop Democratic wins in Texas's Senate and governor races, putting his relocated empire under new scrutiny. | | ---|---|--- Stocks hit hard: Premarket declines hit both names as results showed Democrats taking Texas; one analysis framed the moves as major hurdles for AI build-out tied to Musk. Donations miss: Musk spent heavily in Texas; the outcome left him with fewer political allies in the state where he moved operations from California. Qualcomm deal: SpaceX signed a multiyear agreement to use Qualcomm's Dragonwing hardware and software in base stations for its Starlink Mobile network, challenging the big carriers. Analyst view: Morgan Stanley's Adam Jonas now sees SpaceX generating positive free cash flow by 2031, four years earlier than previously expected, with Starship Flight 15 as a potential catalyst. Super Micro Computer shares jumped more than 7% after fiscal first-quarter results showed revenue nearly quadrupling to $20 billion on surging AI server demand, with guidance also topping estimates. | | ---|---|--- Blowout quarter: Profit reached $1.59 billion, or $1.75 a share, as AI infrastructure orders drove the top-line surge. Demand scale: An executive said a single AI order is now large enough to exceed an entire quarter from a year earlier. Stock reaction: Shares rose over 7% after hours and premarket; analysts called the print one of the best of the season. Outlook strong: Full-year guidance came in above prior targets as the company expands capacity for hyperscaler and AI customers. CVS Health said it will break into two publicly traded companies by the first half of 2028, separating its drugstore operations from Aetna and the PBM while raising its full-year outlook after a beat. | | ---|---|--- Breakup timeline: The split unwinds the $78 billion 2018 Aetna deal; one company will hold the 9,000-plus drugstores, the other the insurance and care businesses. Earnings beat: Adjusted EPS of $2.09 topped the $1.65 expected; the company raised guidance on strength in health-care benefits and pharmacy. Market focus: Investors weighed the strategic shift against risks in a federal drug program that had created a cliffhanger on the prior call. Strategic context: The move comes as pressure mounts on vertical integration in healthcare; Reuters and others traced the empire's assembly before the planned dismantling. Crude prices eased Wednesday after President Trump linked Republican midterm losses to the Iran war and high pump prices, while physical markets flipped from bidding war to fire sale as Gulf barrels returned. | | ---|---|--- Trump connection: Markets assessed the political shift; Trump explicitly tied the defeat to high gasoline prices and the Iran conflict. Physical market: Dated Brent and North Sea Forties, which had stayed parabolic above $140 earlier, saw Gulf flows via ship-to-ship transfers exceed demand. Price levels: Brent traded near $104 and WTI near $97 amid choppy trading; Dubai benchmark slipped into contango for the first time since July. Supply view: JPMorgan said rising Middle East exports and softer demand are pushing the global market back into surplus; Goldman lifted its year-end Brent call to $105. Palantir hits first $2B quarter as commercial surpasses gov Palantir CEO Alex Karp signaled he wants to dominate the entire market after the company posted its first $2 billion quarter, even as shares slid on slower contract momentum and commercial bookings concerns. | | ---|---|--- Milestone quarter: Revenue nearly doubled; American commercial customers generated more revenue than government clients for the first time after a 148% surge. Karp stance: The CEO used the shareholder letter to declare traditional enterprise software sales "dead" and push for broader dominance. Stock reaction: Shares fell despite the beat and raised targets from some analysts; ARK bought the dip while investors focused on contract growth. name: Katie Porter
subject: You helped make this hard-fought victory possible
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Truth to Power PAC
body:
Last night, our slate proved that rejecting corporate PAC money and fighting for working families is still a winning playbook.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41639%2E3422442%2EzF9MCh)
What a night, Peter!
From the moment the first polls closed on the East Coast, it was clear that Democrats were on the path to a historic victory. We took back the House and the Senate—a feat that was a long shot just a year ago—with stunning upset wins along the way.
**I want to say thank you: Truth to Power backed a slate of champions running in some of the toughest races in the country, and many of them won last night.** The support you provided helped us push them over the finish line and deliver victories many said were impossible. I am so proud of this team.
In the Senate, we helped elect **Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota, Josh Turek in Iowa, and Troy Jackson in Maine** —finally unseating Susan Collins and sending fearless new leaders to Washington.
In the House, we shattered the Republican majority by backing **Rebecca Cooke, Sarah Trone Garriott, Christina Bohannan, Lindsay James, Brad Lander, Cait Conley, Will Lawrence, and Sam Forstag.** Each of them ran the right way—listening to voters and fighting to lower costs for working families.
At home in California, we flipped seats that were newly winnable after voters passed Proposition 50. We sent **Marni von Wilpert and Randy Villegas** to Congress with a mandate to stand up for everyday people.
A handful of our targeted races are still too close to call. We’ll share updates with you once we know the results of those elections.
**When I flipped a Republican district in 2018, we did it by rejecting corporate PAC money and fighting tirelessly for working families. Last night, our slate proved that it is still a winning playbook, and the way we build lasting political power.**
Soon, Democrats will start using our majorities to block Donald Trump’s agenda and set the stage to take back the White House. But today, let's take a moment to enjoy this hard-fought victory. You made it happen.
With gratitude,
Katie Porter
