subject: Still celebrating? Us too.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
You helped make these victories possible. Now let’s talk about what comes next.
#
Hi there,
WOW. It’s hard to find the words to describe how transformative last night was. The balance of power has swung—decisively—to Democrats.
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3269?t=1&akid=3402%2E1562180%2EyhzoDJ)
_New York Times map of the shift in Senate vote margin from 2024 as of 12:30 pm ET._
_This_ is what we mean when we talk about swinging the country left. And there are almost too many significant victories to mention. While we’re still waiting for a handful of our target races to be called, here are some of the highlights so far:
* BOTH the House and Senate flipped to Democratic control.
* For the first time in our nation’s history, five states will be led by Black governors, including Georgia, where Keisha Lance Bottoms will become the country’s first Black woman governor. Notably, Republicans have held the governor’s mansion there since 2003.
* Texas turned BLUE! Texans elected Gina Hinojosa as governor and James Talarico as their next U.S. senator. And what’s more, they flipped the Texas House to Democrats, which has been Republican-controlled since 2002. Democrats have not won a statewide election in Texas since 1994, but last night they flipped _every single one._
* Adam Hamilton became the first Democratic senator elected in Kansas since 1932 in a state that has been deeply red for decades.
* Chris Pappas won his Senate race in New Hampshire, filling the seat left open by three-term Democratic Senator Jeanne Shaheen and making him the first openly gay man elected to the Senate.
* In Michigan, voters elected Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, who will become the nation’s first Muslim senator.
* A historic number of Democratic women will now serve as governors, and we elected the first Native American woman to the Senate (or women, depending on Alaska!).

In the states, Democrats now control the majority of state legislative chambers and have so far flipped **12 majorities from red to blue and broken 11 Republican supermajorities.** This includes:
* **Wisconsin** , which now has a Democratic trifecta—meaning Democrats have full governing power—for the first time in over a decade.
* **Arizona** , where voters re-elected Governor Katie Hobbs, flipped the state House and Senate, and created a Democratic trifecta for the first time in **60 years**.
* **Pennsylvania** , where we secured a Democratic trifecta for the first time since 1993.
* **Michigan** and **Minnesota** , where we flipped both state houses and restored the Democratic trifectas that were lost in the 2024 election.
* **Nevada** , where Aaron Ford’s victory restored the Democratic trifecta that was lost in 2022 when Republicans captured the governor’s mansion.

We are so grateful to this community of over 1 million grassroots volunteers and donors. SO many of you showed up to talk with voters, listen, and persuade. Thank you also for donating and fundraising to support Swing Left’s organizing work and the campaigns on our map. You helped reach the most important swing voters in the most important races and make the case for Democratic candidates.
Together in our efforts to help Democrats win in the 2026 midterm elections, the Swing Left community did incredible work:
* Knocked on **237K** doors
* Made **1.5M** phone calls
* Had **80K** conversations with voters
* Raised **over $22.6 million** to help elect Democrats
* Wrote more than **490K letters** with Vote Forward
* Took **34K actions** to boost pro-democracy content online

And through Ground Truth, you helped create and build a new, innovative way for Democrats to do effective voter contact. This program is people-powered and grounded in showing up early, listening deeply, and gathering rich, textured insights that can help campaigns and party committees improve their messaging and outreach strategies. And thanks to you, it’s changing the future of Democratic campaigning.
Now, let’s talk through what comes next.
On Swing Left’s upcoming virtual call, we’ll gather to celebrate last night's enormous wins _and_ dive deep into what we learned from Ground Truth this year. It’s an opportunity to have an honest conversation about what we need to keep doing to ensure the results we saw last night aren't a momentary bright spot for Democrats. We’ll talk about what we do next to maintain and expand durable power that ends MAGA control of the White House _for good._
[**Join us for an Inside Update on November 19th.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3269?t=2&akid=3402%2E1562180%2EyhzoDJ)
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3269?t=3&akid=3402%2E1562180%2EyhzoDJ)
Thank you again for _everything_ you put into this year’s midterm elections. You gave your time, resources, and energy to try something new with us, and we’re tremendously proud of what we built and achieved together.
With hope,
The team at Swing Left

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20261104-1&t=4&refcode2=3402_1562180_yhzoDJ&akid=3402%2E1562180%2EyhzoDJ)

subject: What a tremendous honor.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Morrison for Congress
body:
Thank you!| | | |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142906400/658437939/-1066768109?source=261104_km_ty&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDkzOTAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTFjOTUxYTEtODhkOC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=UUitU1AIEHJt2mWgi3S_nd8HKAl4_nKgfdk5bwoFTG0=)

Peter, it is with profound gratitude that I have the opportunity to say to you today: **I am honored to continue serving Minnesota's 3rd District and bringing your voice to Congress.**

I feel incredibly fortunate to be a part of this remarkable community full of people who care so deeply about our neighbors, our state, and our country. These victories, here in MN-03, all across Minnesota – from Governor-elect Amy Klobuchar (!) and a full sweep of statewide victories to Jake Johnson’s amazing lead in MN-01 – and throughout the entire country, are because of you.

Thank you for every door you knocked, every conversation you had, and every dollar you donated. Your support is what makes this work possible, and I hope you know how much I appreciate you.

In the lead-up to this week, I found myself reflecting on everything that’s happened over the past two years since election night in 2024, and on where we are as a state and a country.

We have lived through more traumas, tragedies, and attacks _from our own federal government_ than we ever thought possible. The chaos, cruelty, and corruption of this administration have represented a historic low for our country.

But when this administration tried to break us, Minnesota didn’t back down. When they tried to intimidate us, Minnesota didn’t go silent. When they tried to inflict their hatred and division on us, Minnesota didn’t turn against our neighbors.

**Minnesota showed the entire country the very best of what being an American can and should look like – and now, we are sending a clear, resounding message that _that_ is who we are as a state, _that_ is what we stand for as a country, and _that_ is what we demand from our leaders. **

The challenges this Republican trifecta has created aren’t going to be solved overnight. There will certainly be hardships ahead. But I can promise you this: I am going to take the grit, resilience, compassion, and decency of who we are as Minnesotans back with me to Washington, DC, and I am going to use it to fight like hell for you.

Together with our new Democratic majority (!!!), I am going to fight every day for hardworking people across this state and country to not just survive, but to _thrive_. To be able to afford to build a good life. To be able to plan a bright future for yourself and for your kids. To be able to be proud of who we are as a country, and what we stand for.

I am so proud of Minnesota, I am so grateful to you, and it is my tremendous honor to continue serving you.

With gratitude,

Kelly

clean_body: Thank you!| | | | = Peter, it is with profound gratitude that I have the opportunity to say to you today: I am honored to continue serving Minnesota's 3rd District and bringing your voice to Congress. I feel incredibly fortunate to be a part of this remarkable community full of people who care so deeply about our neighbors, our state, and our country. These victories, here in MN-03, all across Minnesota – from Governor-elect Amy Klobuchar (!) and a full sweep of statewide victories to Jake Johnson’s amazing lead in MN-01 – and throughout the entire country, are because of you. Thank you for every door you knocked, every conversation you had, and every dollar you donated. Your support is what makes this work possible, and I hope you know how much I appreciate you. In the lead-up to this week, I found myself reflecting on everything that’s happened over the past two years since election night in 2024, and on where we are as a state and a country. We have lived through more traumas, tragedies, and attacks from our own federal government than we ever thought possible. The chaos, cruelty, and corruption of this administration have represented a historic low for our country. But when this administration tried to break us, Minnesota didn’t back down. When they tried to intimidate us, Minnesota didn’t go silent. When they tried to inflict their hatred and division on us, Minnesota didn’t turn against our neighbors. Minnesota showed the entire country the very best of what being an American can and should look like – and now, we are sending a clear, resounding message that that is who we are as a state, that is what we stand for as a country, and that is what we demand from our leaders. The challenges this Republican trifecta has created aren’t going to be solved overnight. There will certainly be hardships ahead. But I can promise you this: I am going to take the grit, resilience, compassion, and decency of who we are as Minnesotans back with me to Washington, DC, and I am going to use it to fight like hell for you. Together with our new Democratic majority (!!!), I am going to fight every day for hardworking people across this state and country to not just survive, but to thrive. To be able to afford to build a good life. To be able to plan a bright future for yourself and for your kids. To be able to be proud of who we are as a country, and what we stand for. I am so proud of Minnesota, I am so grateful to you, and it is my tremendous honor to continue serving you. body:
[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

What. A. Night. And let’s be clear about one thing: this Blue tsunami was
fueled by a progressive wave, powered by you and our movement.

We not only OVERWHELMINGLY flipped the House AND the Senate, we did it by
sending DOZENS of new progressives to DC to grow our power in Congress.
You helped make it possible. Our Revolution shattered our goal of 5
million voter contacts this election. Our volunteers made thousands of
calls, sent thousands of texts and emails, and knocked on doors for
candidates like Abdul El-Sayed, James Talarico, and Troy Jackson, and for
progressives up and down the ballot.

[1]Talarico speaking at the lecturn

You didn’t just help us power MILLIONS of voter contacts — you helped us
change the conversation and put progressives at the center of this
election cycle. Our work lifted our candidates in front of millions of
eyeballs, with viral posts and coverage in dozens of outlets, including
Politico, the New York Times, and USA Today, heading into Election Day. We
helped grow name recognition and grassroots energy for candidates the
establishment wrote off, in places where progressives weren’t supposed to
compete.

[2]Abdul smiling

James, Abdul, Peggy, and Troy won their Senate races. But we also swept
the House. From Bob Brooks and Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania to Donavan
McKinney and Will Lawrence in Michigan, candidates who focused on fighting
for the working class won decisively, flipping red seats and proving that
grassroots power can beat billionaire money.

That’s what organizing does. It turns long shots into real contenders, and
it builds power that lasts beyond a single election.

We just delivered a massive blow to MAGA, but now we have to make sure
that power translates into wins for the working class.

As we send dozens of bold new progressives to the House and Senate, we’re
going to keep up the pressure to make sure our leaders actually deliver
for working people, not billionaires and corporate donors. We’re going to
uproot corruption and take on the dark money trying to buy our democracy.
We’re going to fight Big Tech’s data center boom, which threatens
communities, the climate, and working families. We’re going to stop
Section 219 of the NDAA, which would all but fuse our military with
Israel’s. And we’re gearing up for 2028 by recruiting, training, and
electing the next generation of progressive leaders.

We built this movement from the bottom up, with volunteers, small-dollar
donors, and neighbors talking to neighbors. While the election may be
over, the [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39992?t=1011&akid=11554%2E5885482%2E8e0n7n ]organizing never is.

But today, let’s celebrate. Thank you for everything you did to make it
possible.

When we organize, we win.

Our Revolution

name: Andrew Sypher, Turning Point USA
subject: Before you give up on America — read this
body:
If you ever doubted we could win America’s youth back from the Left...

| | | [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckbuu2zAMhp9G3hxY1MXR4KFA4O10KAp0FBiJdoRjWa4uKfr2hU_yBF3Jnx_Bj78-7AeGLezrd4w05brYXOydlpTpb2preFI70o6RcnCYLQyge877QVp0NTzJSuz85J1H7jqa-GjEFUAa0z2mqxIcCFBy0qO8K68NV2pwQjnOudZdmE4e54OEYeBCX_yitBqN0KPUXoFjcsCNcr1kOtp9Cw73iuVzSdnRxaXYbdOj1qMw8Y3BzGAu5FqmC-7kUz0TDOba8h72tT9S2GvfCjKYR6OWuxqpN2REL8ljb4hEj8t1WRRx0oRMzCW17Mi65ImJ24-fM1cjgGKgW402kg8tMnGjiGF7F18jTNwemD2WT4vu97vlMB4Y1p2JWz1awZfCUOKX1neoUj6RXZ788SdsWyh6ZHJYzxVfJ9f__NJzgn8BAAD__3raomE)
---
| | Friend,
---
If you ever doubted we could win America's youth back from the Left...

If you ever wondered whether we'd lost the next generation for good...

If you ever sat up at night -- watching the news, seeing what's happening in our schools, our culture, our country -- and thought, _" Is it already too late?" _

You're not alone.

A lot of good people have been asking the same question.

**But I want to tell you something that might just change how you feel about the future of this country... **

Just one year ago, Turning Point USA's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.

That was no small feat.

Starting a single chapter today takes serious courage. Students get mocked. Threatened. Investigated. Sometimes even physically attacked.

So reaching 1,200 chapters already felt like a miracle.

_Then Charlie called me... _

He said: "Andrew, I love what we're doing with our high school program -- but we've got to move faster."

I told him, "We are."

Charlie replied, "No you're not thinking what I'm thinking... I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I laughed. I told him, "Charlie, there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said, "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

Without skipping a beat, Charlie said, "Okay, great. Let's do 27,000!"
I'll be honest -- I froze.

We didn't have the numbers. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the roadmap yet.

But he wasn't fazed.

He said, "Don't worry. We'll figure it out. We'll do it together."

That was Charlie.

He didn't think small. He didn't move slow. He didn't settle for "maybe someday."

He believed in going now.

And he believed that if the mission was right, the path would reveal itself.

He chased what others only dreamed about... and turned what others thought impossible into reality.

That's why he built Turning Point USA in the first place.

That's why tens of thousands of students were inspired by Charlie to start chapters of their own -- _many in schools where they were explicitly told not to. _

**And that 's why today -- less than a year later -- we're not in 1,200 schools anymore: **
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckbuu2zAMhp9G3hxY1MXR4KFA4O10KAp0FBiJdoRjWa4uKfr2hU_yBF3Jnx_Bj78-7AeGLezrd4w05brYXOydlpTpb2preFI70o6RcnCYLQyge877QVp0NTzJSuz85J1H7jqa-GjEFUAa0z2mqxIcCFBy0qO8K68NV2pwQjnOudZdmE4e54OEYeBCX_yitBqN0KPUXoFjcsCNcr1kOtp9Cw73iuVzSdnRxaXYbdOj1qMw8Y3BzGAu5FqmC-7kUz0TDOba8h72tT9S2GvfCjKYR6OWuxqpN2REL8ljb4hEj8t1WRRx0oRMzCW17Mi65ImJ24-fM1cjgGKgW402kg8tMnGjiGF7F18jTNwemD2WT4vu97vlMB4Y1p2JWz1awZfCUOKX1neoUj6RXZ788SdsWyh6ZHJYzxVfJ9f__NJzgn8BAAD__3raomE)
---
We're in 3,300.

That's roughly 13% of all high schools in America.

Eight states have officially partnered with Club America to bring our chapters into every school statewide.

✅ Florida
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee
✅ Oklahoma
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Arkansas
✅ Indiana

And we're just getting started.

Think about that: 13% of America's youth now have a place at school where they can say it's okay to love this country...

That it's okay to be bold. That it's okay to believe in God, in family, and in freedom.

_That 's what Club America is about... _

**Giving the next generation a place where they can find their courage, develop grit, and learn how to lead the fight for their country. **
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckbuu2zAMhp9G3hxY1MXR4KFA4O10KAp0FBiJdoRjWa4uKfr2hU_yBF3Jnx_Bj78-7AeGLezrd4w05brYXOydlpTpb2preFI70o6RcnCYLQyge877QVp0NTzJSuz85J1H7jqa-GjEFUAa0z2mqxIcCFBy0qO8K68NV2pwQjnOudZdmE4e54OEYeBCX_yitBqN0KPUXoFjcsCNcr1kOtp9Cw73iuVzSdnRxaXYbdOj1qMw8Y3BzGAu5FqmC-7kUz0TDOba8h72tT9S2GvfCjKYR6OWuxqpN2REL8ljb4hEj8t1WRRx0oRMzCW17Mi65ImJ24-fM1cjgGKgW402kg8tMnGjiGF7F18jTNwemD2WT4vu97vlMB4Y1p2JWz1awZfCUOKX1neoUj6RXZ788SdsWyh6ZHJYzxVfJ9f__NJzgn8BAAD__3raomE)
---
_But now, Friend, the question is... _

**What will it take to bring Club America to the next 3,300 schools? What will it take to bring it to all 27,000? **

Because here's the truth:

These students aren't just signing up. _They 're stepping up. _

They're leading chapters in schools where America is attacked... where they're often targeted for daring to say what they believe... and where speaking the truth is dangerous.

But that isn't stopping them.

They're still showing up. They're speaking out. And they're growing stronger than ever.

They're becoming exactly the kind of young patriots Charlie believed in -- not just bold, _but brave_. Not just loud, but _principled_.

**Every time a student starts a new chapter, we make sure they 're not standing alone. **

**We send them an activism kit -- American flags, pocket Constitutions, chapter materials, and leadership tools. **

These kits give student leaders everything they need to rally their peers and stand strong on their campuses.

Each one costs just $25 to pack and ship.

**[If you're able to, I hope you'll help send a kit to the next student who raises their hand to lead by making your gift to Turning Point USA today.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckbuu2zAMhp9G3hxY1MXR4KFA4O10KAp0FBiJdoRjWa4uKfr2hU_yBF3Jnx_Bj78-7AeGLezrd4w05brYXOydlpTpb2preFI70o6RcnCYLQyge877QVp0NTzJSuz85J1H7jqa-GjEFUAa0z2mqxIcCFBy0qO8K68NV2pwQjnOudZdmE4e54OEYeBCX_yitBqN0KPUXoFjcsCNcr1kOtp9Cw73iuVzSdnRxaXYbdOj1qMw8Y3BzGAu5FqmC-7kUz0TDOba8h72tT9S2GvfCjKYR6OWuxqpN2REL8ljb4hEj8t1WRRx0oRMzCW17Mi65ImJ24-fM1cjgGKgW402kg8tMnGjiGF7F18jTNwemD2WT4vu97vlMB4Y1p2JWz1awZfCUOKX1neoUj6RXZ788SdsWyh6ZHJYzxVfJ9f__NJzgn8BAAD__3raomE)**
---
[ **Sponsor an Activism Kit**
**Make Your Gift Today**](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckbuu2zAMhp9G3hxY1MXR4KFA4O10KAp0FBiJdoRjWa4uKfr2hU_yBF3Jnx_Bj78-7AeGLezrd4w05brYXOydlpTpb2preFI70o6RcnCYLQyge877QVp0NTzJSuz85J1H7jqa-GjEFUAa0z2mqxIcCFBy0qO8K68NV2pwQjnOudZdmE4e54OEYeBCX_yitBqN0KPUXoFjcsCNcr1kOtp9Cw73iuVzSdnRxaXYbdOj1qMw8Y3BzGAu5FqmC-7kUz0TDOba8h72tT9S2GvfCjKYR6OWuxqpN2REL8ljb4hEj8t1WRRx0oRMzCW17Mi65ImJ24-fM1cjgGKgW402kg8tMnGjiGF7F18jTNwemD2WT4vu97vlMB4Y1p2JWz1awZfCUOKX1neoUj6RXZ788SdsWyh6ZHJYzxVfJ9f__NJzgn8BAAD__3raomE)
---
Charlie wanted a Club America chapter in every high school so no student would ever feel alone for loving God, defending their country, or believing in truth.

And so the next generation wouldn't be handed over to the Left by default.

Let's make Charlie's dream real -- 27,000 high schools. And a generation that doesn't apologize for loving this country.

It's up to us to finish what he started.

One chapter. One student. One school at a time.

Let's move faster. Let's push further. Let's get this done -- for Charlie, and for the country we all love.
---
| | **For Charlie,** **Andrew Sypher** Chief Field OfficerTurning Point USA
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckbuu2zAMhp9G3hxY1MXR4KFA4O10KAp0FBiJdoRjWa4uKfr2hU_yBF3Jnx_Bj78-7AeGLezrd4w05brYXOydlpTpb2preFI70o6RcnCYLQyge877QVp0NTzJSuz85J1H7jqa-GjEFUAa0z2mqxIcCFBy0qO8K68NV2pwQjnOudZdmE4e54OEYeBCX_yitBqN0KPUXoFjcsCNcr1kOtp9Cw73iuVzSdnRxaXYbdOj1qMw8Y3BzGAu5FqmC-7kUz0TDOba8h72tT9S2GvfCjKYR6OWuxqpN2REL8ljb4hEj8t1WRRx0oRMzCW17Mi65ImJ24-fM1cjgGKgW402kg8tMnGjiGF7F18jTNwemD2WT4vu97vlMB4Y1p2JWz1awZfCUOKX1neoUj6RXZ788SdsWyh6ZHJYzxVfJ9f__NJzgn8BAAD__3raomE)

[ _**Support Turning Point USA**_](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckbuu2zAMhp9G3hxY1MXR4KFA4O10KAp0FBiJdoRjWa4uKfr2hU_yBF3Jnx_Bj78-7AeGLezrd4w05brYXOydlpTpb2preFI70o6RcnCYLQyge877QVp0NTzJSuz85J1H7jqa-GjEFUAa0z2mqxIcCFBy0qO8K68NV2pwQjnOudZdmE4e54OEYeBCX_yitBqN0KPUXoFjcsCNcr1kOtp9Cw73iuVzSdnRxaXYbdOj1qMw8Y3BzGAu5FqmC-7kUz0TDOba8h72tT9S2GvfCjKYR6OWuxqpN2REL8ljb4hEj8t1WRRx0oRMzCW17Mi65ImJ24-fM1cjgGKgW402kg8tMnGjiGF7F18jTNwemD2WT4vu97vlMB4Y1p2JWz1awZfCUOKX1neoUj6RXZ788SdsWyh6ZHJYzxVfJ9f__NJzgn8BAAD__3raomE)
---
**P.S.** There's one part of that phone call with Charlie I was going to leave out...

He wasn't just dreaming big -- he was issuing a warning.

When he told me we needed to move faster, he added: "The enemy is moving younger. They're coming after students earlier. _**We don 't have time to wait.**_**" **

And he was right.

The Left has deeply embedded themselves in our schools -- rewriting history, poisoning young minds, and raising their next generation of radical foot soldiers.

We may be in 13% of our schools now...

_But in the other 87%? _

The Left has free rein. Zero resistance. No voice to challenge them.

And if we don't flood those schools with truth -- fast -- we'll have a generation that thinks loving America is "fascist," that faith is "hateful," and that freedom and free speech is "dangerous."

You know it. I know it. Charlie knew it.

He knew the fight for America's future would be won or lost in high school classrooms and on college campuses.

And that fight has never been more urgent than it is right now.

**Friend, if you 've ever wondered whether one small act could change the direction of our country -- _this is it._ **

You may not be able to step into a hostile high school and stand for truth like these students do.

But you can send them the tools to do it.

These students are ready. They've raised their hands. They chose courage and decided to lead.

All they're waiting on... is us.

**Every $25 helps send an activism kit to a young patriot and gives them everything they need to win hearts and minds. **

You're gift reminds them they're not alone. It gives them the confidence to stand and fight back.

And you'll be saving our country -- one future freedom fighter at a time.

clean_body: If you ever doubted we could win America’s youth back from the Left... | | | | | Friend, If you ever doubted we could win America's youth back from the Left... If you ever wondered whether we'd lost the next generation for good... If you ever sat up at night -- watching the news, seeing what's happening in our schools, our culture, our country -- and thought, " Is it already too late?" You're not alone. A lot of good people have been asking the same question. But I want to tell you something that might just change how you feel about the future of this country... Just one year ago, Turning Point USA's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools. That was no small feat. Starting a single chapter today takes serious courage. Students get mocked. Threatened. Investigated. Sometimes even physically attacked. So reaching 1,200 chapters already felt like a miracle. Then Charlie called me... He said: "Andrew, I love what we're doing with our high school program -- but we've got to move faster." I told him, "We are." Charlie replied, "No you're not thinking what I'm thinking... I want to be in 35,000 high schools." I laughed. I told him, "Charlie, there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America." "Okay," he said, "How many are there?" "About 27,000." Without skipping a beat, Charlie said, "Okay, great. Let's do 27,000!" I'll be honest -- I froze. We didn't have the numbers. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the roadmap yet. But he wasn't fazed. He said, "Don't worry. We'll figure it out. We'll do it together." That was Charlie. He didn't think small. He didn't move slow. He didn't settle for "maybe someday." He believed in going now. And he believed that if the mission was right, the path would reveal itself. He chased what others only dreamed about... and turned what others thought impossible into reality. That's why he built Turning Point USA in the first place. That's why tens of thousands of students were inspired by Charlie to start chapters of their own -- many in schools where they were explicitly told not to. And that 's why today -- less than a year later -- we're not in 1,200 schools anymore: We're in 3,300. That's roughly 13% of all high schools in America. Eight states have officially partnered with Club America to bring our chapters into every school statewide. ✅ Florida ✅ Texas ✅ Tennessee ✅ Oklahoma ✅ Montana ✅ Nebraska ✅ Arkansas ✅ Indiana And we're just getting started. Think about that: 13% of America's youth now have a place at school where they can say it's okay to love this country... That it's okay to be bold. That it's okay to believe in God, in family, and in freedom. That 's what Club America is about... Giving the next generation a place where they can find their courage, develop grit, and learn how to lead the fight for their country. But now, Friend, the question is... What will it take to bring Club America to the next 3,300 schools? What will it take to bring it to all 27,000? Because here's the truth: These students aren't just signing up. They 're stepping up. They're leading chapters in schools where America is attacked... where they're often targeted for daring to say what they believe... and where speaking the truth is dangerous. But that isn't stopping them. They're still showing up. They're speaking out. And they're growing stronger than ever. They're becoming exactly the kind of young patriots Charlie believed in -- not just bold, but brave. Not just loud, but principled. Every time a student starts a new chapter, we make sure they 're not standing alone. We send them an activism kit -- American flags, pocket Constitutions, chapter materials, and leadership tools. These kits give student leaders everything they need to rally their peers and stand strong on their campuses. Each one costs just $25 to pack and ship. Charlie wanted a Club America chapter in every high school so no student would ever feel alone for loving God, defending their country, or believing in truth. And so the next generation wouldn't be handed over to the Left by default. Let's make Charlie's dream real -- 27,000 high schools. And a generation that doesn't apologize for loving this country. It's up to us to finish what he started. One chapter. One student. One school at a time. Let's move faster. Let's push further. Let's get this done -- for Charlie, and for the country we all love. | | For Charlie, Andrew Sypher Chief Field OfficerTurning Point USA P.S. There's one part of that phone call with Charlie I was going to leave out... He wasn't just dreaming big -- he was issuing a warning. When he told me we needed to move faster, he added: "The enemy is moving younger. They're coming after students earlier. We don 't have time to wait." And he was right. The Left has deeply embedded themselves in our schools -- rewriting history, poisoning young minds, and raising their next generation of radical foot soldiers. We may be in 13% of our schools now... But in the other 87%? The Left has free rein. Zero resistance. No voice to challenge them. And if we don't flood those schools with truth -- fast -- we'll have a generation that thinks loving America is "fascist," that faith is "hateful," and that freedom and free speech is "dangerous." You know it. I know it. Charlie knew it. He knew the fight for America's future would be won or lost in high school classrooms and on college campuses. And that fight has never been more urgent than it is right now. Friend, if you 've ever wondered whether one small act could change the direction of our country -- this is it. You may not be able to step into a hostile high school and stand for truth like these students do. But you can send them the tools to do it. These students are ready. They've raised their hands. They chose courage and decided to lead. All they're waiting on... is us. Every $25 helps send an activism kit to a young patriot and gives them everything they need to win hearts and minds. You're gift reminds them they're not alone. It gives them the confidence to stand and fight back. And you'll be saving our country -- one future freedom fighter at a time. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044 Pop Acta Media | Republican Task Force PO Box 461 Fort Collins, CO 80522 | _

Peter, it's official: **The people of South Texas have elected me as their next member of Congress for TX-15.** And on the same ballot, we chose Gina Hinojosa to be our next Governor and James Talarico to be our next United States Senator. This was a historic night, and we couldn't have done it without you. The other side tried to gerrymander us. To silence us. To deny us a seat at the table. And this community placed hope in me to be their _voice_. _It's what I've done for 30 years._ My music has been the soundtrack of weddings, quinceañeras, and carne asadas. Since we announced this campaign last September, South Texans have let me into their homes, they've joined me at barbecues, and they've come out to our ranch halls. I've been blessed to tour the country, perform in stadiums of all sizes, and win awards, but what's ahead for me is bigger than any song. South Texans are trusting me with their future. **I know the responsibility I'm taking on. It is an honor, and I'll never forget it.** Whether you're out here in the Valley or thousands of miles away, whether you voted for me, volunteered, or donated to our campaign, it was your support that put me in this position. Thank you for placing your trust in me, and know that I'll work every day to live up to it. I want to thank my family, my wife Mariana and four sons, my father Roberto Pulido, and all the tios, tias, and primos who showed up for me during this wild adventure. I wouldn't be here if not for your sacrifice. I love you. I want to thank my team, every member of our staff. You crisscrossed this region by my side, worked many late nights, gave up your weekends to build this movement. **Se vale soñar, South Texas.** And we proved it. Now, everybody's going to be looking to us to deliver. We'll have our work cut out for us, but I know we'll be ready. Thanks again. You'll be hearing from me. — Bobby

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: DEVELOPING: Republicans lost the Senate. Here’s what happens now.
body:
Plus: why JD Vance was the biggest loser | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1BwTIxMMeYK?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | | Republicans lost the Senate. Texas sent James Talarico to Washington over Ken Paxton. And Deb Haaland won the New Mexico governor’s race by double digits while getting fewer votes than every other Democrat on the ballot.
[We stayed up late ](https://us.list-manage.com/GrayZdyv3PU?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)with Jay McCleskey to make sense of it.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/XJz6ubZxiWd?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | **🔥 THE SENATE IS GONE, AND 2028 CAN’T FIX IT**
Paxton didn’t just lose Texas. He took Greg Abbott down with him.
Susan Collins lost Maine. El-Sayed is leading Michigan. Jay counts roughly ten Senate seats gone, and when Mark walks through the 2028 map state by state, there is almost nothing to take back.
One state made Mark say “we’re dead” before any of the big races were called. It’s not the one you’d guess.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/EVL6RUUozuN?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| | **🚨 HAALAND WINS NEW MEXICO AND STILL FINISHES LAST**
She beat Gregg Hull by double digits. Then we pulled up the vote totals.
The Secretary of State candidate, someone Mark admits he’d never heard of, got more votes than the governor-elect. So did the Attorney General. So did the auditor and the treasurer.
**Jay has two words for what that means. Then Mark explains why the people gunning for her hardest aren’t Republicans.

He wasn’t on a ballot. Mark explains why that doesn’t matter.
A second lane to the 2028 nomination just opened. Jay has blunt advice for what Trump has to fix in the next two years, and Krysty reminds everyone who she called for the Democrats two years ago when they told her to calm down.

Hi Peter - it's Evan Brown, Executive Director of the Congressional Progressive Caucus PAC. I'm writing this with very little sleep and a very full heart. **Last night, Democrats took back the House. More than 30 seats flipped from red to blue, the most since 2008, and more are still being counted. Six of those red ‐to‐blue wins were races we directly invested in, which means your support helped make each one possible.** We won in districts the experts told us to give up on and we did it by margins nobody saw coming. This victory belongs to you. It belongs to every supporter in Cresco and across Pennsylvania who chipped in when the polls looked tough, made one more call, or talked to one more neighbor. _Now comes the part we 've all been waiting for:_ For two years, progressive leaders in Congress have been playing defense, fighting off cuts to Social Security and Medicaid and standing up to Trump's attacks on our democracy. Starting in January, we get to go on offense. 6 WFP-endorsed victories, a historic Senate flip, and so much to celebrate! | | | Peter, Last night, Pennsylvania made history. 💜 **For the first time in more than 30 years, Democrats will control the Pennsylvania House, Senate, and governor's office. We defended and expanded our state House majority, flipped the state Senate, and helped elect working families champions across the Commonwealth.** At least **36 WFP-endorsed candidates** won their elections, with a couple of races still being counted! There's so much to celebrate:
* We flipped Pennsylvania's 7th Congressional District! **Bob Brooks** , a union firefighter and labor leader, defeated Republican incumbent Ryan Mackenzie. We're also celebrating **Chris Rabb's** victory in PA-03 and the re-elections of **Summer Lee** and **Chris Deluzio**.

* We helped flip the Pennsylvania Senate! **Mark Pinsley** and **Chris Thomas** unseated Republican state senators, helping deliver a Democratic majority for the first time in decades.

* We flipped key Republican-held Pennsylvania House seats! **Meriam Sabih** (HD-131), **Rachel Cuevas** (HD-187), **Sara Agerton** (HD-88), and **Hadley Haas** (HD-44) won their races, helping expand our majority.

* We sent even more working families champions to Harrisburg! **Ce-Ce Gerlach** won her State House Allentown, while **Sierra McNeil** secured a historic State House victory in Philadelphia after her hard-fought primary earlier this year.

These victories belong to the candidates who stepped up, the organizers and volunteers who showed up day after day, and the supporters who believed these races were worth fighting for. From early fundraising efforts to the final calls, texts, and canvasses before Election Day, so many people came together to make this moment possible. **To everyone who knocked a door, made a call, donated, volunteered, or helped a neighbor get to the polls: thank you. You helped make history in Pennsylvania.** And now, with more working families champions heading to Harrisburg and Washington, we have a real opportunity to build on these victories and keep fighting for **fully funded public schools** , **affordable housing** , **good union jobs** , and **a government that puts working people first.** We're fired up about what's ahead! Philadelphia's 2027 municipal elections are already on the horizon, and while there's more work to do, last night showed us just how much we can accomplish when we organize together. **If you're fired up, too, we'd love for you to be part of what comes next!** **[Become a dues-paying member of the PA WFP with a recurring contribution of $10 or more a month and help sustain the year-round organizing and grassroots campaigns that make victories like these possible. body:

#
Friend, **We won. And I couldn’t have done it without you.** Thank you to our neighbors across mid-Michigan for trusting me with the honor of representing our communities in Congress. In a year when our politics felt more divided than ever, we ran a campaign that brought people together from all walks of life around a vision for a better future. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142909082/658448179/-185804088?refcode=em-11.4.26-all&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjAyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlZDM4ZTY5OS05MGQ4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Cm4YzeYqHqDttGkgW2dGi0rvPX8JfEv2X2-qdwYsfko=) To every volunteer who knocked doors in Flint, made calls from a kitchen table in Saginaw, or talked to a neighbor in Bay City or Midland about what’s at stake. To every grassroots donor who chipped in when it mattered most. And to my team, who worked around the clock and never stopped believing in the mission to make life better for families here at home: thank you. This victory is yours. For the last two years, I’ve been listening to people across mid-Michigan, and I keep hearing the same thing: they’re working hard and doing everything right, and it’s still not adding up. That’s the fight I’m taking back to Washington. And our win wasn’t the only one. Democrats had a massive night across the country, and voters sent a clear message: they’re ready for leaders who will put working families first. Now, we have a responsibility to deliver. Together, we can break the painful fever of division in our politics, put a stop to corruption and self-dealing in Washington, and pass real solutions that will lower costs, build stronger communities, and restore the great American dream. Thank you for everything, Kristen

Thank you.
Last night, we made history, and I am so honored to be your next U.S. Senator from the great state of North Carolina. Surrounded by family, friends and supporters, I shared a few words. This victory belongs to all of us, and I wanted to make sure you heard my message too.
* * *
Hello, North Carolina! Are we having a good time tonight or what?
North Carolinians - you've made your voices heard and they were loud!
Thank you all so much. There's a few people I need to thank before anybody else: To my amazing wife Kristin, my wonderful daughters and the rest of my family over here, I am so grateful for your love and support. You guys are the light of my life and I could not do it without you.
And to everyone here including our volunteers, staff and supporters in this campaign - thank you for everything you did to take this United States Senate seat back for the people of North Carolina!
Now I know this was a hard-fought race and I do wish God's blessings for Michael Whatley and his family. I spoke with him earlier tonight and he acknowledged our victory.
You know, sixteen months ago, we launched this campaign together. We knew that for too many people in North Carolina, the middle-class was feeling like a distant dream. We knew that the Washington DC insiders and the richest Americans were getting unimaginable wealth at our expense. We knew that the chaos and corruption in Washington were hurting our people.
Today, you said this has to stop. And as your new United States Senator, I am ready to take that message to Washington and work to do something about it!
Alright yeah, it would have been easier for all of us to just complain and watch from the sidelines. To shake our heads and turn away. It would have been easier. But it wouldn't have been right.
And I've told you many times, on Sundays in church, I kept coming back to a passage from the book of Luke - "to whom much is given, much is required."
And I thought about the many blessings we have in North Carolina -- that I have in my life. And I knew what was required of me. And you knew what was required of us.
This campaign was powered by you, the people of North Carolina. And together, we're standing up for the people Washington has let down.
The small business owners watching their livelihoods disappear because of tariffs. The people who need health care and are terrified seeing the federal government take it away. The farmers getting crushed by the cost of fertilizer and diesel because of this never ending war. The hardworking families and the people on fixed incomes who desperately need their elected officials to recognize how expensive things are and to work to make stuff cost less!
You know, North Carolinians work hard. And they shouldn't need a lobbyist to unlock the American Dream. That should be the job of the people they elect to represent them. And North Carolinians, I accept your job offer!
Tonight guys, we told Washington loud and clear that North Carolinians will always matter more than the billionaires and the insiders. Tonight, we showed the country that when everyday people come together, we can make change. Tonight, we let everyone know that we are just getting started.
Guys, tonight, this campaign ends. But tomorrow, the work of governing begins.
We have to work to make health care, housing and groceries more affordable. To end this war and stop the pain at the pump. To protect Medicaid expansion we worked so hard for. To stop corruption and take on special interests that get rich while people struggle to get by. To strengthen our democracy and live up to this nation's highest ideals.
Hey guys - it won't be easy. And it won't be simple. But I know that to whom much is given, much is required.
Guys, in North Carolina, we don't just believe in the promise of tomorrow. We become it. First in Flight. First colony to demand independence. First public university. We race to lead because we know what hope the future holds. And when you've got hope, when you've got hope, anything is possible.
Tonight guys, I am deeply grateful for and humbled by the confidence and trust you have once again placed in me.
I am determined that no matter the challenges that confront me, I will be an independent voice ready to work with anyone to do what's right for this amazing state that has given me so much. Guys, I will be your voice.
As your Senator, I will always put YOU, the people of North Carolina, first. I will put YOU before politics. I will put YOU before party. I will put YOU before power. I'm not going to Washington to be something. I'm going to Washington to do something!
And at the end of the day, I am still a prisoner of hope. I truly believe that our best days lie ahead. That we can make the course correction that our great country so badly needs. That North Carolina and the United States have a future teeming with possibilities.
So what do you say, North Carolina. Are you ready for change?
Are you ready to turn things around for hardworking people?
Are you ready to meet the promise of tomorrow?
I am too! May God bless all of you, our country and the great state of North Carolina.
Thank you very much! Thank you!

**Thank you, Peter. Thank you, San Francisco.**

I am so grateful for your trust and support. Last night I walked onto the stage at the Swedish American Hall, where we launched this campaign, and the first results had us well ahead.

In San Francisco, we count every ballot, and that will take a few more days. But I feel very good about where we are.

**There has never been an LGBTQ member of Congress from California anywhere other than Los Angeles County. Ever._That's about to change._ This is a win for everyone, for every single person in San Francisco.**

For me, this is a milestone of a journey that started in 1997, when a young gay guy from New Jersey with a funny last name rode the escalator up from Castro Station, saw people like him everywhere, and knew he was home. I've been in love with this city ever since.

This belongs to every volunteer who walked precincts, every phone banker, every union member who showed up, every house party host, everyone who donated, everyone who put up a window sign. **You turned this campaign into the strongest grassroots movement San Francisco has ever built.**

Across the country, Americans are sending a clear message: **We're taking our country back. We're keeping our democracy. We're restoring the rule of law.**

I'm not going to tell you it'll be easy to get things done in Washington. It won't be. _But, everything worth fighting for is hard._

When I went to Sacramento, they said we couldn't change our broken housing system, and we replaced it. They said we couldn't regulate AI, and we did. When we got knocked down, we came right back again. And that's what we're going to do in Congress.

name: Dr. Shirley Weber
subject: Thank you

body:
https://drshirleyweber.com/?utm_source=email%20wrapper&utm_medium=email%20wrapper&utm_campaign=email%20wrapper [https://drshirleyweber.com/?utm_source=email%20wrapper&utm_medium=email%20wrapper&utm_campaign=email%20wrapper]
Friends,

While results are not yet certified, it seems the voters of California have re-elected me as Secretary of State, and I thank you.

I am honored by the trust that California's voters have placed in me to continue defending and administering our elections.

I was born the daughter of a sharecropper in the Jim Crow South. My family was denied the right to vote. And after a lynch mob came for my father, we fled Arkansas.

My parents cast their first ballots here and even opened our living room as a polling place for our neighbors. I learned the right to vote is sacred. And that it was paid for in blood. I have dedicated my life to protecting that right for every Californian.

Every day in office, I carry that history with me. I look forward to continuing my work as Secretary of State.

We are up against forces trying to turn back the clock and infringe on voting rights. They are trying to shorten polling hours, reduce early voting days, eliminate vote-by-mail, and intimidate the election workers who make democracy run.

I will continue to do everything in my power to defend Californians’ right to vote, and ensure our elections are operated with transparency, integrity, and efficiency.

Together, we fought to ensure that every Californian has the opportunity to participate in safe, transparent, and accessible elections.

I am looking forward to continuing that fight as your Secretary of State.

Onward,

Dr. Shirley N. Weber

What a night, Peter. Here’s what we learned in _the aftermath of the most expensive election in U.S. history:_
# Billionaires and Corporations Lose Big: People Power Wins
Despite MAGA billionaires' heavy interference in our elections from Elon Musk, PA’s Jeffrey Yass, and more pouring millions behind Republicans this cycle, they still lose. This was a huge swing to the left like never before and Democrats now have a trifecta in Pennsylvania to ensure safe, secure elections for 2028 and beyond. What we really saw with these election results: **Pennsylvanians are tired of the same old playbook that lets billionaires and corporations hoard wealth and escape accountability while the rest of us suffer.** Voters rejected Trump’s oligarchy and when under attack from Trump’s fascist enforcement agencies, the people proved we have the power for change, when we take collective action.
# One PA Organizing Gets Results
**We flipped 4 congressional seats.** Democrats needed a net gain of THREE seats to take control from Republicans. Our organizing helped to break up Trump’s loyal group in the House of Representatives. Democrats now have the majority in the House with the ability to block the MAGA agenda in the legislature and launch official investigations with subpoena power on everything from the Epstein files to corruption around the Trump family’s business interests. **We elected working class champions to the Assembly and State Senate.** For the first time in over 30 years, Democrats have a trifecta in Pennsylvania. What this actually means is that PA can block the worst of Trump’s fascist attempts. We now have allies in Harrisburg, who know it was our organizing efforts that got them elected, we can organize with — for a proactive vision of what Pennsylvanians need from lowering costs to affordable housing to transit for all and more. | [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142909747/658451248/-1740112309?refcode=EM_FL_OPA_20261104_fr_results_cm_oc_act_xx_img1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vQ1BELzEvMTEzNTk1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjJkYTU4OGJjLTkyZDgtZjExMS1iZjViLTAwMGQzYTU0NDQyZSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=EwSBui3PS2uAxaquOVk3lyF1LNsBYsjLsHsXKP_z7rE=)

# Organizing Everywhere Wins
If we want to be serious about winning, our organizing has to meet people where they are — at home, in the streets, on the phones, online, and more. That’s why our crew put out all the stops to mobilize the community into their voting power.
Some metrics of our organizing efforts this election cycle:
🗣️ 25,100 conversations with voters
🚪 36,000 doors knocked
☎️ 220,000 calls made
💬 600,000 texts sent
👀 3 million organic views
🎨 450 pieces of organic content
🖥️ 6 waves of targeted digital ads
🤝 Over 1000 volunteers
🎈 Over 2000 event attendees
# We Don’t Stop at Elections
Elections and voting are just one tactic in our overall strategy for community power. We organize year-round because after elections, comes the work of governing and unfortunately the billionaires desperately continue to scratch and claw for control over us. One PA is a regular presence in local city hall and neighborhood hearings in Harrisburg and in DC to get loud, be heard, and win policy that changes lives.
Some of the immediate fights we’re organizing around:
* We fought for and won the Safe Healthy Homes Act, historic legislation with Working Families Party Council Member Nicolas O’Rourke for required core housing quality and basic protections for renters. This went into effect on November 1 and we are holding community trainings to make sure the community is getting what we’re due.
* 925 homes in West and Southwest Philadelphia are at risk of being sold out from under tenants impacting over 3,000 residents, even though the city has only spent $38 million of the $278 million allocated for affordable housing in the HOME plan. The resources to save these homes are sitting right there unused!
* Our members rallied for historic landmark policy to establish paid parental leave and sick leave in Allegheny County. Now we’re building on that win to continue to fight for tenant rights One PA won in Philly to be enacted in Pittsburgh and Allegheny County.

Our journey does not stop at voting. We will continue to organize, grow stronger, and build the power that turns our collective strength into change for the better.

body:
| Victory Day
---
_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you'd like to unsubscribe,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=1&akid=3949%2E259176%2EzthFxb)_

[](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/18060?t=2&akid=3949%2E259176%2EzthFxb)Incredible. Generational. Seismic.

And don't let anyone tell you any differently: YOU made this happen.

You, the incredible members of this community who donated that extra dollar, knocked on that last half-block of doors when your feet hurt, made those extra calls when you were tired.

You, who made sure to get your teenage kids, friends, co-workers, and others who needed your help or plan to the polling place. Because that is how important this election day was.

**Tsunami doesn't quite do justice to what you did. It was more like the meteor from the film Armageddon.**

We pulled off shocking upsets in Texas. And Kansas. And South Carolina. And Maine. We could end up with 56 U.S. Senate seats--almost definitely 55--and we could end up with 260 House seats--almost definitely 255.

You made this happen.

We took back swing states they'd clawed away from us--Ohio and Iowa--up and down the ballot. We cemented North Carolina and Georgia as purple, maybe even purplish-blue states. We elected the first Black female governor of any state in Georgia. We elected Ohio's first female governor.

You made this happen.

We're in a dead heat in Mississippi, where we may elect a Black U.S. Senator for the first time since Reconstruction. We elected the first Latina Governor of Texas, and did it by ousting one of the worst of the pro-ICE bigots, Greg Abbott, who spent his time concentrating on deporting Latinos and Latinas for the crime of wanting a better life.

You made this happen.

State legislatures, Attorneys General who can prosecute federal officials--say ICE--for breaking state law. Secretaries of State who make sure ALL the votes in 2028 are counted. This community played an enormous role in all of this. And I hope you know it. And I hope you can take a second to look in the mirror, reflect, and be proud of what you did. Because you saved our ailing democracy from an authoritarian force. A few times, using history, a life of working on campaigns, and data as a guide, I said this would be a 50-year storm--the biggest electoral thumping since the post-Watergate 1974 election. But, at the risk of repeating myself:

You made this happen.

As just one American. And Ohioan. I can never thank you enough for all you did to make last night and the ongoing elections--where we will ensure every vote is counted--happen.

Incredible. Generational. Seismic. I can never say thank you enough to this amazing community, but the work doesn't stop here.**We're already making plans to use this momentum to take even more seats, and soon, the White House! If you're willing to back our 50-state strategy, you can chip in to support our work below.** | [Support Blue Amp Action →](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/19780?source=SL_EM_ENG_2026.11.04_Cliff-TY_B3_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=3&akid=3949%2E259176%2EzthFxb)

Displaced Palestinians stage a protest demanding to be allowed to return to their homes on November 1, 2026 in Hebron, occupied West Bank. Photo by Mamoun Wazwaz/Anadolu via Getty Images.
HEBRON, Occupied West Bank--Baher Sultan returned to his home in Hebron's Khallet al-Maghariba neighborhood on Monday, nine days after Israeli soldiers arrived at his front door and ordered his family to leave. Sultan, his wife, and his four children were among thousands of families forcibly displaced during a massive Israeli military operation in the city.
The house they returned to had been ransacked. Sultan said soldiers had occupied the home for several days, rifling through cupboards, breaking windows and door locks, and damaging household furniture and other belongings.
Despite the damage and the disruption to their lives, Sultan, 47, said his family was overjoyed simply to be back in their neighborhood. "We returned on the same day the army withdrew. I couldn't wait," he told Drop Site News.
The Israeli army's 11-day assault on Hebron followed an October 23 attack by two Palestinian gunmen on a military checkpoint in the city that killed two Israeli soldiers before the two gunmen were shot dead. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the city soon afterwards and announced a major military operation. "The IDF will enter the neighborhoods from which the terrorists emerged, evacuate the residents, go house-to-house, and dismantle the terror infrastructure. We are prepared for an extensive operation in Judea and Samaria," he said, using Israel's name for the West Bank.
Sultan said the ordeal began on October 24, when Israeli soldiers raided his neighborhood and began knocking on residents' doors.
"We had been frightened from the moment the occupation government made its announcement. We were watching what was happening, and when the army spread through the neighbourhood and the loudspeakers started, we became scared and confused," he said. "Soldiers got out of their vehicles and began knocking on doors. When I opened the door, they asked who lived there and took my identity card. I told them, and then they informed me that I had to leave the house and take only a few essential belongings. Some of them were shouting [in Hebrew], and we couldn't understand what they were saying, but we were frightened."
The Israeli military sealed all the entrances to the city before moving in, displacing nearly 5,000 Palestinians, demolishing buildings, and disrupting schooling for some 80,000 students. Families in the Al-Jalda and Deir Bahha neighborhoods were all ordered to flee, while residents of other neighborhoods were subjected to a strict military cordon.
As the assault was under way, the UN agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA)[ warned](https://substack.com/redirect/341ffbcb-c504-4691-aa55-b3e217eec792?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on October 27 that the Israeli military operation carried alarming echoes of the 2025 Israeli assault on three refugee camps in the northern West Bank that displaced over 32,000 Palestinians in what Human Rights Watch found amounted to war crimes and crimes against humanity.
The soldiers left Sultan and his family to make their way through the streets after ordering them to flee the neighborhood. They spent the first two days moving between relatives' homes before his cousin offered them his apartment in the Sheikh neighbourhood, near Bab al-Zawiya in central Hebron, where they stayed for the next five days without knowing how long their displacement would last.
His children, out of school since the first day of the military operation, struggled to adjust to the unfamiliar environment.
"They don't feel free to move around, and they feel shy and embarrassed whenever they do anything, like asking for food or going to the bathroom. They don't talk about it, so as not to embarrass our cousins," Sultan told Drop Site while the family was still displaced. "Their needs go beyond food and shelter. They need a space to move around, books and notebooks, and an education that allows them to carry on with a normal life."
The Israeli army withdrew from the occupied neighborhoods at dawn on November 2, saying it had completed its operations after confiscating a grand [total](https://substack.com/redirect/39b8a26b-663a-4143-9b71-630b128b8cb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of four weapons. Families began returning to their damaged homes in Al-Jalda and Deir Bahha that same day, and schools, universities, and businesses began to reopen, Mayor Yousef al-Jabari told Al Jazeera.
Most homes in Khallet al-Maghariba sustained light to moderate damage, Sultan said, with broken windows among the most visible signs of the operation, adding that some residents believed some of the damage was caused by the deployment of Israeli snipers in the area.
His children have also returned to school. "They are happy now," he said.
## **A City Ravaged by Occupation**
Located in the southern West Bank, Hebron is the largest city in the territory with some 200,000 residents, and for decades has been one of the most tightly controlled by the Israeli occupation.
Unlike other cities in the West Bank that are ringed by Israeli settlements, usually on the surrounding hilltops, in Hebron Israeli settlements exist in the heart of the city, with armed Israeli settlers living in the midst of Palestinians residents. Also unlike other cities in the West Bank, Hebron did not receive the status of Area A under the Oslo Accords.
In 1997, the Palestinian Liberation Organization and the Israeli government signed the [Hebron Protoco](https://substack.com/redirect/03870a38-2bd8-4f8e-88f3-b0ea11a112d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)l which split the city into two sections: H1, comprising 80% of the city that is nominally under Palestinian control, and H2, comprising 20% of the city that is under full Israeli military control, and includes the Old City and the historic Ibrahimi Mosque. Some 40,000 Palestinians live in H2 alongside several hundred settlers with a heavy Israeli military presence. The city also holds about [40 percent](https://substack.com/redirect/a5ca021f-3ece-4a4a-9845-80553f9f2d30?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the West Bank's 89 main checkpoints and 11 percent of all 925 movement obstacles in the territory, according to the UN.
The Hebron Protocol was signed in the wake of the 1994 Ibrahimi Mosque massacre, when Baruch Goldstein, an American-born settler, [opened fire](https://substack.com/redirect/d7eb68b5-bf3c-473e-bda2-84c07a55bc53?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Palestinians praying at the Ibrahimi Mosque, killing 29 worshippers.
Israel [responded](https://substack.com/redirect/55a720d9-3838-4fd3-8b0a-2b32c9940994?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by partitioning the mosque and closing Shuhada Street, the Old City's main commercial artery, to Palestinians. By 2007, 1,829 businesses in the city center had shut, about 440 of them by military order.
"Today those who rule Israel are followers of the man who carried out the massacre, and they are seeking to displace and expel us," Sultan said, referring to Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel's national security minister, who [kept a portrait of Goldstein](https://substack.com/redirect/2ba59e4c-6e43-41cf-b709-8eb6d1d36acb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on his living room wall for years before entering government.
For Sultan, who lived through the 1994 massacre, Israel's latest operation was almost as bad. He says that back then at least the Israeli government still felt compelled to publicly condemn the violence, however nominally.
"Today, those committing the displacement, killing, and demolition are the government and the right-wing extremists in it," he said.
For residents returning to their homes this week, the attack and their subsequent displacement are part of a much longer story.
## **Mass Expulsion**
Abdul Shakour Mujahid said his was the first house in the neighborhood of Al-Jalda that was raided by the Israeli military.
"They told me I had an hour to take my most important things, and that I was only allowed to take simple things, clothes and some belongings," he said.
The troops also confiscated his car, and what he was able to carry on foot was not enough for him, his wife, and their three children, the eldest of whom is 12.
Mujahid and his family moved into his father's home in an adjacent neighborhood. In addition to relying on his father for food, he received an aid package of basic supplies and milk from the local relief committee. From a distance, he watched soldiers spread across the rooftops of Al-Jalda, where they used dozens of houses as sniper positions.
"The feeling is hard to describe. It is a new Nakba for us, to see your home before your eyes and not be able to reach it," he said, invoking the Arabic word for "catastrophe" that Palestinians use to describe their mass expulsion by Zionist forces in 1948. "It is the greatest crime and the greatest injustice. We have done nothing. What helps us endure is the embrace of family and relatives in the community."
The Hebron Governorate Support and Relief Committee registered 537 affected families, comprising 3,361 people, including 232 infants, 1,193 children aged between two and 17, 326 elderly people, 147 pregnant or breastfeeding women, 32 people with disabilities, and 213 people with chronic illnesses, according to its head Sufian Al-Muhtaseb.
"Hebron's communities refused to open shelters and declared they were ready to host displaced families [in their homes], and the invitations were not limited to relatives," Al-Muhtaseb told Drop Site
Al-Muhtaseb said there were severe supply shortages, with the hardest requests the committee received being food and drink--and, above all, baby formula.
"The occupation did not allow residents to take their money from their homes, and they find it hard to ask the families they are staying with, even if they are relatives, and even those they went to may not be in a good financial situation," he said.
## **A Ripple Effect**
On October 29, Adalah, a legal center for Palestinian citizens of Israel,[ petitioned](https://substack.com/redirect/02a055b3-2e5b-47bd-a169-c9f9b011a8c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Israel's High Court on behalf of the municipality and seven residents of Al-Jalda and Ein Deir Bahha.
The petition said troops forced hundreds of families from their homes late at night with little notice, barred their return indefinitely, and provided no concrete justification for an evacuation on that scale, which it argued amounted to forcible transfer and collective punishment under the Fourth Geneva Convention.
It also cited municipal figures showing that the closure had left about 1,200 tonnes of rubbish piling up in the city, as garbage trucks could not reach the sealed areas.
Hebron Mayor Yousef al-Jabari told Drop Site the municipality worked with partner organizations to provide aid to affected families.
"The municipality is preparing a survey to identify residents' needs and priorities so that aid can be directed according to each family's actual circumstances," al-Jabari said before the Israeli withdrawal.
During the operation, Israeli forces demolished 15 homes and other structures and forced 327 shops to close, exacting a severe toll on the city's economy--one of the most important in the West Bank.
The city [accounts](https://substack.com/redirect/4361e430-8ce3-4bb1-99f5-dbffffcadcfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for about 40% of Palestinian industrial output in the West Bank and 30% of exports, and the closure of whole areas and restrictions on the movement of workers and goods halted factories, markets, and supply chains, while businesses and shops struggled to keep operating.
Adnan al-Natsheh, deputy head of the Hebron Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said the direct losses from the closures "amount to between 10 million and 12 million shekels a day," or about $3.2 million to $3.8 million, including about 1 million shekels in the dairy sector alone.
He warned that hundreds of industrial and commercial businesses have been affected, and said 13 facilities in the Farsh al-Hawa area had suffered vandalism, bulldozing, and demolition.
"The restrictions on workers and goods threaten entire production and supply chains across the West Bank."

As the assault was under way, the UN agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA) on October 27 that the Israeli military operation carried alarming echoes of the 2025 Israeli assault on three refugee camps in the northern West Bank that displaced over 32,000 Palestinians in what Human Rights Watch found amounted to war crimes and crimes against humanity. The soldiers left Sultan and his family to make their way through the streets after ordering them to flee the neighborhood. They spent the first two days moving between relatives' homes before his cousin offered them his apartment in the Sheikh neighbourhood, near Bab al-Zawiya in central Hebron, where they stayed for the next five days without knowing how long their displacement would last. His children, out of school since the first day of the military operation, struggled to adjust to the unfamiliar environment. "They don't feel free to move around, and they feel shy and embarrassed whenever they do anything, like asking for food or going to the bathroom. They don't talk about it, so as not to embarrass our cousins," Sultan told Drop Site while the family was still displaced. "Their needs go beyond food and shelter. They need a space to move around, books and notebooks, and an education that allows them to carry on with a normal life." The Israeli army withdrew from the occupied neighborhoods at dawn on November 2, saying it had completed its operations after confiscating a grand of four weapons. Families began returning to their damaged homes in Al-Jalda and Deir Bahha that same day, and schools, universities, and businesses began to reopen, Mayor Yousef al-Jabari told Al Jazeera. Most homes in Khallet al-Maghariba sustained light to moderate damage, Sultan said, with broken windows among the most visible signs of the operation, adding that some residents believed some of the damage was caused by the deployment of Israeli snipers in the area. His children have also returned to school. "They are happy now," he said. A City Ravaged by Occupation Located in the southern West Bank, Hebron is the largest city in the territory with some 200,000 residents, and for decades has been one of the most tightly controlled by the Israeli occupation. Unlike other cities in the West Bank that are ringed by Israeli settlements, usually on the surrounding hilltops, in Hebron Israeli settlements exist in the heart of the city, with armed Israeli settlers living in the midst of Palestinians residents. Also unlike other cities in the West Bank, Hebron did not receive the status of Area A under the Oslo Accords. In 1997, the Palestinian Liberation Organization and the Israeli government signed the which split the city into two sections: H1, comprising 80% of the city that is nominally under Palestinian control, and H2, comprising 20% of the city that is under full Israeli military control, and includes the Old City and the historic Ibrahimi Mosque. Some 40,000 Palestinians live in H2 alongside several hundred settlers with a heavy Israeli military presence. The city also holds about of the West Bank's 89 main checkpoints and 11 percent of all 925 movement obstacles in the territory, according to the UN. The Hebron Protocol was signed in the wake of the 1994 Ibrahimi Mosque massacre, when Baruch Goldstein, an American-born settler, on Palestinians praying at the Ibrahimi Mosque, killing 29 worshippers. Israel by partitioning the mosque and closing Shuhada Street, the Old City's main commercial artery, to Palestinians. By 2007, 1,829 businesses in the city center had shut, about 440 of them by military order. "Today those who rule Israel are followers of the man who carried out the massacre, and they are seeking to displace and expel us," Sultan said, referring to Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel's national security minister, who on his living room wall for years before entering government. For Sultan, who lived through the 1994 massacre, Israel's latest operation was almost as bad. He says that back then at least the Israeli government still felt compelled to publicly condemn the violence, however nominally. "Today, those committing the displacement, killing, and demolition are the government and the right-wing extremists in it," he said. For residents returning to their homes this week, the attack and their subsequent displacement are part of a much longer story. Mass Expulsion Abdul Shakour Mujahid said his was the first house in the neighborhood of Al-Jalda that was raided by the Israeli military. "They told me I had an hour to take my most important things, and that I was only allowed to take simple things, clothes and some belongings," he said. The troops also confiscated his car, and what he was able to carry on foot was not enough for him, his wife, and their three children, the eldest of whom is 12. Mujahid and his family moved into his father's home in an adjacent neighborhood. In addition to relying on his father for food, he received an aid package of basic supplies and milk from the local relief committee. From a distance, he watched soldiers spread across the rooftops of Al-Jalda, where they used dozens of houses as sniper positions. "The feeling is hard to describe. It is a new Nakba for us, to see your home before your eyes and not be able to reach it," he said, invoking the Arabic word for "catastrophe" that Palestinians use to describe their mass expulsion by Zionist forces in 1948. "It is the greatest crime and the greatest injustice. We have done nothing. What helps us endure is the embrace of family and relatives in the community." The Hebron Governorate Support and Relief Committee registered 537 affected families, comprising 3,361 people, including 232 infants, 1,193 children aged between two and 17, 326 elderly people, 147 pregnant or breastfeeding women, 32 people with disabilities, and 213 people with chronic illnesses, according to its head Sufian Al-Muhtaseb. "Hebron's communities refused to open shelters and declared they were ready to host displaced families [in their homes], and the invitations were not limited to relatives," Al-Muhtaseb told Drop Site Al-Muhtaseb said there were severe supply shortages, with the hardest requests the committee received being food and drink--and, above all, baby formula. "The occupation did not allow residents to take their money from their homes, and they find it hard to ask the families they are staying with, even if they are relatives, and even those they went to may not be in a good financial situation," he said. A Ripple Effect On October 29, Adalah, a legal center for Palestinian citizens of Israel, Israel's High Court on behalf of the municipality and seven residents of Al-Jalda and Ein Deir Bahha. The petition said troops forced hundreds of families from their homes late at night with little notice, barred their return indefinitely, and provided no concrete justification for an evacuation on that scale, which it argued amounted to forcible transfer and collective punishment under the Fourth Geneva Convention. It also cited municipal figures showing that the closure had left about 1,200 tonnes of rubbish piling up in the city, as garbage trucks could not reach the sealed areas. Hebron Mayor Yousef al-Jabari told Drop Site the municipality worked with partner organizations to provide aid to affected families. "The municipality is preparing a survey to identify residents' needs and priorities so that aid can be directed according to each family's actual circumstances," al-Jabari said before the Israeli withdrawal. During the operation, Israeli forces demolished 15 homes and other structures and forced 327 shops to close, exacting a severe toll on the city's economy--one of the most important in the West Bank. The city for about 40% of Palestinian industrial output in the West Bank and 30% of exports, and the closure of whole areas and restrictions on the movement of workers and goods halted factories, markets, and supply chains, while businesses and shops struggled to keep operating. Adnan al-Natsheh, deputy head of the Hebron Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said the direct losses from the closures "amount to between 10 million and 12 million shekels a day," or about $3.2 million to $3.8 million, including about 1 million shekels in the dairy sector alone. He warned that hundreds of industrial and commercial businesses have been affected, and said 13 facilities in the Farsh al-Hawa area had suffered vandalism, bulldozing, and demolition. "The restrictions on workers and goods threaten entire production and supply chains across the West Bank." This piece was produced in collaboration with. subject: I’m damn proud

body:
I’ll tell you what, it feels damned good to see good folks win.
#
Peter,
I’ll tell you what, it feels damned good to see good folks win.
Our Small Town PAC candidates have flipped five Republican House seats and won three governors’ races. They put in the work, gave people a reason to show up, and had this team behind them when it counted. I hope you’re proud of that.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261104-1.v-NSpl&amount=5&refcode=em20261104-1315&t=1&akid=1315%2E34582%2EZN6_ip)
**Across the country, Americans stood up to Donald Trump and said enough. We took back the House and the Senate, elected Democratic governors, and rejected his failed politics of hate, fear, and division.**
I started Small Town PAC because I believe Democrats need to show up in places too many people have written off. Our candidates did that, and they were part of something big last night.
Here’s what I hope Democrats take from this: **Don’t write people off. Show up. Listen. Give them somebody worth voting for.**
People want good schools, good jobs, and health care they can afford. They want somebody looking out for them instead of billionaires. Last night, they voted for it. Now we’ve got to make good on that trust.
Whether you donated, knocked doors, made calls, or talked somebody into getting out and voting, thank you. I’m proud of what we did together.
Take a little time to celebrate. You earned it. Then let’s get back to work.
**[And if you can, chip in to help us keep showing up in communities too often written off, stand up to Trump, and build a Democratic Party that working people know is on their side. We’ve got a lot more work to do, and I’d be grateful to have you with us.](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261104-1.v-NSpl&amount=5&refcode=em20261104-1315&t=2&akid=1315%2E34582%2EZN6_ip)**

I’m grateful,
Tim
