name: Kristin
subject: The fight isn’t over
body:
We have a lot to be proud of.

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142910423/658453406/-463234460?refcode=emailheader&refcode2=95801cb0-93d8-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ms=261104_kh_loss&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTA5NjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTU4MDFjYjAtOTNkOC1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=Bbos6uFf5nrATcC_V6CeMtnmhfDmFoyT9Q5iokbCjZw=)
---
Friend, I have a lot of mixed emotions today. These obviously weren’t the circumstances I wanted to be emailing you under, but this is still an email I’m proud to send to you personally. I stepped into this race in 2023 knowing it would be an uphill battle because of extreme gerrymandering. In the end, that’s what decided this race. Texas Republicans drew these lines to pick their voters before voters ever got to pick their representative, and in a district drawn that way, a candidate has to overcome the map before earning a single vote. As a scientist, I learned how to recognize and be comfortable with failure. But this great experiment over the past year as we’ve campaigned across TX-21 wasn’t a failure. It was an investment. We built something here—a foundation of volunteers, neighbors, and first-time voters in a district that the establishment had written off. We knocked doors in the heat, held conversations with people on the streets, and showed up everywhere, whether or not anyone else did. Many people told me I was the first politician they had at their door in decades. _**And we were a big part in helping flip Texas blue.**_ Republicans here voted blue for the first time. That’s huge, and it’s something we should still be proud of because those welcoming conversations helped give them a little nudge to choose country over party. The foundation we built together doesn’t disappear overnight because an election ended. We can keep growing it, one conversation at a time, until we eventually flip this seat. This fight isn’t over. Thank you to every single one of you who donated, volunteered, and supported this campaign. It’s been an honor of a lifetime to be the Democratic Nominee in TX-21, and I am so incredibly grateful for your support! Onward to justice and in solidarity always, — Kristin
| | |
---|---|---

### About Kristin Hook
Kristin is running to fight for affordability, opportunity, and accountability for working families like her own. As a scientist and former educator, Kristin is trained to solve complex problems — whether it’s fixing our broken health care system, wealth inequality, or underfunded public schools.

body:
# [#] Hi team — we did it. I’m honored to have been elected to serve again as your Representative.

Last night would not have been possible without your support. You knocked on thousands of doors, made phone calls late into the evening, chipped in what you could, and talked to your neighbors.

This victory belongs to everyone who believes that common sense, hard work, and practical results still matter.

Serving as your Representative is the honor of my life. I promise you this: I’m going straight back to work fighting to lower costs and taxes for our families, fix our roads and transit, support our first responders, and deliver real, bipartisan solutions that make life more affordable here at home.

Thank you for your tireless support and for always having my back.

Now, let’s get back to work.

— Josh
Josh Gottheimer represents New Jersey’s Fifth Congressional District. Josh is in Congress to fight for lower taxes and Jersey Values. He’s working across the aisle to find real solutions for New Jersey families and is actively fighting against the ideological gridlock in Washington. name: =?utf-8?q?Mar=C3=ADa_Teresa_Kumar=2C_Voto_Latino?=
subject: Latino voters delivered historic victories, and you helped make that happen.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
#
Wow, Peter. We did it.
Last night, Latino voters across the nation — especially in Texas just proved the nation wrong. For over three decades, pundits wrote this state off. But we never did. And last night, Tejanos answered with record-shattering turnout.
Despite the long lines, shuttered polling locations, and shifting maps, they showed up, and they showed the entire country that Latino voters in Texas have the power, not billionaires who are trying to run the state.
Latino voters delivered historic victories:
\- **Gina Hinojosa** will be the first Latina to lead the state of Texas.
\- **James Talarico** will be the first Texas Democrat in the U.S. Senate since 1993.
\- **Bobby Pulido** flipped a gerrymandered congressional seat Republicans counted on as solid red.
\- The **Texas House** is expected to flip for the first time since 2001.
\- Every **statewide office** on the ballot is trending blue as the final votes are counted.
None of this happened overnight. Voto Latino has been building power in Texas, registering over 412,000 voters and growing our VL On Campus network to 14 campuses. We’re investing in the next generation of Latino voters because we have faith in the state. **Last night, that investment delivered historic wins, and the message could not be clearer: when Latino voters are heard, they decide the future.**
**And it wasn’t just Texas, Peter.** Across the country, Latino voters powered a “blue tsunami” that took back both the U.S. House _and_ the U.S. Senate. Your support helped turn out a massive wave of Latino voters in the states and districts that decided control of Congress, and the whole nation is feeling it this morning.
I have so much gratitude for this community, and hope for the future.
There’s so much more to share about what we accomplished across the country, and I’ll be back to share more — but today, I just wanted to say thank you.
Onward,
María Teresa Kumar
Voto Latino

| | | Peter,
---
I am incredibly honored and grateful that the people of Long Island have once again put their trust in me to represent them in Congress.
Two years ago we flipped this seat. This year we proved that we can hold it.
This was never going to be an easy race. Republicans threw everything they had at us. Donald Trump endorsed my opponent, Mike Johnson came to Nassau County to campaign against me and millions of dollars were spent trying to flip this seat.
But you never gave up. And because of you, we won.
I ran for Congress because I believe American families deserve representatives who will put them first, fight to lower costs and work across the aisle to get things done.
That commitment hasn't changed.
I'm ready to get back to work fighting for our communities and delivering results for the people who put their trust in me.
To every volunteer, donor, supporter and voter who made this victory possible: Thank you from the bottom of my heart.
I'm proud of what we've accomplished together and I'm even more excited about what comes next.
With gratitude,
Laura Gillen

clean_body: Because of you, we won. | | | | = | | | Peter, I am incredibly honored and grateful that the people of Long Island have once again put their trust in me to represent them in Congress. Two years ago we flipped this seat. This year we proved that we can hold it. This was never going to be an easy race. Republicans threw everything they had at us. Donald Trump endorsed my opponent, Mike Johnson came to Nassau County to campaign against me and millions of dollars were spent trying to flip this seat. But you never gave up. And because of you, we won. I ran for Congress because I believe American families deserve representatives who will put them first, fight to lower costs and work across the aisle to get things done. That commitment hasn't changed. I'm ready to get back to work fighting for our communities and delivering results for the people who put their trust in me. To every volunteer, donor, supporter and voter who made this victory possible: Thank you from the bottom of my heart. I'm proud of what we've accomplished together and I'm even more excited about what comes next. name: Alan Bradstock
subject: Thank you
body:
| |
---
I am proud and grateful that America voted for character, competence, civility and caring and voted against corruption, cronyism, cruelty and chaos. I am proud and grateful for the hard work, support and enthusiasm of the campaign staff, volunteers, contributors and supporters. I am especially proud and grateful for the relationships we've built with each other based on belief in each other. That belief started slowly and grew stronger every day. That belief in me got me through my most difficult year. My belief in you resulted in so many people investing so much in the campaign. It also resulted in the creation of teams of strangers who now feel the special bond that only comes from doing important, greater-good work together. Our first accomplishment was shifting PA-14 by 18% from 2024, compared to the national average of 15%. We've only laid the foundation. All day yesterday I communicated with so many people committed to continuing to make what we've created even better. After some decompression, we will soon reach out regarding our plan to move forward. Alan

Peter,

Thank you.

I’m so grateful for what we accomplished together. As chair of the Democratic Governors’ Association, I’m proud to share that **we won a majority of the nation’s governorships for the first time in 16 years.**

And not only did we flip the House and Senate, but right here in the Commonwealth, we won in Kentucky’s 6th district, a district that Donald Trump won by 15 points in 2024, and where In This Together PAC invested heavily.

These results and more are the ultimate proof that Democrats can win anywhere, and we should be fighting everywhere.

**None of this could have happened without you. Your donations and your support made these wins possible. Thank you for believing in good people and good candidates, and for doing it even when the odds were against us.**

Now, we need to celebrate today, and govern tomorrow.

Voters didn’t send Democrats to office to put on a show. They sent us to get things done, and we need to quickly turn these victories into real results. For every hearing Democrats hold about Pete Hegseth, RFK Jr. and the Trump administration’s unprecedented corruption, we need to pass three bills that lower costs, invest in housing, improve health care and make a difference in people’s daily lives.

With Trump still in office and able to veto legislation, Democratic governors, especially, are going to need to lead the charge to get real results. I’m ready for that work, and I know my fellow governors are too.

Thank you again, y’all. Let’s get to it.

Andy | | **Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear and In This Together PAC are working to support leaders who will lead with compassion and decency, reject anger politics, and always do what's right. As chair of the Democratic Governors’ Association, I’m proud to share that we won a majority of the nation’s governorships for the first time in 16 years. With Trump still in office and able to veto legislation, Democratic governors, especially, are going to need to lead the charge to get real results. Friend, an extraordinarily long, grueling, and demanding election cycle has finally come to an end.
Across months of campaigning, debate, and nonstop organizing, millions of people across Connecticut and this nation gave it everything they had. You made calls, had tough conversations, voted, and stayed engaged through every twist and turn.
**I want to pause and simply say _thank you_.**

Elections test the strength of our communities, but they also remind us of the power of everyday people standing up for what they believe in. Regardless of the political map, what endures is our shared commitment to one another, our families, and our neighbors.
Now, as the cycle closes, it is time for a moment of reflection and well-deserved rest. We have collectively given this effort our all, and taking care of ourselves and our communities is how we recharge for whatever lies ahead.
**I am endlessly grateful to serve alongside you and represent the incredible people of Connecticut. Whatever challenges tomorrow brings, we will face them together as we always have. **
Rest up, take care of your loved ones, and know how deeply appreciated you are.
Sincerely,

Dick

name: George Whitesides
subject: Thank you!
body:
Peter, we won!

I’m deeply honored that voters in the Antelope Valley, Santa Clarita Valley, and San Fernando Valley have placed their trust in me again to represent them in Washington. You were a big part of making that happen, and I’m grateful.

In my first term, we brought home federal funding for better roads, safer water, more resources for local law enforcement, and more afterschool programs for kids. We introduced bills to tackle the wildfire crisis, AI safety, and kids’ digital health. And our casework team returned over $15 million in federal benefits that seniors, veterans, and local businesses were owed.

It hasn’t been an easy two years. Three days after I was sworn in, wildfires broke out across Southern California, taking lives and devastating homes and businesses. The administration has enacted policies that have raised prices, incentivized corruption, cut healthcare access, separated families, and forced us into another war. Those decisions have made us less safe and cost the average California family nearly $5,000.

So I’m heading back to DC laser-focused on the affordability crisis and on holding Washington accountable for corruption. When the new Congress is sworn in this January, we need to listen to the American people and get back to pragmatic governing that lets people across this country live their version of the American dream.

That work starts now, and I’m glad to have you with me for it.

Thank you,

George

name: David Crowley (via Battleground Wisconsin)
subject: Thank you
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Democratic Party of Wisconsin, wisdems
body:
| | | | Thank you! Thank you, Wisconsin! Thank you so much. Thank you for believing in me, as I do you. I hope you see that no matter the setbacks life throws at you, if you work hard and be kind, anything is possible. I love you. Last night was for all of you. I always say every day is a good day. Wisconsin, yesterday was a _**very**_ good day. **Because of you, a boy who grew up facing eviction will soon live in the governor’s residence.** Last night, Wisconsin made history. Being your next governor is humbling in its own right. I don’t take any of this lightly, and I know exactly the shoulders I stand on. Thank you for placing your faith in me. That’s ultimately what voting is: a tremendous act of faith. Not faith in one person or party. Faith in the idea that elections matter, that the right leadership can make a difference in people’s lives. And when I say we, I don’t just mean Democrats, I mean we, the public servants of both parties, whom you have elected to work together on your behalf. I ran to be the governor for all of us. And last night, that included everyone who didn’t vote for me. I’ll listen to you. I’ll work for you. And I hope to earn your trust the only way I know how: by showing up and getting results. Let’s be the state where elections make us better, not bitter. Where we stop asking where an idea came from, and instead ask where it will take us. The great Vince Lombardi said, “People who work together will win, whether it be against complex football defenses or the problems of modern society.” People who work together will win. Not Republicans or Democrats. People. My fellow Wisconsinites, we are not a red state or blue state; we are not defined by rural and urban. We are one people, one Wisconsin, and we choose to move forward, together. Thank you! David

clean_body: | | | | Thank you! Thank you, Wisconsin! Thank you so much. Thank you for believing in me, as I do you. I hope you see that no matter the setbacks life throws at you, if you work hard and be kind, anything is possible. I love you. Last night was for all of you. I always say every day is a good day. Wisconsin, yesterday was a very good day. Because of you, a boy who grew up facing eviction will soon live in the governor’s residence. Last night, Wisconsin made history. Being your next governor is humbling in its own right. I don’t take any of this lightly, and I know exactly the shoulders I stand on. Thank you for placing your faith in me. That’s ultimately what voting is: a tremendous act of faith. Not faith in one person or party. Faith in the idea that elections matter, that the right leadership can make a difference in people’s lives. And when I say we, I don’t just mean Democrats, I mean we, the public servants of both parties, whom you have elected to work together on your behalf. I ran to be the governor for all of us. And last night, that included everyone who didn’t vote for me. I’ll listen to you. I’ll work for you. And I hope to earn your trust the only way I know how: by showing up and getting results. Let’s be the state where elections make us better, not bitter. Where we stop asking where an idea came from, and instead ask where it will take us. The great Vince Lombardi said, “People who work together will win, whether it be against complex football defenses or the problems of modern society.” People who work together will win. Not Republicans or Democrats. People. My fellow Wisconsinites, we are not a red state or blue state; we are not defined by rural and urban. We are one people, one Wisconsin, and we choose to move forward, together. Thank you! Peter,

Today we are celebrating historic wins for women candidates around the country.

Every woman who ran this year challenged the idea that men should be making laws about our bodies, our safety, and our futures without us.

I am enormously proud of our candidates, optimistic about what the future holds for women in America – and so very grateful to you, the Her Bold Move friends, supporters, and champions who never gave up on this fight.

Last night, we saw hundreds of women make history. Her Bold Move candidates have flipped Senate and House seats and shattered glass ceilings. In 2027, there will be more women and women of color in the halls of power in America than ever before. Her Bold Move candidates won down ballot races in deep red districts in Alabama, West Virginia, Tennessee, Texas, Missouri and many more. We are thrilled to report that so many of these victories will chip away at GOP male supermajorities in state legislatures that have passed restrictive abortion laws.

That means the sponsors of America’s abortion bans will soon meet their new, fiercely pro-choice, WOMEN colleagues. We could not be more excited.

Her Bold Move’s 2026 Election Tracker can be accessed [**here.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142912574/658462074/-723367959?ref=hbm_header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg4NDk1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjRlMDhkMGNhLTliZDgtZjExMS1iZjViLTAwMGQzYTU0NDQyZSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=FtdAn_SoRIEjT2jdTICD3LMVsJlBQ73XGfhFQvvbXfo=&emci=c1fb2ebc-97d8-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=4e08d0ca-9bd8-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=32015042)

In 2026 alone, Her Bold Move endorsed 137 candidates across 33 states.
* Her Bold Move has an 85% win rate for 2026 so far (a number of races have yet to be called as of this writing)
* 65% of Her Bold Move’s candidates won seats in state legislatures with male supermajorities
* 59% of Her Bold Move’s winning candidates won in states with abortion bans

Women are entitled to power, and we will keep organizing, investing, and pushing until our government is crafting the policies women need and deserve.

Thank you from the bottom of my heart for everything you did this cycle to make these victories possible.

With a decade’s worth of electric optimism,

\- Jordan

Dear Patriot,This letter couldn't wait.That's why Kirk Cameron personally asked me to write you on the post-production budget shortfall for "Iggy and Mr. Kirk." | | | Friends, We won. The people of Florida’s Ninth District have sent me back to Congress, and I want to thank you for making that possible. When MAGA Republicans tried to draw me out of this district, we had a lot of new neighbors to introduce ourselves to. Our staff and volunteers knocked on doors, made calls, and spent hours talking with people who had never seen my name on their ballot before. If you were one of those volunteers, or if you simply told a neighbor why you were voting for me, this victory belongs to you, too. In conversations from Orange County to Glades County, I heard how much harder it’s gotten to fill the grocery cart, pay for gas to get to work, and keep up with health insurance bills. Those conversations will stay with me when I go back to Washington. I’ll work with anyone who’s serious about bringing those costs down, and I’ll keep fighting the corruption that gets in the way. Representing this community for the past decade has been the honor of my life. Thank you for trusting me to keep doing it. Darren
Congressman Darren Soto

I've been quiet here. First-time dad. Newborn during the midterms. Twelve-hour workdays, 3 a.m. changes and feedings. Something had to give, and it was these long posts. But last night is too huge not to say what needs to be said.
Here's the truth: except for 1 in NY-12, every single Congressional District shifted to the Left last night. It didn't matter if that candidate was Establishment D, DSA-backed, AIPAC-funded, centrist, leftist, moderate, progressive, or whatever. Every. single. one. went left.
Take a look at these two maps. The first is the partisan shift from 2020 to 2024 by congressional district. The second is 2024 to 2026
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e706d4d6-4bab-4f7b-9b09-cce581de8e39?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/34ccfb66-ec1e-4e66-b850-0e956eacc9c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
What does this mean?
It's still the damn economy, stupid.
No one went full MAGA in 2024 over trans athletes in sports. Republicans ran that playbook again this year anyway, and it didn't work, especially in a state like South Carolina.
I have said it before, and I will say it again. Voters are inherently selfish creatures. They voted for Donald Trump in 2024, not for these absurd culture war issues that people think, but because they believed the spin from the Right during Biden's presidency that the economy was headed in the wrong direction and Kamala Harris would continue to send us on a downward trajectory.
You can see it in how people are standing up for their neighbors against ICE raids in the most red counties in America. They did not vote for the kind of federal overreach of masked agents coming into people's communities and grabbing people off the street without due process in 2024. That is fundamentally not what they signed up for. They voted with their pocketbooks, and all this sideshow nonsense is distracting from what their main concerns were, which was their livelihoods.
Then came 2026. A President and a Republican Party that promised "no more forever wars in the Middle East" got us into another one. Oil spiked. Gas spiked. Energy bills and grocery bills went through the roof. People were hurting. Businesses started closing down again. And it didn't matter how many false promises of $5000 checks came their way. They weren't buying it.
Going into last night, it was clear something was fundamentally shifting. I said it Monday night. Early vote turnout was historic, and the edge was clearly with Democrats. We didn't know how far voters would swing left. Now we do.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f8d60d01-e072-41a9-b99f-d936ef6b2ad5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And it didn't stop at Congress. For the first time since 2010, Democrats will hold a majority of governorships in the United States. The South is bluer today than it has been in almost half a century. Legislatures flipped in Wisconsin, Minnesota, Michigan, Arizona, Georgia, North Carolina, and Texas.
Y'all, we now have enough state legislatures to overturn the Electoral College and move to a national popular vote. That is where we are in 2026. And it wasn't even on the ballot.
Then there's the money we send overseas. Yes, there is something to be said about military spending and the military aid we give to countries in the Middle East. This issue has been turned into one of culture and religion, but it's much simpler than that. It's a pocketbook issue. Abdul El-Sayed took fire for raising it, and his critics conflated Michiganders' concerns about sending $4 billion to a foreign country's military with an attack on Jewish Americans. That was clearly not the case.
In the 11th hour, even Donald Trump said we would be terminating that $4 billion to Israel in 2027. He saw the writing on the wall when it comes to sending that kind of money somewhere to drop bombs on civilians.
And it's not just Israel. I heard the same thing on doors in 2024 in places like rural Virginia and rural North Carolina about sending money to Ukraine, from Republicans and Democrats alike. People are hurting financially here in America. Why should we be sending trillions of dollars elsewhere when we can't pay for healthcare, shelter, or food for the most vulnerable Americans?
Voters are screaming this at us. You're going to have the Matt Yglesiases and Third Ways of the world saying we need to run to the Center again. And, though I agree with them more, you'll have members of the DSA and the Left saying you need less moderation and more socialist policies to win everywhere. But both are taking the wrong message from the candidates who won last night.
The candidates who won last night won on a message of helping people and getting everyone in our country back to being a place of success, financial stability, and, honestly, a place where people can go back to living their lives without feeling like the sky is going to fall on them every day and wincing every time a news alert comes up.
Americans are hurting financially. They wanted people who are ready, willing, and able to get into office and talk about those kitchen-table issues and not about the random culture war bullshit that they have seen a Republican White House, a Republican House, and a Republican Senate talk about for 2 years without anything to show for it.
The reason Republicans couldn't run on the successes of the past 2 years was that: what successes could Congress point to? They haven't done anything. The only action they have seen has been random executive orders Trump has signed, and they've made minimal, if any, meaningful change in their lives. All the action or inaction that Congress and the White House have taken has either cost them money or made their lives harder. That is the message the voters sent last night.
You could hear it in JD Vance's lackluster final plea, which was, "Just give us 2 more years. We haven't done everything we said we would, but I promise it will get better." Empty promises and inaction.
I want to reiterate something I have said before: When people vote, it almost always comes down to 4 or 5 priorities:
* Putting food on the table
* Paying for housing and keeping the lights on
* Staying healthy without medical debt
* Making sure their kids get a good education
* Getting to a job that pays them well on time

Voters don't always vote with their hearts or even their brains. They vote with their wallets and their pocketbooks. And election after election, the economy tops the list:
* **[2024 Presidential Election:](https://substack.com/redirect/003aced2-e0e6-4153-8c7d-f52c3ef5889a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **the economy was the most critical issue.
* **[2022 Midterms:](https://substack.com/redirect/90ff51d1-e2b1-40f2-82e3-3c27d5bde53e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the economy was the most critical issue.
* **[2020 Presidential Election:](https://substack.com/redirect/c89c50cd-1b1e-435b-8e25-73291518c559?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the economy was the most critical issue.
* **[2018 Midterms:](https://substack.com/redirect/ed848ad3-04bd-4dcb-8b18-d336825f771f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** healthcare was #1, but the economy came right after.
* **[2016 Presidential Election:](https://substack.com/redirect/ce2e3d64-1a5f-4e52-a731-e25c1f9fe5e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **the economy was the most critical issue.

And guess the fuck what? What was the top issue this year?
[That's right. The economy.](https://substack.com/redirect/8deae911-d506-47ff-807b-9c9b92f39f41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
For Democrats, Independents, and Republicans, it was the economy.
It was not a Right versus Left culture war propaganda fight. It was a bottom-up financial, economic struggle. It was who was going to make your life better. Who was going to help you put food on the table, keep your family healthy, keep your kids in school, and get you a job that pays you well on time?
And the candidates who ran on that message: Talarico and Hinojosa in Texas, Sand and Turek in Iowa, Hamilton in Kansas, Brown and Acton in Ohio, Benson and El-Sayed in Michigan. Hell, even Andrews in South Carolina and Forstag in Montana.
Now, it's what Democrats do with this power that matters, and what the message we send to our voters is that makes or breaks us in 2027 and 2028. They have given us the keys. We have to drive them somewhere better. That is going to take bold action and bold stances in Congress, no more strongly worded letters and hemming and hawing about every single decision. People want decisive action. People want boldness.
We have to do something about inflation. We have to do something about healthcare costs. We have to do something about the waste, fraud, and abuse this administration swore DOGE would get rid of. Instead, it gutted much-needed services and went on its own reckless spending spree over unnecessary bullshit.
We have to learn from our mistakes in 2024. And, honestly, from the mistakes of the Trump Administration and Republicans this year. You can't sell something like an economy that smells like shit and tell voters it's gold.
They will sniff that out in a minute when they don't see that as truth in their own lives. If you keep telling people the economy is working but they're hurting at home, they will punish you for it.
And that all starts with the first step after January 6, 2027. Whatever it is must deliver for the American people with the clear message that no matter who you are, where you're from, who you love, how you worship, what your family looks like: you deserve to get ahead and not just get by. Period. It's that simple.
**TL;DR:** Every congressional district but one moved left last night. It didn't matter if the candidate was establishment, DSA, AIPAC-backed, moderate or progressive. Voters didn't go MAGA in 2024 over culture war fights, and they didn't come back in 2026 over them either. They voted their wallets. Another war in the Middle East, spiking gas and grocery prices, and two years of a Republican trifecta with nothing to show for it. The winners last night ran on food, housing, healthcare, schools and good jobs. Voters handed Democrats the keys. Now we have to deliver.

We didn't know how far voters would swing left. Now we do. | | ---|---|--- And it didn't stop at Congress. For the first time since 2010, Democrats will hold a majority of governorships in the United States. The South is bluer today than it has been in almost half a century. Legislatures flipped in Wisconsin, Minnesota, Michigan, Arizona, Georgia, North Carolina, and Texas. Y'all, we now have enough state legislatures to overturn the Electoral College and move to a national popular vote. That is where we are in 2026. And it wasn't even on the ballot. Then there's the money we send overseas. Yes, there is something to be said about military spending and the military aid we give to countries in the Middle East. This issue has been turned into one of culture and religion, but it's much simpler than that. It's a pocketbook issue. Abdul El-Sayed took fire for raising it, and his critics conflated Michiganders' concerns about sending $4 billion to a foreign country's military with an attack on Jewish Americans. That was clearly not the case. In the 11th hour, even Donald Trump said we would be terminating that $4 billion to Israel in 2027. He saw the writing on the wall when it comes to sending that kind of money somewhere to drop bombs on civilians. And it's not just Israel. I heard the same thing on doors in 2024 in places like rural Virginia and rural North Carolina about sending money to Ukraine, from Republicans and Democrats alike. People are hurting financially here in America. Why should we be sending trillions of dollars elsewhere when we can't pay for healthcare, shelter, or food for the most vulnerable Americans? Voters are screaming this at us. You're going to have the Matt Yglesiases and Third Ways of the world saying we need to run to the Center again. And, though I agree with them more, you'll have members of the DSA and the Left saying you need less moderation and more socialist policies to win everywhere. But both are taking the wrong message from the candidates who won last night. The candidates who won last night won on a message of helping people and getting everyone in our country back to being a place of success, financial stability, and, honestly, a place where people can go back to living their lives without feeling like the sky is going to fall on them every day and wincing every time a news alert comes up. Americans are hurting financially. They wanted people who are ready, willing, and able to get into office and talk about those kitchen-table issues and not about the random culture war bullshit that they have seen a Republican White House, a Republican House, and a Republican Senate talk about for 2 years without anything to show for it. The reason Republicans couldn't run on the successes of the past 2 years was that: what successes could Congress point to? They haven't done anything. The only action they have seen has been random executive orders Trump has signed, and they've made minimal, if any, meaningful change in their lives. All the action or inaction that Congress and the White House have taken has either cost them money or made their lives harder. That is the message the voters sent last night. You could hear it in JD Vance's lackluster final plea, which was, "Just give us 2 more years. We haven't done everything we said we would, but I promise it will get better." Empty promises and inaction. I want to reiterate something I have said before: When people vote, it almost always comes down to 4 or 5 priorities: Putting food on the table Paying for housing and keeping the lights on Staying healthy without medical debt Making sure their kids get a good education Getting to a job that pays them well on time Voters don't always vote with their hearts or even their brains. They vote with their wallets and their pocketbooks. And election after election, the economy tops the list: the economy was the most critical issue. the economy was the most critical issue. the economy was the most critical issue. healthcare was #1, but the economy came right after. the economy was the most critical issue. And guess the fuck what? What was the top issue this year? For Democrats, Independents, and Republicans, it was the economy. It was not a Right versus Left culture war propaganda fight. It was a bottom-up financial, economic struggle. It was who was going to make your life better. Who was going to help you put food on the table, keep your family healthy, keep your kids in school, and get you a job that pays you well on time? And the candidates who ran on that message: Talarico and Hinojosa in Texas, Sand and Turek in Iowa, Hamilton in Kansas, Brown and Acton in Ohio, Benson and El-Sayed in Michigan. Hell, even Andrews in South Carolina and Forstag in Montana. Now, it's what Democrats do with this power that matters, and what the message we send to our voters is that makes or breaks us in 2027 and 2028. They have given us the keys. We have to drive them somewhere better. That is going to take bold action and bold stances in Congress, no more strongly worded letters and hemming and hawing about every single decision. People want decisive action. People want boldness. We have to do something about inflation. We have to do something about healthcare costs. We have to do something about the waste, fraud, and abuse this administration swore DOGE would get rid of. Instead, it gutted much-needed services and went on its own reckless spending spree over unnecessary bullshit. We have to learn from our mistakes in 2024. And, honestly, from the mistakes of the Trump Administration and Republicans this year. You can't sell something like an economy that smells like shit and tell voters it's gold. They will sniff that out in a minute when they don't see that as truth in their own lives. If you keep telling people the economy is working but they're hurting at home, they will punish you for it. And that all starts with the first step after January 6, 2027. Whatever it is must deliver for the American people with the clear message that no matter who you are, where you're from, who you love, how you worship, what your family looks like: you deserve to get ahead and not just get by. Period. It's that simple. TL;DR: Every congressional district but one moved left last night. It didn't matter if the candidate was establishment, DSA, AIPAC-backed, moderate or progressive. Voters didn't go MAGA in 2024 over culture war fights, and they didn't come back in 2026 over them either. They voted their wallets. Another war in the Middle East, spiking gas and grocery prices, and two years of a Republican trifecta with nothing to show for it. The winners last night ran on food, housing, healthcare, schools and good jobs. Voters handed Democrats the keys. Now we have to deliver. What is By the Ballot? By the Ballot is a free SubStack that features unapologetic dispatches from the New South 's next generation of Democrats. Commentary on stances, tactics, and news on the Left. We don't claim to know everything or always be right, we just want to be a part of the conversation. While there 's many different ways to power and the Right wants to take over our country by hook or by crook, we want to help Democrats help Americans by making a government for the people by the ballot. It's official:
**The people of South Texas have elected me as their next member of Congress for TX-15.**
And on the same ballot, we chose Gina Hinojosa to be our next Governor and James Talarico to be our next United States Senator.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dd1218e9-8aa4-411b-b7b5-b595099b9a3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This was a historic night, and we couldn't have done it without you.
The other side tried to gerrymander us. To silence us. To deny us a seat at the table. And this community placed hope in me to be their _voice_.
It's what I've done for 30 years.
My music has been the soundtrack of weddings, quinceañeras, and carne asadas. Since we announced this campaign last September, South Texans have let me into their homes, they've joined me at barbecues, and they've come out to our ranch halls.
I've been blessed to tour the country, perform in stadiums of all sizes, and win awards, but what's ahead for me is bigger than any song.
South Texans are trusting me with their future.
**I know the responsibility I 'm taking on. It is an honor, and I'll never forget it.**
Whether you're out here in the Valley or thousands of miles away, whether you voted for me, volunteered, or donated to our campaign, it was your support that put me in this position.
Thank you for placing your trust in me, and know that I'll work every day to live up to it.
I want to thank my family, my wife Mariana and four sons, my father Roberto Pulido, and all the tios, tias, and primos who showed up for me during this wild adventure. I wouldn't be here if not for your sacrifice. I love you.
I want to thank my team, every member of our staff. You crisscrossed this region by my side, worked many late nights, gave up your weekends to build this movement.
**Se vale so ñar, South Texas.** And we proved it.
Now, everybody's going to be looking to us to deliver. We'll have our work cut out for us, but I know we'll be ready.
Thanks again. You'll be hearing from me.
-- Bobby

body:
Last night, Minnesotans made their voices heard loud and clear and delivered the largest midterm defeat of a sitting president in Minnesota history. | | | **[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142913238/658464933/1545412779?amount=10&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzU5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0NjU5OGY0ZS05ZmQ4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wa5eDiBPdDMh3R62fJ3iFfiHJN6hQbdDF0hpBbmdju8=)**
---
Peter, Last night, Minnesotans made their voices heard loud and clear and delivered the largest midterm defeat of a sitting president in Minnesota history. DFLers swept every statewide race, won majorities in both chambers of the state Legislature, kept a U.S. Senate seat blue, and expanded our Congressional delegation. It was an extraordinary night, and it would not have happened without the candidates, organizers, staff, volunteers, donors, and voters who gave this election everything they had. Here’s what we accomplished together:
* **Amy Klobuchar and Ben Schierer won the governor’s race** , electing Amy as the first woman to serve as Governor of Minnesota.

* **Peggy Flanagan won Minnesota’s U.S. Senate race** , becoming the first Native American woman elected to the United States Senate and the first Native American to represent Minnesota in the Senate.

* **Keith Ellison, Steve Simon, and Zack Filipovich won statewide** , completing a DFL sweep of every constitutional office on the ballot.

* **DFLers defended our congressional seats and expanded our delegation** , sending Matt Little to Congress from MN-02 and flipping MN-01 with Jake Johnson.

* **DFLers flipped the Minnesota House and held the Minnesota Senate** , securing DFL control of both chambers.

Donald Trump and his allies spent millions trying to flip Minnesota red and elect candidates who would put his agenda ahead of our state. Minnesotans rejected them, and voters across the country did the same. Here in Minnesota, this election was won person to person. Our DFL campaigns knocked on more than 2.7 million doors, and our volunteers kept working through the final hours of Election Day. Every door, call, conversation, contribution, and shift mattered. Now, it’s time to deliver. Minnesotans expect the people they elected to show up, get results, and solve problems that make their lives better, and I know our DFL leaders are ready to get the job done. **I’m incredibly proud of this team and grateful to be part of it with you. Thank you for everything you did to make these victories possible.** With gratitude, Richard Carlbom
Chair
Minnesota DFL

It was an extraordinary night, and it would not have happened without the candidates, organizers, staff, volunteers, donors, and voters who gave this election everything they had. Here’s what we accomplished together: Amy Klobuchar and Ben Schierer won the governor’s race , electing Amy as the first woman to serve as Governor of Minnesota. Peggy Flanagan won Minnesota’s U.S. Senate race , becoming the first Native American woman elected to the United States Senate and the first Native American to represent Minnesota in the Senate. Keith Ellison, Steve Simon, and Zack Filipovich won statewide , completing a DFL sweep of every constitutional office on the ballot. DFLers defended our congressional seats and expanded our delegation , sending Matt Little to Congress from MN-02 and flipping MN-01 with Jake Johnson. DFLers flipped the Minnesota House and held the Minnesota Senate , securing DFL control of both chambers. Donald Trump and his allies spent millions trying to flip Minnesota red and elect candidates who would put his agenda ahead of our state. Minnesotans rejected them, and voters across the country did the same. Here in Minnesota, this election was won person to person. Our DFL campaigns knocked on more than 2.7 million doors, and our volunteers kept working through the final hours of Election Day. Every door, call, conversation, contribution, and shift mattered. Now, it’s time to deliver. Minnesotans expect the people they elected to show up, get results, and solve problems that make their lives better, and I know our DFL leaders are ready to get the job done. I’m incredibly proud of this team and grateful to be part of it with you. Thank you for everything you did to make these victories possible. With gratitude, Richard Carlbom Chair Minnesota DFL | = = = Monthly supporters are the backbone of all we do. clean_body: Your support powered our victory.| | | | | | Peter, We did it! Thank you for re-electing me to represent Western New York in Congress for another term. I am overwhelmed with humility in the confidence you have placed in me to fight for our community’s future. Whether you’ve been with us from the very beginning or are a new member of Team Kennedy, we could not have achieved this victory without you. Your support — whether it be volunteering, putting up a lawn sign, attending an event, or donating — fueled this campaign, and I could not be more grateful to have you by my side. The past two years were tough, but even on the darkest days, we stood up for our neighbors and fought back. And last night, we proved what we’ve always known: that the power always lies in the people. With historic victories across the country, Democratic majorities in the House and the Senate are ready to restore access to healthcare, hold the crooks accountable, and deliver for working families. The work starts now. I’m heading back to Congress next week to continue holding this administration to account and fight for a brighter future for every Western New Yorker and American, and I’m so proud to have you in this fight with me. | | | Sincerely, Tim | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Paid for by Kennedy for Congress Kennedy for Congress P.O. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142913303/658465126/1325061702?refcode=WUEFEW24_20261104_JMonEDay_ALL&sourceid=1060598&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2OTU2ZWQ0MS05ZmQ4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=f0EDkuuRCQDakM5Uw7rRHpNL094hrDry0p5IkqRi5Jo=) Peter, Two years ago, in the aftermath of the 2024 election, we made a promise: **We would do everything in our power to take back power.** Last night, we delivered. Democrats took back the U.S. House. Democrats took back the U.S. Senate. Democratic pro-choice women shattered records, flipped seats once considered unwinnable, and transformed the political landscape across the country. **But none of this was inevitable. And it certainly wasn't inevitable that women would be at the center of it.** Throughout this election cycle, we heard the same old excuses. That electing women would be nice, but the stakes were too high. That certain districts were too competitive. That we couldn't afford to take the risk. At every turn, EMILYs List refused to accept those excuses. **Because we've said it from the very beginning: Supporting Democratic pro-choice women isn't just the right thing to do. It's smart electoral strategy.** And last night, we proved it:
* **Gina Hinojosa** defeated Greg Abbott to become the first Democratic governor of Texas in more than 30 years, as well as the state's first Latina governor.
* **Keisha Lance Bottoms** flipped Georgia's governor's office, becoming the first Black woman governor in American history and delivering another historic Democratic victory in the South.
* **Dr. Amy Acton** defeated Vivek Ramaswamy to become the first woman to be elected governor in Ohio.
* **Dr. Annie Andrews** flipped South Carolina's U.S. Senate seat; the first Democrat to do so in 28 years.
* **Kristina Knickerbocker** flipped Ohio's 10th Congressional District, winning a race that few believed Democrats could win.

And those are just a handful of the extraordinary victories we helped deliver. **As I write this, 216 EMILYs List candidates have won their races.** More than 110 Democratic women are slated to serve in the U.S. House. We've helped secure eight Democratic governing majorities in key states and break Republican control in four states. These victories didn't happen by accident. They happened because we recruited extraordinary women, stood behind them when others doubted their chances, invested in their campaigns, and refused to let them be sidelined in the fight for our country's future. And they happened because of supporters like you. Through every challenge, every hard-fought race, and every moment when the odds seemed stacked against us, you stood with EMILYs List and the extraordinary women we helped elect. We couldn't have done this without you. Thank you. Together, we didn't just help Democrats take back power. We made sure women were at the center of it. And now, those women will use that power to defend our freedoms, protect reproductive rights, hold the Trump administration accountable, and chart a different course for this country. **This is what EMILYs List was built to do. And it certainly wasn't inevitable that women would be at the center of it. Throughout this election cycle, we heard the same old excuses. That electing women would be nice, but the stakes were too high. That certain districts were too competitive. That we couldn't afford to take the risk. At every turn, EMILYs List refused to accept those excuses. Because we've said it from the very beginning: Supporting Democratic pro-choice women isn't just the right thing to do. It's smart electoral strategy. And last night, we proved it: Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott to become the first Democratic governor of Texas in more than 30 years, as well as the state's first Latina governor. Keisha Lance Bottoms flipped Georgia's governor's office, becoming the first Black woman governor in American history and delivering another historic Democratic victory in the South. Dr. Amy Acton defeated Vivek Ramaswamy to become the first woman to be elected governor in Ohio. Dr. Annie Andrews flipped South Carolina's U.S. Senate seat; the first Democrat to do so in 28 years. Kristina Knickerbocker flipped Ohio's 10th Congressional District, winning a race that few believed Democrats could win. And those are just a handful of the extraordinary victories we helped deliver. As I write this, 216 EMILYs List candidates have won their races. More than 110 Democratic women are slated to serve in the U.S. House. We've helped secure eight Democratic governing majorities in key states and break Republican control in four states. These victories didn't happen by accident. They happened because we recruited extraordinary women, stood behind them when others doubted their chances, invested in their campaigns, and refused to let them be sidelined in the fight for our country's future. And they happened because of supporters like you. Through every challenge, every hard-fought race, and every moment when the odds seemed stacked against us, you stood with EMILYs List and the extraordinary women we helped elect. We couldn't have done this without you. Thank you. Together, we didn't just help Democrats take back power. We made sure women were at the center of it. And now, those women will use that power to defend our freedoms, protect reproductive rights, hold the Trump administration accountable, and chart a different course for this country. This is what EMILYs List was built to do. And we're just getting started. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | =** Thank you, Jessica Mackler (she/her/hers) President, EMILYs List | = | | | | | ---|---|---|---|--- Thank you for being a supporter of EMILYs List. clean_body: Fellow Patriot, We face powerful foes today who are willing to do anything to dominate America, even if it means destroying democracy. The Left's so-called principles are utterly incompatible with those that are the bedrock of our constitutional republic. They're incompatible with individual liberty and free will. They're incompatible with the Judeo-Christian belief system under which this nation was founded. At a time when the very values that make America great are under attack, we must continue to stand strong. We must make sure our fellow citizens understand the seriousness of this situation. I'll never stop defending America, our Constitution, our free market economy, and our Judeo-Christian traditions. And I'll never stop calling out the leftists who want to tear our country down. I know you won't either! I do a lot of things. But one of the most important things I do is work with my colleagues at Landmark Legal Foundation. Landmark Legal Foundation is on a mission. They 're here to protect liberty, property rights, constitutionalism . . . in other words, what you read in the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution. And now, I'd love you to stand with me in supporting this outstanding organization. The Left aren't saviors of democracy.They 're Marxists. And what they're doing is destroying the country. They fight desperately to undermine our election processes and, if elections go against them, they use the courts to obstruct the policies We the People voted for. They persecute their opponents, like when the Biden In justice Department waged relentless lawfare against Trump and his allies. Leftists focus so much energy on the justice system - to control it, to contort it, to use it to promote their insanely radical agenda. Again and again, they turn to rogue left-wing judges to usurp the Constitution and undermine America's founding principles. We must not be silent while these leftists destroy our republic from within. That 's why it's so great to have Landmark Legal Foundation take them on! I love these guys. I've been part of the Landmark family for over three decades . . . as president for 20 years, then Chairman of the Board, and now Chairman Emeritus. These briefs present the strongest possible argument for the constitutional position and help convince judges to do the right thing. In 2024, Landmark made a historic winning argument that special prosecutor Jack Smith lacked the legal authority to target Donald Trump in the classified documents probe. The judge in the case echoed Landmark's arguments in her decision and delivered a huge win over the Left 's lawfare. Landmark also fights to defend free, fair elections. For example, Landmark filed a supportive brief in another key election integrity case. With Bost v. Illinois Board of Elections , they're helping challenge unfair vote-by-mail procedures. Here, Illinois Congressman Mike Bost sued the Illinois Board of Elections over their practice of counting mail-in ballots received after Election Day. Such counting delays results and opens the door for abuse. When the Supreme Court agreed, it marked a major victory for free, fair elections. But this is not the last fight! This isn't political . . . it 's about the Constitution! My Landmark friends are on the frontlines of the battle to preserve our country. They're a vital part of the conservative, constitutionalist force fighting for our country today. Your support will help Landmark Legal Foundation live up to its motto of " Defending Liberty, Fighting Tyranny." Thank you in advance for actively joining the fight! God Bless, Mark Levin Chairman Emeritus Landmark Legal Foundation Landmark Legal Foundation is a 501(c)(3) Not For Profit Organization. All donations are tax-deductible.

Throughout this campaign, I've called on Oregonians and Americans to 'Save our Republic.'
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142913371/658465513/150430950?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTMyNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1YTA0MDNkMC1hMGQ4LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=PNurkPVioAlEQYXrTAawhFwGIsZeZ_9oLZytoK4kovg=&emci=4c6c4a33-91d8-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=5a0403d0-a0d8-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=7731215)

| | Yesterday, Democrats created a massive big blue _TSUNAMI_ , retook the Democratic House and Senate Majorities, and stood together to stop Trump's authoritarian assault on our nation. His goal has been to pursue government by and for the rich and powerful, while caring little about the suffering of ordinary families. It's a 'billionaires win, families lose' strategy. That is not what our nation needs. Democrats stand for a government and nation in which families thrive, and the rich and powerful pay their fair share. I cannot say enough about the support of my family as we weighed running for a fourth term in the Senate. Mary and I wrestled with that question, and decided that at this moment, with Trump launching the greatest attack on our constitutional republic since the Civil War, **_we had to be in the fight._** She and our children have stood with me time and time again, despite the trials and tribulations of serving in the public spotlight. I thank Oregonians across our state for being with me as I fight for a better future. **For years, I've worked to lift up the voices of ordinary Americans and take on the powerful interests that rig our system, and I thank the Oregon voters for sending me back to the U.S. Senate to fight on behalf of all Oregonians.** The future of our country in this century depends on investing in our families and infrastructure. **We must invest in the four foundations for a family to thrive: health care, affordable housing, quality education, and good-paying jobs.** Investments in families will reap rewards many times over for the generations to come. And economic success and security will not come from having the most troops, the most tanks, or the most ships. It will come from investments in research, tech, and a transportation system that supports efficient manufacturing. If we don't make things in America, we won't have a middle class in America. **This is a dark and dangerous time for our democracy, but as we see results across the nation, I am optimistic about the future.** I'm optimistic because Americans have weighed in against Trump's strongman state. Against his grift and corruption; against his vote rigging and manipulation; against his disregard of our constitutional separation of powers; against his war and his secret police; and most of all, against his strategy of enriching the richest among us while pressing families against the wall. Throughout this campaign, I've called on Oregonians and Americans to 'Save our Republic.' **Yesterday, they delivered.** Onward! _Jeff_ | Express Donate: If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution to Jeff Merkley instantly:

name: Mike Lawler
subject: Thank you
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Lawler for Congress, Inc
body:
| | | | [ ](https://links.email.lawlerforcongress.com/els/v4/tgpz2w-yrchk1_eandf8m/YxOC2eSW5FhBvHyJkj9kFTdn0vM9zqe7Utur_W48H0xYemo6vezPxRxGC5a0D7R2afkX/Eh1RhXZan_gmAXcmxGawH7YSKXwXbpwcrmByfpUTo86dFkFgT9h34L8Y2Jtk9WUG8CUmS5aXxrSw3VqmGDGy3lXVZiska20OSgS2Hw9qEET4SoVZoNBZKBhagMyb)

| | Peter, Last night, the voters of New York’s 17th Congressional District made their choice, and I respect it. Before anything else, I want to thank my wife Doina. She has been by my side through every long day, every late night, every tough call this job has asked of us, and she has carried more of the weight than anyone outside our home will ever know. I want to thank my daughters, who are the reason I do all of this in the first place. I want to thank my parents, who raised me to believe that public service is a privilege, not a job. I want to thank my extended family, friends, and everyone who stood with us through four years of some of the hardest and most rewarding work of my life. And I want to thank the Team Lawler staff. To the people of the Hudson Valley, I want to say this. It has been the honor of my life to represent you in Congress. Four years ago, you took a chance on a kid from Rockland County. You trusted me to go to Washington and fight for Rockland, Westchester, Putnam, and Dutchess. I hope that over these two terms I have earned that trust.
* We fought President Trump and Washington Republicans and quadrupled the SALT deduction from $10,000 to $40,000, saving the average Hudson Valley family thousands of dollars every year.
* We passed No Tax on Tips, putting more money in the pockets of waiters, waitresses, bartenders, and working families across the district.
* We delivered over $3 billion in healthcare funding for New York and fixed the MCO tax that was threatening our hospitals.
* We secured full funding for the World Trade Center Health Program for the first responders and survivors who still live with what they saw on September 11.
* We saved the West Nyack Social Security office.
* We protected Social Security and Medicare from cuts.
* We introduced the IVF Access and Affordability Act, the Improving Housing Access Act, the VETRA Act, and the HEAL Act.
* We were ranked one of the most bipartisan members of Congress, because getting things done for Hudson Valley families mattered more than scoring points for a party.

Those are not my victories. Those are yours. Every one of them happened because the people of this district sent someone to Washington who was willing to work with anyone, Republican or Democrat, who was serious about solving problems.To the volunteers who knocked on hundreds of thousands of doors and made even more calls this year, thank you. To the donors who sacrificed to fund this campaign, thank you. To the families who put a sign in their yard, who talked to a neighbor, who drove someone to the polls, thank you. You are the reason this race was close in a district that no Republican was supposed to be able to hold. I congratulate my opponent, Cait Conley, on her victory and wish her well in the 120th Congress. Public service is not easy, and I will do everything in my power to ensure a smooth transition. I hope she will serve the Hudson Valley the way the Hudson Valley deserves to be served. As for me and my family, we are going to take some time to be together, to rest, and to figure out what comes next. Whatever it is, I will spend the rest of my life grateful to the people of New York’s 17th District for giving me the chance to serve. God bless you. God bless the Hudson Valley. And God bless the United States of America. Mike Lawler

body:
#
We just took back Texas.
We proved that all the money in the world is no match for the people of Texas.
We showed that a politics of division is no match for a politics of love.
And we sent a message to every billionaire mega-donor, every trillionaire mega-donor, every corrupt defender of this broken political system: In this state, in this country, power belongs to the people.
This is a win the size of Texas.
And we now have a mandate the size of Texas.
This election was about chasing a vision of what our state can be: Texas public schools that are the envy of the nation, a Texas economy that is second to none, and Texas families that are stronger and healthier than they’ve ever been before. It won’t happen overnight, but a giant state deserves giant dreams.
We know how to get there.
* We must get Big Money out of our politics so no billionaire — or trillionaire — can buy an election.
* We must unrig this economic system that only benefits the top 1%.
* We must pass universal healthcare so no one goes bankrupt just because they get sick.
* We must invest in our teachers and our students so every underdog has a fighting chance.
* We must end these corrupt forever wars that are driving up prices and killing our brave men and women in uniform.

And we must heal the deep, spiritual corruption at the root of all of these crises. We must bridge the divides between us and repair the ties that bind us.
We forged a new kind of politics here in the Lone Star state — an answer to this decade of division.
We showed that when working people come together, across every dividing line, we can do extraordinary things.
We won this race because people are desperate for change. Now change is on the way.
That old politics is dying, and a new politics is being born — through each of us. Through every underdog. Through every David against every Goliath. Through every Texan who believed in our state and believed in this movement.
Now the real work begins.
James

Peter –

Yesterday, Americans sent a message loud and clear.

Across the country, voters turned out in historic numbers. Democrats won major statewide victories, flipped both chambers of Congress, and delivered down-ballot results that will shape our country for years to come.

And there were some particularly historic wins for Democratic attorneys general.

In Texas, Nathan Johnson became the first Democrat elected attorney general in more than 30 years. In Georgia, my friend Tanya Miller handily won her race, helping Democrats sweep the state's top statewide offices after a generation of Republican control. And in Rhode Island, Kim Ahern made history as the state's first Democratic woman elected attorney general. All told, there will be at least five new states with Democratic AGs.

These victories are worth celebrating. But yesterday also reminded us why protecting the right to vote matters so much.

Over the past year, my fellow attorneys general and I have prepared for unprecedented threats to our elections. We challenged unlawful federal actions in court, worked to safeguard election officials, and developed plans to protect voters' rights against potential interference.

That preparation was essential. But voters participated in such historic numbers that many of the worst-case scenarios we had anticipated never materialized. Americans were able to exercise their right to vote and make their voices heard.

The New York Times Editorial Board and Slate have both recognized the important role state attorneys general have played in safeguarding our elections. I am proud of the work we have done.

Our responsibility does not end with Election Day. We must remain committed to upholding the rule of law, protecting fundamental rights, and ensuring every eligible American has the opportunity to participate in our democracy.

Thank you for being part of this fight. It is a great day!

– Nick Brown

* * *
**By Brian Patterson**
As it rains outside my window, it feels as if a deluge is upon us. With the midterms closed and a night to clear one's head, the outcome should have been easier to predict. Nearly every midterm election turns against the party in power. The odious candidates tend to lose, even with huge support from the primary voters. However, a full diagnosis is an ugly one for Trump and the GOP, as well as the future of the Republican Party.
The candidate is still human, and too much human error means no forgiveness on the ballot. Vivek Ramaswamy went on the record insulting rural Americans in December of 2025, and never once apologized for his comments. Voters felt as if he was forced upon them. They responded by turning the red state of Ohio blue.
Darline Graham, sister to Lindsey Graham, was supposed to be a placeholder. She instead decided to run for a full term without real credentials, and voters who would normally vote GOP decided to stay home in South Carolina.
In Georgia, Mike Collins surrounded himself with bad staffers who took too many liberties with social media, causing many news outlets to paint Collins himself as a racist. In the New South, this is a dealbreaker. Even popular YouTuber Brandon Herrera lost his bid despite a fantastic primary run, all thanks to his off hand comments that garnered some laughs, but turned off moderate voters.
That's just the personality side. The deluge rains run far deeper. The Iran War was triggering to the American people, who finally saw refuge from Biden's gas prices, only to watch those prices rise along with the war. It doesn't matter that the war is merely a missile exchange. No one cares about the costs of a nuclear Iran, and no one cares about the impotent allies of the Arab states. The American people care about their wallets, and another war in the Middle East gave flashbacks to the failures in Iraq and Afghanistan.
The biggest reason for the midterm deluge is both seen and unseen: the strength of the mainstream media. After losing much of their influence in the 2024 election, the old newspapers, cable news, and Big 3 outlets of ABC, CBS, and NBC, the mainstream media held its breath to see what came next.
* * *
# **We will not give up hope, and neither should you**
Tuesday was a wake up call to all American patriots...
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d95af197-721b-4ac1-af36-0a0a3a1d71e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The battle ahead will surely be hard and up-hill. But think of the brave Americans who stormed the beaches of Normandy, or the men who fought and bled at Shiloh and Lexington.
They had a dream for America they were willing to die for. We cannot let their sacrifice be in vain.
We must fight for our nation with every thing we have within us, even on the darkest days, as our ancestors did.
**PolitiBrawl will hold our place in line on the battleground for information and news.**
We appreciate your readership and support.

Do not give up hope. Tomorrow is a brighter day.
* * *
_**(Piece continues):**_
When the podcast sphere spun out of orbit the moment of Charlie Kirk's assassination, the media decided to push its advantage. Instead of reporting the deportation numbers and lower crime rates that came with it, we saw crying children whose parents were correctly incarcerated. Instead of Lake Riley memorials, we saw Renee Good and Alex Pretti footage (which in both cases exonerated the officers). Headlines once again ruled the airwaves, and the podcast sphere has not recovered. Old media has regained its former strength, and fought back with a vengeance against MAGA.
These factors overwhelmed the average voter. The promises looked and felt empty from the Trump Administration, the gas prices went back up, the media spun everything negative, and the candidates felt forced or worse, hollow. The Trump agenda now seems listless as the Democrats went from catatonic to meteoric.
The deluge, unfortunately, has only begun. Expect the carnival of politics to crank up before 2028, the year that determines the census and a potential death blow to either of the Democrat or Republican parties. I'm no meteorologist, but it seems as if the deluge has just begun.

The biggest reason for the midterm deluge is both seen and unseen: the strength of the mainstream media... | | | Nov 4 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Help us take back this country! Support PolitiBrawl by becoming a paid subscriber today: By Brian Patterson As it rains outside my window, it feels as if a deluge is upon us. With the midterms closed and a night to clear one's head, the outcome should have been easier to predict. Nearly every midterm election turns against the party in power. The odious candidates tend to lose, even with huge support from the primary voters. However, a full diagnosis is an ugly one for Trump and the GOP, as well as the future of the Republican Party. The candidate is still human, and too much human error means no forgiveness on the ballot. Vivek Ramaswamy went on the record insulting rural Americans in December of 2025, and never once apologized for his comments. Voters felt as if he was forced upon them. They responded by turning the red state of Ohio blue. Darline Graham, sister to Lindsey Graham, was supposed to be a placeholder. She instead decided to run for a full term without real credentials, and voters who would normally vote GOP decided to stay home in South Carolina. In Georgia, Mike Collins surrounded himself with bad staffers who took too many liberties with social media, causing many news outlets to paint Collins himself as a racist. In the New South, this is a dealbreaker. Even popular YouTuber Brandon Herrera lost his bid despite a fantastic primary run, all thanks to his off hand comments that garnered some laughs, but turned off moderate voters. That's just the personality side. The deluge rains run far deeper. The Iran War was triggering to the American people, who finally saw refuge from Biden's gas prices, only to watch those prices rise along with the war. It doesn't matter that the war is merely a missile exchange. No one cares about the costs of a nuclear Iran, and no one cares about the impotent allies of the Arab states. The American people care about their wallets, and another war in the Middle East gave flashbacks to the failures in Iraq and Afghanistan. The biggest reason for the midterm deluge is both seen and unseen: the strength of the mainstream media. After losing much of their influence in the 2024 election, the old newspapers, cable news, and Big 3 outlets of ABC, CBS, and NBC, the mainstream media held its breath to see what came next. We will not give up hope, and neither should you Tuesday was a wake up call to all American patriots... | | ---|---|--- The battle ahead will surely be hard and up-hill. But think of the brave Americans who stormed the beaches of Normandy, or the men who fought and bled at Shiloh and Lexington. They had a dream for America they were willing to die for. We cannot let their sacrifice be in vain. We must fight for our nation with every thing we have within us, even on the darkest days, as our ancestors did. PolitiBrawl will hold our place in line on the battleground for information and news. We appreciate your readership and support. Do not give up hope. Tomorrow is a brighter day. (Piece continues): When the podcast sphere spun out of orbit the moment of Charlie Kirk's assassination, the media decided to push its advantage. Instead of reporting the deportation numbers and lower crime rates that came with it, we saw crying children whose parents were correctly incarcerated. Instead of Lake Riley memorials, we saw Renee Good and Alex Pretti footage (which in both cases exonerated the officers). Headlines once again ruled the airwaves, and the podcast sphere has not recovered. Old media has regained its former strength, and fought back with a vengeance against MAGA. These factors overwhelmed the average voter. The promises looked and felt empty from the Trump Administration, the gas prices went back up, the media spun everything negative, and the candidates felt forced or worse, hollow. The Trump agenda now seems listless as the Democrats went from catatonic to meteoric. The deluge, unfortunately, has only begun. Expect the carnival of politics to crank up before 2028, the year that determines the census and a potential death blow to either of the Democrat or Republican parties. I'm no meteorologist, but it seems as if the deluge has just begun. | | POLL Did you vote in the midterms? | ? ? * You're currently a free subscriber to . Peter,

Words cannot express how grateful I am for your support, your dedication, and your trust.

I am honored that the voters of Rhode Island’s 2nd Congressional District have placed their trust and confidence in me to serve another term in the United States House of Representatives.

Our country is facing many challenges, and working people are struggling. I am focused on making life better for Rhode Islanders, and am committed to my fight in Congress to lower costs, root out corruption in Washington, make health care more affordable, and end the war in Iran.

This victory belongs to every volunteer who knocked doors, every supporter who made calls and sent texts, every person who chipped in what they could, and every voter who made their voice heard at the ballot box.

Throughout this campaign, I spoke about what Rhode Island stands for: hard work, integrity, looking out for our neighbors, and making sure our government works for everyday people, not billionaires and big corporations

I am deeply honored and humbled to continue representing the people of Rhode Island’s 2nd District.

From the bottom of my heart, thank you for standing with me.

With gratitude,

— Seth
