name: Jenny Beth Martin, Tea Party Patriots Action
subject: Patriot, I want to hear from you about last night
body:
Thank you for everything you did this season. Here is what comes next.
[](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org/1/010001a1a8db82c2-518c65fa-d6ea-4138-aa27-ca22e13c0404-000000/mHfBfDPGqM_fHpIXv_M8jijPBa0OcX1HI5Q97Sx_ESo=452)Patriot–Tuesday night was a hard night. We took real losses.Before we dive in, there is a brief survey at the end of this email, and I really need your feedback.Now, Democrats won the House. They won the Senate, flipping at least seven seats held by Republicans, including Maine, North Carolina, and Texas. They won the governorships of Texas, Georgia, and Ohio, and for the first time in sixteen years Democrats will hold more governorships than Republicans. They took state legislative chambers in Michigan, Minnesota, Texas, Georgia, and Wisconsin.Speaker Mike Johnson announced Wednesday that he will not run to lead House Republicans in the next Congress.There is no gentler way to put it. Republicans and conservatives had a very bad night, and the left is celebrating.Before anything else, I want to thank you.You texted voters you didn’t know. You went through the contacts in your phone and helped your friends make a plan to vote. Some of you trained as poll workers and poll watchers and spent Election Day at the polls. Many of you did all of it while working a job and raising a family.I saw all of that work, and I am grateful for every minute of it.Midterm elections are almost always hard on the President's party, and this one held true to that. That history does not make this week any easier.So here is my first recommendation, and it is the same one I gave on The Jenny Beth Show today. Take a deep breath. Turn off the news and social media for a day or two. Spend time with your family and your friends, the people who are the reason you work so hard for this country.Then come back to the principles that brought you into this fight: the Declaration of Independence, the Constitution, and the Bill of Rights. Our rights come from our Creator. That is what you and I are working to conserve: personal freedom, economic freedom, and a debt-free future for America.We have been here before.In November 2008, President Obama won, and Democrats held the House and the Senate. It felt like the whole country had swept past us. A handful of conservatives did not quit. We took a breath, we got on the phone with each other, and we asked what we could learn.In February 2009, the day after Rick Santelli called for a tea party on live television, about three dozen of us got on a conference call. One week later, 48 tea parties were held across the country, with about 35,000 people. By Tax Day, there were more than 850, with about 1.2 million people. In 2010, voters sent 63 more Republicans to the House.We were ready because we did the work when nobody was watching.The other side is not resting either. Within hours of the polls closing, the Democratic Socialists of America posted: "Tomorrow, we continue organizing, fighting, and winning for the working class." At least seven members they endorsed will now sit in the House.The work in Washington does not stop. Congress returns Monday for the final weeks of this session, and government funding runs out December 11th. The new Congress is sworn in January 3rd. I expect the new Democratic majorities to open investigations and possibly impeachment hearings, and we will be watching every one of them.In October 1941, with Britain in the darkest years of the Second World War, Winston Churchill stood before the students of his old school, Harrow School, and told them: "Never give in, never give in, never, never, never, never."That is my message to you this week.**Here is what I am asking you to do:** Over the next few weeks, Tea Party Patriots Action is going back through everything we did this season: what worked, what we need to improve, and what we should drop. I want your answer in that review.[_**Please fill out this survey and tell me what you’re thinking,**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fdocs.google.com%2Fforms%2Fd%2Fe%2F1FAIpQLSeBmlcLhgHkm5PNT-SlI3M8co5jybGnsEvhlXXGtLHMmbCVww%2Fviewform/1/010001a1a8db82c2-518c65fa-d6ea-4138-aa27-ca22e13c0404-000000/kayZGS4shCWMwuXplN2D1KdAgk-R7_jrsB6VVZNCtB4=452)**what we did well, and what we could have done better, and how we should move forward. As a grassroots-led organization, your input is the most important element as we assess what happened and plan for the future.**[ COMPLETE MY SURVEY](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fdocs.google.com%2Fforms%2Fd%2Fe%2F1FAIpQLSeBmlcLhgHkm5PNT-SlI3M8co5jybGnsEvhlXXGtLHMmbCVww%2Fviewform/2/010001a1a8db82c2-518c65fa-d6ea-4138-aa27-ca22e13c0404-000000/rFVVF4_MNH-0VSIwYJunlSukMJCeQSlTwajJIGfjaf8=452)When the Constitutional Convention ended in 1787, Benjamin Franklin is said to have been asked what kind of government the delegates had created. _"A republic,"_ he answered, _"if you can keep it."_ Keeping it was never going to be the work of one night. America is bigger than any single election and bigger than any one politician. Her strength comes from our founding principles and from our fellow Americans, and both were still here this morning.Standing with you,Jenny Beth Martin

Peter, it’s honestly getting hard to keep track of all this winning. But hey, let’s give it a shot. . To start, as you probably heard, Democrats won back both chambers of Congress — a massive outcome and a resounding rejection of the Republicans’ unprecedented power grab. That’s just the beginning. Below is an incomplete list of some of the most impactful victories we won for democracy last night. (Fair warning: This list might leave you with a smile that won’t go away.)
* In Wisconsin, Democrats won a trifecta — holding the governor’s seat by electing David Crowley and flipping both the state assembly and the state senate.
* We also won a trifecta in Pennsylvania — with Gov. Josh Shapiro getting re-elected and Democrats flipping the state senate.
* Democrats appear to have pulled off a trifecta in Arizona, too, which would be the first time that’s happened in six decades — re-electing Katie Hobbs as governor and flipping both the state senate and state house.
* In Michigan, Democrats flipped the state house and retained the governor’s seat to secure yet another trifecta! We also re-elected two critical state supreme court justices.
* In Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms not only won the governorship (becoming the first Black woman ever elected governor in any U.S. state), but we also won the Georgia House for the first time in over two decades.
* Gina Hinosoja won a historic victory in the Texas governor’s race — and it also appears we might win the Texas House majority for the first time since 2002.
* Amy Acton became the first Democrat in 20 years to win the Ohio governor’s seat. We won both Ohio Supreme Court races and flipped the secretary of state. And oh yeah, we broke a Republican supermajority in the state house.
* Don’t forget Minnesota, where the Democratic-Farmer-Labor (DFL) Party flipped the state house to secure another Dem trifecta.
* In North Carolina, Supreme Court Justice Anita Earls won re-election, and the state house saw a dramatic shift as Democrats flipped the chamber after Republicans were just one seat shy of a supermajority.
* Even though we fell short in the Florida governor’s race, we did enough to break a Republican supermajority in the state house.
* Voters in Missouri repealed the state’s Republican gerrymander — and Democrats broke supermajorities in both the state house and state senate.
* Democrats won legislative supermajorities in the Delaware House, the New Hampshire House, New Mexico House, and New York Senate.
* We also broke Republican legislative supermajorities in the Indiana House, Iowa House, Kansas House, and the South Carolina House.
* Colorado saw Democrats hold the governorship with Phil Weiser, and we also appear to have defeated a ballot measure that would prevent the state from responding to the Republican redistricting crisis.
* And in Maryland, voters approved a ballot measure that will allow the state to weigh in on how maps are drawn in response to the Republican redistricting crisis.

Phew. Just look at that list. It’s jaw-dropping. Six Democratic trifectas won in one night! Historic gubernatorial victories! Republican gerrymandering failing! Democrats just pulled off a nationwide and thorough triumph. It’s the single largest shift in the balance of statehouse power since the Republicans crushed the midterms in 2010. And it’s the most chambers flipped by Democrats since 1982. And look, that’s just what we know so far. Votes are still being counted across the country. We are still tracking how many of the 300+ Democracy Defenders we endorsed won their races last night. Nights like that are proof that the work we do matters. Democracy is undeniably stronger today than it was just 24 hours ago. Thank you for the part you played in making that possible. The National Democratic Redistricting Committee P.S. Let’s all gather our strength, because there’s a lot more work to do. And we just proved that when this movement fights back for democracy, we win. clean_body: Fair warning: This email might leave you with a smile that won’t go away. | Peter, it’s honestly getting hard to keep track of all this winning. But hey, let’s give it a shot. . To start, as you probably heard, Democrats won back both chambers of Congress — a massive outcome and a resounding rejection of the Republicans’ unprecedented power grab. That’s just the beginning. Below is an incomplete list of some of the most impactful victories we won for democracy last night. (Fair warning: This list might leave you with a smile that won’t go away.) In Wisconsin, Democrats won a trifecta — holding the governor’s seat by electing David Crowley and flipping both the state assembly and the state senate. We also won a trifecta in Pennsylvania — with Gov. Josh Shapiro getting re-elected and Democrats flipping the state senate. Democrats appear to have pulled off a trifecta in Arizona, too, which would be the first time that’s happened in six decades — re-electing Katie Hobbs as governor and flipping both the state senate and state house. In Michigan, Democrats flipped the state house and retained the governor’s seat to secure yet another trifecta! We also re-elected two critical state supreme court justices. In Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms not only won the governorship (becoming the first Black woman ever elected governor in any U.S. state), but we also won the Georgia House for the first time in over two decades. Gina Hinosoja won a historic victory in the Texas governor’s race — and it also appears we might win the Texas House majority for the first time since 2002. Amy Acton became the first Democrat in 20 years to win the Ohio governor’s seat. We won both Ohio Supreme Court races and flipped the secretary of state. And oh yeah, we broke a Republican supermajority in the state house. Don’t forget Minnesota, where the Democratic-Farmer-Labor (DFL) Party flipped the state house to secure another Dem trifecta. In North Carolina, Supreme Court Justice Anita Earls won re-election, and the state house saw a dramatic shift as Democrats flipped the chamber after Republicans were just one seat shy of a supermajority. Even though we fell short in the Florida governor’s race, we did enough to break a Republican supermajority in the state house. Voters in Missouri repealed the state’s Republican gerrymander — and Democrats broke supermajorities in both the state house and state senate. Democrats won legislative supermajorities in the Delaware House, the New Hampshire House, New Mexico House, and New York Senate. We also broke Republican legislative supermajorities in the Indiana House, Iowa House, Kansas House, and the South Carolina House. Colorado saw Democrats hold the governorship with Phil Weiser, and we also appear to have defeated a ballot measure that would prevent the state from responding to the Republican redistricting crisis. And in Maryland, voters approved a ballot measure that will allow the state to weigh in on how maps are drawn in response to the Republican redistricting crisis. Phew. Just look at that list. It’s jaw-dropping. Six Democratic trifectas won in one night! Historic gubernatorial victories! Republican gerrymandering failing! Democrats just pulled off a nationwide and thorough triumph. It’s the single largest shift in the balance of statehouse power since the Republicans crushed the midterms in 2010. And it’s the most chambers flipped by Democrats since 1982. And look, that’s just what we know so far. Votes are still being counted across the country. We are still tracking how many of the 300+ Democracy Defenders we endorsed won their races last night. Nights like that are proof that the work we do matters. Democracy is undeniably stronger today than it was just 24 hours ago. Thank you for the part you played in making that possible. The National Democratic Redistricting Committee P.S. Let’s all gather our strength, because there’s a lot more work to do. And we just proved that when this movement fights back for democracy, we win. body:
This letter couldn't wait.

[Iggy and Mr. Kirk]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Dear Patriot,

This letter couldn't wait.

That's why Kirk Cameron personally asked me to write you on the
post-production budget shortfall for "Iggy and Mr. Kirk." He wanted to
make sure you heard about this urgent situation as soon as possible.

AND AFTER YOU HEAR WHAT'S GOING ON, I HOPE YOU'LL SUPPORT BRAVE FOR
GOOD.

WE ARE FACING A SERIOUS BUDGET SHORTFALL OF $48,523.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

But before I go into more detail, let me tell you a little about our
mission to help parents instill wholesome and Godly values in
America's children.

Kirk just wrapped up this year's "See You at the Library Day," where
we countered the Left and brought conservative values straight to
America's children.

Kirk is busy spearheading the "Bible Revival" movement that gets
Biblical values -- that America was founded upon -- back into schools.

And Kirk just finished filming Season 3 of our television show "Iggy
and Mr. Kirk" that teaches children how to respond to the deceitful
culture with Biblical values and steadfast faith.

I'M WRITING YOU WITH SUCH URGENCY BECAUSE SEASON 3 OF "IGGY AND MR.
KIRK" IS IN JEOPARDY.

AND IF I CAN'T RAISE $48,523 IN THE NEXT FOUR WEEKS, "IGGY AND MR.
KIRK" WILL BE DELAYED -- OR EVEN POSTPONED INDEFINITELY.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

The radical Leftists who attack us because we're reaching America's
children with God's Truth would love nothing more than to see "Iggy
and Mr. Kirk" shut down.

They hate that "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" has skyrocketed to the top of Angel
Studios' streaming service. They hate that we've created a path around
the addictive mind rot they put on TV.

It's like Kirk always says... It's not enough to complain about
culture raising our children. We must create something better for
them.

The first 2 seasons of "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" have reached millions of
children and counting, but Season 3 is in jeopardy.

If "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" isn't funded, there will be no voice on TV
countering the Left's dangerous lies.

Lies like Drag Queens leading a Pride Parade SingAlong on Blue's
Clues...

Same-sex weddings on Arthur...

And Sesame Street using YOUR tax dollars to normalize same-sex parents
and men in dresses.

And that's just what's on TV. Not to mention the thousands of 'Queer
Kid' videos on platforms like YouTube Kids.

The days of The Andy Griffith Show and Father Knows Best are gone. The
Left has purposely used TV to create a generation of zombie children
who are glued to their screens.

"Iggy and Mr. Kirk" is the antidote to that Leftist TV brainwashing.

It uses low-stimulation production and teaches children how to respond
to the deceitful culture with Biblical values and steadfast faith.
Like when Mr. Kirk teaches Iggy:

* to love how God created him as an iguana, even when the villainous
Culture the Vulture says Iggy must become a human to fit in.
* to rely on the wisdom of parents -- one mom and one dad -- to
solve life's problems.
* to be BRAVE by speaking truth in the face of the Left's lies.

BRAVE FOR GOOD NEEDS TO RAISE $48,523 IN THE NEXT 4 WEEKS JUST FOR
"IGGY AND MR. KIRK."
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

That doesn't even begin to account for our "Bible Revival" efforts and
the conservative Story Hours for the rest of the year.

Fellow Patriot, please help. Because this is so urgent, I wanted to
reach out to Americans who share our concern for the next generation.

On behalf of myself, Kirk, and our entire team, thank you for
considering supporting BRAVE FOR GOOD. Together, we will rebuild a
culture that honors God and His will for our lives.

Sincerely,

Dr. Trent Talbot

Founder, BRAVE for Good

P.S. I told Kirk Cameron I would write you with this URGENT update
while he's swamped with "See You at the Library Day," our "Bible
Revival" movement, and Season 3 of "Iggy and Mr. Kirk." I HOPE YOU CAN
HELP WITH YOUR TAX-DEDUCTIBLE GIFT OF $50, $100, OR EVEN $500. Thank
you for caring about America's families!

DONATE

[BRAVE for Good]

BRAVE FOR GOOD is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. Your gift is
tax-deductible to the full extent allowed by law.

Hey folks,
Donald Trump just got his ass handed to him in the midterms, and the MAGA meltdown is absolutely glorious.
Ted Cruz is panicking about impeachment. J.D. Vance is scrambling to explain the losses. And Trump? He's canceling public appearances while his own advisers admit the Democratic victory was too big to challenge.
But here's the thing: **Winning the election is just the beginning. Now comes the accountability.**
We have a real opportunity to expose the corruption, hold these people responsible, and build a government that actually works for working families. And Democrats cannot afford to waste it.
Here's what we get into:
* [**00:01:01**] Ted Cruz sounds the alarm about Democratic investigations and impeachment proceedings as MAGA faces a political reckoning.
* [**00:04:38**] Trump cancels public appearances after the midterm disaster, and even his own advisers acknowledge the scale of the defeat.

* [**00:10:17**] J.D. Vance faces a devastating political setback as Republicans lose key races and MAGA insiders scramble to defend Trump.
* [**00:13:01**] The message every Democrat needs to hear: Corruption is an affordability issue, and accountability must connect directly to people's everyday lives.

This is about so much more than one election. It's about breaking the grip of billionaires and corrupt politicians on our government. It's about making housing affordable, creating good-paying jobs, and restoring dignity to working people. And it's about proving that democracy can still deliver for all of us.
**We have the momentum. Now we need the courage to use it.**

name: Jon Ossoff
subject: History
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jon Ossoff for Senate
body:
# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=3257%2E5691347%2EpQz3o5)

Last night I addressed a crowd of thousands in downtown Atlanta to mark our historic and decisive victory and discuss what’s next for our state, our country, and our world.
[](https://act.electjon.com/go/7779?t=2&akid=3257%2E5691347%2EpQz3o5)
[**(You can watch my speech here on YouTube.)**](http://act.electjon.com/go/7781?t=3&akid=3257%2E5691347%2EpQz3o5)
Here’s what I said:
Hello, Atlanta!
Thank you, Georgia.
_Georgia, you did it._
And let me be the first to offer public congratulations to the Governor-Elect of the State of Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms.
To every volunteer who poured your heart and soul into this effort and everyone who chipped in so we could face down the dark money Super PACs, thank you.
To Charlie Bailey and his crew at the strongest Democratic Party of Georgia in a generation, thank you.
To my staff, to Ellen and Keenan and Rey and Miryam and Chandra and the best team in American politics, thank you.
To my wonderful wife Alisha and my daughters Eva and Lila, my parents, and my entire family, thank you for your unconditional love and support.
And to the people of the great State of Georgia for the trust you've invested in me to continue representing you in the United States Senate, thank you, thank you, thank you.
**THE FIRST LIGHT OF DAWN IS ON THE HORIZON**
And listen, in sweeping and decisive victories, the American people have rebuked the depravity, corruption, and incompetence of the failed lame duck President Donald J. Trump.
And if, at times these last two years, amidst the ceaseless onslaught of brutality and indecency, you doubted whether our Republic would survive, let tonight's results give you courage that the first light of dawn is on the horizon.
But remember that in living rooms and backyards and at rallies across Georgia these last two years, together we've affirmed that our task is not just to contain one president's wickedness, but to heal the brokenness beneath.
_That this moment is an opening not for restoration, but for reformation._
And so, amidst our celebration tonight, we must acknowledge that the underlying crisis gripping our Republic remains and that therefore our most vital work lies ahead.
**AMERICA'S FORGOTTEN FAMILIES**
Because while the wealthy and well-lobbied feast on inside information and official favors, America's forgotten families are treated to systemic corporate disrespect and official indifference, working harder and harder while the treadmill just gets faster and steeper, and the bills get higher and higher.
Instead of reading your daughter her favorite book that precious spare hour after work, you're on the phone begging the insurance company to cover the medicine that prevents her seizures.
You report the black mold to your landlord, who doesn't fix the leak, and the ambulance for your toddler's asthma attack is followed by a $3,000 bill.
For too many, home ownership's a fantasy. Family farms face ruin. And while health care's never cost more, plastics invade our bodies, blood, and breast milk. Toxic forever chemicals taint half the country's drinking water, and polluters have been granted fresh license to poison our air.
**ADRIFT IN A GALE**
Abroad, American credibility and leadership are in decay, and the world is rearming for global conflict. And at our grave peril, humanity is fast forgetting the terrible lessons of two World Wars and the Holocaust.
Meanwhile, the titans of Silicon Valley dig bunkers for themselves and warn that the artificial intelligence they're creating risks human extinction.
And amidst these challenges of unprecedented consequence and complexity, though we rightly celebrate tonight's historic victory, the fact is we've been too long mired in a small and selfish politics, bought by big money, unmoored from fixed moral principles, and resigned to intractable division.
In other words, the United States has been adrift in a gale. **But, Georgia, we can and will reclaim control over our own destiny.**
**A NEW MAJORITY**
Tonight, we've struck a necessary and undeniable blow on behalf of justice and progress. And tonight, in Georgia, we've proven not just that unity is possible, but that we can overcome division without sacrificing clarity of purpose.
In every corner of Georgia, this campaign urged the necessity of banning corporate and secret money from politics, of American leadership for peace and human rights around the world, and of guaranteeing health care for every single American.
We committed to continuing the work of bringing Big Pharma, Big Insurance, and Big Tech to heel in the defense of struggling Georgia families.
And on that basis, we built a new majority that extends far beyond party lines, and the foundation for that new majority has been trust — trust built through years of phone calls to mayors, pastors, and farmers, and trust measured in problems solved together, without concern for ideology or party affiliation.
I thank Republican Mayors Matheson, Smith, and Fry of Valdosta, Tifton, and Toccoa, and the countless other Republican leaders who joined our team. And I thank the hundreds of thousands of independent and Republican voters who joined our winning coalition.
Never doubt that unity is possible.
Even in his final months, Congressman Lewis always reminded us that we all live in one American house. _Do you remember?_ In one world house. He called it the inevitable truth that we're all members of one human family.
And I know many of you have poured yourselves into this campaign, not for my sake or for the sake of the Democratic Party, but because you're so deeply troubled by the pain our fellow human beings are enduring right now — the terror of a child watching ICE take away her mother, the despair of a cancer patient losing coverage mid-treatment.
But that ache in your heart, that pit in your stomach, that feeling's what reminds us we're all in this together, that we're not just one United States, we're one united people.
_E pluribus unum._ Out of many, one.
And over centuries, despite our sins and through courageous struggle, the flame of American freedom has grown brighter and bolder and given hope to the whole world.
**REAWAKENING**
_We've stumbled. We almost lost our way. But, Georgia, for all our troubles, let me assure you tonight that, propelled by this historic and undeniable victory, I have no doubt we will overcome them._
And now our task is to reawaken that great national spirit that defeated fascism and established Social Security, that put men on the moon and passed civil rights laws in order to meet the challenges and obligations of our time, because I refuse to accept that my two little girls will grow up in a world as dark and dangerous and cruel as this one threatens to become.
I refuse to accept that Eva and Lila will grow up with artificial friends and teachers in a society where the sick die not because there's no cure, but because they have no money. Where we have enough nuclear weapons to destroy the world a thousandfold, but we refuse to guarantee health care for every citizen. On a poisoned planet, rearming for world war, where human life is cheap, and might makes right.
See, when Eva is old enough to ask why I let this happen, I'm determined to answer truthfully that I didn't.
I'll tell her how the same year she turned five, Georgia overcame every doubt and dirty trick not just to win, but to set a new course for our state and our country and our world.
That we defended voting rights and civil rights at home.
That we restored American leadership toward peace and human rights around the world.
That we finally acted to ban corporate money and secret money from our politics, and that we guaranteed health care for every single American.
Thank you, Georgia.
Tonight, we celebrate this victory, and tomorrow we get back to work.
Thank you so much.
👋 Wait! Before you go... 👋
[**Our work isn’t finished. If you’d like to continue supporting Jon Ossoff, you can donate here.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-election.Ndt3em&refcode=em261104-2-subs&utm_campaign=em261104-2-subs&t=4&akid=3257%2E5691347%2EpQz3o5)

Peter, _Today feels good._
There was a mountain of skepticism I had to work against. People thought I couldn't win. But we kept climbing that mountain and here we are, at the top!
I am proud to be the first-ever woman Lieutenant Governor-elect of the great state of Texas.
We stood up against the most powerful Republican in Texas because we know Texans deserve better. We’ve banned Dan, and we've sent Patrick packing. Dan Patrick spent tens of millions of dollars in false advertising. We showed him that his money can't buy an election.
Last night, I couldn't help but think of Governor Ann Richards and the great Barbara Jordan looking down on us smiling and cheering. After 30 long years, a NEW generation of women have shown up to demand change, _ready to lead Texas._
It's long past time that Texans had a Lieutenant Governor who leads with compassion and integrity — who focuses on real issues, instead of using fear to divide us.
No one wins a campaign like this alone.
**To everyone who believed in this race, thank you. We did it.** And to everyone who volunteered your time or donated your money, thank you. I am humbled by the trust that you have placed in me to bring sanity back to the Texas Senate.
To the Texans who may not have voted for me — I will work for you, too.
I want to show all Texans what it's like to have a Lieutenant Governor who serves the people instead of special interests.
Change is in the air. And we're just getting started.
Thank you and God bless Texas,
Vikki Goodwin _Lieutenant Governor-Elect of Texas_

Friend, We just made history together. In his victory speech, our first Muslim Senator Abdul El-Sayed told his racist right-wing opponent: “You chose hate, and Michigan chose hope.” **Americans across the country chose hope over hate** — from the local to state to federal levels. Despite record-breaking spending from billionaires and corporations, the American people didn’t get divided or distracted. We chose each other and showed that **organized people can beat big money**. **Thank you** for voting, volunteering to get out the vote, supporting candidates who refused corporate PAC money, and rebuking Trump’s agenda of violence and dehumanization. Every single demographic and every area across the country swung way to the left of how they voted just two years ago in 2024. Even in most of the districts that Republicans redrew to take away our votes. Over 50 DSA candidates won, and in NBC’s exit polling, one-third of young voters self-identified as democratic socialists. In Michigan, I won re-election with 76 percent of the vote, and 17 of our endorsed candidates won. That includes Will Lawrence, the founder of activist group Sunrise Movement who flipped his congressional district blue. We flipped seats in conservative districts and states across the country. This will make a real difference in people’s lives! Many of my soon-to-be colleagues are rooted in their communities, like Donavan McKinney in the House of Representatives district next to mine. They know what it’s like to be working class and they understand how urgently we need to meet everyday people’s needs. Black and Native and Muslim candidates also made history. Nearly everyone we endorsed outside of Michigan won their races, including New Jersey candidates Analilia Mejia and Dr. Adam Hamawy who won seats in Congress, and Aber Kawas, who’ll be the first Palestinian and Muslim woman to serve in New York’s state legislature. Dr. Hamawy served patients in Gaza. With him and others like Darializa Avila Chevalier and Aisha Wahab winning their elections, **we’re about to have 8 Muslim members of Congress. That’s more than ever before.** **We’ll also have more progressive and more pro-Palestine members of Congress than ever before.** We will be saving lives at home and abroad. We have decisive Democratic majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate. In the House, **I will push on the oversight committee to hold Trump and his allies accountable** for all the laws they broke and all the constitutional rights they violated. Together, **we will push Democrats to not only undo Trump’s harms and lower the cost of living, but also to build toward popular game-changing policies and programs that the American people deserve** , such as free universal healthcare. People have been struggling and oppressed since long before Trump, and they voted in Democrats to show courage and fight for the people. **We have a mandate to root out racism and deliver for working families.** We won on ballot measures across the country, including taking on big money in politics in Michigan and protecting abortion access in Missouri, Virginia, and elsewhere. The biggest U.S. city so far (Providence, Rhode Island) voted to divest from Israel. And people voted to pass 35 measures against data centers! We turned out voters in my state of Michigan, including in my district. Detroit broke all-time records for early voting, and Dearborn saw the highest voter turnout in history. People also broke turnout records in cities across the country, including in Texas and across the South. As we’re seeing in places like Mississippi, which hasn’t been called at the time of writing, every single vote matters. Justin Pearson, who narrowly lost his election in a wildly gerrymandered new district that spanned 200 miles and 15 counties, told us months ago to invest in the South. He was right. Even without support from the national party, anti-genocide democratic socialist Angie Nixon’s race for U.S. Senate in Florida was extremely close — and she announced that she’ll run again for Senate in 2028. **We will keep building the bench of progressives and coming together against oppression.** Against the oligarchy and corporate sell-outs trying to steal our power and our money. Against Big Polluters and fascists and their enablers. Against genocide, apartheid, and endless wars. As Abdul El-Sayed has said, our tax dollars should go toward helping our kids, not to kill other people's kids. Last night Abdul told Trump: “I know you struggle with my name, so... you can just go on and call me Senator.” And he said:
> _“To the super PACs and special interests that tried to beat us, we are coming for your system of politics. To AIPAC, which spent $42 million against us, thank you for giving me the opportunity to beat you twice.”_
**We will keep fighting for a government that serves and helps the people. We will keep fighting to make life better for everyone.** We stand with workers around the world who are rejecting fascism and building our power. We’ve got work to do in the next few weeks, months, and years. For example, in my district alone, 50,000 residents will have to pay more this year for health insurance because Republicans refused to extend ACA tax credits. Let’s celebrate what we’ve won, and let’s keep working to reverse Republicans’ cuts and create the future we need, where all of our rights are respected, and where no one is treated as disposable. We’re at a turning point in our country. Let’s abolish ICE, raise the minimum wage to at least $25 an hour, and secure clean water and healthcare for all — as well as affordable housing, childcare, education, food, utility bills, and more! Everyone deserves to thrive with dignity and safety. I’m looking forward to continuing to fight for better alongside you. # ALL IN FOR ADELITA💙🌵
Adelita for Congress Newsletter
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | Hi Peter,

**WE DID IT!** As I sit down to write this, my heart is full, and the magnitude of what we’ve built together over these past months is just starting to set in.
Campaigns are often talked about in numbers, doors knocked, phone calls made, and ballots counted. But anyone who has ever been in the trenches of a fight this high-stakes knows the truth: a campaign isn’t measured by the numbers. **It’s measured by the people**. It is measured by _**you**_**.** It is measured by **La Máquina.**
When the news felt heavy you didn’t step back, **you stepped up.** You gave up your weekends, your mornings, your resting time, and your peace of mind because you believed in a vision of a better, fairer, more compassionate future for our community. **You believed in Adelita, and more importantly, you believed in each other.**
Because of your relentless grit, we didn't just run a campaign,**we built a movement.** Every time you knocked on a door in the heat, every time you smiled through tired feet, and every time you shared a kind word with a neighbor, you were sewing a stronger fabric for our community. **You showed up for our schools, our children, our Indigenous communities, and our shared dignity.**
History isn't made by those who sit on the sidelines waiting for change to happen. It is forged by people like you, people with the courage to hope and the stamina to fight for it.
You have reminded everyone in this district that when we lock arms, we are unstoppable.
**Thank you for your sacrifice, your passion, and your fierce, unending heart. I am deeply humbled to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with every single one of you.******
---
|
---
| |
I hope you’ll miss reading these emails just as much I will miss writing them. Even when I sounded like a broken record, you listened and you showed up time and time again.
Thank you for everything. **Until 2028 : )**

**With profound gratitude and solidarity,**
Field Director De La Rosa 💙🌵
